title: Human Resources Expert - CDR
body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/228**
- **Position Title**: Human Resources Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 16 November 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 23 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zPWKGabdFSzUtF9pkcm7vR_poJ8-_L84/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zPWKGabdFSzUtF9pkcm7vR_poJ8-_L84/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

To this end, there is a need to strengthen the human resource function itself, including its organization, processes, policies, systems, and service delivery arrangements. A strengthened HR function is essential to support workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, career progression, and other core personnel processes, while also providing the institutional capacity required to support the wider CDR reform programme. In this context, the HR function needs to move beyond the administration of personnel matters toward a more structured and integrated approach to workforce management aligned with CDR's functions, organizational structure, and operational priorities.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Human Resources Expert to support CDR in implementing the human resource measures under Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will review and update the existing and proposed job descriptions against the applicable legislative framework and operational requirements, reassess the HR function identified, and translate the findings into an HR Strategy, HR Policies and Procedures Manual, and target operating model for the Human Resources Department. The assignment will also ensure that the HR Strategy incorporates the human resource requirements arising from other reform areas, including change management and the development and implementation of a Human Resource Information System.

Through this assignment, the Expert will contribute to establishing a clearer, more functional, and sustainable human resource framework for CDR, with defined roles and responsibilities, updated job descriptions, appropriate HR policies and procedures, and an operating model capable of supporting both CDR's immediate staffing needs and the longer-term institutional reforms identified in the roadmap.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Human Resources Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Assessment of the Human Resource Function and HR Strategy**

- Review human resource arrangements, relevant institutional findings and proposed reform priorities to establish the baseline for the assessment.
- Review the legal and regulatory framework that governs CDR staff, including Decree No. 10941 of 2003, Decree No. 10942 of 2003, Section 54 of the 2004 Budget Law, the Council of Ministers freeze on hiring and promotion, the allowance decrees issued between 2021 and 2025, the Council of Ministers decision of 19 June 2025 and the internal regulations of CDR, and record for each human resource process the rule that governs it and the authority that approves it.
- Validate the workforce baseline with the Administrative Affairs Division, covering filled and vacant mandated posts, individual contractors, project implementation unit personnel, projected retirements, resignations and multi-role assignments, and identify any figures that are not substantiated by the available records.
- Assess the mandate, organization, staffing and capacity of the Human Resources Department within the Administrative Affairs Division.
- Map the human resource processes as they operate today, covering workforce planning, recruitment and onboarding, personnel records, attendance and leave, performance evaluation and promotion, training, discipline, and separation and end-of-service, and record where a process is informal, paper-based or undocumented.
- Identify the gaps between current practice, the legal framework and the needs of the reformed structure, and distinguish the gaps that CDR can close within the current legal framework from those that depend on the amendment of Decree No. 10941 and Decree No. 10942.
- Establish the baseline and the method of measurement for human resource indicators including the employee-satisfaction baseline survey, coordinated with the staff survey used for the change indicators so that staff are surveyed once.
- Prepare the HR Strategy for CDR, setting out its objectives, priority measures, responsibilities and sequence, aligned with the Target Roadmap and the Interim Arrangements, and addressing the vacancy, multi-role and key-person dependency risks identified.
- Set out in the Strategy the recruitment route for the transitional period and the longer-term recruitment model, consistent with the position on the Civil Service Board mandate.
- Define the target operating model of the Human Resources Department, comprising its functions, roles, reporting lines and staffing, and its role as business owner of the Human Resource Information System.
- Set out in the Strategy the human resource input to the Change Management Committee on the resistance factors linked to restructuring, redeployment and remuneration, and coordinate the staff messages on these matters with the Change Management and Communications Expert.
- Set out in the Strategy the business requirements of the Human Resources Department for the Human Resource Information System identified, validating the human resource process definitions, the business rules for attendance, leave and missions, and the employee data structure, and confirming the legal basis of the end-of-service calculation before any procurement.
- Prepare the action plan that implements the Strategy, with responsibilities assigned by post and timing reconciled with the master roadmap.

**Workstream 2. Review and Update of Job Descriptions**

- Compile the inventory of the job descriptions already prepared, comprising those prepared by the Administrative Affairs Division including identified positions, Terms of Reference, job description summaries and IT Department job descriptions, and identify the existing and new posts for which no description exists.
- Review each JD against the applicable legislation, including the ranks, sub-grades and qualification requirements under Decree No. 10942, the divisional and departmental mandates under Decree No. 10941 and the reformed structure, and, for procurement posts, the requirements of Law No. 244 of 2021 on the competencies and career paths of procurement staff.
- Review each description against the operational needs of CDR, testing with the Heads of Division whether the scope of work, reporting lines, decision rights and qualifications correspond to the work the role performs under the redesigned business processes.
- Harmonize the descriptions into a single template that records, for each post, the interim placement within the current structure and the position under the reformed structure, so that the same document serves recruitment now and redeployment later.
- Update the descriptions on the basis of the review, remove overlaps between posts, reflect the segregation of duties required in the financial management, procurement and ICT processes, and complete the descriptions for the posts not yet covered.
- Reconcile the rank assigned to each post with the indicative costing identified, and record each discrepancy for the remuneration and financing proposal.
- Confirm the updated descriptions with the Heads of Division and prepare the submission through which the Board approves them.
- Prepare the procedure through which the Administrative Affairs Division maintains the descriptions as the structure changes, and brief the Division on its application.

**Workstream 3. HR Policies, Performance Management and Capacity Development**

- Prepare the HR Policies and Procedures Manual, documenting each human resource process with its steps, responsibilities, approvals, time standards and forms, and removing steps whose risk does not justify them before the process is digitized.
- Review the performance-evaluation system for promotion reactivated in 2025, and propose how it draws on the updated job descriptions within the promotion rules of Decree No. 10942.
- Prepare the human resource provisions on employee protection, covering discrimination and workplace misconduct, conflict-of-interest declarations for staff holding more than one role, and disciplinary consequences for retaliation, in coordination with the Audit Committee, which owns the whistleblower policy set out, and with the Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert.
- Prepare the competency-based capacity development strategy, consolidating the role-based learning pathways with the identified function-specific training and defining the training-needs assessment method, the format of the annual training plan and the pre- and post-training assessment of competency.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 11 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within three months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Human Resources Management, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Management, Public Policy, Law, or a related field.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) assessing and strengthening human resource functions and organizational structures, including workforce planning, HR processes, job descriptions, performance management, recruitment, staff development and HR policies; and (ii) designing and implementing HR strategies, operating models, policies and procedures, including HR information systems and competency-based capacity development frameworks.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

title: [Pipeline Position] Program Implementation and Performance Manager (Africa Regional Office) [Based in Kigali]
body:
## ***\*\*\*This is a pipeline position created to prepare for anticipated hiring needs. Final hiring decisions will be made following internal review processes.\*\*\****

## **We are seeking a Program Implementation and Performance Manager for 2-year-regular position (renewable) to work within Africa Regional Office at the International Vaccine Institute in Kigali, Rwanda. (Duty station: Kigali, Rwanda)**

**Job Description**

This role is responsible for the technical implementation of VEA4A, working with the Program Director, participating institutions and other partners to translate programme objectives into activities and apply technical expertise throughout implementation. Its responsibilities also include institutional readiness, programme performance, monitoring, evaluation and learning, inclusion, safeguarding coordination and implementation learning for VEA4A. It also encompasses the day-to-day management and coordination of programme implementation, including planning, resource and budget monitoring, risk management and reporting, to support the delivery of agreed commitments on time, within budget and to the required quality standards. The role works with the Program Director, participating institutions and other partners to monitor progress and inform programme adaptations.

**Key Roles & Responsibilities**

**1. Institutional readiness assessment and programme performance monitoring**

- Lead HEI readiness assessment, institutional-strengthening monitoring and readiness recommendations with the Training Lead and HEI teams.
- Lead the MEL framework, indicator definitions, data-quality arrangements, performance dashboards, quarterly reviews, learning briefs and programme reporting.
- Integrate evidence from training, HEIs, participants and employment pathways and recommend adaptations to the Program Director.
- Facilitate narrative and performance reporting to the Foundation and ensure timely technical, budget and partner inputs.

**2. Programme planning and implementation**

- Manage day-to-day implementation in accordance with IVI Project Management Guidelines, monitoring progress against the approved workplan, timeline, quality requirements and budget.
- Translate the approved proposal, workplan and budget into integrated annual, quarterly and detailed implementation plans.
- Own the master workplan, critical path, milestones, dependencies, resource plan and consolidated delivery calendar.
- Coordinate routine implementation across ARUA, HEIs, IVI technical teams, functional units, providers and all programme workstreams.
- Manage scope, schedule, deliverables, risks, issues, decisions, changes, assumptions and corrective actions through documented project controls.
- Monitor partner deliverables and programme commitments and ensure that delays or performance concerns receive timely action.
- Chair routine implementation meetings and act for the Program Director on operational matters when formally delegated.

**3. Budget tracking and programme document preparation**

- Monitor programme expenditure and support budget phasing and forecasting, working with the Project Administrator and relevant colleagues to identify and communicate variances against the approved budget.
- Contribute to the preparation of programme-related agreements and contracts with participating institutions, service providers and other partners, in coordination with relevant IVI functions.

**4. Systems oversight and safeguarding & inclusion facilitation**

- Lead data-quality arrangements for programme monitoring and reporting.
- Oversee programme-wide digital operations, including the relationship among applications, LMS, participant records, course records and reporting systems.
- Facilitate the implementation of safeguarding, inclusion and data-protection requirements across the programme, working with IVI specialist functions and partners\*\*.\*\*

**Job Requirements and Qualifications**

**1. Education Requirements**

- Advanced degree in health sciences, public health, project management, development, education, social sciences or a related field.

**2. Related Field Work Experience**

- 8+ years with Master’s degree

**3. Technical and Professional Skills / Knowledge**

- Substantial experience managing complex, multi-partner and donor-funded programmes, preferably across more than one country.
- Demonstrated knowledge of project planning, scope and change control, risk management, partner performance, budget monitoring and donor reporting.
- Experience in monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), data quality and institutional-capacity assessment.
- Understanding of safeguarding and inclusive programme delivery.
- Experience in workforce development, higher education, health training or vaccine-related programmes is desirable.
- Integrated project and programme management.
- Analytical problem-solving and prioritisation.
- Programme performance monitoring and use of evidence.
- Cross-functional coordination and collaboration.
- Donor reporting and concise writing.
- Risk, safeguarding and data-governance awareness.
- Ability to move between strategic context and operational detail.
- Ability to travel internationally.
- Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is desirable.

**4. Key Competency**

- Client Orientation
- Communication
- Commitment to Continuous Learning

**5. Language Proficiency**

- Fluent in English (spoken, written)

**\*\*\*IVI welcomes applications from all sections of the community. We encourage women to apply, especially from countries that are currently under-represented within IVI.\*\*\***

title: Hydrology Database Manager
body:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Geoscience Energy and Maritime (GEM) Division** provides advice, technical assistance, research and training support to Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs). There are four (4) areas of scientific programming within this division:

1. **Oceans and Maritime Programme (OMP)** – assists member countries with services that provide applied ocean science and knowledge for evidence-based policy-making and technical solutions for improved ocean and maritime governance, management and capacity development.
2. **Georesources and Energy Programme (GEP)** – assists member countries by applying technical knowledge in the areas of geoscience and sustainable energy use.
3. **Disaster and Water Resilience Programme (DWRP)** – assists member countries to demonstrate strengthened resilience through integrated action on disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, natural resource management and increased access to water and sanitation.
4. **Earth and Ocean Observation Services** – Promoting spatial data and systems analysis and capacity to improve decision-making to improve resilience and sustainable resource management.

The role – **Hydrology Database Manager** will support the improvement of the integrity, accessibility, and usability of hydrological data across the Pacific region, strengthening information systems and decision-making for drought management.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Technical Advice and Support**

- Provide high-quality technical advice and support on water resource related technical and research needs at the regional, national and local levels.
- Provide high-quality technical advice and support to manage and maintain hydrological databases, including data quality assurance, data integration, data analysis and processing, user support and training, system development and upgrades, data sharing and accessibility, documentation and compliance.

**Networking and Communications**

- Establish and develop effective communication and relationships within member countries, development partners, and SPC to promote drought monitoring, and water resource assessment, development, and management for the region.
- Ensure accurate, audience focused sensitive water resource information is accessible and available to a wide variety of relevant stakeholders.

**Capacity Building**

- Design and implement a structured approach to capacity building in participating member countries to strengthen the long-term capacity of country counterparts in drought monitoring, hydrology, data management, data analysis other water resource assessment and analysis skills.

**Provision of high-quality technical reporting**

- Provision of high-quality technical reports ensuring SPC standards are met for publication.

**Support project implementation**

- Project implementation actions and requirements are undertaken and completed with efficiency, and within SPC policy and procedures.
- Provide support for resource mobilisation for ongoing sustainability.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A bachelor of science degree with a specialisation in a relevant field such as hydrology, hydrogeology, geophysics or water resources engineering or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7-8 years of experience in hydrological services and demonstrated experience working with hydrological databases.
- Experienced in the application and analysis of hydrological data, and database management to develop information products.
- Demonstrated experience in the use and application of GIS.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement and report writing skills.
- Demonstrated project management and organisational skills, including working and managing projects in remote locations.
- Knowledge of Gender Equity and Social Inclusion (GESI), and People Centred Approaches (PCA) in delivery of projects.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **1 year** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Hydrology Database Manager** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,703‒3,379 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 8,354–10,442 (USD 3,623-4,528; EUR 3,269-4,086). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

title: Technical Head of Program Ukraine M/F/X
body:
**Place: Kyiv, Ukraine**  
**Starting Date : February 2027**  
**Length of contrat : 12 months**

**We will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.**

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview.

**CONTEXTUALISATION**

From February 2022, HI has re-opened a Country Programme in Ukraine to respond to the humanitarian needs triggered by the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation.

In 2026, HI pillars of interventions are:

- Health: HI aims to improve access to quality physical rehabilitation and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS) for conflict-affected vulnerable population.
- Protection: Given the scale of humanitarian and protection needs, HI intervenes at various levels to ensure that vulnerable conflict-affected populations have access to multi-sectoral services tailored to their needs. In addition, HI aims to foster a disability-inclusive humanitarian response.
- Humanitarian Mine Action: Ongoing attacks dangerously exacerbated Explosive Ordnance (EO) contamination in Ukraine. HI implements EORE/CPP, Advocacy, NTS/TS/Clearance, VA (Victim Assistance)

HI has 2 hubs, one in the East (based in Dnipro), one in the North East (based in Kharkiv), and the coordination office is in Kyiv.

The position is based in Kiev. The security situation in Ukraine remains relatively stable, although air alert is frequently active. However, markets, restaurants and cafes are open, and life continues as normal. There is a strict curfew, the hours depend on the region

**Technical Head of Program**

**1. Main Mission**

Under the responsibility of the Country Director, the Technical Head of Programme contributes to the implementation of Humanité & Inclusion's mandate and 10-year strategy within his/her programme.

He/she is the driving force behind the programmatic development of social missions within his/her technical scope, and ensures that the quality and impact of the projects implemented in the programme are optimised, in line with the priorities defined in the Technical Strategies.

The Technical Head of Program is responsible for a team of specialists (Technical Field Specialist, Business Developer, MEAL and quality assurance).

**Mission 1: Management**

- Embodies HI's values on a daily basis, and is a role model.
- Understands the strategy, makes it explicit, translating it into operational objectives for the team, leads the necessary changes.
- Organises the operational management of his or her team, structures the work around identified processes, steers performance, and facilitates problem solving.
- Contributes to the development of its employees, creating the conditions to enable their commitment, their professionalism and their attachment to HI.

**2. Responsibilities**

**2.1. Strategy and Management**

- Proposes the development of the programmatic framework of the programme's StratOp, based on an analysis of the sectoral context and following the StraTechs and Development Plans of the Emergency, Atlas and Impact-Innovation-Information divisions, in conjunction with the operational teams.
- Ensures the deployment of cross-cutting approaches within programming, promotes cross-sectoral synergies and intervention themes.
- Proposes the design and evolution of the programme's technical support, based on the skills of the technical specialists and technical profiles assigned to the projects, and according to the key priority sectors and the skills of the project managers.
- Contributes, at least once a year, (regarding its projects and data) to the annual monitoring of the StratOp and to the planning of the following year's programmes (i.e. support missions and evaluations).
- Ensures the MEAL part of the Operational Strategy, pilots the related action plan and the strategy monitoring tool.

**2.2. Development of the Social Mission and Programmatic Vision**

Defines the programme's funding strategy for new themes or innovations in existing sectors, ensures the development of opportunities for each theme within its scope, proposes the geographical development of HI sectors, and ensures the conformity of the technical proposal with nexus issues.

- Provides support to the Country Director and Ops Manager in considering the development of new value propositions (including needs assessment, feasibility, strategic alliances, major contracts).
- Contributes to the development of the fundraising strategy, in coordination with the Operations Manager / Senior Grant Officer.
- Leads the transformation of financial opportunities into projects.
- Produces and drives the design of major projects (multiple countries, one or more themes) or new strategic projects in the Country.
- Identifies and develops regional or local partnerships and/or consortia with NGOs, institutions, companies on technical priorities or important themes in the region in collaboration with the Ops Manager.

**2.3. Quality Standards and Expertise with the MEAL and Technical Profiles of the Programme**

Controls and monitors the technical quality and relevance of HI activities within its scope:

- Ensures that project managers receive appropriate technical and methodological guidance and support from MEAL team members and specialists based at headquarters or at programme level.
- Ensures quality control of projects and the programme and raises alerts and recommendations.
- Follows up the implementation of recommendations from support missions, evaluation or audit, as appropriate.
- Ensures a local sectoral watch and collects good practices.

**Responsibilities Related to MEAL**

- Ensures the improvement of the quality of project management processes, as defined by the Planning Monitoring and Evaluation (PME) policy.
- Leads the improvement of HI's response, including the implementation of impact and effect measurement tools.
- Establishes mechanisms for accountability to beneficiaries.
- Ensures the appropriation of programmes and HI’s frameworks and learning methodologies globally.
- Supports the monitoring of projects.

**Technical Expertise, Learning and Innovation**

- Ensures that specialists develop a local professional channel/talent pool and contributes to the animation of the professional channel of the technical divisions and the MEALs.
- Ensures the development of research and innovation projects in the region, when appropriate.
- Ensures deployment and compliance with global frameworks, institutional policies and standards.

**2.4. External Representation and Promotion of HI's Expertise**

- Represents HI's expertise in all relevant networks (including clusters).
- Supports the specialists and the Country Director in the representation towards partners, institutional donors and authorities.
- Contributes to advocacy (including evidence-based) on specific issues, in line with the StratOp and federal advocacy priorities.
- Contributes locally to communication messages, in line with the StratOp and federal communication priorities.

**2.5. Emergency Preparedness and Response**

- Leads the emergency preparedness actions in his/her department and, in case of emergency, reorganizes the priorities of his/her team according to the humanitarian imperative, in order to ensure a rapid and effective response from HI.

## Requirements

- Master’s degree in one of HI's technical sectors of intervention and/or international cooperation and/or humanitarian development
- You have a minimum of 5 years’ experience in humanitarian development with experience in project management (multi or complex) and experience(s) in one of HI's technical sectors of intervention.
- Excellent english language skills
- You have strong managerial skills: Being able to develop team members: developing the ability of staff to work independently.
- You know how to position yourself to make things happen
- Excellent organization and time management skills: you know how to simplify and prioritize
- You’re a good communicator, Ability to manage stress, Empathy, Autonomy and flexibility

## Benefits

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission:

- 12 months International contract starting from 15h, January 2027;
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
    - Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
    - Pension scheme;
    - Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
    - Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
- Salary from 2869 gross/month upon experience;
- Perdiem: 597€ net/month - paid in the payroll
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary;
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
- R&R: according to the level of the mission Level 3: 5 days every 8 weeks => + possible transport/package support;
- Position:
- **Unaccompanied:**
    - Payment for travel costs (air ticket & visa) and transport of your personal effects; (from 12 months of mission)
    - Mission of more than 12 months: a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child (from the second child) paid in the payroll;
- Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI;
- If you are resident in the country: local package.

title: Project Officer (Distribution_MPCA-Hygiene and MHM) - Hasaka
body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Project Officer (Distribution – MPCA, Hygiene and MHM) is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities related to Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), hygiene distributions, and Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHM). The position ensures that assistance is delivered in a timely, safe, transparent, inclusive, and accountable manner, in line with approved project objectives, workplans, budgets, donor requirements, World Vision policies, and relevant humanitarian standards.

The Project Officer oversees distribution preparations and field implementation, coordinates beneficiary verification and distribution arrangements, supervises Distribution Workers and other assigned field personnel, and works closely with Logistics, Finance, MEAL, Protection, WASH, and other relevant teams. The position also ensures that assistance is responsive to the needs of affected communities, including women and adolescent girls, persons with disabilities, older people, and other vulnerable groups, while promoting dignity, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Project Planning, Coordination and Distribution Implementation 25%**

- Support the development and implementation of activity workplans, distribution plans, schedules, and operational arrangements for MPCA, hygiene, and MHM interventions.
- Coordinate with relevant internal teams and field staff to ensure the timely availability of resources, supplies, beneficiary lists, distribution sites, and other requirements.
- Organize and oversee distribution activities in accordance with approved plans, standard operating procedures, eligibility criteria, and donor requirements.
- Conduct field visits to monitor implementation, verify readiness, assess site accessibility and safety, and ensure that distributions are conducted in an orderly and dignified manner.
- Supervise Distribution Workers and other assigned personnel, provide operational guidance, and ensure that responsibilities are clearly understood.
- Coordinate with Logistics and Warehouse teams regarding the receipt, storage, transportation, dispatch, and reconciliation of hygiene and MHM supplies.
- Coordinate with Finance and relevant service providers regarding MPCA delivery arrangements, ensuring that approved payment mechanisms and controls are followed.
- Identify implementation delays, operational challenges, and resource gaps and propose appropriate solutions to the supervisor.

**Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) Implementation and Follow-up 20%**

- Support the implementation of MPCA activities in accordance with approved targeting criteria, vulnerability assessments, transfer values, payment schedules, and project procedures.
- Coordinate with MEAL, Protection, and other relevant teams to support beneficiary identification, verification, validation, and referral processes in line with approved protocols.
- Ensure that beneficiary lists and required documentation are reviewed through established verification and approval procedures before being submitted to authorized personnel for processing.
- Coordinate with Finance and authorized financial service providers to monitor payment readiness, delivery schedules, and reported payment completion, while ensuring that financial transactions remain under authorized controls.
- Monitor payment-related issues, including unsuccessful transfers, beneficiary access barriers, reported discrepancies, and complaints, and coordinate appropriate follow-up.
- Ensure that beneficiaries receive clear information regarding assistance amounts, payment procedures, collection arrangements, eligibility requirements, and available feedback mechanisms.
- Coordinate post-distribution monitoring and other approved follow-up activities to assess access to assistance, beneficiary experience, and emerging protection or operational concerns.
- Maintain accurate records of MPCA implementation progress, including planned and completed assistance, verified payment status, outstanding cases, and reported challenges.
- Immediately escalate suspected fraud, unauthorized deductions, coercion, exploitation, or other irregularities through established reporting channels.

**Hygiene Distribution and Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHM) Activities 20%**

- Coordinate the planning and implementation of hygiene and MHM distributions in accordance with approved project specifications, beneficiary needs, technical guidance, and distribution schedules.
- Coordinate with WASH, Protection, Logistics, Procurement, and other relevant teams to ensure that hygiene and MHM items meet approved specifications and are available in the required quantities and within the agreed timeframe.
- Verify distribution readiness, including the availability and quality of supplies, beneficiary lists, distribution documentation, staffing, and appropriate distribution arrangements.
- Oversee the distribution of hygiene kits, menstrual hygiene supplies, and other approved items, ensuring that quantities and items provided correspond to approved entitlements.
- Ensure that MHM assistance considers the dignity, privacy, safety, preferences, and specific needs of women and adolescent girls, including appropriate access arrangements and culturally sensitive communication.
- Coordinate with relevant technical staff to ensure that hygiene and MHM messaging is accurate, age-appropriate, inclusive, and consistent with approved technical guidance.
- Support awareness-raising activities on menstrual health, hygiene practices, safe use and disposal of menstrual hygiene materials, and other relevant topics within the approved project scope.
- Monitor the suitability and accessibility of distributed items and collect feedback regarding product quality, appropriateness, and beneficiary satisfaction.
- Report shortages, damaged or unsuitable items, distribution discrepancies, and other quality concerns and coordinate corrective action with responsible teams.

**Monitoring, Accountability, Data Management and Reporting 15%**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of planned, ongoing, and completed activities, beneficiary reach, distribution quantities, and implementation progress.
- Ensure that distribution documentation, beneficiary acknowledgment records, stock reconciliation records, and MPCA implementation records are complete and submitted within agreed deadlines.
- Coordinate with MEAL staff to implement approved monitoring tools, post-distribution monitoring, beneficiary satisfaction assessments, and other relevant data collection activities.
- Review monitoring findings, beneficiary feedback, and implementation data to identify gaps, recurring challenges, access barriers, and opportunities for improvement.
- Ensure that complaints and feedback received during distributions are documented and referred through approved accountability mechanisms, respecting confidentiality and informed consent requirements.
- Prepare regular activity updates, distribution reports, progress summaries, and supporting documentation for the Project Coordinator and other authorized personnel.
- Contribute to donor reporting by providing accurate quantitative and qualitative information, supporting evidence, and explanations of implementation progress and challenges.
- Support data quality checks and ensure that reported figures are consistent with approved beneficiary records, distribution documentation, and monitoring data.
- Ensure that beneficiary information is collected, stored, accessed, and shared securely and only for authorized purposes.

**Coordination, Safeguarding, Protection Mainstreaming and Compliance 20%**

- Coordinate with relevant project teams, Logistics, Finance, MEAL, Protection, WASH, partners, and authorized local stakeholders to facilitate effective implementation of activities.
- Participate in relevant coordination meetings, field planning sessions, and technical discussions as assigned by the supervisor.
- Ensure that distribution arrangements consider protection risks, accessibility, gender sensitivity, age, disability inclusion, and potential tensions between community groups.
- Apply Do No Harm and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout beneficiary engagement, targeting, distribution, and follow-up activities.
- Ensure compliance with World Vision policies, the Code of Conduct, safeguarding requirements, child protection standards, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), fraud prevention procedures, and relevant donor requirements.
- Ensure that staff and Distribution Workers understand and follow established procedures for beneficiary interaction, confidentiality, reporting concerns, and responsible use of project resources.
- Identify and promptly report safeguarding concerns, suspected fraud, exploitation, security incidents, and other serious risks through established organizational channels.
- Monitor compliance with approved workplans, budgets, procurement and distribution procedures, and applicable documentation requirements.
- Support lessons-learned exercises and contribute to identifying practical improvements in distribution processes and beneficiary experience.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**
    - At least 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in humanitarian or development programming, preferably involving cash assistance, distributions, WASH, hygiene promotion, MHM, or related community-based interventions.
        - Demonstrated experience coordinating field activities, distribution processes, beneficiary verification, and implementation follow-up.
        - Experience working with beneficiary registration, distribution documentation, monitoring tools, and activity reporting.
        - Experience coordinating with Logistics, Finance, MEAL, Protection, and other relevant teams to support effective activity implementation.
        - Experience working with vulnerable and crisis-affected communities, including internally displaced persons, returnees, and host communities, is an advantage.
        - Experience supervising field teams, Distribution Workers, volunteers, or community mobilizers is desirable.
        - Experience with post-distribution monitoring, accountability to affected populations, and beneficiary feedback mechanisms is an advantage.
        - Experience supporting cash and voucher assistance, including coordination with financial service providers, is desirable.
2. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**
    - Bachelor's degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Business Administration, Public Health, Economics, Humanitarian Affairs, or another relevant field.
        - Relevant training in cash and voucher assistance, humanitarian distribution management, WASH, MHM, accountability to affected populations, safeguarding, or protection mainstreaming is an advantage.
        - Training in project cycle management, monitoring and evaluation, or humanitarian standards is desirable.
3. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**
    - Good knowledge of FSL programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
        - Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
        - Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
        - Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
        - Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.

title: Protection Officer - Hasaka
body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Protection Officer is responsible for the technical and day-to-day implementation of protection activities within the project, ensuring that interventions are relevant, inclusive, safe, conflict-sensitive, and aligned with approved project objectives, protection standards, workplans, and donor requirements. The position supports the planning, monitoring, quality assurance, and reporting of protection interventions, while providing technical guidance to protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and other relevant field staff. The Protection Officer also works closely with relevant protection stakeholders, communities, authorities, and other project sectors to identify and respond to protection risks and promote safe, dignified, and inclusive support to children, adults, and vulnerable groups.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Protection Programme Implementation and Technical Support 30%**

- Support the planning and implementation of protection activities in line with the approved project design, DIP, performance framework, protection standards, and relevant humanitarian principles.
- Provide technical guidance to protection facilitators, volunteers, partner staff, and other field teams involved in protection activities.
- Ensure protection interventions respond to identified protection risks, needs, vulnerabilities, and barriers to accessing services.
- Support the adaptation of protection activities to the local context and the specific needs of children, women, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups.
- Promote safe, inclusive, gender-sensitive, child-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout protection programming.
- Ensure that activities are implemented according to the principles of Do No Harm, confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, participation, and non-discrimination.

**Protection Monitoring, Risk Identification and Referrals 20%**

- Support the identification and monitoring of protection risks, concerns, trends, and barriers affecting children, adults, and vulnerable groups.
- Conduct or support protection assessments, community consultations, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and other relevant data collection activities.
- Identify individuals or groups requiring additional or specialized protection support and facilitate referrals through established referral pathways.
- Maintain updated information on available protection and other relevant services and referral mechanisms.
- Ensure referrals are conducted safely, confidentially, and in accordance with established procedures.
- Monitor emerging protection concerns and communicate significant risks or trends to the Project Coordinator/Protection Manager and relevant programme teams.
- Support protection risk mitigation measures and follow up on identified protection concerns within the scope of the position.

**Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Capacity Building 20%**

- Develop and follow up on protection activity plans, schedules, and field implementation plans.
- Monitor participation, coverage, quality, and progress against agreed protection indicators and targets.
- Conduct regular field visits and provide technical feedback and recommendations to improve protection activities.
- Support the collection, review, verification, and analysis of protection-related data and ensure that information is accurate and timely.
- Identify implementation gaps, protection risks, and emerging needs and propose appropriate corrective actions.
- Identify capacity-building needs among protection staff, volunteers, partners, and community structures.
- Support the delivery of training, coaching, mentoring, and awareness sessions on relevant protection topics, including protection principles, safeguarding, PSEA, referral mechanisms, and safe programming.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement 15%**

- Coordinate with relevant Protection Sector/Sub-Sector actors, authorities, partners, community representatives, service providers, and other stakeholders as required.
    - Participate in relevant protection coordination meetings, working groups, technical discussions, and inter-agency coordination mechanisms.
    - Engage with communities to understand protection concerns, priorities, barriers, and feedback and ensure that programme responses are appropriate and context-sensitive.
    - Support community-based protection mechanisms and promote meaningful participation of women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, and other potentially marginalized groups.
    - Coordinate with other project sectors to ensure protection is appropriately mainstreamed across programme interventions, including Education, WASH, FSL, PSS, and other relevant sectors.
    - Promote safe, dignified, accessible, and inclusive programme approaches and support teams to identify and mitigate protection risks.
    - Support the identification and strengthening of referral pathways and linkages with specialized services.

**Reporting, Documentation and Learning 15%**

- Prepare regular protection activity updates and contribute to project reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other programme documentation.
    - Maintain comprehensive and secure records of protection activities, including attendance, training, monitoring, assessments, community consultations, referrals, and field visits, in accordance with data protection requirements.
    - Document protection trends, challenges, achievements, good practices, lessons learned, and success stories while ensuring confidentiality and protection of sensitive information.
    - Support the implementation of community feedback and response mechanisms and ensure relevant protection-related feedback is appropriately followed up.
    - Support the preparation and review of protection-related proposals, budgets, activity plans, indicators, and project documents as required.
    - Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality, monitoring, accountability, and learning processes.
    - Ensure protection documentation is maintained in accordance with organizational, donor, safeguarding, and data protection requirements.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in protection, humanitarian, development, or community-based programming, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Experience implementing or monitoring protection, child protection, community-based protection, protection monitoring, awareness-raising, or referral activities is desirable.
- Experience working with children, families, displaced populations, vulnerable groups, and communities affected by conflict or displacement.
- Experience providing technical support, coaching, mentoring, or capacity building to staff, volunteers, community structures, or partner organizations.
- Experience working with Protection Sector/Sub-Sector coordination mechanisms, referral networks, local authorities, service providers, or other humanitarian actors is an advantage..

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, Law, International Development, Social Sciences, or another relevant field.
- Additional qualifications or training in Protection, Child Protection, GBV, PSEA, Safeguarding, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related areas are an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Good knowledge of Protection programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
- Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
- Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
- Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.
- Ability to work effectively with partners, community representatives, education

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

- Good in English and Fluent in Arabic

title: Project Officer (WASH) - Hasaka
body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The WASH Officer will support the implementation, monitoring, and follow-up of Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) activities under the project, ensuring that planned interventions are delivered effectively, safely, and in line with approved project plans, technical standards, and organizational procedures.

The position will primarily focus on hygiene promotion and awareness-raising, the distribution of hygiene kits and other WASH-related supplies, and water quality checks and monitoring. The WASH Officer will work closely with project staff, relevant technical teams, partners, and community representatives to promote safe hygiene practices, improve access to essential hygiene supplies, monitor water quality, identify potential WASH-related risks, and contribute to timely reporting and documentation of project activities.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

1. **WASH Activity Implementation and Technical Support:**

Support the planning, organization, and implementation of WASH activities in targeted communities and locations. Conduct field visits to follow up on activities, identify implementation challenges, and ensure that interventions are delivered in accordance with approved workplans, technical guidance, and project objectives.

1. **Hygiene Promotion and Awareness-Raising:**

 Support the preparation and delivery of hygiene awareness sessions for individuals, households, and communities. Promote safe hygiene practices, including handwashing, safe water handling and storage, household water treatment where appropriate, sanitation, personal hygiene, and other context-specific public health messages. Use appropriate information, education, and communication materials and adapt messages to community needs, language, age, gender, disability, and cultural considerations.

1. **Hygiene Kit Distribution:**

Support the planning and implementation of hygiene kit distributions, including beneficiary verification, distribution-site preparation, coordination with logistics and relevant project teams, and communication with communities regarding distribution arrangements. Monitor the distribution process to ensure that kits reach the intended recipients in a safe, transparent, dignified, and accountable manner. Maintain accurate distribution records and document any challenges, complaints, or discrepancies for appropriate follow-up.

1. **Water Quality Checks and Monitoring:**

Conduct or support routine water quality checks and monitoring at targeted water sources, distribution points, and other relevant locations, in accordance with approved WASH protocols and applicable technical standards. Collect water samples when required, conduct field tests using available equipment and approved procedures, and accurately record and maintain water quality results. Identify and promptly report abnormal results, potential contamination risks, and other concerns to the designated WASH technical focal point for assessment and follow-up. Support repeat testing and monitoring as instructed.

1. **Monitoring, Reporting, and Documentation and Coordination:**

Maintain accurate records of WASH activities, including hygiene awareness sessions, participant attendance, hygiene kit distributions, water quality monitoring results, field observations, and beneficiary feedback. Contribute to the preparation of activity reports, monitoring updates, indicator tracking, and other required documentation. Collect and share relevant monitoring data in a timely manner, ensuring data accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance with reporting requirements. Coordinate with relevant project teams, partners, community representatives, and other stakeholders to facilitate smooth implementation of WASH activities

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in WASH, humanitarian response, public health, community-based programming, or related development interventions, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Experience implementing or monitoring hygiene promotion, community awareness-raising, hygiene kit distributions, or other WASH activities.
- Practical experience conducting community sessions, engaging with beneficiaries, collecting field data, and documenting activity implementation.
- Basic practical experience in water quality checks, water sampling, or the use of field water-testing equipment is desirable.
- Experience working with vulnerable communities, including displaced populations, women, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities.
- Experience coordinating with community representatives, local authorities, service providers, partners, or humanitarian actors is an advantage.
- Experience supporting activity monitoring, reporting, and accountability mechanisms is desirable.

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree or technical diploma in Water and Sanitation, Environmental Health, Public Health, Civil or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Sciences, or another relevant field.
- Relevant technical training or certification in WASH, hygiene promotion, water quality monitoring, water safety, or humanitarian response is an advantage.
- Additional training in safeguarding, PSEA, accountability to affected populations, community engagement, or humanitarian principles is desirable.

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Good understanding of WASH principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and early recovery contexts.
- Knowledge of hygiene promotion methodologies and key hygiene messages, including safe water handling and storage, handwashing, sanitation, and disease prevention.
- Familiarity with hygiene kit contents, distribution processes, beneficiary communication, distribution monitoring, and post-distribution monitoring.
- Basic knowledge of water quality parameters, water sampling, field testing procedures, and the reporting of potential contamination risks.
- Understanding of community engagement, accountability to affected populations, protection mainstreaming, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, and disability inclusion.
- Good monitoring, data collection, documentation, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, organizational, and coordination skills.

Non

Non

- Good in English and Fluent in Arabic

title: CRM Platform Specialist (Cluster)
body:
## **Your mission**

The Platform Specialist (CRM) plays a key operational and strategic role in ensuring the availability, reliability, security, and ongoing improvement of War Child Alliance’s Salesforce platform as a business-critical global service. The role is responsible for the administration, delivery, maintenance, and optimization of the Salesforce environment, ensuring the platform remains stable, secure, scalable, and aligned with evolving organizational needs. This includes hands-on administration, configuration, implementation, release management, access control, integrations, incident resolution, documentation, and continuous service improvement.

In addition to Salesforce, the role provides technical administration and service ownership for a portfolio of smaller SaaS applications used across the organization, applying the same structured and service-led approach. The position ensures these systems are effectively governed, supported, maintained, and continuously improved, while also strengthening the integration and alignment between business applications, workflows, and data flows across the organization.

Working within War Child Alliance’s wider enterprise systems landscape, including Salesforce, Unit4 Business World, and other cloud-based tools, the Application Platform Lead (CRM) ensures that business-critical platforms operate as a stable and integrated ecosystem. The role works closely with business stakeholders, suppliers, and internal IT colleagues to ensure that Salesforce and related SaaS platforms are implemented in a scalable and supportable way, operated as managed services, and enhanced over time to meet changing operational and organizational needs.

The role is ideally to be staffed in within a Country Office, in line with War Child Alliance’s wider strategy to increasingly co-locate global resources closer to program and operational delivery. Embedding Salesforce platform administration within a Country Office environment will help strengthen adoption of the Salesforce platform by ensuring closer alignment between the global solution and operational realities in country programs. This will also provide greater insight into how the platform can be better configured, deployed, and supported to meet both global and country-level needs.

**What you will do:**

- Own and lead the end-to-end administration, delivery, support, and continuous improvement of the Salesforce platform as a business-critical service. The Salesforce platform includes multiple instances of Salesforce Cloud and multiple third-party applications integrations.
- Drive and deliver implementation and enhancement cycles, including requirements gathering, solution design, configuration, testing, deployment, and release management.
- Translate and priorities business requirements into scalable, secure, and sustainable Salesforce and SaaS solutions aligned with organizational needs.
- Administer and optimize the Salesforce environment, including user management, roles, permissions, workflows, automation, data models, and platform configuration.
- Own and manage ITIL service management processes for the platform, including incidents, service requests, problems, changes, releases, and escalation pathways.
- Monitor and proactively improve system performance, reliability, service levels, and user experience through root cause analysis, KPI tracking, and issue prevention.
- Lead continuous improvement by identifying process enhancements, automation opportunities, and roadmap priorities across Salesforce and supporting SaaS applications.
- Ensure accountability for system integration, data flows, data integrity, and alignment across Salesforce, Unit4, and other connected business systems.
- Provide ownership and oversight of user support, adoption, documentation, training, and resolution of recurring issues through sustainable solutions.
- Coordinate and manage internal stakeholders, vendors, and implementation partners to ensure timely delivery, alignment of expectations, and accountability for outcomes.

**ROLE-SPECIFIC OR CONTEXT RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Maintain and safeguard core applications, ensuring system performance, stability, and effective alignment with user and business needs.
- Safeguard and maintain data accuracy, consistency, and application logic across integrated systems, ensuring alignment with business processes and controls.
- Coordinate and support application testing, system upgrades, and change deployments, including documentation updates and user readiness activities.
- Deliver first- and second-line support for core applications, resolving incidents and liaising with vendors where required to ensure timely resolution.
- Collaborate with IT colleagues to maintain system interfaces and ensure seamless data exchange between applications and external platforms.
- Provide and maintain user training, guidance, and support materials, including manuals, FAQs, and system documentation in collaboration with process owners.
- Identify and propose system and process improvements, supporting implementation of enhancements aligned with organizational priorities.
- Establish and monitor user access and authorization structures, ensuring compliance with internal controls, security requirements, and safeguarding standards.
- Participate in cross-functional and multidisciplinary teams focused on improving digital workflows, systems integration, and organizational processes.
- Uphold and embed War Child safeguarding and data protection principles in all application administration, support, and system management activities.
- Maintain and operate ITIL-aligned change, release, and service management processes across supported applications and platforms.
- Evaluate and support adoption of new system features and application capabilities where they improve efficiency, usability, or service delivery.

## **Your profile**

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, EXPERIENCE**

**Education**

- HBO+ (Bachelor’s level or higher applied education) working and thinking level in IT, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
- Relevant certifications in Salesforce Administration and Platform Management are highly desirable.
- Certifications in ITIL, Agile, or service management frameworks are an advantage.

**Experience**

- Minimum 3 years of hands on experience in Salesforce administration, configuration, and implementation.
- Strong experience with Salesforce configuration, including roles, profiles, permission sets, flows, automation, and data models.
- Proven experience managing systems as operational services, including ownership of reliability, performance, and support.
- Experience with ITIL-based service management practices, including incident, problem, change, and release management.
- Experience with release management processes, structured deployments, and controlled system changes.
- Experience administering and supporting SaaS platforms and cloud-based business applications.
- Experience supporting or managing system integrations and data flows between applications.
- Experience working with external vendors, implementation partners, and service providers.
- Experience working in multi-system environments, ideally including enterprise platforms such as Salesforce and ERP systems.
- Experience in NGO, humanitarian, or international development organisations is an advantage.
- Familiarity with Agile and/or Waterfall delivery methodologies.
- Strong experience in stakeholder engagement and translating business needs into technical solutions.
- Strong communication experience across technical and non-technical stakeholders in multi-location environments.

**Languages**

- English, mandatory
- Dutch, French, Spanish or Arabic, desirable.

**(Technical) Knowledge**

- Strong knowledge of Salesforce administration and configuration, including automation, data structures, and user management.
- Strong understanding of service management (ITIL) principles and operational IT service delivery.
- Knowledge of SaaS platform administration and lifecycle management.
- Understanding of system integrations, APIs, and data exchange principles.
- Understanding of data management, data quality, and governance principles.
- Knowledge of release and change management processes.
- Understanding of cloud-based application environments and enterprise systems ecosystems.
- Familiarity with Agile and Waterfall methodologies.
- Awareness of information security, access control, and data protection principles.

**What we offer**

War Child currently operates in: Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Colombia, DR Congo, Jordan, Lebanon, the occupied Palestinian territory, South Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine (soon to be registered), and Yemen. Preference is given to applicants who reside and have valid working permits. War Child does not offer relocation.

title: National Non-Technical Survey/ Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunities for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfillment of the wish to return home. The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced. All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, and honesty and transparency.

**DRC Syria**

DRC has been operating in Syria since 2008, initially responding to the Iraqi refugee crisis before pivoting to a full-scale response to the Syria crisis from 2011 onwards. Our work encompasses the full cycle of displacement—responding to life-saving humanitarian needs and supporting community recovery until durable solutions can be achieved. DRC Syria takes an area-based approach to supporting internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities across our key sectors: Economic Recovery and Resilience, Protection, WASH, Shelter and Infrastructure, and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (including Humanitarian Mine Action). With an established rapid response mechanism, DRC can rapidly respond to emerging crises and shocks to meet acute emergency needs. Recognizing the significant need for early recovery and resilience programming to ensure dignified, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions for fragile communities, DRC’s programmes foster resilience for individuals and communities in situations of protracted displacement and during the initial stages of post-conflict recovery, towards a durable solution of their choice.
