With active portfolios in the neighboring countries of Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye and Iraq, DRC offers a cross-border, regional response to the Syria crisis, through cross-border protection monitoring, advocacy, and trends analysis.

**Overall purpose of the role**: The NTS/EORE Manager leads and oversees DRC’s Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Community Liaison (CL), and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) activities in Syria, ensuring full compliance with International Mine Action Standards (IMAS), national standards, and DRC Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

The role is responsible for the planning, implementation, quality management, and continuous improvement of NTS/EORE operations, while contributing to the strategic development of DRC’s Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) programme. This includes developing and adapting SOPs, tools, and methodologies in line with the evolving operational context.

A key function of the role is to ensure strong integration of NTS/EORE with DRC’s broader recovery portfolio, including HLP, livelihoods, shelter, WASH, and protection, so that mine action activities directly enable safe, sustainable, and area-based recovery outcomes.

The NTS/EORE Manager ensures that DRC effectively maps EO contamination through systematic identification, recording, and analysis of hazardous areas, while delivering targeted EORE to reduce risk-taking behavior among affected populations.

This is a twelve-month, country-wide role designed to support the scale-up, consolidation, and standardization of NTS/EORE operations across Syria. The position offers a unique opportunity to shape operational approaches, systems, and tools during a critical phase of programme expansion.

**Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities:**

**Technical Management and Implementation**

- Lead the planning, implementation, and oversight of NTS, CL, and EORE activities in assigned areas
- Ensure activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in line with IMAS, national standards, and DRC SOPs
- Oversee tasking, deployment, and daily management of NTS/EORE teams
- Ensure systematic integration of NTS/EORE outputs into clearance prioritization and broader HMA programming
- Ensure that NTS/EORE activities are aligned with and support DRC’s recovery interventions, including livelihoods, shelter, infrastructure, WASH, and protection
- Lead the development, revision, and contextualization of SOPs, guidelines, and tools for NTS, CL, and EORE
- Develop and refine data collection tools, prioritization tools, and methodologies
- Ensure alignment of operational tools with IMAS and evolving national standards
- Promote continuous improvement and adaptation of approaches based on operational learning
- Develop monthly team workplans linked to project targets, locations and available resources; coordinate implementation with Technical Field Managers and Area Managers and escalate delivery gaps to the HMA Operations Manager.
- Ensure deployment readiness in accordance with approved safety, communications and medical procedures; suspend unsafe activities and immediately report concerns to the HMA Operations Manager.
- Lead EORE needs assessments, adapt and pre-test messages and materials for different at-risk groups, and work with MEAL to assess understanding and safer behavior.

**Strategy and Programme Development**

- Contribute to the strategic development and expansion of DRC’s HMA programme in Syria
- Provide technical inputs to proposal development, concept notes, and donor engagement
- Actively promote area-based and nexus approaches, ensuring mine action enables and is integrated with recovery and development outcomes
- Identify operational gaps and opportunities for scale-up and cross-sector collaboration

**Staff Management & Capacity Development**

- Line manage and supervise NTS/EORE team leaders and field teams
- Design and deliver initial and refresher training in NTS, CL, and EORE
- Lead capacity development of national staff, including substantial training, mentoring and on-the-job training
- Lead EORE/ NTS capacity development of national authorities (e.g. NMAC) and relevant stakeholders

**Quality Management, Monitoring & IM**

- Ensure strong quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) of all NTS/EORE activities
- Oversee data collection, verification, and analysis related to EO contamination
- Track progress against targets and indicators
- Ensure data is accurately captured, stored, and shared with relevant stakeholders (e.g. SNMAC, MA AoR)
- Strengthen linkages between operations and Information Management (IM)
- Document QA findings and non-conformities, assign corrective actions and deadlines, and verify closure.
- Coordinate with IM and MEAL on indicator definitions, disaggregated beneficiary reporting and prevention of double counting; protect personal and sensitive information and share it only through approved procedures.

**Coordination & External Liaison**

- Liaise with Mine Action AoR, relevant working groups and other operators to ensure alignment and avoid duplication
- Engage with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination forums as required
- Support coordination on tasking, prioritization, and information sharing

**Budget Management, Reporting & Compliance**

- Manage EORE/NTS budgets and track expenditures against targets as well as progress
- Prepare and oversee high-quality internal and donor reporting (weekly, monthly, and ad hoc)
- Ensure timely submission of field reports and data
- Contribute to donor reports with technical inputs and analysis
- Exercise budget responsibilities within delegated authority, coordinating expenditure forecasts and procurement planning with the HMA Operations Manager and the Head of HDP

**Integrated Programming and Housing, Land and Property (HLP)**

- Strengthen operational linkages between NTS/EORE and DRC's Protection, HLP, Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH programmes, ensuring that contamination data and risk assessments inform integrated, area-based interventions.
- Facilitate joint assessments, operational planning and referral pathways with other DRC sectors, enabling mine action to support safe access to land, infrastructure, essential services and livelihoods.
- Act as the HMA technical focal point for a HLP consultancy, supporting the development, field-testing and operationalization of harmonized HLP due diligence guidance, tools and procedures for Syria's mine action sector.
- Ensure HLP considerations, including land ownership, tenure, access, competing claims and potential land-related disputes, are systematically integrated into NTS, community liaison, prioritization and land release planning.
- Coordinate with DRC's HLP specialists, the HLP Technical Working Group, Mine Action AoR and relevant national stakeholders to support the adoption of harmonized HLP approaches and their potential integration into National Mine Action Standards.
- Promote conflict-sensitive approaches to survey and land release, ensuring that HMA interventions do not inadvertently exacerbate land disputes, exclusion or community tensions.
- Refer land disputes and legal questions to qualified HLP specialists; provide operational input to HLP processes within the manager’s technical competence and delegated authority.

**Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability**

- Ensure compliance with DRC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse requirements; report concerns through designated channels.
- Ensure inclusive participation and accessible community complaints and feedback channels, and coordinate appropriate referrals with Protection and Accountability colleagues.
- Undertake any other tasks as required by HMA Operations Manager and Head of HDP.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- Minimum 5 years of experience in EORE and NTS within humanitarian mine action (HMA) programmes
- At least two years of experience supervising teams or managing EORE/NTS activities.
- NTS and EORE qualified
- QMS qualified (is an asset)
- Demonstrated experience in managing and training NTS, Community Liaison (CL), and EORE teams, including capacity development of national staff and authorities
- Strong knowledge of IMAS and SOPs applicable to NTS, CL, and EORE, including quality management (QA/QC)
- Proven experience in developing, adapting, and implementing SOPs, tools, and methodologies
- Solid understanding of EO contamination patterns and operational context in Syria or similar environments, including familiarity with military tactics and their impact on contamination
- Knowledge of land release processes, including NTS–TS–clearance linkages, and familiarity with clearance methodologies and equipment
- Experience integrating HMA with other humanitarian and recovery sectors, particularly HLP, including an understanding of land tenure risks, conflict sensitivity and the role of NTS in supporting integrated, area-based programming (desirable).
- Experience with information management and data analysis, including IMSMA and GIS tools (e.g. QGIS, ArcGIS, Garmin/BaseCamp or similar)
- Experience contributing to programme development, reporting, and donor engagement
- Strong coordination and representation skills, including engagement with national authorities, UN agencies, and other operators.

**Education**:

- Relevant university degree or technical qualification, or substantial directly relevant professional experience in lieu of a formal academic qualification.
- Documented NTS and EORE training and demonstrated technical competence remain essential.

**Languages:**

- Strong working English, both spoken and written.
- Fluent in Arabic, both spoken and written.

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence**: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating**: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead**: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating**: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity**: You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract length**: 12 months (Extension based on performance and funds)
- **Salary Level**: MF2 (in accordance with the DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Rural Damascus
- **Expected Start Date:** As soon as possible

title: Senior Manager, Early Childhood Development and Education
body:
**BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: Senior Manager, Early Childhood Development and Education**

**Job Location:** **Kenya** ***(This position is local to Kenya, thus only Kenyan Nationals are encouraged to apply)***

**Application deadline: 28 November, 2026**

**About the Role:**

BRAC International (BI) is seeking a Senior Manager, Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE) who will provide technical, programmatic and strategic support to present and future ECD and Education interventions in Africa. A key strategic focus for BI will be delivering more integrated development programmes that address multi-dimensional issues of poverty and this implies working in close collaboration with other sectors in BI. Responsibilities also include supporting country teams in developing strong Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Monitoring and Learning systems and tools in an effort that ECDE interventions are of quality, address multiple barriers, and result in impact. S/he will also play a key role in assisting country offices and BI in mobilising additional resources, including supporting new business development and ensuring ECDE or integrated projects in countries under their purview are documented and learnings are disseminated, internally and externally. Furthermore, S/he will also actively participate in developing and supporting integrated programmes.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Programme and Strategy Development**

- Support country teams in the design, implementation of quality ECDE interventions in Africa and as required beyond.
- Work closely with country teams and other sector teams in designing scale-up plans for ECDE and integrated programmes;
- Participate in the project design process (both proactive and in response to calls for proposals), involving country programme teams, especially leveraging an integrated approach
- Support country management in setting strategic directions for ECDE and integrated programming.

**Technical Assistance in Quality ECD and Education Project / Programme Implementation**

- Support quality implementation of ECDE interventions in BI countries in Africa and as requested beyond.
- Collaborate with country teams to develop ECDE specific or integrated SOPs, curricula, training guides, monitoring and learning tools;
- Support the recruitment and onboarding processes of new ECD/Education and other programme staff as needed.
- Conduct field visits to ensure fidelity and impact of ECDE or integrated development interventions and provide capacity strengthening support based on needs.
- Regularly support the assessment of project performance to ensure early identification of implementation challenges and timely guidance and support with appropriate solutions.

**Business Development for Resource Mobilisation**

- Support opportunities for fundraising, and ensure high quality technical support to all ECDE specific or integrated related fundraising within the organisation.
- Write/edit technical parts of the concept note/proposal, review other sections to ensure alignment with the call for proposals, and incorporate experience, learnings, and achievements from past projects.
- Review the scope and requirements of any funding opportunity, check the alignment of the funds/calls with the respective programme strategies, and assess its fund size, scale, strategic importance, and the technical capacity of the country and programme team to design and deliver the project.
- Review of the proposal and project budget to ensure all programme activities in the design are well-resourced, as well as ensuring all costs of the programme team support (salary, travel, capacity building) are captured in the project budget.
- Participate in various meetings with potential donors and partners to present BI’s programme strategy, approach, achievements, and learnings as required.
- Lead or support the project design (as described in the programme development section), review the relevant programmatic sections of the proposal drafted by the country/GRP team and provide their technical inputs.

**Grants Management**

- Participate in and support country teams in Africa (and as required beyond) during grant kick-off meetings for new projects or programmes.
- Regularly participate in grants review meetings that include ECD or Education grants and proactively contribute to issues of concerns and solutions.
- Support countries in budget reviews, monitoring reports review and developing action plans, coordination with other units as per ECDE operation modality.
- Regularly review and provide solution-oriented feedback to donor reports.

**Capacity Strengthening**

- Foster an environment conducive to learning and impact, by supporting the establishment of processes that promote a culture of excellence, learning and knowledge sharing.
- Contribute to country-wise capacity needs assessment, and develop a capacity-building plan for ECDE, in collaboration with country offices, other sector teams, and the Learning & Effectiveness team.
- Plan, organize and facilitate effective capacity strengthening activities in program design, quality implementation, monitoring and knowledge management of ECDE involving the provision of advice, technical assistance, training workshops, seminars and meetings or setup of a community of practice.
- Promote collaboration among team members and with the wider Programme Team and with other relevant functions in the organisation.
- Organize/support the cross-country and cross-sector experience sharing, facilitate exchange visits to enhance the capacity of the programme staff.

**Partnerships, Learning and Advocacy**

- Support country teams in Africa (and as required beyond) in the development and maintenance of strong relationships with key government, donors, partners, and other stakeholders in the area of ECDE as needed.
- Support the establishment of BI as a thought leader in the ECDE space, promoting and showcasing innovation and impact.
- Contribute to advocacy agendas aligned with programme and country strategies.
- Support country and BI ECDE team to develop program-level learning-sharing and advocacy materials.
- Represent BI ECDE as required at select forums, networks, conferences and meetings.
- Support in development and execution of ECDE learning agenda and specific project learning plans, M&L frameworks and TOC development.
- Assist the Learning and Effectiveness and country M&L teams in developing tools to collect ECDE relevant output and outcomes data, review research/evaluation reports, process documentation reports, and other learning reports, and provide inputs for finalization.
- Work with the learning team in the project/programme design stage to formulate project/programme-specific learning questions and ensure adequate budgeting.
- Contribute to the development of research agenda, study designs and coordinate study areas in collaboration with implementation team and research team;
- Coordinate where/when needed external teams to conduct research/studies and ensure fulfillment of research objectives and methodologies.
- Contribute to developing and implementing appropriate monitoring frameworks for the ECDE programmes.

**Safeguarding responsibilities**

- Implement programme decisions keeping the safety and dignity of programme participants/clients at the center, mitigate safeguarding risks and contribute to a safe working environment where staff are respected and feel confident to voice concerns without fear of retaliation.
- Receive mandatory training on the safeguarding policies and reporting channels and have access to policies.
- Participate in discussions on the safeguarding agenda in monthly meetings and actively voice concerns without fear.
- Report safeguarding incidents witnessed or experiences to the Safeguarding department. For known cases, maintain neutrality, be sensitive and non-judgemental to victims/survivors, and cooperate with organisational investigations providing accurate information as needed.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Minimum Bachelor’s degree preferably in Early Childhood Development/ Education/ Social Studies/ Development studies/ Public health/ relevant discipline.

**Experience Requirements:**

- At least 05 years of experience in working directly in Education and/or Early Childhood Development in different African country contexts.
- Overall, 5 to 7 years of working in project management/ implementation/ technical assistance/ research in the development sector.
- Experience in monitoring and evaluation of ECD and/or Education approaches, including TOC design, mixed method research, data monitoring and analysis) and ability to interpret data for decision-making
- Experience in capacity strengthening approaching, including developing and facilitating training, mentorship, and coaching on ECD and/or Education approaches across country teams
- Experience in managing projects and budgets
- Experience of working in multicultural environment will have an added value

**Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:**

- Strong knowledge of international standards and best practices on ECD and/or Education
- Sound and up to date knowledge of policies, trends, evidence-based practices/ approaches with regards to Education and Early Childhood Development, especially in Africa and Asia
- Well informed about the literature pertaining to education and child development issues in low-income countries, particularly where BRAC International operates
- Knowledge of systems, sector priorities, learning resources available, stakeholders and networks with regard to the ECD sector in BI countries
- Ability to work strategically with multiple stakeholders
- Capable of working independently and as part of team(s)
- Ability to lead the development of monitoring, research and learning plans and agenda in relation to ECDE
- Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated success engaging with key stakeholders to improve education/ECD programming and funding
- Strong analytical skills, strategic thinking and conceptual clarity
- Proficient in proposal development and budgeting and project management
- Strong editing, reporting skills and solid planning and organising skills
- Ability to prioritise and deal with competing demands to deliver results
- Ability to work under pressure and manage tight deadlines
- A high degree of personal resilience, flexibility and ability to adapt to changing circumstances
- Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, negotiation, facilitation and presentation skills)
- Excellent in problem solving and decision making
- Excellent networking skills
- Fluent in English (verbal and written communications) and desirable fluency in one of the local languages in Liberia or Sierra Leone.
- Proficient in computer operations including MS Word, MS Excel, Power Point, Email and various internet search engines and web-based platforms
- Flexibility to travel globally and work in different time zones as needed
- Possess high ethical and moral standards.

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 14 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit [www.bracinternational.org](http://www.bracinternational.org)

**Our Core Values:**

**Integrity:** We approach our work with honesty and integrity.

**Innovation:** We innovate and iterate to improve our impact.

**Inclusiveness:** We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most

**Effectiveness:** We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty

title: Procurement Officer, Global Procurement (Multi-Category Generalist)
body:
**Background**

The Global Procurement Unit, within Global Supply Chain, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for IRC. It is organized around categories, with category owners responsible for sourcing strategy, supplier ecosystem development, and contract and supplier performance across programmatic and corporate spend.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Officer provides procurement execution support for assigned corporate and professional services requests, under the guidance and review of the Senior Manager and relevant category owners. Assignments are limited to an agreed subset of travel, translation, insurance, cash and financial services, and People & Culture services, based on workload and complexity. The officer maintains audit-ready records and supports value for money, timely procurement and compliance with applicable IRC requirements.

The Procurement Officer is a hands-on, execution-focused individual contributor supporting assigned sourcing, contract administration and supplier follow-up. The line manager and category owners provide direction and review the officer’s work; category strategy, complex negotiations and award approvals remain with authorized leads.

The role enables IRC to move quickly without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Officer is the day-to-day procurement focal point for assigned requests and escalates material risks, exceptions, and strategic decisions to the category owner or Senior Manager.

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Category Coverage and Procurement Planning**

- Support assigned sourcing events, renewals and supplier requests from intake to award recommendation, under the guidance and review of the line manager and category owners and in line with agreed priorities.
- Analyze spend and market data to support demand aggregation and procurement plans for assigned requests, following IRC standard operating procedures and agreed timelines.
- Support category owners with market assessments and supplier landscape reviews for assigned categories, including ahead of framework renewals, by compiling information on capability, pricing, lead times, risk and total cost of ownership.
- Provide evidence and options to support category strategy and supplier selection; maintain approved supplier lists and support the establishment of framework agreements under category-owner guidance.
- Prepare documentation for justified waiver and single-source requests and route them through the required approval process.

**B. Sourcing Execution and Negotiation**

- Support requests for information (RFI), proposals (RFP) and tenders by coordinating bidder communications and preparing evaluation records, commercial comparisons and draft award recommendations. Run assigned requests for quotation (RFQ) under the guidance and review of the line manager or category owner and within delegated authority.
- Help business teams prepare clear specifications, scopes of work and evaluation criteria.
- Support negotiation of pricing, terms, service levels and performance commitments under the direction of the line manager or category owner and within the agreed mandate.
- Identify procurement savings opportunities through price benchmarking and competitive sourcing. Calculate and document hard savings and cost avoidance separately against approved baselines, submit them for validation under IRC's methodology, and avoid double counting.
- Support requesters with procurement intake forms (PIFs) and purchase requisitions (PRs), and create and track purchase orders (POs) in Integra as assigned under approved workflows. Provide procurement documentation for payment requests in ServiceNow, maintaining segregation of duties.
- Process assigned urgent and emergency procurement requests under approved procedures, using available frameworks where appropriate and documenting required approvals. Follow up supplier milestones and coordinate delivery with the responsible operational teams; escalate delays and capacity constraints to the line manager.

**C. Category-Specific Sourcing Support**

The officer supports a defined subset of the following corporate and professional services categories, agreed with the line manager. Assignments are proportionate to the role’s grade and workload and do not imply responsibility for all categories simultaneously.

- **People & Culture services:** support sourcing of recruitment, staffing, payroll, benefits and learning providers, coordinating reviews with People & Culture, Legal and Finance as applicable.
- **Travel:** support sourcing and administration of travel provider agreements, comparing rates, fees and service levels with input from the responsible travel and duty-of-care teams.
- **Translation services:** support sourcing and administration of translation and interpretation agreements, comparing rates, turnaround times and service requirements with relevant business teams.
- **Insurance:** support sourcing and administration of insurance provider and broker agreements, coordinating documentation and specialist reviews with the responsible business owners, Legal and Finance.
- **Cash and financial services:** support sourcing of financial service and payment providers with Finance, Treasury and program teams, coordinating required licensing, financial, screening and data protection reviews.

**D. Contracting, Framework Agreements and Supplier Performance**

- Prepare contract, framework agreement and statement-of-work drafts using approved templates. Coordinate Legal and specialist review of applicable clauses, route documents for authorized signature, and maintain executed agreements and amendments.
- Administer assigned framework agreements and contracts: maintain approved price lists, supplier records, expiry and notice dates; alert stakeholders early to renewal needs; and communicate approved terms to relevant requesters and Country Programs.
- Maintain scorecards for designated suppliers, coordinate reviews according to the agreed schedule and supplier tier, and record agreed improvement actions with business owners.
- Resolve routine supplier and contract queries within the agreed mandate, escalate material issues, and coordinate follow-up on agreed corrective actions. Liaise with Accounts Payable and requesters on payment delays and report recurring causes.

**E. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate vendor risk assessments and due diligence, risk-based and proportionate to category, value, and data sensitivity: conflict of interest, code of conduct, sanctions, anti-terrorism (ATC) and debarment screening, privacy and data protection, information security, legal, donor compliance, financial viability, implementation risk, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Track required reviews and clearances with Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, Compliance and Finance before the applicable award or commitment stage. Escalate outstanding reviews; specialist assessments and risk acceptance remain with authorized functions.
- Identify and escalate requests involving high-risk suppliers, personal or confidential data, AI-enabled tools, client-facing services, or unapproved vendors; for AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC's AI governance and assessment requirements.
- Keep procurement files complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements, stored in Box; track and follow up missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews; support audit document retrieval.

**F. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented support, helping stakeholders move through the process without unnecessary delay while maintaining compliance and risk controls; serve as first point of contact for routine queries and guidance on global vendors and frameworks.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines, and encourage early engagement before commitments are made to vendors.
- Support the rollout of category sourcing guides, tools, and SOPs, including communication and training materials, and track adoption and gaps.

**G. Reporting, Spend Analytics and Continuous Improvement**

- Maintain the sourcing tracker for assigned activities, covering status, cycle time, approvals, risks, documentation and validated benefits. Report progress and recurring intake or requisition issues to the line manager and relevant category owners.
- Extract, clean and validate Integra data for assigned spend analyses and draft review reports. Report against agreed performance indicators, flag material trends and suggest practical improvements.
- Identify recurring issues across categories and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Internal:** Senior Manager, Global Procurement – Corporate & Professional Services; relevant category owners and Global Procurement peers; Global Supply Chain, Country Program and regional supply chain teams; People & Culture; Finance, Treasury and Accounts Payable; travel and duty-of-care teams; relevant business owners; IT and Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Master Data Management; and other specialist reviewers as required for assigned requests.
- **External:** Vendors, service providers, brokers and agencies within the assigned corporate and professional services portfolio; financial service providers; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

- Bachelor's degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, finance, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- At least 2 years of procurement or sourcing experience, preferably in corporate and professional services or indirect procurement.
- Experience supporting competitive sourcing processes (RFQs, RFPs and tenders) and exposure to contract negotiations.
- Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and compliance risk reviews, including data protection, financial, and operational risk.
- Proficiency in Excel and ERP or procurement systems; ability to prepare accurate spend analysis and reports.
- Fluency in written and spoken English, with strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal stakeholders across diverse functions.
- Strong organizational skills to manage assigned procurement activities and deadlines, identify workload conflicts early, and exercise sound judgment on compliance and escalation.

**Preferred**

- Professional procurement certification such as CIPS (Level 2 or above), CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress.
- NGO, humanitarian, or donor-funded organization experience, including familiarity with donor requirements such as U.S. Government (e.g. State Department), FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations.
- Experience in one or more of the assigned categories (travel, translation, insurance, cash and financial services, or People & Culture services), and willingness to develop knowledge of other categories within the agreed portfolio.
- Experience with Microsoft D365, ServiceNow, Power BI, or similar procurement, workflow, and analytics tools.
- Experience with contract and supplier performance management, framework agreements, and emergency procurement.
- Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage.

**Working Environment**

Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Colombia.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Regional Coordinator, Maestral MENA Office
body:
**About Maestral International**

Maestral International, LLC is a globally recognized consulting firm dedicated to strengthening systems that protect, support, and empower vulnerable children and youth. We work across more than 100 countries with multilateral, bilateral, governmental, philanthropic, and NGO partners. Our technical work spans child protection systems strengthening, care reform, social service workforce development, public finance for children, and child and adolescent wellbeing.

Grounded in evidence and guided by a commitment to children’s rights, Maestral helps clients and partners translate policy into practice, strengthen national systems, and build sustainable, responsive services for children and families. Learn more at [www.maestral.org](http://www.maestral.org)

Maestral established its new MENA regional office in Amman, Jordan, in 2026 to expand its support to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Building on previous and ongoing work in the region, Maestral has developed partnerships across MENA countries as well as through multi-country regional programmes. This office coordinates regional partnerships, supports the management and development of ongoing and future projects, and contributes to global initiatives. As a small office within a small global organization, all team members are expected to collaborate across functions and contribute to both regional and global work. The MENA office also serves as a regional hub, connecting Maestral’s global expertise with locally grounded knowledge, partnerships, and opportunities across the region.

**Position Description**

The Regional Coordinator, MENA, ensures the smooth functioning of the regional office and provides essential support to business development, project coordination, budgeting, financial processes, and administrative operations.

This role requires a high level of coordination between Maestral’s International team and the MENA regional team to ensure that opportunities are effectively identified, pursued, and coordinated, and that projects are aligned and implemented smoothly across global and regional teams.

The Regional Coordinator will initially support both global and MENA business development, operations, and project delivery, while gaining structured training in Maestral’s systems and processes as the regional project portfolio develops. As the MENA office grows, the responsibilities will transition toward primarily MENA-focused projects, operations, and business development support.

This position is a core operational and program support position in a small, dynamic office that requires initiative, organization, collaboration, and a willingness to support multiple functions.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Business Development***

The Regional Coordinator will work closely with the MENA Regional Director and Maestral’s HQ team to support business development across both global and MENA portfolios. The role will provide broader BD support to Maestral HQ, with responsibilities gradually shifting toward primarily MENA-focused business development as the regional portfolio grows.

- Assists the MENA Regional Director in the development, revision and refinement of the MENA business strategy, and ensuring alignment with Maestral’s overall strategy and priorities.
- Conducts market research to identify opportunities in both global and MENA portfolios.
- Supports preparation of Expressions of Interest, proposal packages, CVs, partner documents, and submission materials.
- Maintains opportunity, partner, and proposal tracking systems for both global and MENA pipelines.
- Assists with coordinating input from consultants and partners for technical proposals.
- Provides BD support across the organization during the office’s early phase, scaling back global BD responsibilities as the MENA portfolio expands.
- Supports the development and strengthening of existing strategic partnerships with a diverse range of partners across the MENA region.

***Project Support and Monitoring (Primarily MENA)***

- Maintains project timelines, workplans, and calendars, and supports monitoring progress against agreed deliverables, milestones, and deadlines.
- Oversees project operations and administration; including travel and compliance, keeps financial records, oversees the hiring of additional project support roles (i.e., translators, copy editors, etc.)
- Develops and processes project contracts (client and team) and amendments
- Supports implementation of compliance, safety, security, and safeguarding processes for MENA-based projects, ensuring documentation is complete and aligned with organizational standards.
- Coordinate the collection of end-of-project feedback from clients and team members and maintain summaries for organizational learning.

***Financial Management & Budgeting***

- Supports development and monitoring of project budgets for MENA-based work.
- Processes consultant invoices, vendor payments, and project expenses in collaboration with an external accounting firm.
- Maintains accurate financial records and documentation in accordance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Tracks budget performance and expenditure across MENA-based projects.

***Operations & Office Administration***

- Manages daily operational needs of the MENA office, including procurement, vendor coordination, document management, onboarding, and office logistics.
- Maintains organized systems for files, data, and documentation to support smooth office operations.
- Supports compliance processes in collaboration with HQ Operations & Compliance, including safety, security, legal and safeguarding documentation.
- Supports the MENA Regional Director and HQ team in strengthening Maestral’s visibility, focused MENA communication materials and events, and profiles across the region.

***Cross-Functional Global Support***

- Supports global BD, operational tasks, and project administration as needed to ensure consistency across the organization.
- Participates in team meetings, working groups, and/or initiatives that strengthen Maestral’s global systems.
- Provides operational and administrative support to HQ teams on an as-needed basis.

**Key Relationships**

*Internal*

- Reports to the Regional Director, MENA.
- Works closely with the HQ team, including Operations & Compliance, Business Development, Strategy and Programs.
- Supports consultants and project teams across global and regional portfolios.

*External*

- Works closely with Maestral’s regional accounting firm.
- Interacts with vendors, partners, consultants, and service providers supporting regional operations.
- Coordinates logistics and communications with funders and partners when needed.

**Requirements**

*Education:*

Master's degree in international development, Public Administration, Business, Social Sciences, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience of at least 15 years.

*Experience:*

- Experience working in the MENA region, humanitarian and development contexts.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining partnerships with diverse stakeholders, with experience supporting business development, opportunity identification, and proposal development.
- 10+ years of experience in project coordination, program support, business development, financial tracking, or office administration.
- Experience managing budgets, invoices, and financial documentation.
- Familiarity with international development, child protection, social policy, or related sectors preferred.

*Skills and Competencies:*

- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Arabic and English.
- Strong budgeting and financial tracking ability, with proficiency in Excel.
- Ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Teams, SharePoint, Planner, Excel, Word).
- Ability to rapidly learn new systems and apply consistent processes.
- Professional judgment, discretion, and problem-solving skills.

*Work Style and Values:*

- Proactive and self-directed; able to work independently in a small, start-up office environment.
- Collaborative team member, comfortable supporting multiple workstreams.
- Commitment to integrity, equity, and child safeguarding principles.
- Flexibility and adaptability in a shifting organizational environment.

*Other Requirements:*

- Must be legally eligible to work in Jordan.
- Must sign and uphold Maestral’s Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy Package.
- Ability to travel regionally and internationally, as required.

*\*This role may require occasional regional travel, as well as some global travel to attend Maestral Board Meetings and/or convenings.*

title: Grants, Partnerships and Communication Coordinator
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

***Fluency in both English & Spanish required***.

***Funding until September 30, 2027, potential to extend***.

**BACKGROUND**

Venezuela continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis. Inside the country, millions of people have limited access to food, health care, safe water and other essential services, and needs are most acute among people on the move and returnees, Indigenous communities, women and girls at risk of gender-based violence, and children at risk of acute malnutrition. In 2026, an earthquake affecting La Guaira, Miranda and Caracas added new humanitarian needs. At the same time, more than 7 million refugees and migrants have left Venezuela, making this one of the largest external displacement crises in the world, with Colombia hosting the largest number of them.

In Colombia, the escalation of the internal armed conflict has deepened humanitarian needs. Disputes between non-state armed groups over territorial control are driving forced displacement, confinement, movement restrictions, the recruitment of children and adolescents, and gender-based violence, particularly in border and Pacific regions such as Norte de Santander and Nariño. The crisis in Catatumbo alone, which began in January 2025, has displaced more than 100,000 people. Mixed migration flows continue in several directions, including Venezuelans in transit and pendular movements across the border, as well as reverse flows of people returning south from Central and North America and returns to Venezuela, which add complexity to the response.

The IRC is addressing these needs through an integrated, population-based response in Colombia and Venezuela, covering health (including sexual and reproductive health and mental health), protection and women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, multipurpose cash and economic recovery, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and education. The IRC employs a mixed modality, providing lifesaving services directly and with local partners, and in Venezuela a significant share of funds is channeled through local organizations. Activities are financed by a diverse portfolio of donors, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, OCHA-managed pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Latin America and the Caribbean), the Disasters Emergency Committee, UN agencies and private foundations, among others.

**Purpose of the role:** IRC Colombia and Venezuela is seeking an experienced business development, grants, and partnerships professional for the role of Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator. This role is responsible for leading resource mobilization and the timely production of high-quality funding proposals, modification requests and donor reports; playing a lead role in the full award management cycle, including compliance; facilitating partnership development and management processes; leading the communications strategy that positions the IRC’s work with donors, partners and the public and protects the organization’s reputation; and coordinating grants management-related capacity building efforts among IRC staff and partners. The Grants, and Partnerships Coordinator ensures the quality of and efficient processes for proposal development and grants management, and manages the delivery of the IRC’s partnership ambitions while supporting program coordinators and country leadership to ensure that IRC Colombia and Venezuela lives up to the partnership principles of responsibility, results-oriented approaches, equality, transparency, and complementarity.

The postholder will need to work under tight deadlines and deal with competing and changing priorities. The postholder will need to gather inputs by influencing other functions and roles while submitting quality and timely deliverables, will work with diverse country, region and headquarters-based teams, and will need to ensure adherence to organizational and donor compliance requirements. The position will be based in Bogota with frequent visits to field sites in Colombia and Venezuela.

**Scope and authority:** The Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator will lead a team of 15 members (both direct and indirect) divided in three sub-teams: grants, partnerships, and communications. The postholder will line manage 6 direct reports.

**Key Accountabilities & responsibilities:**

***Business Development and Resource Mobilization:***

- Lead the development and annual update of a resource mobilization strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country Strategy Action Plan, with clear targets by donor, sector and geography.
- Manage the funding pipeline: investigate and track funding opportunities, maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker, and regularly report on its status to country leadership.
- Lead the Go/No-Go analysis for each opportunity, assessing strategic fit, competitiveness, implementation capacity, risks, cost recovery and compliance requirements, and facilitate timely decisions with country leadership.
- Drive donor diversification and positioning beyond traditional institutional donors, including pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund), multilateral agencies and development banks, the private sector and foundations, and funding dedicated to localization and to partnerships with local organizations.
- Lead program design workshops for new business development opportunities with relevant IRC staff, and partners’ staff where applicable.
- Develop, lead, and track proposal development processes, including consortium proposals, directly coordinating and managing the development of proposals and concept notes in collaboration with multiple departments and stakeholders; write sections of proposals and conduct final reviews, editing, and polishing of proposal documents for accuracy and quality control.
- Assist in compiling and editing proposal budgets and ensure communication and coordination between all departments (finance, programs, and operations) in drafting of budgets, bringing a strategic and competitive lens to the process.

***Grants/Sub-Grants Management:***

- Ensure that IRC awards and sub-awards in Colombia and Venezuela are well-administered and implemented in compliance with the relevant donor regulations and IRC procedures throughout the full award cycle.
- Lead award start-up, including grant summaries and kick-off meetings (pre-award and opening meetings) with programs, finance, operations and partners, so that all teams understand donor requirements from the outset.
- Lead the review and negotiation of grant and sub-grant agreements, in coordination with the Awards Management Unit, finance and other relevant departments.
- Coordinate award modifications, including cost and no-cost extensions, budget realignments and changes in scope, ensuring timely submission and donor approval.
- Take the lead on internal and external reporting in coordination with programs, MEAL, and finance, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and IRC requirements. Maintain close collaboration with all relevant departments in preparation of donor reports.
- Maintain award tracking systems, including the grants tracker, reporting and deadline calendars and award dashboards, ensuring that information is accurate and available to budget holders and senior management.
- Supervise the GPU in the coordination and facilitation of project cycle meetings.
- Lead award close-out processes, ensuring that final reports, financial reconciliation, asset disposition and documentation are completed on time.
- Coordinate the preparation for and follow-up of donor audits, verifications and monitoring visits, including the implementation of their recommendations.
- Play a significant role in efforts to strengthen and maintain country program project management capacities.
- Ensure that sub-grantees are being monitored for donor compliance and progress against objectives, and that key compliance monitoring information and learning are documented.
- Assist program technical leads, operations staff, and partners with understanding the reporting and other compliance requirements on their grants and sub-grants.
- Proactively identify compliance risks throughout the portfolio and advise programs, operations, finance and senior management on necessary actions.

***Partnerships Management:***

- Play a lead role in stakeholder analysis and potential partner mapping and vetting.
- Working closely with other senior staff, play a lead role in identifying, liaising on, and negotiating teaming arrangements with potential partners; collaborate with other departments as needed to verify and issue various types of partnership agreements.
- Ensure and coordinate adherence to IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) in the selection and management of IRC Colombia and Venezuela’s partnerships.
- Co-lead the review of the performance of different partnerships, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
- Support country leadership in promoting an enabling environment for effective work in partnership.
- Provide a quarterly Partnership Management Report to the CD, incorporating input from technical coordinators and operational leads as appropriate.

***Staff management and capacity building***

- Maintain a broad and deep understanding of donor policies, regulations, and procedures and build this knowledge among grants team members.
- Build grant management capacity of field staff, and provide supportive supervision in report writing, budget management, indicator tracking, IRC-specific tools, and other topics as/if needed.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Maintain documentation of institutional knowledge and program activities in coordination with relevant sector coordinators and department leads.

***Communications***

- **Communications strategy:** Lead the development and implementation of a communications strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country strategy, resource mobilization priorities and IRC regional and global communications.
- **Brand management and visibility:** Ensure consistent and appropriate use of the IRC brand across materials, events, field sites and partner activities; provide advice on donor visibility requirements and proactively engage with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility.
- **Creation of communication materials:** Lead Colombia and Venezuela’s efforts in designing, writing and editing key communication materials (factsheets, capacity statements, stories from the field, digital content or special reports on IRC’s activities) in coordination with DDPs, program leads, and sector and field coordinators.
- **Crisis communications and reputational risk:** Develop and maintain protocols for crisis communications and reputational risk management, and advise the CD and senior management on sensitive issues, including security, data protection and the political context in Colombia and Venezuela.
- **Internal communications:** Promote clear and timely internal communication across offices and teams in Colombia and Venezuela, so that staff are informed about the country program’s priorities, results and key decisions.
- **Media:** Support media and communications activities in coordination with IRC regional and global communications teams, ensuring the safety, dignity and informed consent of clients.
- **Advocacy:** Support the CD and DDPs as needed.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Country Director, Colombia and Venezuela

**Position directly supervises:** Grants, Partnerships and Communications Unit staff

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Venezuela Country Manager and Venezuela senior management team, with whom the postholder works closely on the Venezuela portfolio; Colombia/Venezuela Deputy Directors of Programs and leads of programs, Finance and Operations, Budget Officers/Managers, HR Lead, Access & Security Department; MEAL Unit; Awards Management Unit (Regional), regional partnerships advisor, regional and global communications teams, and Technical Advisors.

**External:** Donors and pooled fund managers, consortium partners, local partner organizations, UN agencies and humanitarian coordination mechanisms, other NGO counterparts and media, as needed and indicated by Country Director, Country Manager or Deputy Director of Programs.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline, Master’s degree desired.
- At least five years international work experience in humanitarian and development programs; experience in a similar position/role is desired.
- Demonstrated, successful experience in program design and writing proposals for public and private donors.
- Solid knowledge of donor rules and regulations, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, UN agencies and OCHA-managed pooled funds; knowledge of other European, multilateral and private donor requirements is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience managing the full award cycle, including compliance, modifications, audits and close-out, and in managing partnerships with local organizations.
- Experience in communications, brand management or external relations in a humanitarian or development organization is desirable.
- Demonstrable understanding of project planning and management cycles.
- Highly organized, close attention to detail, and ability to effectively prioritize tasks in a fluid environment.
- Demonstrable high-level performance management and team-working skills, and well developed negotiation skills.
- Highly developed interpersonal, communication and relationship skills, with the ability to influence and represent the organization with external organizations and stakeholders.
- Effective people- and program-management skills in acute emergency contexts: can train and lead staff productively under stressful circumstances.
- Flexible, focused and reliable, with the ability to work well under administrative and programmatic pressures in an environment of changing demands.
- Experience in the region is an asset; knowledge of the Colombian and Venezuelan contexts is strongly desired.
- Digital literacy and strong computer skills: MS Word, Excel & email applications required.

**Language Preference**

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish, with high quality copywriting and editing skills in both languages.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate around: 10,051,500 COP/monthly). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Project Management Support Specialist [Counter Terrorism]
body:
## **Job Highlight**

This is a position in UNOPS for supporting projects carried out for or in the United Nations Office of Counter Terrorism (UNOCT). The position supports the work of the Global Programme on Prosecution, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (PRR) . The incumbent of this position will be a personnel of UNOPS under its full responsibility.

## **About the Region**

The UNOPS Global Portfolios Office (GPO) brings together diverse expertise to help partners deliver impact worldwide. With hubs in New York, Geneva, and Vienna, and expert teams operating globally, GPO leads multi-regional initiatives that advance sustainable development, climate action, and peacebuilding - including in some of the world’s most challenging environments. By leveraging our collective expertise and global networks, GPO supports UNOPS’ strategic priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals across more than 130 countries. We work closely with major global partners - including governments, international financial institutions, and UN agencies - to deliver a wide range of services, such as project management, fund management, hosting services, and HR support.

## **About the Country/Multi-Country Office**

UNOPS Development and Special Initiatives team works with UN partners and Member States. This portfolio offers support for various initiatives and priorities of the UN Secretary-General in pursuit of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Additionally, it helps the UN Secretariat in implementing global programs in areas such as political affairs, climate, counterterrorism and peacebuilding, among others.

## **Job Specific Context**

UNOPS DSI has signed an agreement with the United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism to implement project activities under the Global Programme on Prosecution, Rehabilitation, and Reintegration (PRR).

The United Nations Office of Counter Terrorism (UNOCT) was established by the General Assembly in June 2017. UNOCT has five mandated functions:

 (1) Provide leadership on the General Assembly counter-terrorism mandates entrusted to the Secretary-General from across the United Nations system;

(2) Enhance coordination and coherence across the Global Counter-Terrorism Coordination Compact entities to ensure the balanced implementation of the four pillars of the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy;

(3) Strengthen the delivery of United Nations counter-terrorism capacity-building assistance to Member States;

(4) Improve visibility, advocacy and resource mobilization for United Nations counter-terrorism efforts; and

(5) Ensure that due priority is given to counterterrorism across the United Nations system and that the important work on preventing violent extremism is firmly rooted in the Strategy.

## **Role Purpose**

Under UNOPS supervision and working in close collaboration with UNOCT, the Project Management Support Specialist will support the implementation of activities under the Global Programme on PRR.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

Under the supervision of the UNOPS Project Manager and in close collaboration with the UNOCT Programme Manager of the Global Programme on Prosecution, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (PRR), the Project Management Support Specialist will support the delivery, coordination, monitoring and development of project activities and will be responsible for the following:

**1. Project Delivery and Performance**

- Support in the planning, implementation and monitoring of project activities in line with approved work plans, budgets and quality standards.
- Coordinate project activities and develop project management tools to ensure timely delivery of outputs and adherence to UNOPS and donor/partner requirements.
- Support the design and development of programmes and projects, including the preparation of project documents, implementation plans, budgets and results frameworks.
- Conduct or support needs assessments, stakeholder consultations and gap analyses to inform programme development and implementation.
- Manage and monitor progress against scope, time, cost and quality tolerances. Identify risks and deviations, propose corrective actions, and escalate when required.
- Support resource mobilization efforts through the preparation of concept notes, project proposals, donor briefs and related documentation.
- Embed sustainability principles - including gender equality, social inclusion and environmental considerations - across project activities.
- Contribute to the identification and development of new project opportunities or extensions of existing engagements.

**2. Financial and Procurement Management**

- Support financial planning, monitoring and reporting to ensure effective budget utilization and cost control in line with UNOPS Financial Rules and Regulations.
- Support procurement and grant management processes, including preparation of Terms of Reference (ToRs).

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

- Maintain effective working relationships with donors, partners, national authorities and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated delivery and alignment with project objectives.
- Coordinate project steering committees and country level coordination mechanisms.
- Support the development and implementation of stakeholder engagement and communication plans, ensuring timely and consistent information sharing.
- Facilitate internal coordination among project teams, technical experts and support functions.
- Represent the project in meetings, consultations and external engagements as delegated by the supervisor.

**4. Monitoring, Reporting and Quality Assurance**

- Monitor project performance against agreed indicators, preparing progress, financial and completion reports in accordance with UNOPS and donor/partner standards.
- Conduct data analysis and provide inputs for management decisions and strategic planning.
- Ensure quality assurance processes are applied to all deliverables, documents and outputs.
- Support compliance with internal audit and quality standards, coordinating corrective action as required.

**5. Knowledge Building and Sharing**

- Support the organization, facilitation and delivery of capacity building workshops.
- Participate in knowledge-sharing initiatives and Communities of Practice (CoPs), contributing insights and lessons learned.
- Conduct research on PRR-related topics and contribute to the drafting of reports, summaries and briefing notes.

## **Education Requirements**

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent), preferably in law, political science, international relations, management, economics or related fields with five (5) years of relevant experience is required; or
- First-level university degree (bachelor's degree or equivalent), preferably in law, political science, international relations, management, economics or related fields with seven (7) years of relevant experience is required.

A globally recognized professional certificate or membership in Project Management is desired.

## **Experience Requirements**

Required

- Relevant experience is defined as work in programme and project management in areas related to preventing and countering violent extremism or PRR.
- Demonstrable proficiency in the use of collaboration and productivity tools (e.g. MS Office, G-Suite, etc) and web-based management systems.

Desired

- Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country.
- Experience in development or peacekeeping contexts.

## **Language Requirements**

Fluent English is required.

Fluent Arabic is desirable.

title: Officer, Planned Giving - South
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee's (IRC) External Relations (ER) department enables the IRC to respond to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Within ER, the Philanthropy team leads on the organization’s work with High-Net-Worth Individuals and planned giving donors.

**Job Overview**:

The Officer, Planned Giving, will work with donors and prospects in an assigned geography across the Southern U.S. to support an increased number of legacy gift commitments and a growing and engaged legacy society. They will support the securing and sustaining of planned gifts by working directly with prospects and donors and Philanthropy colleagues to help ensure a healthy financial future for our humanitarian work. This may entail following up on new leads; soliciting donors for planned gifts; building positive relationships to steward legacy donors; carrying out cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies, set with the Senior Director, to connect with and inspire planned giving donors and prospects; supporting colleagues on collaborations; and reporting results of efforts.

The Officer will be expected to understand the needs of older donors and prospects, communicate and connect superbly with colleagues and supporters, use knowledge of various gift planning instruments to assist colleagues and donors, continue to learn about IRC programs, and maintain accurate donor records to support the IRC’s donor relationships and prospecting with high wealth individuals and families.

Additionally, the Officer will be expected to work directly with other development officers, ER colleagues, and local area leadership to increase awareness about planned giving, support education opportunities, and support planned giving conversations and asks for appropriate donors across Major and Principal Giving portfolios.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Manage an assigned portfolio of planned gift prospects and donors.
- Provide timely follow-up to new marketing leads to educate prospects, creating new planned gifts for the IRC.
- Implement meaningful engagement opportunities for planned giving donors and prospects, in line with the team’s stewardship plan, to deepen their understanding of the mission and the benefits of legacy giving and gifts of complex assets.
- Execute regional donor trips, with travel plans approved by manager, maximizing geographic clusters of donors and prospects
- Focus on significant interactions during in person visits, events, and digital and mail communications.
- Support engagement with the IRC legacy society (Changemakers) to recognize and retain committed donors, including an annual in-person recognition event in NYC and other regional market events.
- Partner with Major Gifts and Principal Gifts colleagues on planned gift conversations for appropriate prospects within their portfolios, with strategy set by senior staff
- Contribute to internal education across ER teams and IRC regional office leadership (RAI) on planned giving’s role and process with the organization, using materials developed by the team
- Successfully meet individual goals for significant interactions, prospect conversions, lead identification, and outright giving, in alignment with overall team goals.
- Review donor file data (Salesforce) to flag prospects and bring portfolio balance recommendations to manager
- Timely and accurately input opportunity data into Salesforce to drive pipeline activity, report on progress towards goals, and find areas of improvement.
- Promote and practice inclusive behavior and demonstrate a willingness to learn about the IRC’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion.

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience:**

- 3-5 years of experience working with individual donors, preferably in major gifts, annual giving, or planned giving.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of or familiarity with planned giving vehicles and benefits preferred;
- Ability to communicate effectively with older donors about the IRC’s mission and planning tools;
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines, in consultation with manager;
- Effective collaboration with colleagues at all levels across the organization;
- Proficient with Microsoft Office; experience with CRM databases such as Salesforce or Raiser’s Edge preferred;
- Outstanding attention to detail and commitment to timeframes;
- Commitment to respect and maintain confidentiality of donor information;
- Work successfully in a sophisticated, fast-paced organization.
- Driver’s license and ability to travel up to 25% of the time, including overnight travel, is required.

**Working Environment:** This role is remote and ability to travel to see donors and prospects required. Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $77,600-$93,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of IT Operations - HQ
body:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**Job Summary**

As Head of IT Operations, you’ll own INSO’s IT infrastructure and make sure it is secure, reliable, and efficient. You’ll report to the Director of Operations and lead the IT team, set its goals, and hold it to high standards. You’ll also lead the secure and responsible use of AI and automation across INSO’s operations. The technology you run helps keep humanitarian workers safe in some of the world’s most difficult environments.

**Major Responsibilities**

*Strategy and policy*

- Set and maintain INSO’s IT vision, strategy and roadmap, aligned with organisational goals and operational needs
- Write and maintain IT policies and standards that comply with GDPR, the EU AI Act and ISO/IEC 27001
- Advise HQ departments, projects and Country Offices on infrastructure, systems and technology, including evaluating and integrating new software
- Agree a clear IT ownership and governance model with HQ Directors. IT is accountable for identity and access management, security standards, licensing, technical integration and architecture
- Manage software licences across HQ and Country Offices for compliance, cost and fit
- Review existing systems to keep them secure, resilient and fit for purpose
- Assess emerging technologies, including AI, for their operational, security, compliance and financial impact, and recommend what to adopt
- Manage strategic relationships with global technology vendors and partners to get the best service, value and innovation

*AI in IT infrastructure and support systems*

- Contribute to INSO’s AI strategy and lead its implementation within IT operations
- Own the AI acceptable use and security policy (approved tools, data handling, access and compliance), developed with DTL
- Lead AI integration into infrastructure and support systems such as Microsoft 365, finance, HR and IT service management
- Advise on and review the infrastructure, security and compliance (GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001) side of AI features in INSO-developed software and programme platforms, which DTL owns and leads
- Identify and manage AI and automation projects in support processes (finance, HR, logistics and administration) across HQ and Country Offices, working with system owners and referring programme-related opportunities to DTL
- Lead staff training on the safe use of INSO-approved AI tools and the AI policy, coordinating with DTL on training for the AI solutions it builds for programmes
- Track and report on the adoption, cost and benefits of AI tools to inform reviews of the AI strategy

*IT risk*

- Identify, assess and reduce risks to the security, resilience and availability of INSO’s IT
