- Provide the Deputy General Director (DGD) and Management Team with timely analysis, options and recommendations on procurement, facilities, workplace services, assets, logistics, risks and resource priorities.
- Maintain a clear operating model across Procurement and Facilities, ensuring responsibilities, decision rights, escalation pathways and service expectations are understood and applied.
- Anticipate changing organizational and humanitarian support needs and guide proportionate, practical solutions that strengthen readiness, resilience and service continuity.
- Act as a strategic business partner in translating the logistics unit’s needs to workforce solutions.
- Champion digital transformation across procurement and facilities promoting automation and workflow optimization, and efficiency in governance and controls.

**Technical and Operational Responsibilities**

***Procurement governance and performance oversight***

- Drive strategic direction and management of major procurements and compliances to improve planning, execution and expenditures monitoring supplier relationships & value creation.
- Provide oversight for procurement planning, sourcing, tendering, contracting, supplier management, purchasing and procurement analytics, with operational delivery led by the Procurement Team Leader.
- Ensure transparent, fair and competitive procurement in line with MSF policies, delegated authority, segregation of duties, the four-eye principle, applicable law and ethical standards.
- Oversee procurement plans, high-value or high-risk sourcing processes, framework agreements, contract portfolios and supplier-risk controls; escalate material exceptions and decisions to the Deputy General Director or appropriate authority.
- Promote value for money through demand planning, market intelligence, category strategies, supplier performance management, spend analysis and responsible sourcing, without reducing decisions to cost alone.
- Roll-out procurement planning and ensure procurement systems, records, dashboards and reporting on real-time visibility, commitments, compliance & quality, supplier dependency, cost effectiveness.

***Facilities, workplace and support services oversight***

- Set direction and provide oversight for safe, functional, inclusive and welcoming workplaces.
- Provide strategic oversight of the organization's fleet and facilities maintenance programmes, ensuring vehicles, buildings, technical installations and critical equipment are maintained through preventive and corrective maintenance plans that maximize reliability, safety, operational availability and cost efficiency.
- Ensure comprehensive preventive maintenance schedules are developed, implemented and monitored for buildings, office and guest-houses infrastructures, fleet, electrical installations, plumbing, fire protection systems and other critical assets.
- Monitor fleet performance, vehicle utilization, maintenance costs, fuel efficiency and replacement planning to ensure safe, reliable and cost-effective transport services.
- Promote quality workforce experience through facility contribution to staff well-being and productivity.
- Oversee space planning, leases, fit-outs, maintenance, utilities, physical access arrangements, workplace equipment and facilities service contracts to support staff wellbeing and organizational effectiveness.
- Enhance workspace optimization through efficient utilization of office space and facility resources
- Ensure preventive maintenance, statutory inspections, accessibility, occupational safety, emergency preparedness and business-continuity measures are planned, resourced and monitored.
- Guide decisions on workplace utilization and service improvements using staff feedback, operational evidence, cost, safety, sustainability and duty-of-care considerations.

***Asset, inventory and lifecycle stewardship***

- Ensure an organization-wide framework for planning, acquisition, receipt, tagging, assignment, movement, maintenance, verification, loss reporting and disposal of assets and inventory.
- Clarify ownership and controls across Procurement, Facilities, ICT, Finance, P&C and user departments, including secure data handling and environmentally responsible disposal of ICT and other sensitive assets.
- Ensure proper assets management, inventory optimization and replacements, through planning, lifecycle forecasting, appropriate stocking strategies, reduction of obsolete inventories, and capital investment recommendations.
- Ensure effective fleet lifecycle management including acquisition planning, registration, insurance, preventive maintenance, licensing, utilization monitoring, replacement planning and environmentally responsible disposal of vehicles.
- Ensure that maintenance records, asset histories, service schedules, warranties and technical documentation are accurately maintained and regularly reviewed to support lifecycle management and audit readiness.
- Monitor asset utilization, condition, insurance, stock exposure and disposal decisions so that resources remain traceable, useful and appropriately safeguarded throughout their lifecycle.

***Risk, compliance, safety and sustainability***

- Maintain logistics and procurement risk registers and ensure proportionate controls for fraud, conflicts of interest, supplier dependency, contract failure, service interruption, safety incidents, information exposure and environmental impacts.
- Work with Legal, Finance, Data Protection, ICT, ASA/Security, Safeguarding and other relevant functions to integrate contractual, financial, cybersecurity, privacy, security, duty-of-care and safeguarding requirements into decisions and services.
- Ensure facilities and fleet operations comply with applicable statutory inspection requirements, occupational health and safety standards, vehicle licensing regulations, environmental obligations and manufacturer maintenance recommendations.
- Provide oversight of outsourced maintenance contractors and fleet service providers to ensure contract compliance, service quality, timely interventions and continuous performance improvement.
- Ensure concerns, incidents, audit findings and policy exceptions are reported promptly, investigated through the appropriate channels and followed by documented corrective action.
- Advance practical environmental commitments, including energy and water efficiency, renewable energy options, waste reduction, responsible purchasing, sustainable mobility and carbon-conscious supplier practices.
- Ensure third party risk management practices are applied across suppliers, contractors and services providers throughout the contract lifecycle.
- Promote environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations, innovation and climate smart considerations in procurement, facility and supplier management with MSF operational priorities.

***People leadership and functional capability***

- Lead planning, coaching, delegation and mentorship support to the Procurement and Facility Units through clear objectives, regular dialogue, constructive feedback, performance management, succession plan and opportunities for professional growth.
- Create a respectful, inclusive and psychologically safe working environment in which managers and teams can raise concerns, learn from mistakes, collaborate and exercise appropriate professional judgement.
- Ensure the function has suitable capacity, role clarity, succession arrangements and technical capability; support recruitment, induction, learning and workload prioritization as needed.
- Encourage cross-functional teamwork and shared problem-solving while avoiding unnecessary operational interference or duplication of the managers' delegated responsibilities.

***Financial management, assurance and improvement***

- Provide strategic financial needs analysis and scenario modeling to support efficient and cost-effective strategic investment and resource prioritization.
- Oversee maintenance and fleet operating budgets, ensuring lifecycle costs, preventive maintenance investments and replacement plans are financially sustainable and aligned with organizational priorities.
- Develop long-term capital replacement plans for facilities infrastructure, fleet and major operational equipment to minimize operational disruptions and optimize total cost of ownership.
- Develop and control the unit budget, monitor expenditure and commitments, and ensure that forecasts, recharges and financial information are accurate, timely and aligned with approved plans.
- Establish meaningful service and performance indicators and lead regular reviews of cost, quality, timeliness, compliance, user experience, sustainability and risk.
- Coordinate responses to audits and reviews, ensure recommendations are addressed, and foster continuous improvement through documented learning, process simplification and appropriate digital tools.
- Ensure technology supports professional judgement, transparency and efficiency, with appropriate human review, access controls, data quality checks and accountability for decisions.

***Stakeholder, vendor and movement collaboration, and Reporting***

- Build trusted relationships with departments, hosted entities and MSF counterparts, ensuring needs are understood, priorities are agreed and service challenges are addressed transparently.
- Develop strategic partnerships with maintenance contractors, fleet service providers, equipment manufacturers and technical specialists to ensure high-quality service delivery, innovation and business continuity.
- Represent MSF EA in relevant internal and external forums and contribute to joint sourcing, shared services, contract mutualization and movement-wide learning where these add value and preserve MSF EA accountability.
- Promote professional, fair and respectful relationships with vendors and service providers, including clear expectations, regular performance dialogue and responsible resolution of disputes.
- Provide regular executive reporting to the DGD and management Team where applicable on strategic initiatives, risks and improvement opportunities.
- Represent MSF EA in strategic supplier engagements at appropriate external logistics or procurement forum

**Other Responsibilities**

- Ensure accurate integration of EDI & Safeguarding aspects into all policies and practices within the Procurement and Facilities units.
- Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
- Compliance Assurance - Ensure that all data processing activities within the Procurement and Facilities comply with relevant data protection laws and regulations, including the Data Protection Act, 2019 and support the team to receive necessary training in this area.
- Policy Adherence - Enforce data protection policies, procedures, and guidelines within the Procurement and Facilities units, ensuring that all team members are aware of and adhere to these protocols.
- Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.
- Recognize and reinforce strong performance in supervisees; identify and encourage improvement where needed; and ensure quality and timely performance management process is carried out for supervisees.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Bachelor's degree in logistics, supply chain management, procurement, business administration, facilities management, engineering or another relevant field.
- A relevant postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.
- Recognized professional certification or membership in procurement, supply chain, logistics, facilities or contract management is strongly desirable.
- Professional fluency in English; knowledge of French or another language used within the MSF movement is an asset.

**Experience**

- At least eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in logistics, procurement, supply chain, facilities or corporate support services, including at least three years leading managers or multidisciplinary teams.
- Sound knowledge of procurement and supply-chain principles, facilities and workplace management, contract and supplier management, asset lifecycle controls, budgeting, risk management and business continuity.
- Knowledge of applicable Kenyan procurement, contracting, occupational safety, environmental, employment and data-protection requirements relevant to the function; familiarity with international humanitarian standards is an advantage.
- Strong digital literacy, including procurement/ERP systems, contract and asset registers, data analysis and performance dashboards; able to apply technology responsibly while retaining human oversight and accountability.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing procurement and facilities portfolios, budgets, contracts, suppliers, assets, workplace projects and organizational risk in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
- Experience strengthening systems, governance, service quality and team capability while maintaining operational responsiveness.
- Experience in an international, humanitarian, health, non-profit or matrix organization is strongly desirable; prior MSF experience is an advantage but not essential.

**Competencies**

- **Technical**
    - Strong understanding of end-to-end supply-chain and procurement procedures, including demand planning, sourcing, tendering, contracting, supplier management and procurement analytics.
    - Facilities, workplace, maintenance, transport, asset and inventory management oversight.
    - Contract governance, commercial judgement, negotiation and value-for-money analysis.
    - Budgeting, forecasting, cost control, recharge principles and performance reporting.
    - Enterprise risk, internal controls, audit readiness, business continuity, safety and incident management.
    - Strategic planning, project and change management, process improvement and responsible use of digital systems and data.
- **Behavioural**
    - People-centred leadership: builds trust, listens actively, coaches’ managers and creates conditions for teams to do their best work.
    - Strategic thinking and judgement: connect operational realities to long-term priorities and make balanced, evidence-informed decisions.
    - Integrity and accountability: acts transparently, protects resources, addresses conflicts of interest and takes responsibility for outcomes.
    - Collaboration and influence: works across functions and entities, manages competing expectations and builds workable agreements without relying only on hierarchy.
    - Service orientation: understands user needs and improves services while maintaining policy, safety, quality and financial discipline.
    - Communication: explains complex matters clearly, gives constructive feedback and adapts messages to technical and non-technical audiences.
    - Adaptability and composure: remains practical, respectful and decisive during uncertainty, incidents and shifting priorities.
    - Inclusion and respect: values diverse perspectives, addresses bias and exclusion, and supports safe, accessible and equitable workplaces and services.
    - Learning and improvement: encourages reflection, uses feedback and data responsibly, and turns lessons into proportionate improvements.
    - Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

## ***Conditions and Benefits:*** 

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya)

title: Deployment Officers - Single Data Entry (SDE) program
body:
## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for two Deployment Officers** - **Single Data Entry (SDE) program**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **medium** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Single Data Entry (SDE) project is a transformational initiative led by MSF to significantly improve the quality and efficiency of supply chain data entry in stock management processes (cargo reception, order preparation, stock count) across all OCs. The solution uses QR codes and OCR technologies to automate data capture and integrate with MSF’s existing supply chain tools. With planned deployment across over 120 countries, the SDE project is a complex, multi-OC endeavour requiring a dedicated Deployment Officer to lead and coordinate its successful field implementation.

**Mission :**

The Deployment Officer is responsible for ensuring the effective execution, training and reporting on the SDE solution’s deployment in all designated missions. He/she will ensure readiness checks are validated, conduct deployment with the end users et post deployment follow up, ensure stakeholder engagement, and effective user training. They will collect feedback from the users, monitor performance, and contribute towards improvement of deployment processes based on field experience and feedback.

The Deployment Officer, based in Nairobi, will conduct deployments in MSF missions and projects both in-person and remotely. The role requires frequent travel to field locations (up to 75% of the time). In addition to deployment execution, the Deployment Officer plays a key role in enabling user adoption through user training and change management, acting as a bridge between the field and the SDE product team to ensure that user feedback is collected, and escalated for incorporation into the product as solutions adapted to mission realities. This role also demands strong political acumen to navigate the diverse cultures, organizational dynamics, and power structures across multiple OCs.

The Deployment Officer will also be involved in the facilitation of (TOT) workshops for end users in collaboration with multiple team members.

This position will be **hierarchically** and **functionally** accountable to the **SDE Deployment Manager**.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

 **1. Deployment Execution & Technical Readiness**

- Send out, follow up on, and consolidate pre-deployment readiness checklists for target field missions and projects.
- Physically or remotely inspect site readiness based on specific location requirements (e.g., Pharmacies & Warehouses)
- Coordinate with field focal points to secure resource availability for upcoming deployment cycles
- Execute on-site deployment activities, including user onboarding, Go-Live support, and immediate troubleshooting

 **2. Field Readiness & Stakeholder Engagement**

- Ensure missions are fully deployment-ready by bridging coordination between field leadership, IT, and supply teams
- Facilitate local change management initiatives to actively drive stakeholder engagement and user buy-in
- Support capacity transfer to field teams to enable autonomous post-deployment troubleshooting, progressively reducing central support reliance

 **3. Training Workshops & Capacity building**

- Collaborate with training stakeholders to prepare localized training materials and pre-workshop checklists
- Conduct high-impact in-person training and interactive webinars for various trainee demographics
- Facilitate Training of Trainers (TOT) workshops to build autonomous, sustainable local capacity

 **4. Go-Live, Adoption & Deployment Material Evolution**

- Monitor user adoption metrics and address deployment resistance or localized blockers
- Track and report key deployment KPIs to the Deployment manager, including time-to-deploy, adoption rates, error reduction, and user satisfaction
- Capture lessons learned from field deployments and share with the Deployment manager for updates to the central deployment kit, tools, and user guidance
- Ensure all deployment materials remain adapted to local mission contexts, infrastructure, and user profiles (connectivity, language, literacy)

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Degree in Supply Chain, Project Management, IT Systems, Pharmacy Stock/Warehouse management or related field.
- Relevant certifications (Training of Trainers, Change Management) are assets.

**Experience**

- At least 2 years of experience in project deployment, ideally within new digital tools in complex field environments.
- Strong MSF field experience in supply chain, logistics or pharma (minimum 1 year).
- Proven experience in conducting complex roll-outs and change management in challenging humanitarian settings.

**Languages:**

- Fluent in English (written and spoken); French is essential.
- Spanish or Arabic an asset

**Competencies**

- ***Technical Competencies***
    - Strong understanding of supply chain workflows, particularly stock management.
    - Strong capacity building and knowledge transfer skills.
    - Solid knowledge of deployment of IT solutions is an advantage.
    - Familiarity with UniField, Isystock, or other MSF-relevant tools preferred.
- ***Behavioral/General Competencies***
    - Highly Organized: Able to manage multiple locations in different phases of deployment in parallel.
    - Agile Problem Solver: Strong troubleshooting abilities with ability to spot patterns to resolve challenges on the fly.
    - Independent & Mobile: High flexibility to navigate various travel contexts independently with minimal assistance.
    - Interpersonal dynamics: Strong influencing, negotiation, and cross-cultural communication skills tailored for matrixed, non-hierarchical environments.

## ***Conditions and Benefits:*** 

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya), or Johannesburg (South Africa).
- **Contract**: Up to Sept 2027 (with the possibility of renewal).
- **Start date**: As Soon As Possible.

title: TOR: PROVISION OF KNOWLEDGE PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT SERVICES FOR THE SYNNEFA-SOLIDARIDAD P4G PARTNERSHIP PROJECT IN MAKUENI COUNTY, KENYA
body:
1.0 INTRODUCTION

**1.1 Solidaridad Network**

Solidaridad is an international civil society organization with 55 years of experience in developing solutions to make communities more resilient and create more sustainable supply chains. The organization works in over 40 countries, on five continents (Asia, Africa, Europe, North America, and South America) through seven independent regional centers (Asia, East and Central Africa, Europe, North America, LATAM, Southern Africa, and West Africa). Solidaridad operates across East and Central Africa in the agribusiness and agriculture sectors with programs in Ethiopia, Kenya (which also serves as the headquarters of Solidaridad East and Central Africa), Tanzania, and Uganda. Solidaridad envisions a world in which all we produce, and all we consume, can sustain us while respecting the planet, each other, and the next generations. Solidaridad embraces public-private and people partnerships (PPPP) to test innovations, speed up change, and take success to scale.

**1.2 The Synnefa Solidaridad - Partnering for Green Growth and the Global Goals 2030 (P4G)project**

Funded by the Embassies of Denmark, the Netherlands, and the Republic of Korea. The Synnefa Solidaridad - [\*\*Partnering for Green Growth and the Global Goals 2030 (P4G),\*\*t](https://p4gpartnerships.org/)his18-month initiative targets smallholder horticulture farmers in Makueni County, Kenya. The goal of the action is to enhance climate resilience, food security, income, and social and economic empowerment among 800 small-scale fruit (Mangoes), vegetables, and spice farmers organized in farmer groups/cooperatives in Makueni County by 2027 through a 45% reduction in **food loss, food waste, and an increase in** shelf life produce. This will be achieved by enhancing farmers’ knowledge in post-harvest handling and climate-smart agriculture through the solar dryer innovation. Equally, we will improve gender and social inclusivity, increasing access to inputs and services, fostering an enabling policy environment for sustainable post-harvest management solutions such as the Solar dryer.

**1.3 Project Pathways**

**The project works through 4 main pathways:**

1. **Knowledge and awareness on post-harvest handling** and climate-smart agriculture practices for 800 small-scale fruit and vegetable farmers organized in farmer groups/cooperatives
2. **Increased capacity of the youths** to actively pursue the establishment of group-based or individual-based solar dryer enterprise
3. **Service Provider & Market Linkages:** Increased access to services (post-harvest technologies, financial and markets)
4. **An improved enabling policy environment** that allows uptake of solar dryer technology

**1.4 Expected Results**

- Increased Knowledge and awareness on post-harvest handling and climate-smart agriculture practices for small-scale fruit, spices, and vegetable farmers.
- Improved knowledge and skills in finance and entrepreneurship for youth farmers
- Increased access to climate-smart solar dryers among small-scale farmers
- Improved enabling policy environment supporting the adoption and scale-up of solar dryer technology.

## 2.0 PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The purpose of this assignment is to develop two strategic, actionable knowledge products that document, analyze, and translate evidence, technical standards, and practical experiences emerging from the Synnefa-Solidaridad P4G project interventions and external research. These products will bridge the gap regulatory frameworks and day-to-day operations, directly informing policy, unlocking commercial off-taker markets , driving private sector investment, and adoption of sustainable post-harvest technologies (solar-drying) among smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and agro-enterprise on quality standard for solar-dried mangoes in Makueni County, Kenya.

**Knowledge Product 1**

**Quality and Standards for Solar-Dried Foods: Unlocking Market Access and Investment Opportunities in Makueni County - A Technical Paper with Policy Influence**

The product will bridge the gap regulatory frameworks and day-to-day operations, directly informing policy, unlocking commercial off-taker markets, driving private sector investment, and adoption of sustainable post-harvest technologies (solar-drying) among smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and agro-enterprise on quality standard for solar-dried mangoes in Makueni County, Kenya.

**Knowledge Product 2**

**Integrating Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Practices and Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) for Improved Farmer Resilience: A Business Case and Scaling Strategy**

Document and analyze the integration of climate-smart agricultural practices alongside the VSLA model, demonstrating how combining sustainable production with community-level microfinance and financial inclusion accelerates technology adoption (including solar dryers), enhances climate resilience, improves household economic stability, and de-risks capital investment for smallholder farmer groups and youth-led enterprises.

**The two knowledge products will focus on:**

**1. Policy and Regulatory Frameworks for Solar Drying in Horticultural Post-Harvest Management:** Examine the existing policy, institutional and regulatory frameworks governing post-harvest management of horticultural produce, particularly fruits, spices and vegetables, with a focus on the use of solar drying technologies. The product will identify policy gaps, regulatory challenges and opportunities for strengthening the enabling environment for the adoption and commercialisation of solar drying technologies.

**2. Integrating Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Practices and Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) for Improved Farmer Resilience:** Document and analyse the implementation of climate-smart agriculture practices alongside the VSLA approach, highlighting how the integration of sustainable agricultural practices and community-based savings and financial inclusion mechanisms contributes to improved agricultural productivity, climate resilience, access to finance, investment in climate-smart technologies and household economic resilience. The product will also explore lessons, outcomes and opportunities for scaling this integrated approach.

## 2.1 ASSIGNMENT OBJECTIVES

The overall objective of the assignment is to develop two evidence-based, action-oriented knowledge products that establish clear quality benchmarks and market-access toolkits for solar-dried foods, while documenting how the nexus of Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) and Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) fosters financial inclusion and climate resilience to inform policy, investment, and enterprise scale-up across Makueni County.

**The assignment will pursue the following specific objectives:**

1. **Assess the policy and regulatory frameworks** governing post-harvest management (solar drying) of horticultural produce (fruits, mangoes), identifying gaps, challenges and opportunities for promoting the adoption of quality storage standards (moisture levels, hygienic processing, handling, packaging, and traceability) for market readiness specifically on solar-dried Mango produce in Makueni County.
2. **Document and analyse the integration of CSA practices** and the VSLA approach, highlighting how the combined interventions contribute to improved agricultural productivity, climate resilience, household financial inclusion and farmers' capacity to invest in climate-smart agricultural practices and technologies.
3. **Generate actionable recommendations and lessons** to inform policy development, programme implementation and the scaling of effective approaches across horticultural value chains and smallholder farming communities.
4. **Design a final technical paper and Business Case** aligned to Solidaridad East and Central Africa brand guidelines, use of high resolution photos, graphics and icons to support narrative and insights communication.

**Target Audiences & Dissemination Channels**

- Targeted Donors, Partners, Government institutions, private sector actors and other agricultural stakeholders.
- Publication on the P4G Website
- Project partners websites
- Feature inclusion in the P4G 2026 Annual Report and global digital channels
- Solidaridad Network Website, Social Media (LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Facebook), and knowledge products (newsletters, flyers, banners)

## 2.2 ASSIGNMENT LOCATION

- Makueni County, Kenya.

## 3.0 DELIVERABLES

**1. Knowledge Product 1** – Policy and Regulatory Frameworks for Solar Drying in Horticultural Post-Harvest Management: A draft knowledge product examining the existing policy, institutional and regulatory frameworks governing post-harvest management of horticultural produce (fruits- mangoes), with emphasis on solar drying technologies. It should identify policy gaps, regulatory challenges, opportunities and recommendations for promoting the adoption and commercialisation of solar drying technologies.

**2. Knowledge Product 2** – Integrating Climate-Smart Agriculture and VSLA Approaches for Improved Farmer Resilience: A draft knowledge product documenting the integration of climate-smart agriculture practices and Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), highlighting implementation approaches, farmer experiences, outcomes and lessons learned, particularly their contribution to agricultural productivity, climate resilience, financial inclusion and household economic empowerment.

**3. Final Knowledge Products:** Two final, professionally written, edited, and designed knowledge products incorporating stakeholder feedback, evidence-based findings, practical recommendations, and appropriate visual elements, ready for publication and dissemination.

## 3.1 PRODUCTION QUALITY STANDARDS:

- **Digital Formats:** Fully editable text files and publication-ready, high-resolution vector layout files.
- **Editable Assets:** Original open design source files (e.g., InDesign, Illustrator, or Canva templates) to permit future updates, along with executive presentation decks summarizing the outputs for external partners and donors.
- **Editorial Standards:** Flawless English prose that is technically sound yet accessible to both non-technical cooperative leaders and institutional investors, thoroughly proofread and fact-checked prior to formal submission.
- **Evidence-Based Insights:** All findings must draw directly from field project data, farmer focus group consultations, and observed village savings and loan dynamics in Makueni County and additional desktop research
- **Causal Links:** Clearly articulate *how* VSLA liquidity directly translates into the purchase, maintenance, or collective investment in post-harvest technologies (such as solar dryers), rather than presenting CSA and VSLAs as parallel, disconnected interventions.
- **Disaggregated Impact:** Highlight specific outcomes and adoption barriers across gender and youth demographics.
- **Length:** Approximately 5 pages per knowledge product (excluding references and technical annexes), structured as a high-level technical paper, white paper, or executive policy brief.
- **Core Document Anatomy:** Every product must contain a standard executive structure: Title and Executive Summary, Background and Context, Objectives and Methodology, Findings, Analysis, and Field Evidence and Lessons Learned, Conclusions, and Actionable Recommendations

## 4.0 DETAILED DOCUMENTATION PLAN & TIMELINE SCHEDULE

## 4.1 Production Timeline Schedule

**Activity / Milestone**

**Key Date / Deadline**

Inception Report and Work Plan : An inception report outlining the proposed methodology, approach, key activities, information requirements, and timelines for developing the two knowledge products.

30/11/2026-4/12/2026

1st Draft Knowledge **Product 1** and **Product 2**

7/12/2026-11/12/2026

**Review & Editorial Period:** Technical and editorial review by Solidaridad.

11/01/2027-15/01/2027

**Stakeholder Review and Validation:** Facilitation of consultations or validation sessions with relevant government institutions, farmers, cooperatives, private sector actors and project partners to review the draft knowledge products, gather feedback and incorporate stakeholder inputs.

25/01/2027-30/01/2023

**Submission Deadline:** Delivery of complete knowledge product 1

25/01/2027-30/01/2023

### 4.2 CONSENT AND USAGE RIGHTS

Verbal and written consent has already been issued to subjects within photos before filming or photographing participants using standard consent forms from Solidaridad East and Central Africa.

5.0 REQUIREMENT AND SELECTION CRITERIA OF SERVICE PROVIDER

**Analytical & Knowledge Product Development:** Proven track record of authoring high-impact policy briefs, white papers, technical guides, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and operational checklists for development partners, governments, or commercial food processors.

**Subject-Matter Expertise:** Verifiable experience in post-harvest handling of horticultural crops (particularly mangoes, vegetables, and spices) and solar drying/thermal dehydration systems within smallholder contexts. Prior working familiarity with agricultural value chains in Eastern Kenya (specifically Makueni County) is an added advantage.

**Agrifinance & Village Banking Familiarity:** Demonstrated understanding of rural financial inclusion mechanisms, Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), and climate-smart agriculture (CSA) business models.

**Understanding of the Assignment:** Clear articulation of the objectives, scope, and target knowledge products, specifically detailing the approach to translating quality standards into field-level checklists and analyzing the CSA–VSLA nexus.

**Methodology & Work Plan:** Detailed conceptual framework, stakeholder engagement strategy (Makueni field validation approach), drafting timeline, and internal review mechanism

**5.1 Technical Proposal Requirements**

- Organization Profile (max 1 page): Demonstrating suitability for the assignment.
- Relevant Experience (max 1 page): Highlights of similar climate/agriculture visual assignments.
- Methodology Framework (3–5 pages): Detailed workplan, field strategy in Makueni, key roles, and technical equipment specifications.
- CVs of Technical Team.
- Legal Documentation: Company Registration and PIN certificates.
- References: 3 reference letters/testimonials from prior client organizations.

**5.2 Financial Proposal Requirements**

- Fixed professional fees in local currency (KES) itemizing preparation, fieldwork in Makueni County, post-production, transport, fixers, local permits, translators, and government taxes.

**6.0 COPYRIGHT CREDITS**

Solidaridad maintains full, non-exclusive perpetual rights over all media assets created under this assignment. Proper attribution credits (e.g., *© Solidaridad \[Photographer Name\]*) will be applied where standard colophon formats are used.

**7.0 VISUAL BRANDING AND TYPOGRAPHY GUIDELINES**

Document Layout & Branding

- Header: The official Solidaridad primary logo must be positioned in the top header.
- Footer: The bottom footer section must feature the full partner logo strip including Solidaridad, P4G, Synnefa , and Makueni County Government.

**ANNEX 1- IMAGES GUIDELINES:**

All people shown in images related to work that P4G is funding should give their consent to appear in the photos and for the photos to be used in promotional materials and media.

**Images should:**

• Communicate innovation and solutions

•Include people that represent the breadth and diversity of P4G’s impact and collaboration

• Ideally, come from P4G partnerships and show specific/accurate areas of impact

• Show natural emotion or expression

• Be authentic

**Images should not:**

• Show overly development-oriented scenarios

• Be idyllic, staged or overly curated

• Be artificial or symbolic

• Portray people as victims or show direct suffering

• Portray AI-generated settings or people

title: Operations and Administration Officer
body:
**Position Overview**

We are excited to offer an excellent opportunity for a professional with 2-4 years experience in operations, administration or management to join our team.

SEED Madagascar is a UK charity dedicated to creating long-term, sustainable change in partnership with communities in the southeast of Madagascar. We integrate high-quality community health, WASH, education, rural livelihoods and conservation programmes, while contributing to international best practices through research and publications.

This office-based role is located in the small coastal town of Fort Dauphin, where you'll work alongside a diverse team of national and international staff. As the Operations and Administration Officer, you’ll oversee and support the Junior Operations and Fundraising Officer, manage onboarding and training for international staff, improve systems and procedures, and support our short-term conservation programme volunteers.

This position is ideal for a candidate with a strong background in operations or administration who is ready to take on a management role. You’ll provide high-quality administrative support while gaining hands-on experience in the development sector and learning how an international NGO operates. We're looking for a passionate and dedicated individual eager to contribute to SEED's mission and the growth of our programmes in Madagascar.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar

*Commitment:* 2 years with potential to extend; Monday to Friday (40 hours a week)

*Salary:* a local stipend with a contribution of £650 towards insurance and £1,200 towards a return flight per year.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

1. Line manage the Junior Operations and Fundraising Officer, providing support and guidance and delegating tasks effectively to ensure alignment with departmental objectives, reporting deadlines and SEED’s organisational values and strategy
2. Provide pre-departure logistical oversight, support and advice with visas, hotels, flights, accommodation, medication, etc to new international staff
3. Support international staff during their initial time with SEED, including arrival, social inclusion, cultural understanding, housing and integration into the SEED team
4. Offer pastoral care and guidance, and act as a role model for a team of early-career professionals living and working in-country, supporting both their professional growth and personal well-being
5. Lead on the recruitment of international staff, including the advertisement of vacancies and initial vetting of applications
6. Lead on the due diligence, onboarding and logistical support for short-term conservation volunteers
7. Manage the training schedule across the staff team, working closely with the Senior HR Officer to ensure that all staff are trained and confident in the roles
8. Alongside the International operations manager, develop and facilitate trainings on operational and procedural themes, including whistleblowing, Code of Conduct, Accident reporting.
9. Work with national staff to increase their skills and capacity, providing mentoring or training and encouraging skill sharing across the team
10. Support the Director of Programmes and Operations in the management, monitoring and reporting of SEED's internal audit function
11. Assist in the preparation of reports for internal and external audiences, including Annual Reports, Malagasy Ministry reports and Trustee briefings
12. Work with the Director of Operations and Programmes, and the International Operations Manager in developing, updating and implementing organisational databases, processes , policies and procedures and health and safety culture across the NGO
13. Project manage our Cyber Security implementation and development alongside the IT Officer
14. Manage SEEDs Data Protection compliance, in line with UK GDPR and relevant Malagasy law.
15. Provide core support to the International Operations Manager and the Director of Programmes & Operations in ensuring the support and security of all international staff, including acting as an intermediary of organisational priorities to the wider team
16. Work flexibly, including changing work priorities at short notice to meet short deadlines
17. Ensure all of SEED’s policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anti-corruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are always promoted
18. Assist with administration tasks and any other tasks required by the International Operations Manager or Director of Programmes and Operations in line with the tasks of the post.

**Required Skills & Experience/Person Specification**

- Hold an undergraduate degree in or relating to Business or Development, or be able to demonstrate a passion for these areas.
- Minimum of 2 years’ professional experience in Operations.
- Be able to work independently and be proactive.
- Have good all-round computing skills and experience in Microsoft Office.
- Have previous experience working to deadlines and have the ability to successfully manage their time.
- Communicate clearly and engagingly in written English across a range of media forms
- Be able to communicate verbally to encompass the range of cultures you will be working with.
- To have a good level of written English and be able to proofread documents to a high standard.
- To have a curious mind and a patient, problem-solving attitude.
- Ideally have previous experience living, working or travelling in a developing country, though it is not essential.
- Be fluent in English. A working knowledge of French is desirable but not essential.
- Be capable and comfortable adapting to life in a least developed country with sometimes basic living conditions.
- Be able to work and socialise within a small group of people and to be respectful and take personal responsibility for maintaining a good reputation for the NGO in the community
- Be able to adjust to life in another culture and a foreign language and be able to work at all times with cultural sensitivity.
- Ability to work within, and advocate for all of SEED’s policies and procedures, ensuring that SEED's protection from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment values are followed,
- Demonstrate the ability, social skills, values and confidence to give clear guidance and support to other members of the team in respect of the philosophy and procedures of SEED in order to protect both their safety and the reputation of the NGO.

title: 23896 Project Development Support Unit Coordinator (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and in close coordination with relevant coordinators and project managers in Burundi and with the Regional Office (RO) for East Africa in Nairobi, the Project Development Support Unit Coordinator will be primarily responsible for project conceptualization, proposal development, streamlining internal communications, and overseeing the mission’s external communication strategy.

**Responsibilities**

1. Lead and consolidate the drafting of concepts and project proposals in the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) in line with IOM’s mandate, the Mission’s strategy, operational priorities and needs in Burundi, with donors’ interests and requirements, for negotiations and submission to existing and new potential donors.
2. Ensure that institutional and regional frameworks/strategies (e.g., Strategic Results Framework, East and Horn of Africa Regional Strategy & Matrix, etc.) are embedded throughout the project cycle, especially in project development.
3. Directly supervise international and national staff of the Project Development Support Unit (PDSU), including the PDSU Officer, the Monitoring & Evaluation Officer (M&E), the PDSU Assistant and Communication Assistant, and perform all related human resources requirements for successful team operations.
4. Enhance the Mission’s relations with donors in Bujumbura. Organise, attend, report, and follow up on contacts and meetings with donors, collate and provide updates on the Mission’s programmes and activities, collect information about donors’ policies, approaches and funding opportunities, provide feedback to relevant colleagues and services, and provide advice on the follow-up as needed in view of new project opportunities.
5. Identify potential and realistic funding opportunities by collecting donor information and maintaining thorough knowledge of donor priorities for Burundi, and specific requirements related to the project planning, development, and reporting.
6. Streamline communication between the Burundi mission and international teams and offices (RO, Office of Legal Affairs (LEG), Accounting and Financial Reporting Division (ACO), Global Procurement Supply Unit (GPSU), etc.) by reviewing the content of documents, translating when necessary, and ensuring proper administrative processes for review and endorsement are respected.
7. Support the facilitation of project inception and progress review meetings.
8. Ensure the regular update of the universal project tracking and funding opportunity database.
9. Oversee the mission’s external communication strategy, including the development and dissemination of communications, including the utilization of social media communication tools (including but not limited to Twitter, Facebook, IOM, reports, and various media resources) for crisis-affected communities based on key messages and concerns in the context of Burundi to increase awareness of IOM’s work in the country.
10. Design and prepare appropriate information campaigns for a variety of target groups, including within the Mission and to external sources, IOM Missions, headquarters, donors, United Nations agencies, government counterparts, and other interested stakeholders.
11. Develop and strengthen links with local, regional and international media to promote the work of IOM in Burundi.
12. Provide input and coordinate the project development/monitoring and evaluation work plan and the development and updating of projects, as well as reporting and contract schedules for all IOM Burundi projects in line with the donors’ requirements.
13. Participate in inter-agency media and communication working groups to encourage information flow across agencies and to develop complementary media strategies.
14. Advise field and programme staff in the sub-offices on public information, media, and communication issues.
15. Identify and organize outreach activities and assist the CoM in carrying out initiatives to promote IOM’s image and to increase awareness of IOM activities in the country. Advise the CoM and Programme Managers on media and communication issues/campaigns.
16. Consolidate and analyse data on programme implementation and Mission’s activities, to ensure the preparation of donor reports as well as mission, regional and Headquarters periodic and activity-specific reports, as may be required.
17. Facilitate the generation and use of knowledge to promote improved policy engagement, project development and management in Burundi and the region.
18. Participate in mission key events and workshops and undertake field duty travel as needed to acquire material, including photographs of work being undertaken in the field, that would promote IOM with donors and governments.
19. Liaise closely with programme managers to regularly update the mission website.
20. Provide input, as necessary, to Public Information (PI) products with regard to donor coordination and relevance and assist the departments with regular reporting, infographics and situation reports.
21. Provide and coordinate inputs for information requests from Headquarters, the RO, other IOM missions, and external partners, such as donors, partner agencies, implementing partners, etc.
22. Represent IOM Burundi at various stakeholder meetings, conferences, or workshops as needed.
23. Perform such other related duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Political or Social Science, International Relations, International Development, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Work experience in technical writing, editing, and reporting in English and French; and,
- Experience in donor relations and report writing for relevant donors is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Familiarity with a multitude of international development and humanitarian areas of intervention;
- Advanced research, writing, outreach and communications skills;
- Familiarity with monitoring and evaluation concepts and methods; and,
- Demonstrable knowledge of Burundi political and humanitarian issues.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23305 Programme Manager (Immigration and Border Governance, Migration Governance, and Labour Mobility) (P)
Housing Counseling Program Manager
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**JOB OVERVIEW**

The Program Manager, Housing Counseling provides technical and administrative support for the development of network-wide Housing Counseling toolkits, curricula, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that build IRC’s capacity to deliver and sustain housing counseling services under IRC’s Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Housing Counseling Multi-State Organization (MSO). The role will support local offices in expanding housing counseling activities that strengthen client housing stabilization and homelessness prevention. This role will also support IRC’s housing programs and services in collaboration with the HQ Resettlement Team, Economic Empowerment Team, and other teams across RAI US. The position sits within the HQ Resettlement Housing Team and reports to the Director, Initial Resettlement.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Draft and update Housing Counseling curricula, toolkits, and SOPs aligned with HUD regulations and guidance (e.g., Handbook 7610.1 and 24 CFR part 214) and IRC’s Strategy 100, for use by housing counseling staff across IRC’s U.S. network and those preparing to take the HUD Housing Counselor Certification exam.
- Prepare client-facing housing counseling curriculum materials for in-person counseling and workshop, plus online LMS platforms.
- Maintain and update Resource Navigation tools that map available local, state, and federal housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, and rental assistance resources across the network.
- Help plan and facilitate Housing Counseling and counselor certification training, as well as other IRC housing training, peer learning, and knowledge-sharing opportunities across the network, including through the Monthly Housing Call, Communities of Practice, Switchboard, and similar forums.
- Serve as a first point of contact for day-to-day operational questions, providing technical assistance to support offices in launching, expanding, and sustaining housing counseling programming and other IRC housing programs and their requirements.
- Respond to office requests for guidance on housing counseling program design, documentation, and compliance, applying established HUD requirements and IRC guidance, and escalating complex or ambiguous cases as needed.
- Collaborate with the HQ Housing Team, HQ Economic Empowerment Team, Resettlement colleagues, and other HQ departments (e.g., Preferred Communities and Policy) to support the alignment of housing counseling programming with IRC’s broader housing and resettlement strategy.
- Support data collection, outcome tracking, and HUD-required reporting (e.g., HUD Form 9902), compile and summarize program data to flag trends and gaps for program improvements, and contribute to housing related grant proposals, donor reports and applications, including mapping local funding opportunities in collaboration with field offices and HQ staff.
- Draft standardized practices and quality assurance protocols (e.g., case file review guidance, supervisory monitoring templates) that align affiliate housing counseling practice with HUD Housing Counseling Program requirements, for review and approval.
- Monitor changes to HUD Housing Counseling Program regulations and guidance, flag their implications for the network, and update network tools, curricula, and training materials as directed.
- Attend HUD, intermediary, and national housing counseling meetings or forums, as assigned, and share key updates with the team.
- Other duties as assigned.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Social Work, Urban Planning, Public Policy and Administration, or a related field preferred.
- HUD Housing Counselor Certification strongly preferred, or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire; demonstrated working knowledge of HUD Housing Counseling Program requirements (24 CFR part 214, HUD Handbook 7610.1) required. Experience supporting HUD-approved housing counseling agency in compliance, technical assistance and capacity-building support preferred.
- Minimum of 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in housing counseling, affordable housing programs, or housing case management, including experience contributing to curricula, SOPs, or training materials.
- Demonstrated ability to draft, adapt, and facilitate curricula, toolkits, and training materials for adult learners across diverse organizational contexts.
- Excellent project management and organizational skills, with experience supporting multi-site or multi-state initiatives, and the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Experience working with refugee, immigrant, or other underserved populations preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of integrity, service, equality, and accountability.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office required; familiarity with types of AI solutions for operational productivity and accuracy required; experience with the HUD Housing Counseling System (HCS), client management systems (CMS), reporting, and other software used for counseling and IRC housing services is a plus.
- Ability to travel up to 25% of the time to visit IRC field offices and affiliates as required. Preference for candidates living within reasonable proximity of an IRC Housing Counseling location, to perform housing counseling activities as needed.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $60,000-75,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Middle East, Regional Expert
body:
**About ACLED**  
ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data) is an independent, impartial conflict and protest monitoring organization providing real-time data and analysis on violent conflict and protest in all countries and territories across the world.

**The Role**  
ACLED seeks a Regional Expert on Gulf security politics who will assess how regional conflict dynamics shape the security politics and policy decisions of the Gulf states, and what those decisions mean for national security and business interests, including critical infrastructure, supply lines, trade corridors. The role covers the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — and their security relationships with Iran, Iraq, Yemen, Israel, the Horn of Africa, and other theaters where Gulf states project influence or face security challenges. This is an opportunity to shape ACLED’s analysis of one of the world’s most consequential security environments.

The Regional Expert analyzes how conflict dynamics and security policy affect these interests, and how these interests in turn shape security policy. The role covers conflict and security analysis only; the Regional Expert will not model trade data, map supply chains, or assess investments directly.

You will work with ACLED’s industry-leading conflict data and alongside a dedicated regional team of conflict monitors who produce daily event data and context information. This frees you to focus on analysis rather than raw collection. You will combine these data with your own knowledge of the region and your network in policy circles to analyze conflict developments, make risk assessments, and inform government policymakers, private-sector clients, and international media. The analyses you create will be clear, concise, timely, and informed by locally grounded information, and will speak directly to the concerns of the governments, business sector and organizations who rely on it.

Analysis is the core of the role. Your work with clients and stakeholders will also surface new opportunities, and you will have the chance to develop these alongside the revenue and regional team. As one of ACLED’s public voices on the Middle East, you will feature frequently in international media and represent ACLED at high-level venues in the region.

As Regional Expert you are located within the Middle East regional team of the Global Data Collection department and report to the Middle East Regional Team Lead. You will work together with other regional experts on the Middle East and with experts and monitors on the Africa team regarding the Horn of Africa. Your work also intersects with ACLED’s Risk Centre, External Affairs, Global Engagement, and Revenue teams who you directly engage with for risk outputs, client briefings, media commentary and commercial opportunities.

ACLED is a fully remote organization, and this position offers the flexibility to work from anywhere. You will work with clients and colleagues across time zones, typically US mornings, Europe afternoons, and Asia evenings, and will travel to the Gulf states and the wider region to meet clients and stakeholders in person.

**Analysis and risk assessment**

- Monitor conflict and political developments affecting the Gulf states and assess their consequences for Gulf national security policy and for business interests in and linked to the region.
- Explain how regional conflict dynamics shape Gulf security decisions, including threat perceptions of Iran and its partners, the Houthi movement and Red Sea maritime security, Iraqi armed groups, the Israel–Iran confrontation, and instability in the Horn of Africa.
- Analyze Gulf states’ security policy choices and their drivers, such as defense partnerships and basing arrangements, de-escalation and normalization diplomacy, hedging between major powers, and direct or proxy involvement in regional conflicts.
- Explain how these dynamics affect, and are affected by, Gulf states’ economic interests, including attacks on energy and port infrastructure, threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, sanctions-related escalation, and spillover from conflicts where Gulf states hold interests, for example those in the Horn of Africa.
- Produce forward-looking risk assessments for countries, critical sites, and maritime corridors, built on evidence and observed trends, with clear indicators, thresholds, scenarios, and stated confidence levels behind each judgment.
- Produce other regular and ad hoc outputs, including risk briefs, crisis alerts, regional outlooks, and contributions to ACLED’s thematic reports.

**Data and methodology**

- Work with data collection, risk, and data science teams to strengthen ACLED coverage of conflict relevant to Gulf security, including cross-border, maritime, and long-range strike activity, and conflict that matters for critical infrastructure and economic risk.

**Client and stakeholder engagement**

- Brief government policymakers and private-sector clients and partners on Gulf security and conflict risk in writing and in meetings, remotely and in person.
- Build and maintain a network of contacts in Gulf and international policy circles, including government, security, diplomatic, and research communities.
- Develop opportunities that arise from client and stakeholder contact with the revenue team, contributing to demonstrations, tailored briefings, and product development.
- Provide expert commentary to international media and represent ACLED at conferences, policy forums, and other high-level events in the region and beyond.

**Project development**

- Support develop new products and projects on Gulf security, critical infrastructure, and economic risk.
- Contribute to proposals and partnerships.

**Requirements ( Skills and Experience)**

- A master’s degree in international relations, political science, security studies, Middle East studies, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- At least five years of professional experience in political or security risk analysis, conflict research, or policy analysis focused on the Gulf or the wider Middle East, in a consultancy, government, research, or in-house role.
- In-depth knowledge of Gulf security politics, the foreign and defense policies of the GCC states, and the regional conflicts that shape them.
- An established network in Gulf or international policy circles.
- A record of published or client-facing analysis, such as risk assessments, policy briefs, or forecasts.
- Fluency in English, with excellent writing and briefing skills.
- Fluency in Arabic is necessary.
- Ability and willingness to travel to the Gulf states.
- Ability to work across time zones, with flexibility during crises.

**What you bring**

- Sound judgment grounded in evidence and reason, and the confidence to make clear assessments without fear of being proven wrong.
- Rigor in assessing the reliability of sources and the validity of information, and the ability to draw insight from large volumes of data and reporting.
- The ability to turn complex regional dynamics into concise, actionable analysis for both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
- Comfort engaging with senior government and private-sector stakeholders, and an instinct for spotting where ACLED analysis can meet client needs.
- An understanding of how businesses and governments use risk analysis to make decisions.
- Familiarity with conflict event data, ideally including ACLED data, and an interest in strengthening data-driven analysis.
- Independence and good time management in a remote team, alongside a collaborative approach across departments.

**Compensation and Benefits**  
The salary range for this position is 50,000-60,000 (USD) annually, depending on previous experience and seniority. Other benefits vary according to local legislation in the country of employment.

**Terms**

Start Date: January 2027, Type of Position: Remote, Full-Time Employment.

title: Senior Researcher, Violence Protection and Response
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Background/IRC Summary:**

The International Rescue Committee responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees, IDPs, and others affected by war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and in 22 U.S. cities, the IRC restores safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. We address both the immediate, lifesaving needs of conflict-affected people in an emergency and the reconstruction needs in post-conflict societies. This position is based in the Airbel Impact Lab, within the Research and Innovation team at the IRC’s headquarters. It will also collaborate closely with technical and country teams within the Violence Prevention and Response Unit (VPRU).

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The IRC is a pioneer in violence prevention and response research and programming, spanning women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, and protection and rule of law.

The Violence Prevention and Response Senior Researcher sits within the IRC’s Airbel Impact Lab with a dual reporting line into the VPRU, and provides oversight, guidance and support to the VPRU’s research portfolio on the prevention of and response to violence against children, women and other vulnerable individuals in crisis- and conflict-affected contexts. The Senior Researcher will be responsible for coordinating the implementation of the violence prevention and response research portfolio, including: i) designing and managing studies; ii) engaging proactively with relevant research networks and university partners; iii) ensuring a strong pipeline of research funding; and iv) summarizing and sharing the results of protection research and learning to ensure protection programming is based on the best available evidence. Close attention to the ethics of research on violence against children and women is paramount in this work.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Research Coordination and Study Support: Oversee the coordination of active studies in collaboration with external academic partners and internal IRC stakeholders, including supporting data collection activities and designing survey tools, interview guides, study protocols and referral pathways; ensure research adheres to IRC research standards and ethical guidance on violence research; and contribute to drafting policy reports and academic articles, including as first author.
- Research Agenda Leadership: In collaboration with VPRU Global Practice Leads and the VPRU MEAL lead, lead the development and oversee the roll-out of the violence prevention and response research agenda in line with the VPRU's safety strategies across the three Global Practice Areas (Child Protection, Women’s Protection and Empowerment, Protection and Rule of Law) and Impact at Scale priorities, including contributing to the development of novel and inclusive measurement tools and data collection approaches.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Evidence-Informed Programming: Liaise with internal stakeholders across VPRU and country-based teams to ensure that VPRU programming is evidence-based, assessing upcoming and ongoing protection programming so that it reflects recent developments and the best available practice and evidence.
- External Collaboration, Business Development and Thought Leadership: Proactively build partnerships, foster cross-learning, and strengthen collaboration with key research organizations and networks, particularly those in IRC contexts. Represent the IRC at key external research fora. Identify business development opportunities to finance the research agenda, including delivering a robust business development plan, engaging university partners, and steering individual bids, to secure research funding and advance IRC's position as a leader in protection evidence generation.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Director of Research, Airbel Impact Lab

**Other key relationships:** VPRU team members (including the VPRU MEAL lead), country-based teams supporting research priorities, and academic partners.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** PhD preferred in public health, child development, psychology, or another relevant quantitative or qualitative discipline.

**Work Experience:** PhD with 3–5 years of experience, or Master’s degree with 6–8 years of experience, working in research on topics related to violence against children and women, child protection, humanitarian emergencies or other relevant topics.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Experience conducting research in child protection, women’s protection and empowerment, and violence prevention and response in humanitarian settings.
- Knowledge of ethical principles related to sensitive study topics, such as child protection, women’s protection and GBV, and violence research.
- Ability to work across sectors, coordinating research studies and bringing together people with different perspectives to work collaboratively.
- Proven qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis skills.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills and attention to detail.
- Strong research publication and funding track record.
- Commitment to upholding Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion principles, data protection principles and Safeguarding standards.
- English is required, French is highly preferred, and Arabic, Spanish, Swahili or other languages would be beneficial.

**Working Environment:** Standard office work environment; up to 30% travel to countries of implementation.

***This contract position is expected to end on July 31, 2027.***

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***
