Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview:**   
As the Director of Advocacy, you will lead development of the IRC’s advocacy efforts to support key priorities across crisis and solutions-driven global influence priorities for the International Rescue Committee. You are responsible for crafting our influence strategies using IRC’s programmatic and research evidence, surgical policy and practice solutions, and trusted brand to inspire collective action. You are the expert for understanding current federal legislative and policy trends in the US and how our policies cut across political agendas. You will engage key stakeholders across government and civil society. You will work across the IRC to develop advocacy campaigns and build relationships including with Congressional representatives, U.S. and other government officials in D.C. as well as foundations, think tanks, multilateral organizations, and other humanitarian organizations. You will also look across IRC’s global priorities, engaging relevant embassies and crafting specific advocacy messages for donor governments.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Advocacy Strategy:** Lead advocacy strategies for specific policy goals, including thought leadership objectives relevant to the U.S. market, collaborating with policy leads to advance IRCs key influence priorities and maximize the opportunity for IRC to advance our influence objectives. Engage across the IRC with all relevant stakeholders. Craft advocacy strategies, drawing on IRC’s policy expertise, that are suited to global donor government priorities.
- **Influence Analysis:** Develop U.S. power maps for key policy issues to identify influence priorities. Cultivate relationships across the U.S. Government and lead Congressional engagement. Work with team to support development and execution of creative influence strategies, including with nontraditional partners. Look across IRC’s global priorities and ensure they are integrated into advocacy and influence strategies.
- **Advocacy:** Support efforts to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships by engaging with key policy stakeholders and supporting opportunities to raise IRC’s profile at key meetings and fora. Collaborate closely with other U.S. market staff and global policy and advocacy staff, contributing to efforts designed to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships in Washington.
- Legislative and Policy Tracking. Expand IRC’s legislative reach by tracking and analyzing shifting Congressional and Executive branch positions, individuals engaging on our issues, and the politics around our issues. Translate policy asks into legislative asks. Engage U.S. Government stakeholders relevant to the IRC’s work in the U.S. Track U.S. legislative and executive processes.
- **Policy Engagement:** Contribute to policy generation by providing U.S.-specific analysis that increases the credibility and efficacy of our solutions through constant collaboration. Support IRC’s policy team in identifying and developing policy priorities that are impactful and achievable in the U.S. as well as in global markets.
- **Communications:** Provide market and audience expertise to communications team to shape policy communications specific to the U.S.Support the team in developing communications strategy and develop materials for advocacy targets. Support planning and implementation of strategic activities including events. Facilitate development and editing of internal and external advocacy products to ensure resonance in U.S. market and adherence to high standards of quality.
- **Steward Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:** both in the culture of IRC, as well as in the policy solutions we develop and the ways we wield influence.
- **Spokesperson:** Act as an IRC influence spokespersonon focused advocacy areas. Act as key interlocutor with legislative and governmental staffers**.**
- **Board and Advisors:** Support relationships with IRC's Board and Advisors by identifying points of mutual interest and opportunities around our priority issues.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Potential supervision of Senior Advisor or other staff.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position reports to:** Senior Director, Advocacy & Influence and Vice President of Policy and Advocacy
- **Internal contacts:** Policy and Advocacy colleagues across the globe; Technical Excellence leads; International Programs leads; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Communications; Awards Management; President’s Office, External Relations Department
- **External contacts:** Key Opinion Formers and policy makers in the U.S. Government and U.S. Congress, other humanitarian leaders and thinktanks, relevant embassies, multilateral institutions

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Degree in relevant field such as Public Policy, Law or International Relations

***Work experience:***

- Demonstrated experience in advocacy and advocacy strategy development with a focus on creativity and strategic thinking
- 10-12 years of experience working on complex humanitarian and/or development issues
- Knowledge of U.S. Government functioning and prior work the U.S. Government or Congress are a plus.
- Understanding of global issues, multilateral engagement experience.

***Demonstrated skills and competencies:***

- Examples of influence/impact on legislative and executive policy. Strong network of influencers and policy makers
- Deep understanding of global issues related to the humanitarian field.
- Ability to think strategically and creatively, being solutions-oriented
- Extensive knowledge of humanitarian aid and refugee issues, particularly around the complex drivers of humanitarian need
- Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate successfully with experts, high level decision and policy makers, and colleagues in the humanitarian and development fields. Good public speaking skills.
- Excellent writing skills and the ability to translate complex material and data into coherent narratives that resonate with policymakers
- Fluency with key parts of the IRC’s strategy and existing policy strategy
- Ability to work on tight deadlines and juggle competing demands
- Self-motivated

**Working Environment:** Remote

**Compensation:** ***($130,000 - $156,000 - annually).*** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: External consultancy - MEAL and Program Data Management best practices documents
body:
1\. INTRODUCTION

1.1. PRESENTATION OF PREMIERE URGENCE INTERNATIONALE

Première Urgence Internationale is a non-governmental organisation dedicated to international solidarity – non-profit and with no political or religious affiliation. Its teams is mobilized, by carrying out humanitarian and development work across the globe, without discrimination, to support of civilian who are at risk, marginalised or excluded due to the effects of armed conflict, natural disasters or economic collapse resulting from political upheaval or the consequences of environmental and climate degradation.  
The Association runs around 200 projects a year, including in the fields of Health, Nutrition, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support, Food Security and Livelihoods, Protection, Water, Hygiene and Sanitation. PUI supports nearly 7 million people in around 24 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Eastern Europe and Latin America.

1.2. GENERAL CONTEXT OF THE CONSULTANCY

As a humanitarian organization implementing numerous projects in various contexts and across several sectors, PUI needs to foster its capitalization to improve Institutional Knowledge Building (IKB).  
Since 2022, the PUI MEAL and Program Data Unit launched a capitalization cycle with all MEAL Cos to build on mission best practices documents to later develop a library of documents available for practitioners in the field.

2\. OBJECTIVES OF MEAL AND PROGRAM DATA MANAGEMENT CAPITALIZATION CONSULTANCY

2.1. GENERAL OBJECTIVE

Provide a one-month support on sorting out mission MEAL and Program Data Management best practices documents to feed the upcoming PUI MEAL and Program Data Management library.

2.2. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES

1\. Propose a folder tree organization in English for the PUI library of MEAL best practices documents;

2\. Pick up the best MEAL tools/SOPs for each type of documents among the mission MEAL best practices documents in English capitalized since 2022 and apply personal data protection filter to all selected documents;

3\. Pick up the best XLS forms from the centralized Kobo plan library for the different typologies of data collection;

4\. Complement the library with some missing documents from capitalization (lessons learnt workshop, examples of specific M&E surveys, specific evaluations) conducting some consultations with all MEAL Cos and HQ Program officers;

5\. Make several propositions of catchy names for this library;

6\. If time, propose a list of target MEAL-Program Data Management empty tools/templates and SOPs to design at PUI global level for the upcoming associated MEAL and Program Data toolbox;

3\. METHODOLOGY

The consultant will need to base his/her selection on the existing raw documentation capitalized since 2022 and make the folder tree and the selection coherent with PUI background and culture in terms of MEAL and Program Data Management.

4\. ORGANISATION OF THE CONSULTANCY

4.1. COLLABORATION WITH PUI MEMBERS

Firstly, the consultant will be required to collaborate regularly and closely with Deputy Head of Technical Department (STC) for the MEAL and Program Data Management Branch as well as the other technical focal in each mission (mainly MEAL Co). Furthermore, the consultant will meet with some program officers at headquarters.

4.2. LOGISTICAL, SECURITY AND ADMINISTRATIVE ARRANGEMENTS

- PUI will be able to provide a professional email address for the duration of the consultancy and the raw data on a PUI computer
- There is no need for the consultant to come to headquarters for this consultancy, he/she can work remotely

4.3. MONITORING ARRANGEMENTS

The consultant’s work and progress will be monitored through:

- Induction and recommendations to develop the consultancy action plan
- Weekly meetings with the Deputy Head of Technical Department for the MEAL and Program Data Management Branch at HQ.

4.4. DURATION OF THE CONSULTANCY

The consultancy is expected to start in December for a duration of 1 month.

5\. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES

- Deliverable 1 – Folder tree in English for the library
- Deliverable 2 – Proposed names for the library
- Deliverable 3 – Selection of best practices documents in the proposed folder tree (and sub folders with “documents not selected”) including XLS forms
- Deliverable 4 – If time, list of target MEAL-Program Data Management empty tools/templates and SOPs to design at PUI global level

6\. BUDGET

The budget must be provided by the consultant as part of the financial proposal. The consultant must submit a budget covering a period of 1 month (fees/hourly rates…).

7\. APPLICATION

Interested parties must submit in English:

- A 1 pager narrative to explain your understanding of the consultancy objectives and deliverables
- A short action plan to carry out the work
- A financial proposal
- An up-to-date CV
- Proven expertise in MEAL and Program Data Management within the humanitarian sector (≥5 years).
- Proven experience in MEAL and Program Data Management strategy and tools/SOPs design
- Experience of working with international NGOs – with PUI being clearly an asset
- Fluency in English (spoken and written)
- References

Selection criteria :

- Overall quality of the 1 pager and action plan
- Past experiences and references
- Proposed budget

Comparative advantage:

• Experience with PUI as a MEAL Co

[TdR MEAL External Consultancy](https://www.coordinationsud.org/wp-content/uploads/2026_PUI_ToRs_HQ-Consultancy-MEAL-Program-Data-Management.pdf)

title: MEAL Officer
source: Amal Organization for Relief and Development
body:
**Job title:** MEAL Officer

**Location:** Syria /Aleppo/ Afrin

**Reports to:** MEAL Manager

**About AMAL Organization For Relief& Development**

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established and registered in Turkey on 6/6/2014, to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war turned

**About the Job:**

A Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Officer manages information and reporting processes and products to ensure professional, high-quality communication in an organization's activities and results. A MEAL Officer also plays an important role in improving information management and data quality, and in strengthening knowledge sharing and learning across the organization.

MEAL Officers are also responsible for full-cycle monitoring and evaluation of programs, developing appropriate methodologies and tools to design evaluations.

**Duties and responsibilities:**

- Coordinate data collection and synthesize and analyze quantitative data from the field.
- Conduct regular field visits to the projects sites, and collect the relevant data according to the MEAL Plan.
- Update and add to the MEAL field guide as necessary.
- Synthesize and analyze M&E quantitative data received monthly
- Conduct need assessment, baseline survey, project review, end-line survey, and impact assessment of the relevant projects as per need and requirement.
- Assist in creating reports based on quantitative M&E data gathered
- Assist in creating M&E policies and procedures.
- Assist in preparing timely regular monthly, mid-year, and annual progress reports on all activities.
- Ensure that the M&E database is up to date with all relevant attachments.
- Responsible for the management of the M&E database, a compilation of monthly results reporting, analysis of raw data, and oversight of data quality checking.
- Responsible for the implementation of the project M&E plan and design of related monitoring tools.
- Conduct regular field visits to the projects sites, and collect the relevant data according to the MEAL Plan.

**Skills and qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s degree required, Master’s degree in statistics, demographics, public health, or international development preferred
- Minimum of five years of experience working in the field of monitoring and evaluation
- Proven success in designing, implementing, and operating M&E systems from project initiation to close out
- Experience in strategic planning and performance management, including indicator selection, target setting, reporting, database management, and developing M&E and performance monitoring plans
- Knowledge of the major evaluation methodologies (qualitative, quantitative, mixed method, and impact) and data collection and analysis methodologies
- Ability to manage critical relationships with diplomacy and tact and engage a wide range of stakeholders
- Excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Strong attention to detail, organizational. and time management skills
- Willingness and ability to travel
- Computer proficiency
- Experience in planning and managing surveys, developing and refining data collection tools, and with data quality assessments and oversight
- Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment, set priorities, and meet deadlines
- Ability to synthesize complex information and communicate it effectively to diverse audiences;
- Ability to design and implement efficient work flows and procedures

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND NON-DISCRIMINATION:**

Amal dedicated to promoting equal opportunities in our recruitment practices so the maintaining equal opportunities and nondiscrimination is a foundational principle:

Discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, age, disability, social status, origin, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, or any other grounds is strictly prohibited across all aspects of employment, organizational practices, work arrangements, salary, dismissal, and service provision.

Preference among employees or candidates for employment may be granted based on objective criteria and qualifications essential for the job, and such preferences do not constitute discrimination.

In instances where specific provisions apply to contracting concerning gender, qualifications, working conditions, or contract type (daily, weekly, seasonal), rights and responsibilities remain equitable

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. Amal Organization unequivocally prohibits and will not tolerate (zero tolerate) any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (whether sexual or otherwise), based on race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. Employees and associated personnel must strictly refrain from engaging in any discriminatory, harassing, or abusive behavior, whether physical, sexual, verbal, or otherwise, both within and outside the Amal organization.

**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**

Amal Organization recognizes that ensuring a secure environment for children begins with the recruitment of qualified employees equipped with the necessary competencies and skills to perform their duties effectively, safely, and reliably. This commitment is geared towards safeguarding children from all forms of exploitation, labor, or potential harm.

In our dedication to children's safety, our selection process incorporates comprehensive background checks, underscoring our unwavering commitment to preventing abuse and ensuring the well-being of children.

**SAFEGUARDING EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:**

In line with our commitment to fostering a secure and respectful work environment, the post holder is required to adhere to Amal's anti-harassment policy. This policy underscores our dedication to safeguarding the well-being of our staff by promoting a workplace culture characterized by mutual respect and professionalism. The role holder plays a vital part in this commitment, ensuring a supportive atmosphere and contributing to the safeguarding of their colleagues through promoting positive employee relations.

title: Regional Senior Research and Learning Manager
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

In the MENAU region (Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, oPt, Iraq, Libya, and Yemen) IRC responds to displaced people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives.

**The IRC's MENA Early Childhood Development Portfolio**

The IRC's MENA Early Childhood Development (ECD) portfolio builds on over eight years of programming, starting with the Ahlan Simsim and Play to Learn initiatives, launched in 2018. These initiatives reached millions of children and caregivers with ECD services, generated a library of high-quality ECD content, and established a resource bank of proven program models. Partnerships with Ministries of Education, Health, and Social Development produced co-designed programs that are now embedded within government services across the region.

The portfolio today spans multiple grants and donors across the MENA region, with an overarching aim of supporting the youngest children and their caregivers — particularly those affected by crisis and conflict — with high-quality, scalable, and sustainable interventions. Interventions target children directly and through their caregivers and communities. The portfolio also strengthens the capacity of the ECD workforce — including teachers, multi-sector facilitators, and health workers — advances national systems and policy through advocacy efforts, and delivers innovative digital technology solutions. The IRC works alongside key public and private stakeholders across health, protection, education, and economic recovery and development to co-design and expand partner-led interventions. For more information on the IRC's ECD work in the region, visit: [https://www.rescue.org/ahlansimsim](https://www.rescue.org/ahlansimsim).

The MENA regional ECD team manages core regional grants, supports country programs on country-specific awards, and actively contributes to business development efforts to expand programming reach, deepen impact, and mobilize resources from a growing base of public and private donors. The team also supports country programs in program quality and fidelity, content development, research, learning and monitoring, policy, advocacy and communications, project and financial management, and digital technology solutions.

**Job Overview/ Summary:**

The Regional Senior Research and Learning Manager will be responsible to coordinate, design, manage, implement, and disseminate research and learning related to ECD in the MENA region, and support country teams to collect, store, analyze, validate, use, and disseminate research and learning internally and externally. He/she will work closely with IRC’s global team, MENA regional ECD team and country-based teams in support of quality evidence-building and actionable learning activities. This role also serves as a key coordination point between the IRC, its internal research teams and external research partners, ensuring alignment across technical design, implementation timelines, and evidence dissemination.

**Major Responsibilities:**

The Regional Senior Research and Learning Manager will lead and support a broad range of research and learning activities, including the following:

**Lead, Coordinate and Manage the Operationalization of the Research and Evaluation Agenda:**

- Lead and/or contribute to the design of the research agenda, in coordination with relevant IRC HQ, regional and country-program ECD and MEAL teams, and external stakeholders (such as donors and external evaluators).
- In collaboration with IRC’s relevant research teams, external evaluators and donors, support in Randomized Controlled Trials (RCT) preparation across countries, including support with path to scale planning, RCT design, timelines, data collection strategies, logistics, etc.
- In coordination with relevant IRC research, regional and country-program teams, external partners and donors, lead the planning, management, and implementation of research and evaluation studies, that utilize a range of methods and analytical strategies, including:
    - Coordinate on study design, data management, budget/level-of-effort alignment, and quality assurance of research outputs.
    - Ensure communication and harmonization between research activities and program implementation, including ensuring fidelity of research design implementation.
    - Secure required approvals – IRC’s Institutional Review Board (IRB) and any local IRB or government approvals if needed.
    - Ensure that research instruments are adapted and contextualized, including piloting of tools across languages and cultures.
    - Coordinate programming of tools as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities.
    - Conduct or support in enumerator recruitment and trainings, as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities.
    - Oversee implementation of research work plans, ensuring that field data collection is accurate, standardized, complete, and timely.
    - Lead and/or contribute with data cleaning and analysis, including both quantitative and qualitative analysis.
    - Ensure compliance with IRC research standards and protocols, and implement best practices in research ethics, data protection, and data management throughout all stages of the research process.
- Support in and contribute to the write-up, quality assurance, and review of research products and peer-reviewed articles, as needed.
- Translate research results into user friendly-briefs, reports, Powerpoint presentations, and other products, for dissemination to non-research audiences.
- Serve as a key point of contact and coordination lead between the various IRC teams and external stakeholders (donors and external evaluators).

**Lead the Regional ECD Learning Agenda design and implementation:**

- Co-design and lead the implementation of the Regional ECD Learning Agenda and Learning and Reflection Cycle, including a range of learning studies and questions utilizing quantitative and qualitative methods.
- Provide support to country teams in the implementation of the learning agenda and learning questions, such as developing data collection tools, training, analysis and reporting.
- Support the collection, storage, analysis, use, and dissemination of learning across global, regional, and country avenues.
- Recruit consultants to support with the implementation of learning studies, as needed.
- Facilitate learning activities, including learning and reflection meetings, workshops, presentations, webinars, etc.
- Co-develop and/or input into learning products (including reports, briefs, blogs) and disseminate findings to influence practice and policy.
- Provide high-quality connections with IRC’s HQ to connect with broader organizational and Education sector learning, strategy and programs.
- Serve as a focal point for learning, providing strategic thinking and design to establish a culture of learning and viable learning products and opportunities.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position Reports to: Regional Research, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Lead, MENA Regional ECD Team
- Position directly supervises: N/A
- Indirect Reporting: N/A
- Other Internal and/or external contacts: 
    - Internal: IRC Research Teams, relevant award-management and leadership teams; Regional ECD Team, Country Program and MEAL Teams, Education Technical Unit within IRC, other IRC projects contributing to connected learning agendas.
    - External: Partners including international, national and local entities, External Evaluators, Donors, Academic Institutions, consultants and service providers.

**Required Education, Skills and Competencies**

- University degree in public health, Public Administration, International Relief and Development, Statistics, Applied Statistics, Social Sciences, Education, Early Childhood Development or any relevant related field.
- At least four years of experience implementing mixed-method research or evaluation studies in emergency, humanitarian, or development settings.
- Experience conducting randomized impact evaluations (or randomized controlled trials) of development or humanitarian interventions.
- Experience coordinating research and evaluation activities across multiple institutional partners (e.g., research organizations, academic institutions, or external evaluators).
- Demonstrated experience managing large scale quantitative and qualitative data collection in the field.
- Experience analyzing qualitative data using Dedoose, nVivo or other qualitative data analysis software.
- Experience analyzing quantitative data using SPSS, Stata, or other statistical analysis packages.
- At least three years of experience in training and facilitation.
- Excellent writing and oral skills (in English and Arabic).
- Experience working in MENA Region.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills across a wide range, including clients, community members, government officials, academics, partners, donors, etc.
- Demonstrated experience communicating complex research results to non-research audiences, including program teams and policymakers.
- Strong ability to work independently, organize work, meet deadlines, prioritize work under pressure, proactively coordinate multiple tasks, and maintain attention to detail.
- Excellent knowledge of and experience with humanitarian guidelines and principles.

**Preferred Education, Skills and Competencies**

- Experience working on research or evaluation studies in education or ECD in low-resource environments.
- Experience publishing in peer-reviewed journals is a plus.
- Experience supporting the implementation of measurement and learning systems in complex programs.
- Master’s Degree in Public Health, Public Administration, International Relief and Development, Statistics, Applied Statistics, Social Sciences, Education, Early Childhood Development or any relevant related field is a plus.

**Working Environment:**

- Standard office working environment; partial remote work is possible.
- Travel required ~ 15%.
- The position may be based in Jordan or Lebanon.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: HR Admin Officer
body:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** HR Admin Officer

**Code:** SR-00-10283

**Duty station:** HQ Rome (hybrid)

**Starting date:** 01/01/2027

**Contract duration:** 36 months

**Reporting to:** HR Generalist

## **General context of the project**

INTERSOS is a humanitarian organisation founded in 1992 that operates on the front lines of crises. In the countries where it operates, INTERSOS intervenes to assist the most vulnerable populations affected by conflict, extreme poverty, and natural or man-made disasters. The organisation works in complex, hard-to-reach areas where humanitarian needs remain acute, and the humanitarian presence is often limited. In these contexts, INTERSOS focuses on providing life-saving humanitarian assistance to displaced populations and host communities, primarily in the sectors of Protection and Health & Nutrition.

INTERSOS’s operations are guided by its Charter of Values and the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence. Specifically, INTERSOS is an organisation that is borderless, impartial, independent, culturally sensitive, committed to leveraging local capacities, professional in its solidarity, and transparent. INTERSOS also adheres to the Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and NGOs in Disaster Relief.  
The INTERSOS HR department operates globally through Recruitment, HR Admin, and Learning & Development units, complemented by Regional HR Coordinators. You will join an international team that is closely connected to field operations, where you will play a direct role in managing our international and headquarters staff.

## **General purpose of the position**

The HR Admin Officer will support the daily administrative functions of the HR administration unit, assisting the team with personnel administration for both HQ and site-based staff. Specifically, they will provide support in managing contracts and preparing documentation related to payroll processes, audits, and staff mobility.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks:**

**Contract Management and Onboarding**

- Support the team in preparing staff contracts in compliance with legal requirements, handling notifications to relevant hiring authorities (e.g., ANPAL), and managing the administration of contract amendments, extensions, resignations, and terminations.
- Enter and maintain personnel records in the company management system as part of the onboarding process for new hires.
- Manage the filing and archiving of contracts for international and HQ staff.
- Provide operational support for administrative procedures related to staff mobility.

**Personnel Administration, HQ Support, and Audit Support**

- Assist in gathering and preparing administrative documentation required for internal and external audits and financial reporting, in coordination with the admin team.
- Assist in the preparation of staff tax statements (\*Certificazioni Uniche\*).
- Assist in managing meal vouchers and tracking leave/vacation time.
- Support the administration of workplace safety-related procedures.

## **Required profile**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Economics, Law, Political Science, Labour Consultancy, or related fields.

**Professional experience**

- Brief experience (including internships or traineeships) in administration, HR management, or back-office roles is desirable.
- Junior profile (not above 29 years old)
- Work experience or an internship abroad—preferably with humanitarian organisations or in the third sector—represents a significant asset.

**Professional requirements**

- Excellent knowledge of key IT tools.
- Basic understanding of HR-related administrative processes.

**Languages**

- Italian: Native speaker or C2 level.
- English: Excellent written and spoken proficiency.
- French: Knowledge of the language is an asset.

**Personal requirements**

- Strong organisational and priority-setting skills.
- Aptitude for teamwork.
- High level of accuracy, confidentiality, and attention to detail in handling sensitive data.
- Flexibility, adaptability, and a proactive approach.
- Commitment to and alignment with INTERSOS’s values and ethical principles.

## **General conditions and benefits:**

- **Salary range:** 23.500-27.000€ per year
- **Accommodation: N/A**
- **R&R:** N/A
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard HQ salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian worker in case of field visits.
- **Medical insurance:** Medical insurance, vaccines and psychological support are provided for the humanitarian worker on request.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- Annual leave: 2 days per month
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to Staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Family, Non-Family, and Accompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.

title: Graphic Design & Layout Artist
body:
## **Project Overview**

The Project “**Enabling the Philippines to prepare its Second Biennial Transparency Report with a combined Third National Communication (BTR2/NC3) and Third Biennial Transparency Report (BTR3)**” aims to assist the Philippines in responding to the reporting requirements under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement to address climate change and its impacts and to take part in review processes that consider the information Parties provide.

Under this project, BTR2/NC3 and BTR3 reports will be prepared in close coordination with any other climate-related ongoing project and activity in the country, funded by the GEF and/or other donors.

The main objective of this project is to to support the Philippines prepare and submit to the UNFCCC the Second Biennial Transparency Report with a combined Third National Communication (BTR2/NC3) and Third Biennial Transparency Report (BTR3) all in compliance with the UNFCCC Convention and Paris Agreement’s reporting obligations.

## **Roles and Responsibilities**

1. Co-develop the visual identity, including the style guide and visual guidelines with the BTR2/NC3 Project Team
    
    a. Propose a design concept and visual identity for BTR2/NC3 (colour palette, typography, publication template/masterpage, iconography, charts, graphs, tables, and at least three (3) cover designs) consistent with relevant CCC, FAO, GEF and OML Center branding and logo-use guidelines
    
    b. Revise and finalize the design concept based on what is agreed with the Project Manager and lead authors
2. Produce the publication layout, including graphics, infographics, and data visualizations.
    
    a. Infographics on key results, including the national GHG inventory by sector (Energy, IPPU, AFOLU/LULUCF, Waste), NDC progress tracking, mitigation and adaptation actions, and support needed and received
    
    b. Diagrams and flowcharts explaining processes such as the MRV/transparency arrangements, institutional arrangements, and data flows
    
    c. Maps, icons and illustrations for vulnerability, impacts and adaptation content
    
    d. Gender-responsive and inclusive visuals, consistent with the project’s gender mainstreaming commitments as needed.
3. Develop the BTR2/NC3 as an interactive publication, with print version as needed
    
    a. Interactive PDF versions of the main reports, with hyperlinked tables of contents, cross-references and page navigation
    
    b.Prepare a print-ready version, complete with its packaged files based on the digital BTR2/NC3 document.
4. Quality checking and finalization
    
    a. Quality check of laid-out outputs for readiness for printing, digital publication and submission to the UNFCCC
    
    b. Ensure all figures, tables and annexes are consistent with the approved style guide and visual guidelines.
    
    c. Prepare print-ready files (with print specifications) and optimized digital files with manageable file sizes.
5. Prepare all assets and images created for turnover
    
    a. Turn over all source files (editable design files, fonts and image licenses, templates and raw graphics) in .indd and .ai complete with its package and/or embedded link to OML Center at project completion.

## **QUALIFICATION** 

- Should have extensive experience in publication design in both digital and print
- Experience in reports publication (experience in similar climate change projects an advantage)
- Experience in visual storytelling and developing infographics based on technical information
- Knowledgeable in the use of InDesign (for layout), Illustrator (for vector images) and Photoshop (for raster images) or similar software for the respective graphics needs as itemized (use of generative AI highly discouraged).

title: Consultant: US Business Development and Fundraising
body:
At ATNi (Acess to Nutrition initiative) we're looking for a US Business Development and Fundraising Consultant to work with our team.

## **Organization and overall purpose**

ATNi (Access to Nutrition initiative) is a global nonprofit actively challenging the food industry, investors and policymakers to shape healthier food systems. We analyze and translate data into actionable insights, driving partnerships and innovations for market transformation so that all people have access to nutritious and sustainable food. ATNi is registered in the Netherlands with approximately 22 staff and consultants around the world. The majority of staff work from the Netherlands. For more information on ATNi, please visit our website [www.accesstonutrition.org](http://www.accesstonutrition.org/).

## **The role and candidate profile**

ATNi has been undergoing steady growth since 2021. Raising additional resources is required to deliver our [2023-2027 Strategy](https://accesstonutrition.org/news/why-access-to-nutrition-initiatives-new-strategy-aims-to-transform-markets-for-healthier-food/#:~:text=ATNi's%20Policy%20Platform-,Why%20Access%20to%20Nutrition%20Initiative's%20New%20Strategy,Transform%20Markets%20for%20Healthier%20Food&text=Building%20on%20ten%20years%20of,2027%29%20focused%20on%20transforming%20markets.) and our 2030 strategic goal to ensure at least 50% of global food sales are based on healthier and affordable options. We aim to raise resources equivalent to approximately 3.8-4M USD a year until 2029 (our current annual revenue is about 3M USD). In total, our objective is to raise approximately 18M USD total between mid-2026 and end 2029. Establishing new donor relationships in the USA is essential to reach these financial and strategic goals.

Establishing new donor relationships in the US remains essential to reach these financial and strategic goals — but the US funding landscape has changed fundamentally since this target was set. US assistance now flows increasingly through bilateral, multi-year, co-financed country agreements rather than direct NGO grants. Given this volatility, ATNi's US resource mobilization strategy — and this role — must pursue a more diversified funding mix across US government and quasi-governmental sources, private philanthropy, and blended finance. The financial targets above should be reviewed periodically against this shifting landscape.

Reporting to the Head of Business Development and working closely with the Executive Director and ATNi’s management team, the consultant will bring significant and successful resource mobilization experience working with US government institutions and philanthropies. S/he will also interact as needed with some ATNi’s US-based Board members. S/he will have strong partnership development and writing skills, familiarity with international programs and projects, and technical/programmatic understanding of nutrition, food systems transformation and global public health. S/he will have extensive experience successfully positioning for and responding to donor-funding (solicited and unsolicited). This is a part-time engagement at approximately 50% for an initial period of three months, with the possibility of extension.

This role offers a unique opportunity to have a substantial positive impact on a small but growing and influential global nonprofit.

## **Primary responsibilities**

Resource development leadership

•Serve as a senior ATNi representative in the US

•Support fundraising for ATNi's programmatic priorities in the US market, including MarketFit Nutrition and our sodium reduction work, by identifying and cultivating funders active in diet-related disease prevention, and positioning these workstreams within broader pitches to government, and philanthropic donors.

•Design and deliver a US fundraising outreach strategy and plan with identified targets for relevant US government and quasi-governmental funders and philanthropies who fund international work including in low- and middle-income countries. This should also include:

o Establish and maintain an active US-based donor mapping database for ATNi a targeted plan of outreach to potential partners who are already grantees/subcontractors in the US of relevant funders key performance metrics to inform donor revenue forecasting and improve win/loss performance

o Ongoing monitoring of US foreign assistance policy (State Department, USDA, Congress) to anticipate shifts that affect funding availability, given the volatility of the current environment

• Build ATNI’s network by leveraging ATNi’s new fiscal sponsorship arrangement with the [Myriad USA](https://myriadusa.org/)

• Network strategically and widely seeking out partnerships with organizations active in the food, nutrition, health and development finance space to broaden fundraising reach.

• Mentor ATNi’s fundraising team on proposal development processes and good practices, updating internal systems and tools as needed.

• Inform ATNi’s strategic direction based on evolving US funding priorities, identifying key areas for organizational growth and diversification of funding streams while ensuring alignment with ATNi’s mission and long-term goals.

Proposal and capture processes

•Develop, update and maintain compelling ‘pitch decks’ and cases for support tailored to government, philanthropic, and private-sector audiences

•Monitor and analyze trends in the donor landscape, with particular focus on the State Department's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy, USDA, and major US foundations funding nutrition and food systems, to inform short- and long-term strategic planning and positioning

•Pro-actively apply or respond to funding opportunities (i.e., calls for proposals, spontaneous proposals, foundation grant cycles, etc.)

•Lead the coordination of or support the submission of new concepts and proposals for US-based donors. Support other concepts and proposals as needed (e.g. for the EU)

•As needed, coordinate proposal development to ensure timely decision making with inputs from relevant technical experts

## **Qualifications**

- Minimum 8 years' experience in resource mobilization/business development for a global nonprofit, including a minimum of 3-5 years working with US government funding mechanisms and/or major US private foundations.
- Master’s degree, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Experience in public health, food systems, nutrition, health economics, health promotion or relevant field would be beneficial.
- Exceptional English writer/editor with a solid understanding of nutrition and public health and experience mobilizing resources for non-profit organizations.
- In-depth knowledge and existing network of institutions, partners and leaders working in global public health and nutrition, food systems, agriculture, water, health economics.
- Hands-on experience working with key US government and private funders and knowledge of different funding mechanisms (e.g., grants, contracts) of each.
- Proven track record coordinating and contributing to successful business development and proposal efforts that have secured substantial funding from US government, multilateral and/or private funders
- Ability to prioritize, assume responsibility for work, and follow through to completion.
- Flexible, self-starter and innovator, with ability to develop and implement new ideas independently and as a member of a team.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to exercise diplomacy and tact as demonstrated in previous roles that required communication with a broad and diverse set of partners.
- Ability to work independently but with strong accountability, driving projects effectively from conceptual stages to launch, and handling multiple and often competing deadlines.
- Ability and willingness to work under pressure with a positive attitude, as a part of a team.
- Demonstrable respect for all persons regardless of religion, ethnicity, class or gender, with a high comfort level working in a diverse environment with a demonstrated commitment to high professional ethical standards.
- Personal commitment to ATNi’s organization’s mission and goals and our values.

Candidate must be eligible to work in the USA.

title: ICT Officer
body:
Plan International is an independent child rights and humanitarian organisation committed to children living a life free of poverty, violence and injustice. Plan actively unite children, communities and other people who share our mission to make positive lasting changes in children’s and young people’s lives. Plan support children to gain the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to claim their rights to a fulfilling life, today and in the future. Plan place a specific focus on girls and women, who are most often left behind. Plan have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years and are now active in more than 70 countries. Plan International Jordan is established in 2016 and has programmes in governorates in the centre, north and south regions as well as host communities and Azraq camp.

**Role PURPOSE**

The ICT Officer reports to the Head of Operations and Finance and is responsible for providing IT support to staff, and for maintaining the IT infrastructure of the office according to Plan's policies and procedures. The role supports the management of IT assets, networks, devices and servers, and implements ICT standards, security and policies within Plan Jordan.

**Dimensions of the Role**

 The ICT Officer will be responsible for supporting and following on Operational ICT policies, goals, objectives and guidelines and for the ICT planning and implementation. Specifically, s/he will support the Head of Operations and Finance in leading an effective administration, procurement of IT assets , services and ICT Road Map and plans, supervise and/or implement the necessary administration, procurement & logistics processes to ensure the purchase and delivery of ICT supplies and capital equipment in line with the approved response budget.

The role encompasses a broad range of responsibilities, including the effective management and tracking of IT assets, maintenance of ICT infrastructure, and provision of timely technical support to staff to ensure smooth and efficient operations.

**Accountabilities**

**ICT Duties:**

1\. ICT Infrastructure and Systems Administration

- Administer, maintain, and support PIJO's ICT infrastructure, including servers, networks, storage systems, hardware, software, and related technology resources, ensuring reliable and efficient operations.
- Install, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Windows Server environments, including Active Directory (AD), DNS, DHCP, Group Policy (GPO), file services, print services, and user profiles.
- Manage and maintain virtualized server environments using Microsoft Hyper-V, including virtual machines, resource allocation, and system availability.
- Administer and maintain network infrastructure, including LAN, WAN, wireless networks, switches, access points, routers, and network connectivity.
- Configure, manage, and monitor network security appliances, including Cisco Meraki MX Firewall, security policies, traffic filtering, intrusion detection and prevention, and network access controls.
- Manage and troubleshoot VPN connectivity and remote access services, ensuring secure access to organizational resources in accordance with approved security policies.
- Monitor internet connectivity, network performance, bandwidth utilization, and ISP services, coordinating with telecommunications providers to resolve service interruptions.
- Administer and monitor wireless network infrastructure, including access point configuration, connectivity, coverage, and performance.
- Maintain and support CCTV systems, including cameras, recording devices, monitoring systems, and associated network connectivity.
- Monitor the performance, availability, and capacity of ICT infrastructure and recommend corrective or preventive actions to minimize service disruptions.
- Maintain and support ICT infrastructure across all Plan International Jordan locations, including field offices and camps, ensuring reliable network connectivity, system availability, and technical support.
- Conduct ICT infrastructure assessments for new offices, premises, and field locations, identifying connectivity, hardware, network, security, and system integration requirements to ensure operational readiness before staff deployment.

2\. Helpdesk and End-User Technical Support

- Manage and maintain an effective ICT helpdesk support process, ensuring that user requests, incidents, and technical issues are properly recorded, monitored, prioritized, and resolved.
- Provide first- and second-line technical support to employees and beneficiaries, where applicable, through onsite, remote, telephone, and other approved support channels.
- Install, configure, maintain, upgrade, and troubleshoot desktops, laptops, printers, scanners, mobile devices, and other ICT equipment.
- Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, operating system, network connectivity, email, login, user profile, and access permission issues.
- Provide support for Microsoft Windows operating systems, Microsoft Office applications, email clients, and other organizational software.
- Perform software installations, system configurations, hardware upgrades, operating system updates, and troubleshooting in accordance with organizational ICT standards.
- Coordinate laptop and equipment preparation, configuration, allocation, and delivery for new employees.
- Provide technical guidance and awareness sessions to employees on ICT systems, applications, cybersecurity, and appropriate technology usage.
- Maintain records of ICT incidents, support requests, troubleshooting activities, and recurring technical issues to identify improvement opportunities.

3.Cybersecurity, Backup and Business Continuity

- Implement and monitor ICT security measures, including firewalls, VPNs, endpoint protection, access controls, MFA, and security updates.
- Administer backup, storage, and recovery solutions, ensuring data integrity, availability, and business continuity.
- Monitor security alerts, vulnerabilities, and backup logs, and coordinate incident response and corrective actions.
- Support phishing awareness campaigns, security testing, and employee cybersecurity awareness initiatives.
- Document security incidents, vulnerabilities, corrective actions, and mitigation measures.
- Coordinate with regional and global ICT security teams to address security incidents, implement security requirements, and ensure compliance with organizational standards.
- Maintain backup schedules, recovery procedures, and disaster recovery documentation.

4.Microsoft 365, Cloud Services and Document Management

- Administer Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and related cloud applications.
- Manage user accounts, licenses, shared mailboxes, distribution groups, security groups, permissions, and email services.
- Administer SharePoint sites, document libraries, access permissions, and departmental file structures.
- Support digital document archiving, file migration, and SharePoint–OneDrive integration to improve document accessibility and promote paperless workflows.
- Manage and support Google Workspace, organizational domains, DNS records, hosting, and related digital platforms.
- Provide technical guidance and user support on Microsoft 365 applications, cloud services, and collaboration tools.

5\. ICT Projects, Digital Transformation and Strategic Planning

- Contribute to the development and implementation of annual ICT work plans, technology roadmaps, and initiatives aligned with organizational objectives and operational requirements.
- Plan and support ICT infrastructure upgrades, system migrations, technology deployments, and digital transformation projects.
- Coordinate the implementation, testing, and verification of new systems, Microsoft 365 services, data migrations, and other approved technology solutions while minimizing operational disruptions.
- Identify opportunities to improve ICT services, automate manual processes, enhance cybersecurity, and increase operational efficiency through appropriate digital solutions.
- Evaluate and test new technologies, applications, and equipment to ensure compatibility, security, and suitability before implementation.
- Provide technical advice and recommendations to management on ICT infrastructure, technology investments, system improvements, and operational risks.
- Coordinate with internal departments, regional and global ICT teams, and external service providers to ensure the successful implementation of ICT projects.
- Prepare periodic ICT reports covering infrastructure performance, service delivery, security, asset management, ongoing projects, and technology requirements.
- Provide technical training, guidance, and knowledge-sharing sessions to employees and ensure proper handover of ICT projects, systems, documentation, and ongoing activities

6\. ICT Procurement, Vendor Management and Documentation

- Provide technical input into ICT procurement processes, including preparing technical specifications, evaluating technical proposals, and recommending suitable hardware, software, and services.
- Coordinate with procurement and finance departments, vendors, suppliers, internet service providers, and maintenance companies to ensure the effective delivery and maintenance of ICT services and equipment.
- Follow up on service requests, warranties, software licenses, subscriptions, maintenance agreements, and service contracts.
- Verify the delivery, installation, configuration, and acceptance of ICT equipment and services against approved technical specifications.
- Maintain and regularly update ICT documentation, including network diagrams, server configurations, system inventories, asset records, user access records, and infrastructure documentation.
- Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) covering user onboarding and offboarding, account management, equipment allocation, software installation, backups, recovery, and incident reporting.
- Maintain secure records of system configurations, administrative access information, security procedures, and technical changes to support operational continuity and knowledge transfer.
- Serve as the local ICT focal point for technical coordination with regional and global ICT teams and external service providers.

**Other Duties (IT related)**

- Act as a focal point for Electronic signatures
- Follow all asset management procedures effectively at Plan’s offices for IT items.
- Responsible for Asset database (developing database and entry of data);
- Manage a consistent record of the Office's IT asset to ensure accuracy in the current location of all asset with the support of the asset’s custodian.
- responsible for certificates of completion of the receipt of assets and that all assets described in a classified card according to the procedures in Plan’s policies and asset assigning cards.
- Coordinate with the Admin and Logistics Officer for the annual physical asset inventory, ensuring IT asset records reconcile with physical counts and discrepancies are documented and resolved.

***Other Duties***

- Any other tasks requested by the line manager.

Child protection, gender equality and inclusion

- Ensures that Plan International’s global policies for Safeguarding Children, Young People and Programmes Participants and Gender Equality and Inclusion are fully embedded in accordance with the principles and requirements of the policy including relevant Implementation Standards and Guidelines as applicable to their area of responsibility. This includes, but is not limited to, ensuring staff and associates are aware of and understand their responsibilities under these policies and Plan

**Key relationships**

**Internal:** Head of Operations and Finance (line manager). All departments within Plan Jordan.

**External:** Local Partner, Plan International GH, Plan International’s IT Vendors

Technical expertise, skills and knowledge

**Qualifications and Job Skills**

- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
- 2–5 years of relevant experience in ICT operations, IT infrastructure, systems administration, and technical support.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Windows Server, Active Directory, Group Policy (GPO), DNS, and DHCP.
- Practical experience in computer hardware, software, network administration (LAN/WAN), switches, wireless networks, firewalls, VPNs, and cybersecurity.
- Knowledge of CCTV systems, IP cameras, video surveillance, and electronic access control systems (door access systems).
- Experience in implementing, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining ICT systems, servers, and business applications, including SAP.
- Knowledge of data backup, recovery, storage management, ICT asset management, and user access administration.
- Basic knowledge of website administration, WordPress, HTML, CSS.
- Good analytical, problem-solving, communication, negotiation, and teamwork skills.
- Good command of written and spoken English and Arabic.
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a dynamic work environment.
- Ability to work independently, take initiative, learn new technologies, and undertake additional responsibilities as required.

**​​Plan International’s Values in Practice**

**​We are open and accountable**

- ​Promotes a culture of openness and transparency, including with sponsors and donors.
- ​Holds self and others accountable to achieve the highest standards of integrity.
- ​Consistent and fair in the treatment of people.
- ​Open about mistakes and keen to learn from them.
- ​Accountable for ensuring we are a safe organisation for all children, girls & young people

**​We strive for lasting impact**

- ​Articulates a clear purpose for staff and sets high expectations.
- ​Creates a climate of continuous improvement, open to challenge and new ideas.
- ​Focuses resources to drive change and maximise long-term impact, responsive to changed priorities or crises.
- ​Evidence-based and evaluates effectiveness.

**​We work well together**

- ​Seeks constructive outcomes, listens to others, willing to compromise when appropriate.
- ​Builds constructive relationships across Plan International to support our shared goals.
- ​Develops trusting and ‘win-win’ relationships with funders, partners and communities.
- ​Engages and works well with others outside the organization to build a better world for girls and all children.

**​We are inclusive and empowering**

- ​We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential
- ​We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge equality in our programs and our workplace
- ​We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives. ​

**Physical Environment**

Typical office environment

**Level of contact with children**

Low contact: No contact or very low frequency of interaction

**ROLE PROFILE**

**Type of Role:** Fixed-Term

**Contract Duration:** 6 months fixed term contract, renewable subject to the availability of funds and satisfactory performance.

**Reports to:** Head of Operations and Finance

**Location:** Amman, Jordan

**Grade:** Level 13

*Female candidates are highly encouraged to apply. Plan International operates an equal opportunities policy and actively encourages diversity, welcoming applications from all areas of the international community.*

*Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early.*

*Please note that only applications and CVs written in English will be accepted.*

*A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Child Safeguarding Policy.*

title: Human Resources Manager
body:
**Location**: Damascus

**Job summary**

The Human Resources Manager is responsible for leading and managing the Association’s overall Human Resources function through developing HR strategies, policies, and organizational plans, and overseeing the implementation of all HR operations to ensure alignment with the Association’s needs and enhance institutional performance. The role also ensures compliance with applicable legislation, approved policies, and donor requirements, while leading the HR team and developing its systems and procedures to achieve organizational objectives.

**Qualifications and education requirements**:

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Human Resources Management, or an equivalent field.

**Required Skills and Experience**:

- Leadership, guidance, and delegation
- Strategic planning
- Effective communication
- Priority setting and time management
- Negotiation and problem-solving
- Strategic decision-making
- Interpersonal and presentation skills
- Ability to work remotely
- Team motivation
- Resource and budget management
- Analytical and critical thinking
- Report preparation and writing
- Computer proficiency, including:
    - Microsoft Outlook
    - Microsoft Teams
    - Microsoft Word
    - Microsoft Excel
    - Microsoft PowerPoint
    - Microsoft OneDrive

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

- Participate with senior management in defining organizational objectives related to Human Resources, contribute to the development of the Association’s overall strategy, and lead the development, review, and improvement of HR strategies, policies, and objectives. Participate in organizational decision-making within the scope of assigned responsibilities and authority.
- Lead the review and development of the Association’s organizational structure in coordination with relevant departments. Analyze organizational needs and provide recommendations regarding the establishment, modification, or abolition of organizational units and administrative reporting lines, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and the effective distribution of responsibilities and authorities. Submit proposals to senior management for approval.
- Prepare presentations and reports reflecting the activities and achievements of the HR Department internally and externally.
- Represent the HR Department as its primary focal point before donors, partners, and relevant external stakeholders on all HR-related matters, providing necessary clarifications and information within the scope of assigned authority.
- Develop the HR Department’s annual operational plan and budget in alignment with the Association’s vision and objectives. Monitor implementation, periodically assess progress, and take necessary corrective actions.
- Establish, develop, and review HR operational procedures to ensure that approved policies are translated into clear and effective working mechanisms that meet the Association’s needs and donor requirements.
- Lead and manage the HR team by providing technical and administrative guidance and support. Oversee the allocation of tasks and responsibilities, delegate appropriate authority based on priorities and capabilities, monitor performance and achievements, and motivate and develop team members to ensure the efficient and effective achievement of departmental objectives.
- Lead workforce planning across the Association in coordination with relevant departments by analyzing current and future staffing needs in terms of positions, headcount, and competencies. Develop and review the workforce plan and budget to ensure alignment with operational priorities and available financial resources.
- Lead and follow up on addressing departments’ HR needs by assessing opportunities to fill vacancies and staffing gaps through internal resources, including transfers and redistribution, or external recruitment when necessary, in accordance with the approved workforce plan, budgets, and relevant policies and procedures.
- Oversee, review, and approve recruitment processes within the scope of assigned authority, ensuring compliance with recruitment policies and procedures, the workforce plan, and approved budgets, and verifying that all required approvals are obtained before completing hiring procedures.
- Serve as a focal point between senior management and employees on HR-related matters by following up on employee inquiries, feedback, and employment-related concerns, coordinating with relevant departments to address them, and escalating matters requiring senior management intervention or decisions, thereby strengthening organizational communication and facilitating appropriate solutions.
- Oversee personnel administration processes, including leave management, transfers, promotions, retirement, salary increments, allowances, disciplinary actions, grievances, complaints, termination of employment, and other related matters.
- Ensure that employee files are complete, updated, and securely maintained, and verify their compliance with internal policies and procedures and applicable labor legislation in coordination with the Legal Department. Follow up on addressing any deficiencies or cases of non-compliance.
- Follow up on employee inquiries and complaints and ensure they are addressed in accordance with approved procedures. Participate in investigation committees related to employment matters and oversee the follow-up of grievances and completion of related procedures in accordance with approved policies and regulations.
- Oversee payroll preparation and review the integrity of payroll procedures, ensuring the proper application of approved policies and procedures and the accuracy of employee data, entitlements, and deductions, in coordination with the Finance Department. Ensure that all required reviews and approvals are completed before disbursement.
- Develop the performance appraisal policy, system, and implementation plan to ensure fairness, transparency, and alignment with the Association’s objectives.
- Approve the sharing of performance appraisal results with senior management, ensuring the confidentiality and sensitivity of information and preventing conflicts of interest in handling appraisal outcomes.
- Manage matters arising from performance appraisal results, including grievances and corrective actions. Link appraisal outcomes to promotions, salary increments, and rewards, while following up on the implementation of performance improvement plans.
- Analyze training needs in coordination with relevant departments.
- Develop training plans within the approved budget to ensure that organizational needs are met.
- Coordinate with supporting entities and partners to implement training programs.
- Oversee the evaluation of training program effectiveness and measure their impact on employee performance and their responsiveness to training and organizational needs. Analyze evaluation results and use them to improve future training plans and programs.
- Coordinate with the Digital Transformation Unit to follow up on the development of the ERP system in relation to HR operations. Identify functional requirements and review and approve proposed modifications to ensure that the system aligns with approved procedures, policies, and operational needs, in coordination with relevant departments within the Association.
- Attend regular meetings with the direct supervisor, subordinates, and relevant colleagues to discuss and review the latest updates.

**Protection Policy:**

Ataa Association considers any type of child abuse unacceptable, as it recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. Ataa Association confirms that it is committed to ensuring a safe environment for children and takes a strict stance against any type of child abuse and exploitation.

**Discrimination, Abuse, and Harassment Policy:**

Ataa Association provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, or harassment (sexual or otherwise) based on race, religion, origin, age, marital status, nationality, or disability. , or the military situation.

title: Gender Officer
body:
**The Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund**

**About Us**

AECF is a leading African-based development organization that leverages the power of the private sector to address systemic issues of rural poverty and employment across the continent. We find and fund innovative, game changing commercial businesses in the agribusiness and renewable energy sectors that transform the lives of low-income households. By catalyzing funding, we help companies surface and commercialize new ideas, business models, and technologies that increase agricultural productivity, expand energy access, and alleviate poverty, particularly where these efforts impact women and young people. AECF works in frontier markets, fragile contexts, and high-risk countries where few mainstream financing institutions go. We back bold enterprises to tackle climate risk, expand opportunity for women and youth, and build resilience in fragile contexts so rural and marginalized communities can rise out of poverty

Since 2008, we have deployed over US$290 million, leveraged $916 million in additional capital, provided funding to 698 businesses in 27 countries – impacting 36 million people.

**About the Programme**

AECF is implementing Investing in Women’s Entrepreneurship for a Greener Economy in Benin and Burkina Faso, a six-year gender equality and economic inclusion programme funded by Global Affairs Canada. The programme provides investment capital and technical assistance to women-owned and women-led enterprises, financial institutions, cooperatives and associations operating in climate-positive sectors. It also works with women’s rights organisations and other local actors to address structural barriers, strengthen women’s agency and advance policy advocacy and social norm change at community and national levels.

**About the Role**

This role supports implementation of AECF’s current Gender Lens Investing Strategy through the Investing in Women Benin and Burkina Faso programme (IFEV-Benin and Burkina Faso). The role will lead and coordinate gender-responsive activities, help the programme achieve its gender equality and women’s economic empowerment targets, and ensure that gender considerations are integrated across investment, technical assistance, advocacy, learning and results measurement.

The successful candidate will work closely with women entrepreneurs, women-led enterprises, agricultural cooperatives and farmer associations, financial institutions, women’s rights organisations, gender champions and other programme partners.

The incumbent will be based in Burkina Faso. This role will report to the Programme Manager, Benin/ Burkina Faso.

**Key Responsibilities**
