International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

## Equal Opportunities

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

## Misconduct Disclosure Scheme

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

title: Supply Chain and Operations Manager - Sudan
body:
We are currently recruiting a **Supply Chain and Operations Manager** to join our **Supply Chain and Operations** team.

This is a **country-based position** in **Khartoum, Sudan**, with regular travel to field locations subject to access and security conditions.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks and enhanced due diligence**.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team work across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

We work with local actors to deliver safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs. Relief International is an alliance of multiple international entities operating under a one-team approach with a shared mission and leadership structure.

**About the Opportunity**

This is a critical leadership role supporting Relief International's operations in one of the world's most complex humanitarian environments.

The Supply Chain and Operations Manager leads the delivery and continuous improvement of procurement, warehousing, medical supply logistics, transport and fleet management, asset management and office operations across Sudan. Based in Khartoum and supporting teams operating in dispersed and often insecure locations, the role is responsible for ensuring country operations remain reliable, cost-effective, compliant and responsive to programme needs.

Working closely with Area Managers, programme teams, Finance, HR, Security, IT and global supply chain colleagues, you will strengthen systems, build the capacity of field teams, improve operational visibility and ensure supply chains continue to function effectively in challenging circumstances.

This is a hands-on leadership position requiring someone who has successfully managed complex field operations and can balance strategic oversight with practical problem-solving.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead and manage supply chain and operations functions across country and field offices, providing leadership, supervision and clear accountability for operational performance.
- Oversee procurement planning and implementation, ensuring timely, competitive and compliant procurement of goods and services while maintaining strong supplier relationships and value for money.
- Manage warehousing, inventory control and medical supply logistics systems, ensuring accurate stock visibility, quality standards, reconciliation processes and reporting.
- Lead fleet, transport, asset and office operations management across country and field locations, ensuring operational continuity, cost controls and compliance with organizational and donor requirements.
- Strengthen procurement, inventory, fleet and asset tracking systems through practical, user-friendly tools and reporting mechanisms.
- Produce regular operational performance reporting, identifying risks, bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement and ensuring corrective actions are implemented.
- Support cross-border supply chain activities and importation processes where required, including medical commodities and specialized programme supplies.
- Work closely with Finance and programme teams to strengthen controls, reconcile commitments and proactively address operational, compliance and fraud risks.
- Build and develop high-performing teams through coaching, mentoring, performance management and capacity strengthening initiatives.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- University degree in logistics, supply chain management, business administration or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- Minimum seven years' experience in humanitarian supply chain, logistics or operations management, including at least three years in a senior management role within conflict-affected, post-conflict or similarly fragile environments.
- Demonstrated hands-on experience across procurement, warehousing and inventory management, medical logistics, transport and fleet management, asset management and multi-site operations.
- Proven ability to lead and support geographically dispersed teams operating in challenging and low-connectivity environments.
- Experience designing or improving practical operational tracking systems and using data to strengthen controls, decision-making and performance management.
- Strong knowledge of donor procurement compliance requirements, supplier management, inventory controls, operational budgeting and risk management.
- Excellent leadership, coaching and problem-solving skills, with the ability to simplify processes while maintaining effective controls and accountability.
- Strong written and spoken English and willingness to travel regularly to field locations.
- Arabic language skills would be an advantage.
- Previous experience in Sudan, Chad, Darfur or similar humanitarian contexts would be a bonus
- Experience supporting health and nutrition supply chains, emergency scale-ups and complex humanitarian donor-funded programmes is desirable.

title: Programme Officer - TradeMark Africa - Nigeria
body:
**Location** Abuja, Nigeria, based at the joint TTF-ECOWAS project office  
**Department** Programmes  
**Reports to** Programme Manager and Customs Specialist, TTF-ECOWAS  
**Direct reports** None

## Job Summary

TradeMark Africa (TMA) is seeking a Programme Officer to support delivery of its work under the ECOWAS Trade and Transport Facilitation Programme (TTF-ECOWAS). The programme is the ECOWAS-anchored component of the EU’s Trade and Transport Facilitation Measures for Strategic Corridors in West Africa. GIZ leads implementation in partnership with TMA and ENABEL.

Working closely with the Programme Manager, the Programme Officer will track agreed actions and deadlines, keep records and monitoring data current, and follow up with consultants and partners. The role also coordinates meeting and workshop logistics and flags delays, risks and implementation issues early.

## Key Responsibilities

- **Programme delivery and implementation support** Maintain activity plans, schedules, budget tracking sheets, risk registers and programme records. Support procurement documentation, track consultant and partner deliverables, and keep TMA’s internal project records up to date.
- **Monitoring, reporting and consortium coordination** Collect and analyse quantitative and qualitative results data, including gender-disaggregated data, and draft inputs for progress and annual reports. Maintain shared coordination tools with GIZ and ENABEL, support committee meetings, and compile evidence for audits and reviews.
- **Stakeholder coordination** Liaise with ECOWAS directorates, national ministries, customs administrations and other agencies. Coordinate workshops, training sessions and technical meetings with the Project Assistant, and follow up on agreed actions.
- **Communications, visibility and knowledge management** Prepare briefs, presentations and programme updates. Document lessons and good practices, contribute content to programme communications, and help meet EU and TMA visibility requirements.
- **Gender, inclusion and safeguards** Help integrate gender equality and inclusion into programme activities, with attention to women, youth and small-scale cross-border traders. Ensure safeguarding, environmental and climate considerations are addressed during implementation, and escalate concerns promptly.

## Qualifications and Experience

- Undergraduate or postgraduate degree in International Trade, Development Studies, Economics or Business Administration.
- At least **three years of relevant experience for postgraduate degree holders** or **five years for undergraduate degree holders** in supporting donor-funded projects, with hands-on experience in project coordination, monitoring and reporting.

## Essential Skills and Languages

- Good understanding of Project Cycle Management, including planning, activity tracking, risk management and reporting.
- Practical experience with data management, monitoring systems and results reporting.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and familiarity with project management tools.
- Good analytical, report-writing and problem-solving skills.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to handle competing priorities under pressure.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work with a wide range of stakeholders and within a multi-partner team.
- Initiative, self-motivation and a collaborative approach.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.

## Desirable Qualifications, Experience and Skills

- Professional training or certification in Project Cycle Management, project management such as PRINCE2 or PMP, or monitoring and evaluation.
- Familiarity with trade facilitation, customs or regional integration initiatives.
- Experience with EU-funded or multi-partner programmes.
- Working knowledge of French.
- Familiarity with ECOWAS institutions and with trade and customs agencies in Nigeria.

title: Human Resources Officer, West Africa - TradeMark Africa - Côte d'Ivoire
body:
**Location** Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire  
**Department** Human Resources  
**Reports to** Senior Human Resources Manager  
**Direct reports** None

## Job Summary

TradeMark Africa (TMA) is seeking a Human Resources Officer to support staff and managers across assigned West African countries. Based in Abidjan, the Officer will advise on employee relations and coordinate recruitment, onboarding, payroll, benefits, performance management, and learning and development.

The Officer will help ensure that TMA’s HR policies and practices comply with applicable employment legislation in each country. The role will use workforce data to identify risks and improve HR services, and will provide agreed cover for other country offices and headquarters during absences.

## Key Responsibilities

- **HR advice and employee relations** Advise managers and employees on HR policies, performance, conduct, grievances, disciplinary matters, absence and workplace conflict. Maintain confidential case records, coordinate investigations and legal input when required, and escalate material risks. Support organisational change, staff engagement, performance reviews and learning and development.
- **Workforce planning and reporting** Help country and functional leaders forecast staffing needs and review organisational structures. Track headcount and employment costs, maintain reliable employee data, and report workforce trends and risks.
- **Recruitment, onboarding and employee administration** Coordinate approved recruitment, including vacancy announcements, screening and interviews. Follow up on reference and background checks, prepare offer letters and contracts for approval, and coordinate onboarding, statutory registration, probation reviews, transfers and exits.
- **Payroll, employee records and benefits** Coordinate monthly payroll inputs with HR, Finance and Employers of Record, check payroll outputs for accuracy, and resolve queries. Maintain employee and leave records in line with data protection requirements. Administer insurance, the Employee Assistance Programme and staff welfare support.
- **Staff mobility and expatriate support** Coordinate relocation, immigration, visas, work permits, statutory registration and other assignment arrangements for expatriate staff and their dependants. Liaise with internal teams and external advisers when specialist guidance is required.
- **Employment compliance and service providers** Monitor changes in employment legislation and statutory requirements, maintain country compliance calendars, and support filings and updates to policies and contracts. Manage Employers of Record and other HR service providers, including service quality, compliance, invoicing and issue resolution.
- **Audits, controls and service improvement** Prepare evidence for internal and external audits, track corrective actions and improve HR processes, data quality and service delivery. Apply TMA’s safeguarding and risk management procedures and promptly report concerns, including suspected fraud, bribery or corruption.
- **HR cover for other offices and headquarters** Handle employee queries, casework and approvals within delegated authority during agreed periods of cover. Apply the relevant local legislation and policy, escalate complex matters and document open items for handover.

## Qualifications and Experience

- Undergraduate or postgraduate degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Organisational Psychology or a related field.
- Recognised professional qualification or certification in Human Resource Management, such as CIPD, SHRM or equivalent.
- At least **five years of progressive HR experience for undergraduate degree holders** or **three years for postgraduate degree holders**, including substantial responsibility for HR operations in a medium-sized organisation.
- Demonstrated experience supporting employees and managers across multiple countries, preferably in West Africa, and applying country-specific employment legislation and HR practices.
- Experience managing employee relations cases, coordinating payroll and benefits, managing HR vendors and applying compliance controls.
- Experience providing HR support across multiple jurisdictions, including covering for colleagues and quickly learning unfamiliar legal and policy requirements.

## Essential Skills and Languages

- Full professional proficiency in **English and French**, including the ability to advise employees and managers and prepare clear HR correspondence in both languages.
- Sound knowledge of HR operations, employee relations, employment compliance, payroll controls, data protection and HR information systems.
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to use workforce data to identify trends, assess risks and determine follow-up actions.
- Ability to handle sensitive matters with confidentiality, discretion, empathy and procedural fairness.
- Sound judgement, integrity and resilience, with the ability to work independently, adjust priorities across countries and escalate material risks promptly.
- Excellent communication, influencing, stakeholder management, presentation and problem-solving skills. Ability to build effective working relationships across cultures, functions and locations.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly within West Africa and occasionally to headquarters or other countries, with flexibility across time zones when providing cover.

## Desirable Qualifications

- Membership of a recognised professional human resources body.

title: Programme Manager, Customs - TradeMark Africa - Nigeria
body:
**Location** Abuja, Nigeria, based at the joint TTF-ECOWAS project office  
**Department** Programmes  
**Reports to** Country Director, Nigeria / Strategic Expert TTF-ECOWAS  
**Direct reports** Project Assistant, TTF-ECOWAS

## Job Summary

TradeMark Africa (TMA) is seeking a Programme Manager to lead day-to-day delivery of its work under the ECOWAS Trade and Transport Facilitation Programme (TTF-ECOWAS), with a focus on customs operations. The programme is the ECOWAS-anchored component of the EU’s Trade and Transport Facilitation Measures for Strategic Corridors in West Africa. GIZ leads implementation in partnership with TMA and ENABEL.

The Programme Manager will implement approved workplans and budgets, provide technical input on customs reforms and serve as TMA’s operational contact for GIZ and ENABEL. The role dedicates approximately 80% of its time to TTF-ECOWAS and 20% to supporting other TMA programming in Nigeria.

## Key Responsibilities

- **TTF-ECOWAS programme management and delivery (40%)** Develop detailed activity plans and oversee delivery, procurement and contracts. Track spending and forecasts, coordinate workshops and technical meetings, maintain audit-ready records, and supervise the Project Assistant. Apply TMA, EU and safeguarding requirements across activities.
- **Customs technical support (20%)** Advise on customs data exchange, interconnectivity of customs and transit systems such as SIGMAT, common external tariffs, tariff schedules, rules of origin and customs management regulations. Support pilot Member States in transposing ECOWAS customs instruments. Work with the ECOWAS Customs Union and Taxation Directorate, national customs administrations, TMA specialists and GIZ advisers.
- **Monitoring, reporting and coordination (20%)** Verify results data and prepare TMA’s narrative and financial inputs to consolidated reports. Coordinate operational planning with GIZ and ENABEL, support steering and technical committee meetings, and document lessons and programme results.
- **Nigeria programme support (20%)** Support planning, procurement, monitoring and quarterly reporting for other TMA projects in Nigeria. Contribute to new project design and engagement with government, private-sector and development partners.

## Qualifications and Experience

- Undergraduate or postgraduate degree in Economics, International Trade, Customs Administration, International Trade Law or Development Studies.
- At least **10 years of relevant work experience** for undergraduate degree holders or **eight years** for postgraduate degree holders.
- At least **five years of experience in customs administration, customs modernisation or trade facilitation programming**, preferably in West Africa.
- At least **three years of experience managing donor-funded projects**, including procurement, contract management, budget tracking and reporting.
- At least **three years of experience supervising staff**.

## Essential Skills and Languages

- Good knowledge of customs procedures, transit regimes, customs IT systems, and ECOWAS trade and customs instruments, including the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS).
- Strong programme management skills, with attention to detail in planning, procurement and financial follow-up.
- Good understanding of regional integration and the socio-political context in Nigeria and West Africa.
- Excellent written and spoken English, including the ability to draft reports and present to senior counterparts.
- Ability to work constructively and diplomatically with government officials, regional institutions and partner organisations, and to collaborate within a multi-partner team.
- Initiative and ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

## Desirable Qualifications, Experience and Skills

- Professional training in customs or project planning and management.
- Experience with EU-funded programmes and knowledge of EU contracting, financial and reporting rules.
- Working knowledge of French.
- Familiarity with digital trade and customs connectivity systems in West Africa.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:** The Employment Specialist assists newly arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to attain self-sufficiency through employment by guiding them through employment preparation, coordinating job placements, and other career advancement services.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake, assessment and provide program orientation to clients eligible for employment services.
- Provide job readiness training and job search coaching and connect clients with job opportunities.
- Develop and cultivate long-term relationships with area employers and staffing agencies to identify appropriate employment opportunities for clients.
- Assist clients and employers as necessary with post-placement issues and continuing employment needs.
- Monitor client job performance, wage levels, and related metrics.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

title: Conduct a rapid learning review of Ground Truth Solutions' project: "Practical accountability in complex humanitarian crises"
body:
**Background**

Ground Truth Solutions implemented a project between January and December 2026 with the aim to **provide a comprehensive, evidence-based understanding of the views and priorities of crisis-affected communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Palestine, and to ensure that these priorities are driving humanitarian action in complex and resource-scarce conflict environments**.

Building on our previous work and engagement in these two contexts, this project supported by the Belgian Federal Public Service (FPS) Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation, and implemented with longstanding local partners, included **evidence-based perception research involving quantitative and qualitative enquiry**. Following data analysis, we worked on actively **translating findings into action** by convening communities, local leaders, and decisionmakers in the aid sector to interpret the evidence together, identify barriers and opportunities, and co-develop practical steps for change. Through targeted workshops, bilateral dialogue, and strategic engagement, we initiated advocacy and will continue these efforts over the coming months, to ensure that community perspectives inform both operational adjustments and higher-level policy and funding decisions, Throughout, we prioritised capacity sharing with local partners and spotlighted community-led responses that demonstrate agency and mutual support – shifting the narrative from aid dependency toward autonomy, grounded in evidence and lived experience.

**About us**

Ground Truth Solutions (GTS) is an international non-governmental organisation that works with crisis-affected communities worldwide to ensure their views and priorities shape how aid and climate action is designed, funded, and delivered. Through more than 15 years of perception research and strong partnerships with local actors, we generate evidence on what people in crisis are experiencing, what they want for their futures, and the support they need to get there. We use this evidence to inform decisionmakers, influence policy and funding processes, and strengthen accountability across the humanitarian system. Our work is grounded in a simple principle: aid that doesn’t listen, fails.

**Objectives**

To conduct an independent rapid review of the “Practical accountability in complex humanitarian crises” project, assessing efforts to promote a culture of accountability in complex conflicts through public-good perception data, promotion of local knowledge and expertise, and contribution to people-centred aid in a changing humanitarian sector. The project will evaluate progress toward meeting project objectives and make suggestions for improvement in future projects of this nature.

***Specific Objectives***

1. **Relevance and design:** Assess whether the project objectives and design were appropriate for the objectives.
2. **Effectiveness and results:** Measure the extent to which the project achieved its intended outputs and outcomes.
3. **Advocacy and relationships:** Analyse engagement of different actors in this project and identify factors enabling or hindering utilisation of the results.
4. **Lessons learned and good practices:** identify insights to inform future projects.
5. **Scope**

The review will cover:

- Project design in DRC and Palestine
- Outputs and uptake
- Relationships and promotion of local knowledge
- Contribution to systemic change

**Key review questions**

The review will address the following overarching questions:

- To what extent were local actors involved in project design?

Were project outputs clear, accessible and useful?

- How strategic and influential were advocacy efforts locally and globally?
- What could we do differently to ensure uptake of evidence next time?

**Methodology**

We are open to methodologies candidates propose, but at a minimum the learning review should include:

- Inception phase and clarifying the methodology
- Desk review of project documentation
- Speaking to partners in key informant interviews who engaged with the project about their experiences
- Production of a short report highlighting lessons learned for future projects

**Key deliverables & timelines**

- Interviews with partners: by February 5th, 2027
- Draft report: by February 15th, 2027
- Feedback from GTS: by February 17th, 2027
- Final report: by February 24th, 2027

**Maximum overall budget**

EUR 6,000

title: Vivier – Chargé(e) de suivi
body:
**Vivier – Chargé(e) de suivi**

**Résumé**

**Langues :** L’anglais et/ou l’arabe et/ou le français ET l’une des 12 langues du vivier (Pachto, dari, arabe levantin, arabe soudanais, bengali, arabe égyptien, ourdou, darija marocaine, arabe irakien, kurde sorani, kurde badini et somali).

**Rôle :** Réaliser des appels de suivi structurés auprès d’un échantillon de personnes ayant bénéficié du soutien de nos conseillers.

**Lieu :** À distance, depuis n’importe où.

**Vivier :** Réserve non rémunéré de janvier 2027 à mai 2029. L’intégration au vivier ne constitue pas une offre d’emploi.

**Rattachement :** Responsable S&E.

**Contrat :** Contrat de consultant par campagne.

## **Pourquoi ce vivier**

New Pathways to Resilience (NPR) est un projet de trois ans financé par le Fonds « Asile, migration et intégration » (AMIF) de l’UE. Il repose sur le Mécanisme d’adaptation aux crises (CAM) de Seefar, qui permet au projet de réagir en s'adaptant à l'évolution des dynamiques migratoires. Lorsqu’un indicateur suivi franchit son seuil, une campagne peut être activée pour un nouveau public ou une nouvelle langue, et Seefar dispose alors de deux semaines pour la lancer. Ce délai est trop court pour recruter à partir de zéro ; nous maintenons donc un vivier de réserve non rémunéré de Conseillers, de Chargés des réseaux sociaux et de Chargés de suivi présélectionnés, couvrant 12 langues, prêts à être engagés dès qu’une campagne est approuvée.

## **Qui sommes-nous**

Seefar Foundation est une entreprise sociale dotée d’une mission simple : transformer la vie des personnes vulnérables. Grâce à des programmes fondés sur la technologie, la psychologie et le changement de comportement, nous aidons les personnes à acquérir les compétences et la confiance nécessaires pour contribuer positivement à leurs communautés. C’est ainsi que nous accompagnons les gouvernements dans la recherche de solutions aux défis liés à la migration irrégulière, à la pauvreté, à la traite des êtres humains, à l’extrémisme violent, à l’accès à la justice, entre autres.

Notre équipe exceptionnelle de plus de 100 consultants réunit des personnes orientées résolution des problèmes et innovation, en mettant en œuvre des programmes et des recherches à fort impact. Ensemble, nous résolvons des problèmes complexes et à fort impact pour des gouvernements et des ONG dans les domaines de la communication, du numérique, ainsi que de la recherche, du suivi et de l’évaluation, en Afrique, en Asie et en Europe.

## **Vos responsabilités**

1. Appels de suivi (80 %). Participer à une session de formation d’introduction rémunérée et vous familiariser avec la campagne, les outils de suivi et les lignes directrices éthiques relatives aux échanges avec des personnes vulnérables. Mener ensuite des appels de suivi structurés par téléphone auprès d’un échantillon de personnes ayant bénéficié du soutien de nos conseillers, 3 semaines, 3 mois ou 12 mois après leur séance individuelle avec un conseiller de Seefar. Administrer de manière cohérente, à chaque appel, les outils de suivi standardisés (formulaires Kobo), en recueillant des données quantitatives et qualitatives sur le bien-être, les décisions migratoires, les orientations et la satisfaction à l’égard du soutien reçu. Soumettre les fiches complétées dans les 24 heures suivant chaque appel.
2. Qualité des données et apprentissage (15 %). Partager vos observations sur les tendances des réponses, les problèmes de qualité des données et tout élément pouvant affecter la fiabilité des résultats. Contribuer, si nécessaire, à la traduction ou à la rétrotraduction des outils et modèles de S&E entre votre langue et l’anglais. Gérer votre propre calendrier d’appels et signaler rapidement les participants injoignables.
3. Indépendance et protection (5 %). Les appels de suivi étant un processus de contrôle qualité, rester indépendant(e) des conseillers et des Chargés des réseaux sociaux qui mettent en œuvre la campagne, afin que les données de résultats restent neutres et crédibles. Traiter toutes les données des participants avec une stricte confidentialité, conformément aux normes de protection des données de Seefar, et faire remonter immédiatement toute préoccupation en matière de protection.

## **Votre profil**

**Pour réussir, vous aurez besoin de :**

- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience en suivi et évaluation, en collecte de données ou dans un domaine connexe.
- Expérience dans la conduite d’enquêtes ou d’entretiens structurés par téléphone ou à distance.
- Maîtrise courante d’au moins une langue du vivier, et bonne maîtrise professionnelle d’au moins une de ces langues : anglais, arabe ou français, à l’écrit et à l’oral.
- Maîtrise de l’informatique.
- Une connexion internet fiable.
- Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles et de communication, et capacité à échanger avec tact avec des personnes vulnérables.
- La capacité de travailler de manière autonome et à distance, et de gérer votre charge de travail dans le respect des délais.
- Grande attention aux détails et sens de l’organisation.
- Un espace privé et calme pour les appels confidentiels.
- La capacité de travailler en tant que consultant(e) indépendant(e) et de recevoir des paiements en EUR par virement bancaire international.

Vous devez remplir toutes les conditions ci-dessus. Un atout si vous avez une expérience sur des programmes humanitaires, de développement ou liés à la migration, une connaissance du soutien psychosocial ou des contextes de retour, ou une expérience de Kobo Toolbox ou de plateformes similaires.

## **Votre façon de travailler**

**Anglais et/ou français et/ou arabe, oral/écrit**

Anglais, arabe ou français (oral et écrit) : vous vous exprimez avec aisance à l’oral et rédigez, dans l’une de ces langues, des notes et observations claires et exploitables par d’autres.

**Langue du vivier**

Vous menez des entretiens couramment dans l’une de ces 12 langues : pachto, dari, arabe levantin, arabe soudanais, bengali, arabe égyptien, ourdou, darija marocaine, arabe irakien, kurde sorani, kurde badini, somali.

**Entretiens structurés**

Vous suivez un questionnaire de manière cohérente, sans paraître réciter un texte.

**Sensibilité**

Vous mettez les gens à l’aise, reconnaissez la détresse et réagissez avec bienveillance.

**Exactitude des données**

vous collectez des données complètes et cohérentes, et les saisissez dans les 24 heures..

**Indépendance**

Vous maintenez une séparation claire avec l’équipe de mise en œuvre afin que les données restent crédibles.

**Traduction**

Vous traduisez et rétrotraduisez avec précision les outils de S&E.

**Compétences numériques**

Vous êtes à l’aise avec Kobo ou des outils similaires et Google Suite.

**Autorégulation**

Vous réagissez de manière constructive aux défis professionnels et émotionnels.

## **Fonctionnement du vivier**

- **Ce n’est pas une offre d’emploi.** L’intégration au vivier ne garantit pas de travail, et vous pouvez travailler ailleurs en attendant. Seuls les mois travaillés sur une campagne activée sont rémunérés.
- **Toutes les personnes du vivier sont considérées comme qualifiées.** Lorsqu’une campagne est activée, nous choisissons la personne la plus adaptée selon la langue, le genre, la localisation et la disponibilité. La raison de chaque choix est consignée.
- **Lorsqu’une campagne est approuvée,** nous contactons les Chargés de suivi environ six semaines avant le démarrage.
- **Points trimestriels.** Tous les trois mois, nous vous demandons si vous souhaitez rester, faire une pause ou partir, et si vous pourriez commencer dans votre délai de préavis. Manquer un point rend votre place inactive ; en manquer deux d’affilée entraîne son expiration et la suppression de vos données.
- **Vous restez dans le vivier** jusqu’à ce que vous choisissiez de partir, que vous manquiez deux points d’affilée, ou que NPR prenne fin en mai 2029.

### **Ce que nous offrons**

- Une formation rémunérée une fois engagé(e).
- La liberté de travailler ailleurs pendant votre présence dans le vivier, et de refuser une offre sans pénalité.
- La possibilité de travailler depuis n’importe où, puis de revenir dans le vivier ou postuler à d’autres postes chez Seefar après une campagne.
- Seuls les mois travaillés sur une campagne activée sont rémunérés.

### **Avec qui vous travaillerez**

Vous serez rattaché(e) au Responsable S&E de NPR. Afin de garantir la neutralité des données de résultats, vous travaillerez indépendamment des conseillers et des Chargés des réseaux sociaux qui mettent en œuvre la campagne, tout en partageant vos enseignements avec l’équipe S&E. Vous rejoindrez une équipe aux perspectives, parcours, expertises techniques et expériences vécues variés, qui travaille en Europe, au Moyen-Orient, en Afrique et en Asie.

- Un espace privé et calme pour les appels confidentiels.
- La capacité de travailler en tant que consultant indépendant et de recevoir des paiements en EUR par virement bancaire international.

- Une licence en conseil psychologique, travail social, psychologie ou dans un autre domaine lié à la santé mentale.
- Connaissance des voies de migration légale pertinentes pour votre public.
- Expérience de travail avec des migrants originaires des pays de votre public ou se trouvant en transit..

Vous rédigez et vous exprimez en anglais et/ou en français et/ou en arabe des notes et observations claires et exploitables par d’autres.

Vous restez calme, patient(e) et présent(e) auprès des personnes en détresse.

**Évaluation**

Vous reconnaissez la détresse et les besoins en santé mentale, et y répondez de manière appropriée.

Vous expliquez sans jugement les risques de la migration et les alternatives sûres et légales.

Vous protégez les données des participants et savez quand signaler une préoccupation en matière de protection.

**Tenue des dossiers**

Vous documentez chaque séance dans les délais, à chaque fois.

Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’utilisation d’un ordinateur portable ou d’un téléphone et de Google Suite.

title: Vivier – Chargé(e) des réseaux sociaux
body:
**Vivier – Chargé(e) des réseaux sociaux**

**Résumé**

**Langues :** anglais, plus l’une des 12 langues du vivier (pachto, dari, arabe levantin, arabe soudanais, bengali, arabe égyptien, ourdou, darija marocaine, arabe irakien, kurde sorani, kurde badini et somali).

**Rôle :** Lancer, gérer et modérer des campagnes Facebook et Instagram localisées, y compris des publicités payantes de génération de prospects (Lead Generation Ads), dans votre langue.

**Lieu :** À distance, depuis n’importe où.

**Vivier :** Réserve non rémunéré de janvier 2027 à mai 2029. L’intégration au vivier ne constitue pas une offre d’emploi.

**Rattachement :** Responsable des réseaux sociaux.

**Contrat :** Contrat de consultant(e) pour chaque campagne.

## **Pourquoi ce vivier**

New Pathways to Resilience (NPR) est un projet de trois ans financé par le Fonds « Asile, migration et intégration » (AMIF) de l’UE. Il repose sur le Mécanisme d’adaptation aux crises (CAM) de Seefar, qui permet au projet de réagir lorsque les dynamiques migratoires évoluent. Lorsqu’un indicateur suivi franchit son seuil, une campagne peut être activée pour un nouveau public ou une nouvelle langue, et Seefar dispose alors de deux semaines pour la lancer. Ce délai est trop court pour recruter à partir de zéro ; nous maintenons donc un vivier de réserve non rémunéré de Conseillers, de Chargés des réseaux sociaux et de Chargés de suivi présélectionnés, couvrant 12 langues, prêts à être engagés dès qu’une campagne est approuvée.

## **Qui sommes-nous**

Seefar Foundation est une entreprise sociale dotée d’une mission simple : transformer la vie des personnes vulnérables. Grâce à des programmes fondés sur la technologie, la psychologie et le changement de comportement, nous aidons les personnes à acquérir les compétences et la confiance nécessaires pour contribuer positivement à leurs communautés. C’est ainsi que nous accompagnons les gouvernements dans la recherche de solutions aux défis liés à la migration irrégulière, à la pauvreté, à la traite des êtres humains, à l’extrémisme violent, à l’accès à la justice, entre autres.

Notre équipe de plus de 100 consultants réunit des personnes orientées résolution des problèmes et innovent, en mettant en œuvre des programmes et des recherches à fort impact. Ensemble, nous résolvons des problèmes complexes et à fort impact pour des gouvernements et des ONG dans les domaines de la communication, du numérique, ainsi que de la recherche, du suivi et de l’évaluation, en Afrique, en Asie et en Europe.

## **Vos responsabilités**

1. Lancement de campagnes, contenus et publicité (70 %). Adapter dans votre langue les modèles de publicités, le manuel de messages, les formulaires de suivi-évaluation et les modules de formation de NPR. Créer, lancer et modérer des publicités Facebook et Instagram localisées de génération de prospects. Gérer la publicité payante, en particulier les Lead Generation Ads via Meta Ads Manager, utiliser des outils d’IA pour orienter le ciblage et la segmentation des publics, suivre les statistiques, réaliser des tests A/B et ajuster la campagne en conséquence. Identifier et contacter des influenceurs pertinents sur les réseaux sociaux afin de les engager pour produire du contenu publicitaire.

- Maîtrise de Meta Ads Manager et des Lead Generation Ads.
- Expérience avérée dans la création et l’optimisation de contenus multimédias visant le changement de comportement.
- Connaissance des dynamiques migratoires et de l’écosystème numérique de votre public.
- Solides compétences en recherche, rédaction et analyse.
- Aisance dans le travail entièrement à distance avec Google Suite, et une connexion internet fiable.
- Votre propre ordinateur portable.
- La capacité de travailler en tant que consultant indépendant et de recevoir des paiements en EUR par virement bancaire international.

Vous devez remplir toutes les conditions ci-dessus. Un atout apprécié :

- Maîtrise courante d’une deuxième langue ou d’un deuxième dialecte du vivier.
- Maîtrise de Google Ads et de Google Analytics.
- Expérience de collaboration avec des influenceurs sur des campagnes numériques, et connaissance du paysage des influenceurs dans le pays d’origine de votre public.
