title: TO PROVIDE PSYCHOSOCIAL SERVICES TO HUMANITY & INCLUSION (HI) STAFF IN KENYA
body:
**CONTEXT**  
Handicap International Federation (HI), operating as Humanity & Inclusion, is an international organisation working alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations. In Kenya, HI operates from Nairobi and from field locations including Kakuma and Dadaab, where staff often work in demanding, remote and humanitarian settings that expose them to stress, critical incidents and workplace hazards.  
HI Kenya recognises that the mental health and wellbeing of its staff are central to delivering quality programmes and to caring for its people. Staff working in humanitarian and field settings may be exposed to prolonged stress, burnout and distressing events, and need access to professional, confidential support.  
To support this, HI is seeking a qualified service provider to offer psychosocial services for HI staff in Kenya

**DESCRIPTION OF THE EXPECTED SERVICE**  
The contracted service provider is to provide the following services: -  
**Specific objectives of the assignment**  
• To provide confidential, professional and accessible psychosocial support services that promote the mental health and wellbeing of HI staff in Kenya.  
• To provide timely psychological support to individuals and teams affected by critical incidents.  
• To strengthen the capacity of managers and Human Resources staff to recognize distress and support staff wellbeing.  
**Responsibilities and Tasks**  
The service provider will carry out the following activities: -  
a) Individual and Group Support  
• Provide confidential individual counselling sessions, delivered in person or virtually, by qualified and licensed counsellors or psychologists, with the number of sessions per staff member to be agreed with HI.  
• Facilitate group sessions and workshops on stress and burnout management, resilience, self-care and work-life balance.  
• Refer staff requiring specialised psychiatric or medical care to appropriate providers, with  
the staff member’s consent.  
b) Critical Incident Response  
• Provide psychological first aid and critical incident debriefing for individuals and teams following distressing events, such as accidents, security incidents or the loss of a colleague, within an agreed response time.  
• Provide a mechanism for urgent support outside normal working hours, such as an on-call counsellor or helpline.  
c) Manager and Human Resources Support • Orient managers and Human Resources staff on recognising signs of distress, supportive supervision and referral pathways.  
• Advise HI on staff wellbeing initiatives based on anonymised trends.  
d) Confidentiality and Inclusion  
• Ensure strict confidentiality and safe handling of records in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 and professional codes of ethics. HI will not have access to individual counselling content.  
• Ensure services are inclusive and accessible, including for staff with disabilities, culturally sensitive, and available in English and Kiswahili.

**Scope and Target**  
The assignment covers HI Kenya staff based in Nairobi and in the field locations of Kakuma and Dadaab. The estimated number of staff eligible for the service is 59  
The scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:  
• Providing individual and group psychosocial support to HI staff throughout the contract period.  
• Providing psychological first aid and critical incident debriefing when required.  
• Providing urgent support outside normal working hours.  
• Referring staff to specialised care where needed.  
• Orienting managers and Human Resources staff on supporting staff wellbeing.  
• Preparing and submitting the reports and deliverables listed in this TOR.

**Profile of the service provider**  
The service provider will need to have the following capacities:  
• Registered business entity in Kenya with a proven track record of providing psychosocial or counselling services to organisations. Experience with NGOs or humanitarian organisations is an added advantage.  
• Counsellors and psychologists must be licensed by the Counsellors and Psychologists Board of Kenya, with experience in trauma, stress and burnout management and critical incident debriefing.  
• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and protect client data in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019.  
• Ability to deliver services in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab (in person or virtually), in English and Kiswahili.  
• Experience in or commitment to disability inclusion is an added advantage.

Duration and Place of Performance of the Service  
The contract will be for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of signing, renewable subject to satisfactory performance. Psychosocial services will be available throughout the contract period. The service shall be carried out in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab, with virtual counselling options where appropriate.  
**Work Plan**  
Based on the proposed assignment, the timeline shall be agreed upon by the service provider and HI. The service provider shall submit a service delivery plan within one (1) week of signing the contract.

**Report**  
The service provider shall provide the following deliverables:-  
• Psychosocial service delivery plan  
• Quarterly psychosocial service report, with anonymised utilisation data, key themes and recommendations  
• Summary report (without identifying details) for each critical incident response  
• Final end-of-assignment report  
All reports shall be submitted in both editable electronic format and PDF format. Reports shall not contain information that identifies individual staff members.  
**Contact Person**  
During the performance of the service, the service provider will be assisted by the Human Resources Officer – Kenya in coordinating schedules and logistics with the field offices.  
**Appendices**  
Willingness to adhere to Handicap International's Federation institutional policies (Prevention and fight against corruption, Child Protection, Protection of Beneficiaries against sexual abuse and harassment). Available on the website: [https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies.](https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies.)

**Evaluation**  
Application documents submitted will be evaluated in three (stages);  
**General Mandatory Evaluation Criteria**  
**For firms or institutions**

-Certificate of Registration  
-Trade license Certificate/ Business Permit  
-PIN/VAT Registration Certificate  
-Current Tax Compliance Certificate  
-Personal Accident Insurance cover  
-Valid practising licences of the proposed counsellors and psychologists (Counsellors and Psychologists Board)

**For Individuals**

-National ID  
-Relevant certifications, professional licences and accreditations  
-PIN/VAT Registration Certificate  
-Current Tax Compliance Certificate  
-Personal Accident insurance cover

**Technical Capacity Evaluation**  
**(a) Profile and experience of the service provider:**

- The firm should have proven expertise and experience in providing psychosocial services. Attach three reference letters.
- Provide a list of assignments of similar scope of work undertaken within the last 2 years, along with names of clients (including contact person, email contacts, postal address and telephone numbers – this must include the three referees provided above)
    
    **(b)Professional/technical capacity/ capability:**
- The proposed counsellors and psychologists should have relevant experience and professional qualifications in the relevant field.
- The proposal should describe the proposed approach to service delivery and the measures to ensure confidentiality and protection of staff data.
    
    **Financial Evaluation**  
    \- At the Financial stage, the Lowest Competitive Evaluated bidder and within budget estimates will be considered for the award of the contract.
    
    **NB: Your Financial proposal should Include flights, meals, accomodation,communication and any other contigency / miscelleneous costs for Kakuma ,Dadaab and Nairobi.**

title: 23740 Public Health Officer (Emergency Health) (P)
body:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) plays a leading role in supporting governments and communities to build health systems that are responsive to the needs of these populations and address public health concerns along the mobility continuum. IOM uses targeted interventions such as direct health service provision, establishment of referral networks for specialized care, and health promotion for migration-affected people and host communities.

In Afghanistan, IOM provides and supports access to good-quality primary and secondary healthcare services, with a focus on returnees, migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), and underserved host communities in border regions, as well as other vulnerable populations across the country. IOM employs a direct implementation modality of healthcare services through its Mobile Health Teams (MHTs), Community-Based Vaccination Centres (CBVC), Vaccination Outreach Teams (VOT), and Basic Health Centres (BHC), which ensures greater responsiveness to community needs. The primary health care services provided include reproductive health, maternal, neonatal and child health services, trauma care, basic nutrition and community-based Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). IOM also provides technical support as well as procurement, warehousing, and transportation of medical commodities for external partner health facilities.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programmes and Operations, with direct supervision from the Programme Coordinator (Migration Health), the Public Health Officer (Emergency Health) will provide management support, expert technical guidance and advice to the Migration Health Programme Coordinator towards successful implementation of the multi-programme Health Assistance to Crisis Affected Populations (H3) activities/emergency health portfolio, including implementation of the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005), and vaccination and polio interventions. The Public Health Officer (Emergency Health) is expected to carry out the duties in accordance with the strictest ethical standards and with due respect for gender and socio-cultural sensitivities.

**Responsibilities**

1. Substantively support the operationalization of the Country Office’s (CO) public health and emergency health preparedness, response, and recovery strategy.
2. Provide technical leadership for vaccination and polio interventions by ensuring high‑quality micro‑planning, cold chain continuity, vaccine accountability, and evidence‑based outbreak response across mobility‑affected and disaster‑impacted locations.
3. Manage and coordinate project activation, implementation, reporting, and evaluation of emergency health programs in coordination with the Migration Health Officer.
4. Develop and/or support the development of proposals in coordination with the Program Support Unit, and ensure regular reporting requirements are met, including on achievements, projects, problems encountered, pertinent developments, and strategic needs.
5. Strengthen national disease surveillance capacity in coordination with relevant stakeholders, alert and response capacity of border level/PoE staffing, and support the development of early warning systems (including event-based and indicator-based surveillance).
6. Regularly coordinate with IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Unit to ensure utilization of mobility data for health programme planning and response, and coordinate with other units, including the Program Support Unit, Cross-Border Post Arrival Humanitarian Assistance (CB-PAHA) and other units as necessary.
7. Prioritize and ensure information sharing between internal units, cluster partners, and IOM and other emergency response actors to facilitate effective and efficient coordination;
8. Provide expert technical support and advice for vulnerability assessments, risk mapping, and development of preparedness/contingency planning at the provincial level.
9. Monitor and ensure that national health staff and partners are familiar with internationally recognized tools and standards and lead organizing trainings/capacity building on an ad-hoc/as needed basis on migration health.
10. Lead organizing meetings, workshops, orientations, and training for different stakeholders on implementation of the International Health Regulations and disease surveillance.
11. Represent IOM at Health Cluster meetings and other relevant cluster meetings and liaise and coordinate with national and international health and humanitarian assistance authorities, agencies, and organizations regarding the planning and implementation of health-related activities. Key counterparts include the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH), World Health Organization (WHO), Health Cluster partner agencies, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Working Group and other stakeholders.
12. Undertake travel duties, as required and in line with prevailing security restrictions, related to project implementation and oversight, staff training, and liaison with partners, including regular travel duties to the borders with Afghanistan, Pakistan and Iran, and the Sub-Offices, to coordinate, develop and/or support programme implementation.
13. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

  
**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Nursing, Medicine, Health Sciences, Community or Public Health, Epidemiology, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.
- An additional qualification in clinical medicine, tropical medicine, maternal and child health, or public health is an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Minimum three years of relevant working experience in the design and implementation of International Health Regulations/public health in conflict settings and response at national and international levels;
- Experience in vaccination programmes, polio eradication, or Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPDs)- focused public health interventions.
- Experience in proposal development and reporting required;
- Demonstrated experience with the UN, IOM, or International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) preferred;
- Demonstrated cluster experience is an advantage;
- Experience working in hardship duty stations and emergency settings with complex operating environments preferred;
- Demonstrated computer background, including experience with databases, Microsoft applications, spreadsheets, word processing, and SPSS/STATA;
- Demonstrated clinical experience is an advantage; and,
- Demonstrated operational and field experience in migration, refugee and displaced persons related programming is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Excellent analytical, communication, presentation and writing skills;
- Proven capacity to develop and implement programmes in the area of migration and health.
- Ability to work effectively in high-pressure, rapidly changing environments; and,
- Demonstrated good people skills, and demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with stakeholders and partners.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23572 Deputy Chief of Mission (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD) and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and in close coordination with relevant Departments in Headquarters (HQ), the Deputy Chief of Mission (DCoM) will be responsible and accountable for providing support to the CoM in their responsibility to ensure coherence between the Programmes and Support Services of the Country Office (CO), including Programme Development for the CO. The DCoM will ensure that implementation of IOM programmes is done in an effective and efficient manner consistent with CO’s Strategy and in line with the expectations of the IOM’s donors and beneficiaries, while collaborating with the national and regional authorities.

**Responsibilities**

1. In coordination with the CoM, represent the CO by promoting IOM activities with the national authorities, diplomatic corps, governmental and private donors, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), government authorities/ or de facto government authorities, and other partners in the Country and Region.
2. Oversee the formulation of Country Strategies, policies and approaches across IOM’s operational portfolio, and identify and develop new programmes to address emerging needs while ensuring systematic implementation capacity, in close coordination with the Programme Support Unit (PSU).
3. Contribute to ensuring the highest efficiency in CO’s Risk Management and Compliance functions, to ensure strengthening internal controls and compliance with contractual rules and regulations through effective management and the provision of accurate, researched, and documented risk and compliance information, effective delivery of services, transparent utilization, and management of programme resources.
4. Ensure the continuous, effective, and efficient planning, coordination, and integration between the CoM and DCoM Offices and the Sub-Offices.
5. Work closely with the CoM/ Special Envoy, Heads of Sub-Offices, and Heads of Units to enhance inter-unit collaboration and coordination, to maximize efficiencies and efficacy within the CO programming to ensure that all CO’s Units work towards common goals and a consistent and coherent strategy.
6. Make strategic recommendations and provide advice to the CoM and Senior Management to improve overall performance of the CO and support the CoM’s Office with development of strategy/policies/guidance notes, organize regular Senior Management Meetings (SMT), set up meetings with external partners (UN/ de facto authorities), prepare speeches/talking points, and support/facilitate consultation process with defector authorities/UN/international community on CO’s strategies.
7. In close coordination with the Resources Management Unit (RMU), Programme Support Unit and respective Programme Managers, ensure compliance of all projects with IOM and donor regulations, policies and obligations as indicated in the funding agreements, project documents, work plans and budgets.
8. Oversee field operations to ensure implementation of the humanitarian, development and peace building nexus to ensure timely, effective and efficient programming delivery, ensuring through sound leadership, supervision and monitoring that all blockages, disruptions and delays are avoided in order to achieve program results and that these results are measurable.
9. Lead the development of strong donor contacts and relations, monitoring, updating programme funding priorities across the migration management spectrum and provide expert support to the CoM in fundraising activities. Participate in all strategic inter-sector coordination and performance management mechanisms.
10. Ensure IOM participation in appropriate policy and operational United Nations Country Team (UNCT) inter-agency mechanisms; engage with UN agencies in the development and implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), and coordinate with UNCT and partners on the implementation and review processes of the migration-relevant Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Global Compact for Migration and the UN Network on Migration related activities as these processes move forward.
11. Formally deputize for CoM on an ongoing basis and exercising mission, staff, and financial management responsibility in CO, including chairing the Senior Management Team and/or Senior Operational Team meetings in the absence of the CoM.
12. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, Law, International Relations, Business Administration, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with ten years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with twelve years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Excellent understanding of and proven experience in inter-agency coordination and strategic engagement, UN structures and systems, and experience in both crisis contexts and development settings;
- Extensive experience formulating and delivering internal displacement and solutions policy, strategy, and programming;
- Experience at international level on managing programmes, covering emergency, stabilization, and development areas;
- Previous experience as a Head of Office, Chief of Mission and/or Senior Programme Manager with a Government or UN agency, or a regional or international organization;
- Extensive experience in external relations or strategic engagement, as well as liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities and institutions;
- Experience in managing IOM Offices and liaising with governmental authorities, other national/international institutions; and,
- Work experience in the Region.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated knowledge of programme development, management and capacity-building methodologies;
- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Good knowledge of financial and administrative management;
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming; and,
- Knowledge of programme management in emergency context.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23770 MHPSS Response Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)) (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations and overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD), and the guidance of the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides advice and supports the implementation of institutional policy from HQ in Country Offices (COs) across the Region. Specifically, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides oversight, quality control, and thematic expertise to promote consistent, cohesive, and quality evidence-based programming. Together with other Regional Thematic Units (RTUs), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) contributes to thought leadership on saving lives and protecting individuals on the move, driving solutions to displacement, and facilitating regular pathways for migration. The RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit also identifies regional opportunities and risks, fosters knowledge sharing, encourages policy and research development, and supports cross-thematic collaboration internally. Externally, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) offers advocacy, policy, and technical programme recommendations to regional entities, Member States, and relevant migration fora, spearheaded by IOM’s Regional Office (RO) and CO leadership. For both IOM teams and partners in the region, the Regional Thematic Specialist Humanitarian Response and Recovery is the go-to source for humanitarian response and recovery expertise and guidance.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Advocacy, and Representation:**

1\. Strategic Direction: Lead and manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit in the delivery of regular thematic guidance and technical support to COs in the contextualization of the Strategic Plan.

2\. Advocacy and Representation: Assist and provide strategic advice to the DRD for Operations by articulating IOM's Strategic Plan to external stakeholders or in fora, discussions, and platforms, based on HQ and Global Offices' (GOs) guidance.

**Technical Support and Capacity Building:**

3\. Technical Assistance: Lead the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit's delivery of technical assistance on thematic and cross-cutting priorities based on identified or requested needs in collaboration with HQ and COs. Coordinate across regional units, relevant COs, and HQ for crisis responses, focusing on preparedness, protection in emergencies and AAP, life-saving actions, displacement tracking, peace, recovery and solutions.

4\. Training and Capacity Development: In coordination with HQ functional homes and the Staff Development and Learning Unit, provide thematic training and capacity building to COs and RO staff as well as external partners as requested.

**Partnerships and Resource Mobilization:**

5\. Strategic Partnerships: Develop and maintain partnerships with a diverse range of regional actors, including donors, regional political and economic bodies, UN, private sector, non-government institutions, academic institutions, community-based organizations, international financial institutions, international organizations, and Member States, to promote IOM’s Strategic Plan.

6\. Resource Mobilization: In coordination with HQ, GOs, Country Offices for Partnership and Advocacy, COs, and the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), advocate programmatic priorities with new and traditional donors, including the private sector.

**Quality Control and Oversight:**

7\. Project Development and Reporting: In coordination with the RPDOs, facilitate the project development and reporting process through technical inputs, review, approval, and endorsement in line with IOM’s Project Handbook and thematic guidance from DHRR HQ.

8\. Monitoring and Evaluation: In coordination with the Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, hold regular bilateral discussions with CO thematic focal points to assess

challenges, opportunities, and trends. Flag issues and opportunities to senior regional and HQ staff and guide COs' adjustments. Actively support COs to integrate audit, evaluation, and donor feedback. 9. Risk Management: In coordination with the Risk and Compliance Officer, provide oversight and support to COs on the identification, management, and treatment of risks pertaining to DHRR, in line with IOM's Risk Management Framework and Policy (IN/213 Rev.1).

10\. Cash-Based Interventions: In coordination with the global CBI Officer, promote the use of cash-based modalities, where feasible, in line with IOM's global strategies, standards and commitments, and provide guidance and support to COs in designing, implementing and coordinating CBI.

**Knowledge Management, Policy, and Research:**

11\. Knowledge Management and Innovation: In coordination with the RPDO, contribute to and facilitate the use of knowledge-sharing platforms, and disseminate innovative and best practices related to DHRR.

12\. Policy: In coordination with the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer, provide thematic support and recommendations on regional and country-level policies and frameworks to COs, donors, and key partners.

13\. Data, Research, and Foresight: In coordination with HQ and the Regional Data Hub, analyse and disseminate thematic data to inform evidence-based strategic planning, resource mobilization, policymaking, and programming.

**Communication and Coordination:**

14\. Thematic Community of Practice: Convene and maintain a community of practice in the region for thematic focal points in COs, with involvement of HQ functional homes as relevant, to promote sharing of new practices, innovative approaches, partnerships, training opportunities, and other areas of regional thematic interest.

15\. Coordination: Lead engagement in inter-regional, continental, and multi-country initiatives, programmes, and strategies with corresponding RTSs, Global Thematic Specialists, and CO focal points; where necessary, coordinate the involvement of HQ functional homes.

**Cross-Cutting Priorities:**

16\. Mainstream: In line with the IOM Strategic Plan and corresponding custodianship outlined in the Regional Office Terms of Reference, promote, integrate, and mainstream cross-cutting priorities and modalities (i.e., Cash-Based Interventions) in all areas of DHRR’s work in the region. The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is responsible for mainstreaming protection-centered approaches in all areas of IOM's work.

17\. Custodianship: The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is the regional custodian of IOM’s Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion in humanitarian settings, AAP, and Cash-Based Initiatives. Custodianship entails support to other RTUs, as requested, with technical knowledge and capacity on protection mainstreaming as outlined under the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery Terms of Reference and the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit Terms of Reference.

**DHRR Regional Thematic Unit Management:**

18\. Manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit, including overseeing and managing the delivery of the Unit’s specific responsibilities in their entirety as outlined in the Unit’s Terms of Reference.

19\. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Social Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian response and recovery, and related areas relevant to project development and management, thematic capacity building, and liaison;
- Minimum five years experience working in non-OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) countries managing humanitarian response and recovery projects;
- Experience in liaison, resource mobilization, and advocacy with governmental and diplomatic officials, national and international institutions and organizations, civil society, and private sector actors;
- Experience working in an international, inter-governmental, or non-governmental organization, United Nations, or government; and,
- Experience in the design and implementation of capacity building on humanitarian response and recovery.

**Skills**

- Ability to understand complex contexts and fast-changing migration and displacement dynamics and ability to frame them in their regional, global, and political contexts;
- Proven track record of successful engagement with donors, developing projects, and mobilizing resources for IOM priority areas;
- Demonstrated ability to effectively lead and manage a diverse teams of specialists;
- Strong analytical skills combined with the ability to effectively summarize, present, and communicate findings;
- Demonstrated knowledge and expertise of relevant international standards and classifications relevant to humanitarian response and recovery; and,
- Proven agent of change or willingness to foster a culture of learning and knowledge management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23758 Programme Development Officer (SHIFT Africa) (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (Operations) and the direct supervision and strategic and technical direction of the Regional Thematic Specialist (Labour Migration), and in coordination with the Head of Unit, Partnerships and Development, Private Sector Partnerships (PSP), Headquarters (HQ), the Programme Development Officer (SHIFT Africa) will be responsible and accountable for coordinating the end-to-end programme-development process for SHIFT Africa, translating approved strategic and technical direction and inputs from relevant IOM functions into a coherent, technically sound and investment-ready programme package.

The Programme Development Officer (SHIFT Africa) will support the integration of relevant private-sector, market and partnership considerations into programme design, drawing on PSP expertise on private-sector engagement, partnership structuring, investment and co-investment, while working with regional and country teams to translate opportunity-system and market intelligence into viable programme pathways.

**Responsibilities**

1. Coordinate the end-to-end development of the SHIFT Africa programme, preparing and maintaining a programme-development plan covering required products, consultations, reviews, decisions, dependencies, responsibilities and submission timelines, under the guidance of the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS).
2. Coordinate and consolidate regional, country and HQ contributions, including relevant private-sector, market and partnership inputs, into one coherent continental programme design, identifying gaps and inconsistencies and supporting alignment between the overarching programme architecture and its proposed regional, country and partnership components, under the guidance of the RTS.
3. Translate approved strategic and technical thematic inputs into programme development, including theory of change, results chain, results framework, intervention logic, implementation arrangements, workplan, budget, and risk framework, under the guidance of the RTS.
4. Support structured engagement with Mastercard Foundation and other strategic partners throughout the co-creation and programme-development process, preparing working and decision materials, translating feedback into programme-design implications, tracking requests and commitments, and ensuring timely consolidation of IOM inputs, in coordination with the RTS.
5. Coordinate and support the development and consolidation of the programme budget with relevant units, including cost assumptions, unit-cost methodologies, cost-per-transition scenarios, leverage assumptions and distinctions between programme expenditure and contributions expected from governments, employers, financial institutions and other partners, in coordination with the Resources Management Unit (RMU).
6. Coordinate the integration of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) considerations into programme and project design, working with MEAL, data and thematic specialists to support the development of indicators, baselines, targets, and verification approaches that are internally consistent.
7. Compile and analyse programme-development evidence and opportunity-system intelligence, including country and regional inputs, opportunity assessments, market and institutional information, delivery experience, partnership intelligence and costing information, for use in programme design decisions, in coordination with the RTS.
8. Coordinate programme-design consultations and working sessions involving Country Offices (COs), Regional Offices (ROs), HQ units, governments, private-sector and market actors, development partners, youth organisations and other stakeholders, working with relevant PSP colleagues on private-sector and partnership-related engagements, in coordination with the RTS.
9. Promote coherence between the programme’s continental ambition and country-level implementation realities, including alignment across IOM regions and operating contexts.
10. Support the development and integration of partnership models involving private-sector actors, employers, financial institutions, training providers and regional organisations, including the articulation of partner value propositions, potential contributions and roles within opportunity-led portfolios, in coordination with PSP and relevant technical and regional teams.
11. Support compliance with IOM programme-development requirements, coordinating inputs from legal, finance, procurement, risk, safeguarding, data protection and other relevant functions and tracking the resolution of review comments.
12. Maintain an organised programme-development repository, including current and archived versions, source evidence, assumptions, costing files, consultation records, partner information, review comments, approvals and decision logs.
13. Support the transition from concept development to full proposal development and inception planning, documenting assumptions requiring validation, outstanding design questions and preparatory actions for subsequent approval and action.
14. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Economics, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Development, Labour Market Development, Social Sciences, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience coordinating the development of large-scale, complex, multi-country and multi-partner programmes;
- Experience in the design and application of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning approaches, including indicator development, target setting, results measurement, data analysis and the use of evidence for programme adaptation;
- Experience coordinating programme development across multiple technical, operational and
    
    geographic teams is an advantage;
- Experience working in an international, inter-governmental, or non-governmental organisation, the United Nations, or government;
- Experience engaging with governments, development partners, private-sector actors, financial institutions and other market actors in the context of programme development, partnership development or resource mobilisation; and,
- Experience applying programme development approaches to employment, labour mobility,
    
    livelihoods, economic inclusion or related programming is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated programme and project development skills, with demonstrated ability to translate technical concepts, evidence and strategic priorities into coherent, scalable, and measurable programme designs;
- Demonstrated analytical skills, including the ability to synthesise quantitative and qualitative evidence;
- Demonstrated ability to develop results frameworks and integrate monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning into programme design and adaptive management;

title: 23769 Protection Coordinator (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programmes (HoP), the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM), and the overall guidance and technical support of the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) on Protection (PxD), the Protection Coordinator coordinates and support the implementation of protection institutional policy in the Rwanda Country Office (CO). The Global Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR) program aims to provide Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR) to migrants in Rwanda, ensuring that returns are safe, dignified, and based on the migrants’ free, prior, and informed consent. Additionally, the program offers independent, needs-based post-arrival assistance at the request of countries of origin or receiving countries, always with the explicit consent of the migrants.

Specifically, the Protection Coordinator provides oversight, quality control, and thematic coordination and support to promote consistent, cohesive, and quality evidence-based programming while fostering opportunities and risks as well as knowledge sharing.

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee and manage the Protection programming across the CO and provide technical support to other units of the CO on Protection Mainstreaming to ensure safe programming and capacity development.
2. Oversee the effective development and implementation of the CO’s Protection programming by exercising administrative, operational, and financial management for relevant projects.  
    Provide operational management, guidance and supervision to the relevant staff, assisting with programmatic strategy and implementation, including where to focus programme resources and address operational challenges with a focus on protection. Mentor and support staff, conduct relevant training, and ensure capacity building of Programme staff.
3. Establish, maintain and further expand strong relationships across UN Agencies, humanitarian  
    organizations, government and community interlocutors, and with a broad range of other local interests toward the successful implementation of CO’s Protection programming, including IOM’s representation at national and international levels.
4. In close coordination with the relevant units at the CO, Regional Offices and HQ, as well as with government counterparts and other relevant partner organizations, identify priorities arising during implementation of the Programme and develop new projects and activities, aligning them with the identified areas of focus based on a solid results framework and in response to emerging trends and priorities, as well as donor interests and requirements based on IOM’s institutional strategies, policies and guidelines.
5. Ensure the key programmatic directions are shared with international stakeholders, including donors, to maximize impact, minimize overlapping and stimulate fund mobilization for new programmes.
6. Ensure timely and quality preparation and submission of Programme reports, in close  
    coordination with relevant units in the CO and according to requirements of IOM, donors  
    and relevant stakeholders.
7. Monitor progress against strategic objectives, programme benchmarks, and provide advice  
    with respect to improvements and corrections; oversee the establishment of a common  
    Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework that incorporates regular reporting requirements  
    and impact evaluation strategies, in close coordination with CO’s Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) team.
8. Oversee the production of visibility/communications materials in close coordination with  
    Public Information Officer/Focal Point of the CO.
9. Oversee the development and maintenance of data collection and analysis mechanisms for  
    IOM’s ongoing or new programmes and share relevant information with partners.
10. Undertake regular visits to the Sub-Offices to oversee, coordinate, and support the Protection programme implementation.
11. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Social Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least seven years of relevant professional experience.
