## Contexte de la mission

***Mission et vision de Médecins du Monde***

Médecins du Monde Belgique (MdM-BE) est une association internationale de développement médical faisant partie d'un réseau international. Nous fournissons une assistance médicale aux groupes vulnérables, en Belgique, Europe du Sud-Est, Afrique du Nord, de l’Ouest et Centrale. Nous voulons une couverture universelle de santé où chaque personne a accès aux soins, sans obstacles (financiers, culturels, géographiques, etc.).

Nos projets se destinent à toutes les personnes qui n'ont pas ou plus d'accès aux soins de santé. En particulier, ils se structurent en cinq axes : les personnes en marge de la société (personnes sans-abri, sans papier, usagères de drogues, travailleuses du sexe, etc.) ; les enfants en situation de vulnérabilité ; les femmes (accompagnées dans leur combat pour l'égalité ou contre les violences sexuelles par exemple) ; les personnes migrantes ou déplacées et les victimes de crises ou de conflits.

Pour mener à bien notre mission, nous nous basons sur trois piliers :

- Soigner : donner un réel accès aux soins aux populations.
- Changer : plus qu'aider, nous voulons changer les choses à long terme.
- Témoigner : nous ne restons pas silencieux.

Grâce à notre expérience et notre présence sur le terrain, nous interpellons les pouvoirs (locaux, régionaux et (inter)nationaux) avec des faits, des chiffres et des réalités. Nos projets suivent une série de valeurs communes à toute notre organisation : Justice sociale, Empowerment, Indépendance, Engagement, Equilibre.

La présente évaluation s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme quinquennal (2022-2026), financé par la DGD à travers les outcomes SDSR intitulé « L’accès à des services de santé de qualité assure le droit et la capacité à la population d’exercer librement sa vie affective, sexuelle et reproductive dans le district sanitaire d'Agadez Commune, au Niger. » et SDM intitulé « La protection des personnes en situation de migration est renforcée par l’accès à des services de santé et d’appui psychosocial de qualité adaptés, dans la commune d’Agadez, au Niger ».

Cette évaluation finale porte en particulier sur les projets partie du programme liées aux deux outcomes, qui s’intègrent également dans les objectives spécifique du programme commun.

## Objectif de l'évaluation

**Objectifs général et spécifique(s)**

L'objectif de cette évaluation finale est de rendre compte des résultats obtenus des outcomes 4 & 5 «L’accès à des services de santé de qualité assure le droit et la capacité à la population d’exercer librement sa vie affective, sexuelle et reproductive dans le district sanitaire d'Agadez Commune, au Niger.», et «La protection des personnes en situati on de migration est renforcée par l’accès à des services de santé et d’appui psychosocial de qualité adaptés, dans la commune d’Agadez, au Niger. », et portera sur l’ensemble de ses résultats et activités mis en œuvre au Niger dans la commune d’Agadez. **Elle permet d’apprécier, à la fin du programme quinquennal l'efficacité, l’impact, et la durabilité, ainsi que l’intégration transversale du genre et de l’environnement, du plaidoyer et de la santé mentale.**

**Cette évaluation finale sera menée par un.e consultant.e/équipe de consultant.e.s. externe qui devra également identifier les bonnes pratiques et fournir des recommandations** pour des interventions similaires visant à renforcer la capacité des communautés et du système de santé. Les résultats de cette évaluation permettront de soutenir le plaidoyer en direction des autorités sanitaires afin de faire évoluer les approches et modèles de formation en santé sexuelle et reproduction, droits humains, équité, accès aux services ainsi qu’à la coordination et bonne gouvernance pour mieux adapter la stratégie. Ils seront autant d’arguments pour une mise à l’échelle sur d’autres districts sanitaires au niveau national ainsi que dans d’autres pays d’intervention.

Les résultats du projet étant généraux, l’équipe d’évaluation devra se référer aux principaux types d’indicateurs du cadre de résultats qui seront fournis dans la documentation du projet.

**L’évaluation devra analyser la théorie du changement du projet**.

**L’évaluation conjointe** de ces deux outcomes, mis en œuvre au Niger dans la commune d’Agadez, devra inclure **une analyse comparative du modèle** d’intervention conçu historiquement au niveau du siège de MdM et utilisé dans ces deux projets, **et son adaptabilité contextuelle**.

**L’évaluation finale du programme quinquennal** adoptera une approche intégrée et transversale permettant d’apprécier conjointement les changements générés par les outcomes SDSR et SDM, tout en tenant compte de leurs objectifs, de leurs cibles et de leurs contextes d’intervention spécifiques. Elle examinera la contribution à l’amélioration de l’accès équitable à des services de santé de qualité, au renforcement de la connaissance et de l’exercice des droits, à l’autonomisation des personnes et à la participation communautaires. Elle analysera également les effets du renforcement des capacités des prestataires et des acteurs institutionnels, de la coordination entre les parties prenantes et des actions de plaidoyer sur la qualité, l’accessibilité et la pérennité des services. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux changements observés auprès des femmes, des adolescentes, des personnes migrantes et des autres groupes vulnérables, ainsi qu’aux évolution des pratiques professionnelles, des normes sociales et des mécanismes de gouvernance. Cette démarche permettra d’identifier les résultats communs, les complémentarités entre les deux outcomes, les facteurs ayant favorisé ou limité les changements et les enseignements à tirer pour renforcer la durabilité des acquis et orienter les interventions futures de MdM- BE et des ses partenaires au Niger selon le contexte du pays.

**Cette évaluation finale vise les objectifs spécifiques suivants :**

1. **Evaluer la performance et les résultats du projet** :

- Évaluer la performance globale du projet au regard des critères d'évaluation définis:efficacité, l'impact et la durabilité, afin d’apprécier le niveau d’atteinte des objectifs et des résultats escomptés.
- Mesurer les changements et les effets observés auprès des ayants droit et des autres parties prenantes, et apprécier dans quelle mesure les interventions ont contribué à répondre aux besoins identifiés.

1. **Apprécier l’intégration des dimensions transversales**:

- Analyser dans quelle mesure les principes liés au genre, l’environnement, le plaidoyer, la participation des communautés hôtes, migrantes, et l’accès équitable de tous les groupes cibles aux activités du projet, surtout les plus vulnérables, ont été intégrés dans la conception et la mise en œuvre du projet.
- Apprécier les effets du projet sur les différents groupes bénéficiaires, en tenant compte notamment des éventuelles disparités liées au genre, à la santé mentale, au plaidoyer mené à la vulnérabilité ou à l’accès aux services.

1. **Identifier les bonnes pratiques et tirer les leçons apprises**:

- Identifier, documenter et analyser les bonnes pratiques, approches innovantes et facteurs de succès ayant contribué à l’atteinte des résultats du projet.
- Identifier les principales difficultés, contraintes et leçons apprises au cours de la mise en œuvre afin d’éclairer la conception et la mise en œuvre de futures interventions selon le contexte du pays.

1. **Formuler des recommandations pour les futures interventions :**

- Formuler les recommandations opérationnelles, réalistes et contextualisées fondées sur les résultats et les enseignements de l’évaluation, en vue de renforcer, l’efficacité, l’impact et la durabilité des interventions futures sur la SDSR et la SDM.
- Identifier les conditions nécessaires à la pérennisation et/ou à la réplication des approches ayant démontré leur pertinence et efficacité.

1. **Evaluer la redevabilité envers les populations**

- Apprécier dans quelle mesure les mécanismes de participation, d’information, des retours d’information et de gestion des plaintes ont permis de renforcer la redevabilité du projet envers les populations vulnérables.
- Evaluer la perception des populations, des autorités et des parties prenantes concernant la pertinence, la qualité et les résultats des interventions.
- Documenter les principaux résultats et enseignements de l’évaluation afin de favoriser une communication transparente et fondée sur les évidences auprès des différentes parties prenantes.

## **Profil recherché**

**Education**

- Diplôme universitaire de 2ème cycle (BAC + 5) en : statistique, sciences sociales, santé publique, gestion, protection ou autre discipline connexe
- Disposer d’un certificat valide en technique d’évaluation de projets humanitaires / de développement ou être membre ou affilié à une association d’experts en évaluation reconnue, est un atout

**Expérience**

- Expérience d’au moins 5 ans dans le travail d’évaluation de projets dans les secteurs de la santé et de la migration
- Expérience avec des méthodes d'évaluation innovantes (qualitatives) et des méthodes d'enquête sociale (collecte de données, saisie, analyse), des entretiens semi-structurés et des discussions de groupe.
- Expérience avérée dans l’utilisation de méthodes d’évaluation qualitatives, innovantes et participatives (entretiens semi-structurés, discussions de groupe, observation, ateliers, outils visuels et interactifs adaptés aux contextes de faible littératie), ainsi que dans la collecte, l’analyse qualitative et la triangulation des données.
- Expérience dans la collecte et l’analyse des données, et dans la consultation de groupes marginalisés (femmes, jeunes, personnes en situation de vulnérabilité).
- Expérience dans la mise en œuvre de démarches éthiques rigoureuses : consentement éclairé, confidentialité, principe « do no harm », sauvegarde et gestion des situations sensibles, y compris auprès de mineur·e·s et d’adolescent·e·s.
- Expérience dans le ou les pays d’intervention. Les équipes d’évaluation incluant des personnes résidant dans les pays ou régions du projet, ou associant des expert·e·s nationaux, sont appréciées.
- Expérience dans l’évaluation de projets financés par la DGD appréciée.

**Qualité et justification de la méthodologie**

- Proposition technique claire et adaptée basée sur la bonne compréhension des questions d’évaluation.
- Description générale et pertinence de la méthodologie.
- Présentation des outils proposés à chaque étape du processus d’évaluation.
- Calendrier de travail cohérent avec la méthodologie et les délais escomptés.
- Capacité démontrée de déployer les équipes d’évaluation dans les zones d’intervention, avec une composition d’équipe adaptée (genre, langues locales, connaissance du terrain).
- Présentation des outils proposés à chaque étape du processus d’évaluation, y compris les modalités de validation et de restitution aux parties prenantes.

**Autres atouts**

- Excellente maîtrise du français.
- La connaissance des langues locales est appréciée.
- Expérience de travail au sein ou avec une association internationale, en particulier dans le domaine de la Santé et de la Migration.
- Connaissance du contexte des pays d’intervention.

## Budget

Le budget devra inclure au minimum les éléments suivants :

- Les journées d’expertise des différents membres de l’équipe de consultance pour la réalisation de cette évaluation (Hébergement, frais de voyage, d’assurance et de séjour)
- Les frais occasionnés pour les déplacements (la logistique, l'hébergement, frais de voyage, d’assurance et de séjour) seront à la charge du consultant pour la phase terrain, et donc à prévoir dans le budget. L'équipe MdM-BE facilitera les démarches avec les autorités pour les mouvements sur le terrain au niveau de la commune d’Agadez.
- Les frais annexes nécessaires à la réalisation de l’évaluation et de sa restitution (reprographie,…)

**Le budget de cette consultance s’élève à maximum 32 500 euros pour les deux outcomes.**

title: Consultancy for a Feasibility Study to Inform a BMZ (PT) Project Proposal
body:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Consultancy for a Feasibility Study to Inform a BMZ (PT) Project Proposal**

**Contracting organization**

arche nova (AN)

## 1. Introduction

arche nova (AN) ([www.arche-nova.org](http://www.arche-nova.org)), a German non-governmental organization, has since 2012, been supporting vulnerable communities in Kenya to strengthen resilience to climate change, water scarcity, food insecurity, environmental degradation, and recurrent humanitarian shocks. Working at the humanitarian-development-climate nexus, arche nova combines emergency response, disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate adaptation, and sustainable development approaches to build long-term resilience and self-reliance. Together with our local partners working in Kibera; Human Needs Project (HNP) and Action for Social and Economic Progress (ASEP), we are preparing a project proposal for submission to the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The proposed intervention is envisaged for Kibera, Nairobi County, Kenya.

## 2. Background

The proposed project; “Strengthening urban resilience through a climate-smart, multifunctional satellite community hub in the Kibera slum, Nairobi, seeks to address interconnected water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), public-health, climate-resilience and community livelihood needs in Kibera. Objective: To strengthen urban resilience through WASH, income generation and social cohesion in the Kibera slum, Kenya. Target group: 20,000 people, including 55 per cent women, 35 per cent young people (18-25 years) and 10 per cent people with disability. The target groups are closely interconnected with overlapping co-benefits from the project hence a validation of the total beneficiaries reached by the project is necessary. The Junior Partner; HNP also directly benefit from the project through strengthened capacities from the senior partner ASEP.

The project components include construction of a climate-smart community hub for improved access to safe water and sanitation, livelihoods and social cohesion. Potential measures may include a solar-powered water supply, greywater treatment using nano-filtration for reuse e.g. for hydroponic farming, sanitation and bathing facilities, menstrual health and hygiene (MHM), and inclusive community engagement, a digital innovation training lab for green business, entrepreneurship, job placement, and conflict/legal advice. Building on HNP’s ‘Kibera Town Centre’, which successfully operates as a self-sustaining WASH, training and community centre. A senior-junior partnership model is being introduced: as an experienced stakeholder and AN partner, ASEP supports the smaller, locally-rooted organization HNP to facilitate better access to funding, technical support and innovation.

These are options for assessment and are not predetermined technical decisions. The project is structured around four results:

Result 1: Improved access to climate-resilient and inclusive WASH services for vulnerable residents in Kibera.

Result 2: Improved economic empowerment and green skills development for women and youth.

Result 3: Strengthened social cohesion and improved access to community justice services for underserved vulnerable community members.

Result 4: Strengthened institutional capacity and inclusive governance for sustainable service delivery.

A feasibility study is required to verify priority needs supporting the project idea to assess the suitability, affordability and sustainability of proposed measures as well as beneficiary, stakeholder and partner relationships and identify the key risks and recommend concrete adjustments to the project concept, the impact matrix and the planned measures. The study must be independent and sufficiently critical to recommend redesign, deferral or non-selection of any measure where evidence does not support it.

The study should consider applicable BMZ PT requirements and relevant OECD/DAC criteria: relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability. Cross-cutting considerations include gender equality, disability inclusion, human rights, environmental and climate safeguards, conflict sensitivity, accountability and Do No Harm.

## 3. Purpose and Scope of the Assignment

The purpose of the assignment is to provide AN and its partners with an independent, participatory and evidence-based basis for deciding on the proposed intervention and preparing a coherent, technically sound, costed and sustainable BMZ PT project proposal.

The feasibility study will:

- Validate priority needs, vulnerabilities, capacities and intended target groups in the proposed project area.
- Assess the technical, social, institutional, environmental, regulatory, operational and financial feasibility of proposed measures and compare viable alternatives.
- Analyze target groups and stakeholders, including their relationships, interests, influence, roles, coordination and potential risks of exclusion or conflict.
- Identify prerequisites, including land tenure and site access, asset ownership, water availability and rights, permits, environmental and social assessments, technical investigations, utility connections, and operation and maintenance arrangements.
- Recommend intervention logic, target groups, objectives, outputs, indicators, means of verification, assumptions and risks for the logical framework matrix; establish baseline values where feasible and propose evidence-based targets.
- Recommend sustainability, exit or transition, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) arrangements.

## 4. Methodology

The study should combine qualitative and quantitative methods and follow a participatory approach that reflects the needs and perspectives of intended beneficiaries and relevant stakeholders. The consultant shall propose a rigorous but proportionate methodology in the inception report, triangulating secondary evidence with field-based verification.

- The sampling approach must be justified, including selection of locations, respondent groups and sample size. A census or large-scale survey should not be assumed necessary unless justified by the study questions, available time and budget.
- Recent and relevant secondary data should be used wherever suitable. Sources, dates, geographic coverage and limitations must be stated; primary data collection should fill material evidence gaps rather than duplicate existing assessments.
- Data collection methods may include desk review, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, community consultations, site observations, structured facility assessments, quantitative data collection where justified, stakeholder and service mapping, risk analysis and preliminary costing.
- For every proposed outcome- and output-level indicator in the draft logical framework, assess measurability, data sources, disaggregation and feasibility of collection; establish a baseline value where evidence permits and recommend a realistic target.
- Assess the concept against the OECD/DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, explaining how each informs the feasibility judgement and recommendations.
- Data-collection tools must be shared with AN and partners for comment before fieldwork. Participation must be voluntary and informed. Personal data must be minimized, securely handled and reported in aggregated or anonymized form wherever possible.
- Validation with AN and partners should improve factual accuracy and usability but must not compromise the consultant’s independent judgement.

## 5. Tasks and Deliverables

### 5.1 Tasks

The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks. The detailed methodology and sequencing will be agreed during inception.

#### Context and Initial Situation Analysis

- Review the concept note, available WASH and public-health data, relevant research, local plans and applicable national and county policies.
- Analyze Kibera’s socio-economic, public-health, environmental, climate, institutional and governance context relevant to the proposed intervention.
- Map existing and planned WASH, sanitation, MHM, livelihood and climate-resilience actors and interventions and identify synergies, referral pathways and duplication risks. Assess whether the established St. Juliet is complemented by the community service hub and or establish existing gaps.
- Verify the nature, scale and location of priority needs and identify population groups facing the greatest barriers or risks.
- Identify evidence gaps, stakeholder perceptions and assumptions requiring further investigation and prepare an evidence matrix.

1. **Stakeholder and Partner Analysis**

- Identify and engage key stakeholders, including young women, young men, parents, community and religious leaders, county and national government actors, and other civil society organisations.
- Assess the Partners regarding their roles, resources and competencies for
- project implementation.
- Evaluate the formal agreements and ownership structures between AN, ASEP, HNP
- Identify and analyse any gaps in collaboration and coordination.
- Identify synergies and confirm whether all official preconditions and authorizations for project implementation are in place

#### Needs, Target Groups and Beneficiary Analysis

- Consult residents and intended beneficiaries, including women and girls, youth, persons with disabilities, older people and other potentially marginalized groups, using safe and accessible methods.
- Suggest a beneficiary selection criterion, expected reach, affordability, barriers to access, protection concerns, participation and possible unintended consequences.
    
    **Skills Training, Employment and Income-Generation Feasibility**
- Assess the gaps and needs among intended beneficiaries for the proposed skills training, including priority skills, participation barriers, existing competencies and the extent to which the proposed training responds to local needs and market demand.
- Analyse realistic employment, self-employment and income-generation opportunities linked to the proposed skills areas, including local labour-market conditions, viable value chains, market access, competition, start-up requirements. Technical and Operational Feasibility
- Assess proposed boreholes, toilets, showers and related facilities site suitability, accessibility, privacy, safety, gender responsiveness, MHM needs, cleaning, wastewater containment and disposal, desludging, drainage and recurrent costs.
- Assess whether proposed user fees are affordable and acceptable to intended beneficiaries and determine if the expected income can adequately cover recurrent operational and maintenance costs. Environmental, Social, Regulatory and Safeguarding Analysis
- Identify risks and mitigation needs related to groundwater abstraction, wastewater, sludge, solid waste, drainage, construction, energy use and treatment residuals.
- Identify the required environmental assessment and approval pathway, permits, land-access documentation, water-resource approvals and other statutory requirements; verify status where evidence is available.
- Assess gender, disability inclusion, child and adult safeguarding, protection, community safety, affordability and equitable access.
- Identify risks of exclusion, tension, elite capture, unequal benefits, displacement or disruption of existing services, and recommend practical mitigation measures.
- Recommend proportionate community consultation, complaints and feedback mechanisms, and ethical data-protection practices.

#### Project Concept Evaluation, Design and Recommendations

- Test the theory of change and causal links between needs, activities, outputs, outcomes and intended longer-term effects.
- Assess the coherence and manageability of combining WASH, livelihoods, access to justice and institutional strengthening in one hub, and recommend whether any component should be scaled down, phased or dropped.
- Map and assess the potential legal services gaps of intended beneficiaries,availability of qualified and legally authorized legal aid providers, community justice organizations, paralegals and relevant referral services operating in Kibera.
- Review and refine the draft logical framework, including indicators, potential baselines, proposed targets where evidence permits, sources of verification, assumptions and risks.
- Recommend MEAL responsibilities, data-collection frequency, disaggregation, community feedback and learning reviews.

### 5.2 Deliverables

The consultant shall submit the following deliverables in English. Due dates will be finalized at contracting and aligned with AN’s BMZ PT proposal-development schedule.

**Inception report:** Desk-review summary and evidence gaps; refined questions; justified sampling and respondent-selection approach; stakeholder plan; fieldwork locations and schedule; ethics, safeguarding and data-management arrangements; limitations; draft tools.

**Preliminary findings briefing**: Emerging findings, evidence gaps, options, key risks and decisions requiring partner input.

**Draft feasibility study**: Context and problem analysis; needs and target groups; stakeholder and partner analysis; options appraisal; technical and operational feasibility; safeguards; OECD/DAC assessment; risks and sustainability; indicator-by-indicator review with baseline values where feasible and proposed targets.

**Project-design annexes:** Draft logical framework matrix; intervention logic/theory of change; indicators and baseline information; implementation timetable; risk register; indicative activity-based budget

**Validation and final report:** Validation session with AN and partners; final report incorporating comments; stakeholder contact list, bibliography/source list and curated, captioned photographs where appropriate and consented.

- The final report should not exceed 30 pages excluding annexes and should open with an executive summary of no more than 3 pages.
- The report must give a clear, evidence-based recommendation for each proposed measure (proceed, proceed with modifications, defer or do not proceed), with the reasons and conditions attached.
- All reports and annexes must be submitted in PDF and editable formats (MS Word and Excel) and cleaned; anonymized datasets and data-collection tools shall be submitted as annexes

## 6. Supporting Documents

AN and its partners will provide relevant available documents to support the assignment, which may include:

- The latest project concept notes, draft proposal narrative, draft logical framework/results matrix and draft budget.
- Available site information, maps and previous project report relevant to Kibera and the proposed intervention.
- Relevant BMZ PT feasibility-study guidance, templates and proposal requirements.

## 7. Skills and Experience- consultant profile

AN invites application from Kenya-based independent consultants, teams of consultants or consulting firms. Where a multidisciplinary team is proposed, one team member must act as team leader and take responsibility for the quality and timely delivery of all outputs. The team should collectively demonstrate:

- Postgraduate qualification in development studies, social sciences, public health, engineering, environmental studies, economics or another relevant field.
- Demonstrated experience conducting feasibility studies, assessments or project design for development programmes in Kenya, preferably in urban informal settlements or similarly complex settings
- Experience developing institutional-donor proposals, logical frameworks, results chains, implementation plans and activity-based budgets.
- Relevant WASH and public-health expertise. Specialist engineering or water-resource conclusions must be reviewed by appropriately qualified professionals.
- Experience with participatory and mixed-methods research, stakeholder analysis and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
- Competence in gender equality, disability inclusion, safeguarding, environmental and social risk assessment, conflict sensitivity, social cohesion and accountability.
- Strong analytical, facilitation and report-writing skills; excellent written and spoken English; willingness to conduct fieldwork in Kibera.

## 8. Work Plan and Submission

The assignment is expected to be delivered within 21 consultant working days, completed within a period agreed with AN and aligned to the proposal-development schedule. The consultant should propose a realistic allocation of days. The following distribution is indicative:

- Inception and desk review: 2–3 days.
- Fieldwork and stakeholder consultations: 5–7 days.
- Analysis and options appraisal: 4–5 days.
- Draft report and design annexes: 3–4 days.
- Validation, revisions and finalization: 2–3 days.

Fieldwork dates and submission deadlines will be agreed during inception. AN’s review periods and partner feedback must be built into the detailed workplan. Deliverables are complete only after review and acceptance by AN.

## 9. Management, Coordination, Ethics and Data Management

- The consultant reports to the designated AN focal point, who coordinates comments and confirms acceptance of deliverables.
- AN and partners will provide available project documents, facilitate introductions to stakeholders and support agreed field logistics.
- The consultant is responsible for the quality and independence of the analysis, tools, fieldwork, analysis and timely delivery. Changes to scope, fieldwork, deliverables or timeline require written agreement by AN before additional work is undertaken.
- Obtain informed consent before interviews, discussions, photographs or collection of personal information; participation must be voluntary. Use safe, accessible and culturally appropriate methods and avoid creating expectations about project approval or benefits.
- Apply safeguarding and Do No Harm principles, including appropriate protections when engaging children or other groups requiring additional safeguards.
- Protect confidentiality and securely store notes, recordings and datasets in line with the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019, and applicable research-ethics requirements. The consultant must identify any research licence, ethical clearance or other authorization required and include the time and cost in the workplan and financial proposal.
- All reports, tools, datasets, photographs commissioned under the assignment and project-design annexes shall be provided to AN and handled in accordance with the consultancy contract. The consultant may not publish confidential project information or identifiable participant data without prior written authorization. Third-party sources must be acknowledged.

## 10. Application Requirements

Applications are invited from Kenya-based individual consultants, teams of consultants or consulting firms, in line with Section 7. Applications must include:

- **Cover letter** (max. 2 pages) explaining interest and suitability for the assignment, and confirming availability for the proposed period.
- **Technical proposal** (max. 10 pages) setting out understanding of the assignment and the Kibera context; proposed methodology, sampling and options-appraisal approach; work plan with allocation of days per team member and per phase; team composition and roles; quality-assurance arrangements; and ethics, safeguarding and data-protection arrangements.
- **CVs** of all proposed team members (max. 2 pages each), including at least two references from recent, similar assignments.
- **Financial proposal** in Kenya Shillings (KES), with professional fees shown as daily rate × number of days for each team member, and separate lines for field costs (e.g. enumerators, transport, venues, consultation costs), research licence or ethical-clearance costs, and applicable taxes.
- **One sample** of a feasibility study, assessment or project-design report recently completed by the lead consultant or team (or a link to it).
- **Compliance documents:** copy of KRA PIN and valid tax compliance certificate; for firms, certificate of registration or incorporation.
- **Signed declaration** of no conflict of interest.

title: Reserve Director
body:
**About WCS**

Founded in 1895, the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a U.S.-based, tax-exempt nonprofit dedicated to saving wildlife and wild places through science and conservation action. Working in more than 60 countries, WCS has supported the establishment of over 150 protected areas, combining biological expertise, local knowledge, and long-term partnerships to conserve species, habitats, and ecosystems while supporting communities whose livelihoods depend on natural resources. Our mission is to save wildlife and wild places through science, conservation action, education, and inspiring people to value nature. Our vision is thriving wildlife in healthy lands and seas, valued by societies that embrace and benefit from life’s diversity and integrity. Our goal is to conserve the world’s largest wild places across 16 priority regions containing more than 50% of global biodiversity. Our values are Respect, Accountability and Transparency, Innovation, Diversity and Inclusion, Collaboration, and Integrity.

Since 2001, WCS has worked in Nigeria to protect threatened species, including Cross River gorillas and savannah and forest elephants, while supporting local livelihoods, conservation awareness, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. In Cross River State, WCS supports Cross River National Park, Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary, and the Mbe Mountains Community Forest; in Bauchi State, it provides technical expertise for the conservation and management of Yankari Game Reserve.

At Yankari Game Reserve, WCS supports ranger patrols and wildlife monitoring to strengthen the protection of wildlife and habitats. Through its community-based Elephant Guardian network, WCS also supports elephant monitoring, early warning, and conflict mitigation to help communities respond to human-elephant conflict. Building on this work, WCS plans to deepen its collaboration with the Bauchi State Government through a strengthened collaborative management partnership aimed at improving governance, conservation management, community participation, and sustainable financing for the Reserve.

The WCS Nigeria Program is seeking a Reserve Director for the Yankari Landscape.

**Job Summary**

The Reserve Director provides overall leadership and management of Yankari Game Reserve and the wider Yankari Landscape, leading protected area and wildlife and habitat management, community engagement, and institutional strengthening initiatives to ensure the long-term ecological and financial sustainability of the Reserve

The position reports to the WCS Nigeria Country Director and is accountable to the Yankari Game Reserve Steering Committee. The Director oversees all aspects of Reserve operations, leads multidisciplinary teams, and ensures delivery of agreed conservation and organisational objectives, including the landscape strategy.

As WCS's senior representative in Yankari, the Director serves as the principal liaison with government, communities, donors, conservation partners, and other stakeholders, fostering collaborative management, strategic partnerships, resource mobilisation, and stakeholder engagement in support of the Reserve's conservation and development goals.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Leadership, Management and Operations**

- Lead Yankari Game Reserve and the wider Yankari Landscape to deliver conservation and community engagement objectives.
- Lead implementation of the Reserve Management Plan and annual work plans, aligning budgets, performance targets, and operational priorities.
- Supervise and coordinate multidisciplinary teams in conservation law enforcement, wildlife management and monitoring, community conservation and safeguards, tourism, administration, and finance; foster accountability, staff development, and high organisational performance.
- Oversee financial, administrative, and operational systems to ensure compliance, efficiency, and effective resource use.

**Conservation, Protection and Community Engagement**

- Oversee wildlife protection, habitat management, biodiversity monitoring, and research to support evidence-based conservation and adaptive management.
- Work with the Conservation Law Enforcement Advisor and Wildlife Management Coordinator to strengthen law enforcement, improve the use of SMART, EarthRanger, and other management tools, and address poaching, encroachment, insecurity, and other threats.
- Support the Community Conservation Coordinator to strengthen community relations, advance participatory governance and collaborative management structures, reduce human-wildlife conflict, and promote conservation-linked livelihood and resilience initiatives.
- Partnerships and Reporting
- Represent WCS and Yankari Game Reserve with government agencies, donors, local communities, traditional institutions, conservation partners, and other stakeholders.
- Support fundraising, donor relations, proposal development, and strategic partnerships to strengthen the Reserve’s long-term sustainability.
- Monitor progress against conservation and operational targets and ensure timely, high-quality reports, proposals, and communications for WCS, donors, government partners, and the Steering Committee.
- Contribute to the WCS CWT strategy and the WCS Africa CWT strategy.

**Job Qualifications:**

- Master's degree or equivalent experience in conservation biology, ecology, environmental management, natural resource governance, protected area management, or a related field.
- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in conservation programs or protected area management, including leadership of complex, multi-component programs.
- Demonstrated experience in protected area management, conservation law enforcement coordination, biodiversity monitoring, and community engagement.
- Strong understanding of governance systems, collaborative management approaches, and stakeholder coordination in Nigeria or similar contexts.
- Proven track record of leading multidisciplinary teams and building effective institutional partnerships.
- Excellent leadership, team management, mentoring, and interpersonal skills.
- Strong strategic planning, organisational management, and problem-solving abilities.
- Effective communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Demonstrated ability to manage complex partnerships and multi-stakeholder processes.

**Additional Requirements:**

- Proficiency in conservation management and monitoring tools, including SMART, EarthRanger, GIS, KoboToolbox, and related platforms.
- Strong analytical skills and ability to apply data and evidence to management decisions.
- Ability to work effectively in challenging field environments with resilience, adaptability, and sound judgement.
- Fluency in English; working knowledge of Hausa is highly desirable.
- Willingness to be based in Yankari Game Reserve with travel throughout the Yankari Landscape and nationally.
- Demonstrated commitment to biodiversity conservation and community-based conservation approaches.
- Ability to represent WCS effectively with government agencies, traditional institutions, donors, partners, and local communities.

**Why Join Us?**

- Leverage WSC’s conservation, protection, and law enforcement expertise to strategically guide the WSC's protection of wild places and wild species.
- Exceptional opportunity to make significant contributions to the protection of biodiversity conservation.
- Dynamic Team: Join a dynamic team and work in a collaborative and conducive environment where your ideas and everyone's input are valued.
- Growth Opportunities: We believe in providing an enabling environment to develop your career. We are committed to developing your skills and competencies and offer opportunities for career advancement.
- Supportive Environment: Work with a team that values respect, teamwork, and excellence

title: Emergency Food Security and Nutrition Advisor
body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 1 year. There are very good prospects for an extension. Employment location will be Amman, Jordan (JO).

WHH has recently established its office in Jordan (Amman Hub), with the aim of managing its country programs in OPT, Jordan, Yemen and Iraq. As a member of the Amman Hub, your duty will be to provide hands on support for the emergency nutrition and Food security components of these country programs with your high level technical expertise.

You will work closely with other Hub members to strengthen the quality and consistency of nutrition and food security programming across the region, ensuring high technical standards, particularly in emergency settings and you will ensure that WHH is well recognized as an emergency nutrition and food security actor in these countries.

## Your responsibilities

- Support WHH country programs and partners in developing and implementing emergency nutrition and food security strategies, aligned with regional and global priorities and a food systems approach.
- Conduct regular field visits and facilitate workshops to provide hands-on technical advice and strengthen program quality.
- Provide technical guidance on emergency nutrition interventions (including CMAM and IYCF-E) and food security responses, including in-kind assistance and cash and voucher assistance (CVA).
- Support needs assessments, nutrition and food security service mapping, and context-specific interventions linking emergency response with early recovery and long-term resilience.
- Collaborate with WHH's global technical teams and MEAL colleagues to develop guidance, training materials, indicators, and evidence-based monitoring approaches.
- Support the design, implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance of nutrition and food security projects, including proposal reviews and recommendations for improvement.
- Develop innovative program concepts, contribute to funding proposals, and support engagement with institutional and private donors.
- Represent WHH in relevant national and regional clusters, technical networks, and working groups, ensuring alignment with inter-agency standards and priorities.
- Build strategic partnerships with research institutions and peer organizations, and promote knowledge sharing, learning, and collaboration across country programs.
- Support the expansion of emergency nutrition and food security interventions, communicate technical priorities, and regularly report progress to program management and the Head Office Sector Unit.

## Your profile

- Professional / formal qualification and degree in food security, nutrition, health or related field
- At least 5 years of humanitarian and development sector experience of which at least 3 years of must be at a technical advisor level in an INGO,
- At least 2 years of experience in working in programs related to treatment of acute malnutrition,
- For international candidates, experience in MENA region is a must
    
    For national candidates, previous international experience in similar roles beyond Jordan is a must
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office
- Excellent inter-personal, communication, advisory and facilitation skills
- Experience in working in hard-to-reach areas and emergency set-ups would be an asset
- Willingness and ability to travel to OPT (West Bank and Gaza), Yemen, Iraq and possibly Syria and Lebanon (candidates who are barred from entering to any of the countries/regions might not be shortlisted)
- You recognize the growing value of data within an organization and inspire teams to make decisions grounded in analysis and evidence
- Excellent spoken and written English is required, knowledge of Arabic would be an asset

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Commitment to Well-Being: We attach great importance to our duty of care with a focus on safety, security & health.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which you can find under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-expatriate-employees).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

title: Call Centre Operator (Monitoring & Data Collection)
body:
Overview of position

Under the direct supervision of the Call Centre Supervisor / Project Manager, and in coordination with WFP Monitoring and VAM teams, Call Centre Operators will undertake the following duties and responsibilities as listed in this TOR.

Role objectives

- Accurately record responses in real time using WFP-approved digital data collection platforms (e.g. MoDA, KOBO, ODK), ensuring completeness and consistency of data.
- Apply appropriate probing techniques and clarification methods while maintaining neutrality and avoiding bias.
- Identify and flag anomalies, inconsistencies, or potential risks (e.g., assistance issues, protection concerns, fraud/diversion signals) during interviews and report them through established escalation channels.
- Ensure correct classification of call outcomes (e.g. completed, refusal, no answer, callback) and maintain accurate disposition codes.
- Administer structured questionnaires through phone-based interviews (CATI), SMS, or hybrid modalities, ensuring alignment with WFP standardised survey tools and methodologies (applicable across RPM, TPM, and WFP field monitoring systems).
- Prior to survey implementation, review questionnaires, call scripts, training materials, and relevant programme documentation to ensure full understanding of objectives and context.
- Ensure efficient use of resources (call time, systems, devices) and adherence to operational plans.
- Demonstrate professional conduct at all times, treating respondents with respect, dignity, and cultural sensitivity.
- Maintain daily tracking of performance indicators, including number of calls completed, response rates, and adherence to quotas.
- Undertake any other related tasks as required for monitoring, data collection, or survey implementation.

Conduct remote data collection activities in alignment with WFP monitoring requirements. This includes, but is not limited to:

- Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM)
- Distribution Monitoring (DM)
- Market Monitoring / Price Surveys
- Outcome monitoring (food security, satisfaction, protection)
- Beneficiary feedback and accountability surveys
- Qualitative data collection (where applicable)

Ensure strict adherence to WFP-approved call scripts, including:

- Privacy notice and informed consent procedures
- Ethical engagement with respondents
- Proper handling of sensitive questions (e.g., protection, complaints)

Participate in quality assurance processes, including:

- Call monitoring and review sessions
- Verification of data against call recordings (where applicable)
- Implementation of feedback and corrective actions

Contribute to regular reporting by documenting:

- Operational challenges (e.g., low response rates, language barriers)
- Recommendations to improve data collection processes

Ensure full compliance with WFP data protection and confidentiality requirements, including:

- Secure handling of personal data
- Non-retention of data outside authorised systems
- Adherence to data access protocols and timelines

Support multi-modal monitoring integration by ensuring compatibility of collected data with:

- Remote monitoring systems (RPM)
- Third-party monitoring (TPM)
- WFP field monitoring datasets

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

- Bachelor’s degree in statistics, economics, social sciences, development studies, public health, or a related field.
- Minimum 3–5 years of experience in data collection, call centre operations, or monitoring activities in humanitarian or development contexts.
- Experience supporting remote data collection (phone-based surveys) and/or digital data collection for field monitoring.
- Familiarity with multi-modal monitoring approaches (RPM, TPM, and field monitoring) is highly desirable.
- Strong communication and interviewing skills, with the ability to engage respondents effectively over the phone.
- Good understanding of monitoring and evaluation principles, including quantitative and qualitative data collection.
- Familiarity with WFP monitoring tools and standardised questionnaires is an asset.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to ensure data accuracy and quality.
- Experience in using digital data collection platforms (e.g. MoDA, KOBO, ODK, SurveyCTO).
- Ability to follow structured scripts while adapting to respondent needs and context.
- Awareness of protection, gender, and accountability to affected populations (AAP) principles.
- Understanding data protection and confidentiality standards in humanitarian contexts.
- Ability to identify and escalate risks or sensitive issues appropriately.
- Strong organizational skills and ability to meet daily targets and deadlines.
- Proficiency in relevant local languages and good command of English (written and spoken).
- Experience in call centre environments supporting humanitarian or food security data collection.
- Familiarity with call monitoring systems, dashboards, and performance tracking tools.
- Experience contributing to data quality assurance processes (call recordings, validation checks).
- Ability to operate in complex and high-risk environments with sensitivity to context.

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

title: Agriculture Field Engineer
source: Amal Organization for Relief and Development
body:
**Job title:** Agriculture Field Engineer

**Location:** Syria, Aleppo,Afrin

**Contract :** 10 months | Full-time (100%)

**Reports to:** Project Manager

Project Manager

**Project component:** Food Security and Agriculture (FSAL) – Agricultural Livelihoods and Cash-for-Work

**About AMAL Organization For Relief& Development**

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established and registered in Turkey on 6/6/2014, to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war turned

**Purpose of the Position**

Support field implementation of AMAL’s FSAL activities in Afrin through technical assessments, tailored agricultural and agri-food support, farmer training and follow-up, and supervision of agricultural Cash-for-Work assignments. Ensure accurate technical verification, safe implementation, field documentation and coordination with MEAL and project teams.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Conduct farm and household technical assessments, including crop/orchard conditions, land access, irrigation and water sources, existing assets, seasonal needs, and suitability for proposed support.
- Support transparent beneficiary verification and profiling for households
- Help tailor package contents to verified needs; develop technical specifications and BoQs, verify quality and quantities, and support receiving and distribution in coordination with logistics and procurement teams.
- Provide practical guidance and field follow-up on pruning, soil fertility, irrigation efficiency, crop management, integrated pest management, intercropping and safe input use; support appropriate food-processing technical follow-up.
- Support the organization of agricultural training for supported households and document application of promoted practices through structured field visits.
- Identify and assess agricultural Cash-for-Work sites and tasks, define appropriate work norms, supervise seasonal works and certify quality and completion for activities
- Ensure attendance and technical work-completion records are accurate and shared with the responsible project and finance teams for payment verification; do not independently authorize payments.
- Check land access and site suitability, report HLP or explosive ordnance concerns, and suspend or relocate unsafe assignments through approved procedures and competent actors.
- Collect and maintain reliable field data, distribution verification and monitoring records; coordinate with MEAL on baseline, PDM, spot checks and endline verification.
- Promote inclusion, occupational health and safety, Code of Conduct, PSEA, confidentiality and accessible complaints/referral pathways in all field interactions.
- Prepare weekly/monthly field progress reports; flag delays, technical problems, beneficiary feedback and corrective-action needs to the Project Manager.

**Required Qualifications**

- University degree in Agricultural Engineering (horticulture, crop production, irrigation or a related field).
- Practical experience in agricultural field projects, farmer technical assistance, irrigation systems and/or agricultural livelihood recovery.
- Knowledge of climate-smart agriculture, integrated pest management and safe agricultural input use.
- Ability to supervise field works, verify technical specifications, prepare basic BoQs and maintain accurate records.
- Strong communication and reporting skills; proficiency in Excel and Word. NGO and Cash-for-Work experience is an advantage.
- Ability to travel regularly to farms and implementation locations in Afrin and work with diverse community groups.

**Core Skills & Language**

Technical judgment, field coordination, impartiality, teamwork, problem-solving, attention to safety and data confidentiality. Arabic required; English preferred.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND NON-DISCRIMINATION:**

Amal is dedicated to promoting equal opportunities in our recruitment practices so maintaining equal opportunities and non-discrimination is a foundational principle:

Discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, age, disability, social status, origin, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, or any other grounds is strictly prohibited across all aspects of employment, organizational practices, work arrangements, salary, dismissal, and service provision.

Preference among employees or candidates for employment may be granted based on objective criteria and qualifications essential for the job, and such preferences do not constitute discrimination.

In instances where specific provisions apply to contracting concerning gender, qualifications, working conditions, or contract type (daily, weekly, seasonal), rights and responsibilities remain equitable

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. Amal Organization unequivocally prohibits and will not tolerate (zero tolerate) any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (whether sexual or otherwise), based on race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. Employees and associated personnel must strictly refrain from engaging in any discriminatory, harassing, or abusive behavior, whether physical, sexual, verbal, or otherwise, both within and outside the Amal organization.

**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**

Amal Organization recognizes that ensuring a secure environment for children begins with the recruitment of qualified employees equipped with the necessary competencies and skills to perform their duties effectively, safely, and reliably. This commitment is geared towards safeguarding children from all forms of exploitation, labor, or potential harm.

In our dedication to children's safety, our selection process incorporates comprehensive background checks, underscoring our unwavering commitment to preventing abuse and ensuring the well-being of children.

**SAFEGUARDING EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:**

In line with our commitment to fostering a secure and respectful work environment, the post holder is required to adhere to Amal's anti-harassment policy.
