title: Country Director Pakistan - Islamabad, Pakistan
body:
***Location: Islamabad, Pakistan***  
***Position Status Full-time,***

***THIS POSITION IS OPEN TO PAKISTAN NATIONALS ONLY.***

***closing date: Please apply by November 30th.***

**Risk Level:** X Level 3 ☐ Level 2 ☐ Level 1

Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned, non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data.

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [**here**](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption.

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible.  
In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions  
into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.  
Now, and for the future.

## **Program / Department Summary**

Mercy Corps has been present in Pakistan since 1986, focusing its interventions on Public Health, (Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health, Tuberculosis Control), Economic Opportunities, Water Security, Food Security and Disaster Relief and Recovery. Currently, with funding from Global Fund and the Gates Foundation, Mercy Corps has been able to work together with communities to improve health services, create economic opportunities and build resilience. Our team is comprised of a hundred percent Pakistan nationals (475 team members). We work hand in hand with the Pakistan Government and in partnership with national and international stakeholders present in our sectors of work. Mercy Corps Pakistan implements its programs in 120 districts of the country through offices in Islamabad, Quetta, Lahore, and Hyderabad.

## **General Position Summary**

The Country Director (CD) is an innovative and visionary leader responsible for resourcefully managing all programming in Pakistan, resulting in lasting improvement in the lives of our team members and program participants. S/He helps formulate the strategic direction for the country program in line with the local context and Mercy Corps’ 10-year Pathway to Possibility. The CD has supervisory responsibility for the country team and provides overall guidance and management of a portfolio of health, education, protection, livelihoods, and emergency response programs with an average yearly budget of USD 15 million. S/he is also responsible for the implementation of all security protocols. The CD develops sustainable, multi-sector programming and is accountable to beneficiaries and donors, placing a high value on innovative solutions to development issues and creative partnerships in tough environments. The CD provides overall team management, capacity building, mentoring to a large team spread across Pakistan, and ensures adherence to Mercy Corps policies and procedures including Mercy Corps’ code of ethics.

## **Essential Job Responsibilities**

### **Strategy & Vision**

- In the evolving context, with a participatory approach, formulate and communicate a clear vision to team members and stakeholders that translates into concrete programs and plans.
- Lead the annual country strategy planning and update process. Ensure the alignment of the country strategy to Mercy Corps’ Pathway to Possibility.
- Set direction by prioritizing and organizing actions and resources to achieve program and agency objectives.
- Use technical support teams collaboratively as well as external consultants that could support our business development and/or quality program implementation efforts.
- Share Mercy Corps Pakistan successes and technical approaches with other Mercy Corps teams in the region and/or globally. Promote cross collaboration and learning.
- Explore and present funding opportunities that integrate initiatives and leverage impact for the communities; support and direct fund-raising activities with institutional and private donors.
- Ensure networking with key donors as well as government stakeholders to grow Mercy Corps Pakistan’s programs in areas such as food security, economic opportunity, water security. The CD will especially explore and build climate change resilience and DRR programming.

### **Influence & Representation**

- Proactively represent Mercy Corps with all levels of government, as well as donor, partners, local and international stakeholders, and the communities we serve.
- Ensure compliance to the MoU/registration signed with the Ministry of Interior of Pakistan
- Work with the team especially the Security and Government Liaison manager to ensure timely approvals, No Objection Certificates for program implementation
- Develop and nurture relationships with relevant government departments for timely implementation of planned interventions
- Represent Mercy Corps programs with national and international media and participate in community activities as appropriate.
- Maintain productive relationships with internal and external constituents such as private partners, local governments, foundations, the private sector, etc.
- Develop and foster partnerships that add value to our programming strengths and position us to be competitive for large funding opportunities.
- Anticipate needs, understand donor pool and contribute to shaping donor’s views on development.
- Demonstrate flexibility, resilience and ability to maintain positive relationships and composure.
- Maintain high ethical standards and treat people with respect and dignity.
- Exhibit awareness of his/her own strengths and development needs.

### **Team Management**

- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence and understand and live Mercy Corps organizational culture and values.
- Oversee and lead training and learning processes (including People with Possibility) where team members internalize and behave according to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct, Safeguarding and all our Ethics Policies.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations and provide constructive feedback informally and formally via regular one on ones and performance reviews
- Develop the capacity of the team, deepen understanding of their roles and assist with career development.
- Assist team members with information, tools and resources to improve performance & reach objectives.
- Hire, orient and lead team members as necessary.
- Facilitate meetings and processes where team members feel empowered and equipped to take actions towards achieving our programs’ and agency goals.
- Facilitate and lead regular staff meetings and ad-com meetings. Follow up with required actions as needed.

### **Program Operations Management**

- Oversee program quality and impact by ensuring programs are based on sound design principles and utilize Mercy Corps and donor required M&E systems.
- Ensure effective, transparent use of resources in compliance with Mercy Corps and donor policies/procedures.
- Oversee budget management of sub-grantees/sub-contractors
- Build and maintain operational systems that ensure proper administrative support for programs, as well as segregation of duties between finance and operations.
- Fulfill Mercy Corps’ Program Management Minimum Standards based on the organization-wide guide.
- Ensure all interventions adhere to Mercy Corps’ Gender Policy, Do No Harm principles, and beneficiary accountability standards.

### **Finance & Compliance Management**

- Ensure compliance with donor and Mercy Corps regulations related to emergency programming.
- Draft and/or review scope of work to hire and manage any technical consultants, including review for technical efficacy and contract budget.
- Build and maintain operational structures that ensure proper segregation of duties between finance, administration and logistics and fully support field programs.

### **SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work
- Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

### **Security**

- Liaise with the Regional and Global security team and Regional Director on crucial events, high-risk periods, incident reporting and security policy changes.

## **Accountability**

## **Supervisory Responsibility: Director of Programs, Senior Finance Manager, Senior Program Manager, HR Manager, Manager Security and Govt. Liaison, Operations Manager, Ethics and Internal Control Manager, Team Leader Quetta, Business Development Manager**

**Reports Directly To:** Regional Director

**Works Directly With:** Deputy Regional Directors, Asia Desk teams and other teams at Headquarters as needed.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects

## **Knowledge and Experience**

- MA/S or equivalent in relevant field required.
- 7-10 years of field experience in international relief and development programs, including demonstrable success in managing large and complex development programs.
- 5 years of senior-level leadership, capacity building and field management experience.
- Previous experience as a country director for large country offices
- Demonstrated success working effectively and respectfully with host country government, private sector, INGO, NGO partners, UN and other stakeholders in complex environments.
- Internationally recognized qualification in project or program management or a commitment to obtain the qualification in the early months of work.
- Demonstrated experience in effectively managing large teams in complex operating environment
- Proven skills in financial and grants management; prior experience with USAID, USDS, Global Fund, FCDO, EC, UN, private donors, BHA, ECHO
- Experience and expertise in climate change, resilience, and disaster preparedness and disaster risk reduction will be preferred
- Successful and proven negotiation, communication and organization skills.
- Proven capacity to analyze the political and social context in which our organization operates to make informed decisions.
- Excellent oral and written English skills required; proficiency in Urdu and other local languages is a plus.
- Ability to work effectively with an ethnically diverse team in a sensitive environment.
- Previous work experience in Pakistan required, experience in the region and in insecure environments is preferred.
- Capacity to respond to emergency and disaster response as appropriate.
- Knowledge of Sphere standards and other training in emergency response preferred.

## **Success Factors**

The successful Pakistan CD will be a gracious, personable leader who has an energizing effect on our team, partners and communities. A politically savvy, balanced, and astute individual who has the persona to successfully convene and partner with relevant stakeholders in the ever shifting and complex ecosystem in Pakistan. Calm and emotionally intelligent, personifying grace under fire, especially in leading our team through the management of urgent, security and emergency situations. S/he will have the vision to see possibilities for positive change where others see deprivation; and be able to lead the design and implementation of bold solutions. S/he will skillfully acquire support of donors and regional partners for meeting the priorities of our communities while providing effective leadership. S/he will have high emotional intelligence, constructive mentoring skills and proven experience with capacity building and will be committed to long-term program sustainability and the delivery of high-impact activities at the community level. Successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and challenging environments, and make effective written and verbal communication a priority.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The CD is based in Islamabad. This position requires approximately 15%-20% of time of travel by terrestrial or aerial means of transportation to field offices that present stable, moderate and high levels of operational risks.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/STA to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC's policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Fostering a diverse and open workplace is an important part of Mercy Corps’ vision. Mercy Corps is an Equal Opportunity Employer regardless of background. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

We are committed to providing an environment of respect and psychological safety where equal employment opportunities are available to all. We do not engage in or tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, disability (including HIV/AIDS status), marital status, military veteran status or any other protected group in the locations where we work.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and participate in the[ Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct e-learning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

title: Evaluation of the awareness campaign
body:
## GENERAL INFORMATION

FRC Project Code and Project Title : Ready 360 Phase 2 – PF 272  
Activity Title : Implementation of the regional awareness campaign on risks and climate change  
Location of the Activity: N/A  
Activity Managers (Name and Position) : Julie Oddon, Regional Project Operational Quality Officer  
Planned Period / Scheduled Dates: March - April 2027  
Points of contact (Name and Title) : Sandrine Désiré, Head of Regional Projects

Emmeline Da Silva, Communications Manager

## CONTEXT AND OVERVIEW OF THE ACTIVITY

**PIRAC**  
Established in 2005, the Regional Intervention Platform for the Americas and the Caribbean (PIRAC) is the French Red Cross’s (FRC) representative delegation for the Caribbean region, based in Guadeloupe, as well as its operational arm for humanitarian action and regional cooperation. PIRAC provides assistance to Caribbean communities in the event of major disasters and works to develop initiatives that strengthen the resilience of communities in French territories as well as in the countries of the Caribbean arc and the Guiana Shield.

**The Project: Ready 360 Phase 2**  
PIRAC launched the READY 360° program in January 2023, co-financed by the INTERREG Caribbean program, the French Development Agency (AFD), and CMA CGM. The READY 360° program aims to build comprehensive and greener resilience in Caribbean territories by strengthening disaster preparedness and response capacities at all levels: from individuals and families, to organizations and businesses, up to the level of regional institutional coordination of risk management. It seeks to achieve four main objectives: (i) Strengthen regional coordination and legislative frameworks for disaster management; (ii) Prepare for, anticipate, and respond to disasters and crises with more eco-responsible, inclusive, and sustainable preparedness measures. (iii) Improve public information, awareness, and preparedness for disasters and crises; (iv) Conduct technical studies and research on disaster management in collaboration with experts and academic stakeholders.

The program involves 8 Caribbean territories: Antigua & Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Saint Kitts & Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent & the Grenadines.

**The Activity: Regional Awareness Campaign**  
This activity falls within the following frameworks:

**Overall Objective :** To strengthen the resilience of populations in the face of disasters, crises, and the effects of climate change in the Caribbean

**Specific Objective :** To develop the prevention, preparedness, and response capacities of Caribbean territories to protect themselves against and overcome natural hazards through an approach aimed at pooling regional and national capacities to address disasters and the effects of climate change  
**Outcome :** Outcome 3: Caribbean citizens increase their self-determination as agents of their own resilience through improved information, awareness, and preparedness for disasters and crises.  
WP4: Development of a risk culture among citizens and entrepreneurs aimed at strengthening their preparedness and resilience  
WP4.1: Implementation of joint regional initiatives to provide information and raise awareness about risks among local populations

One of the main outcomes of the READY 360° Phase 2 program is to raise awareness among Caribbean populations about disaster risks and the effects of climate change through a regional public awareness campaign. This campaign emphasizes the role of citizens in their own preparedness and safety. By “general public,” PIRAC means adults, young adults, teenagers, children, seniors, caregivers, and people with disabilities.  
The messages address risks specific to the Caribbean:

The risks addressed include: hurricanes, floods, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, drought, landslides, tsunamis, and the impacts of climate change on ecosystems.  
This content is disseminated on a large scale through various channels: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, the PIRAC website (with sponsorships and display ads), the Caribbean-Risks portal, public posters, and community events. The campaign, which is primarily digital, utilizes various formats: infographics, animated videos, testimonials, songs, and music videos. The campaign also includes a print component featuring posters and booklets.

Here are the materials that have been produced:

- Hurricane: 1 infographic, 1 video, 1 poster
- Emergency Kit: 1 infographic, 1 poster
- Flood: 1 infographic, 1 video, 1 poster
- Tsunami: 1 infographic, 1 poster
- Earthquake: 1 infographic, 2 videos, 1 poster
- First Aid: 3 videos
- Social Impacts & Return to Normal Life: 1 infographic, 1 video, 1 booklet
- Landslides: 1 infographic, 1 poster
- Drought: 1 infographic, 1 poster
- Volcanic eruption: 1 infographic, 1 video, 1 poster
- Climate Change: 1 infographic, 1 poster
- SAP: 1 video
- 1 song
- 1 choreographed music video
- Viral challenge
- Radio and TV spots
- Creation of a dedicated page on the PIRAC website in French and English

The regional awareness campaign unfolded in several stages:

- Campaign definition (2023–2025)

Several studies were conducted, particularly on accessibility for people with disabilities. A workshop with National Society focal points was held in Saint Martin in November 2023, with the goal of mobilizing partner National Societies and involving their focal points in this campaign. More specifically, the goal was to plan the work to be carried out with them—particularly during the preparation and development phases—as well as to identify avenues for collaboration.

PIRAC then defined the following elements:

- The methodology: It details the target audience, themes, characteristics, information needed to develop messages, collaboration with partners, methods for disseminating messages, the selection of activities, and the definition of monitoring indicators.
- The communication strategy outlines the target audiences, the type of campaign, the desired tone, and accessibility, adaptability to the Caribbean context, the AIDA model, and the tools. It was developed in consultation with the partners’ focal points.
- Visual identity: a name, a slogan, a logo, and a style guide.
- Campaign Development (2024–2026)

Partner engagement: An initial engagement phase took place around the JIRRC on October 13, 2024. National societies were invited to join the editorial committee.  
Co-creation of messages: The messages for each hazard were developed in collaboration with a technical committee.  
Development of campaign materials: These were created by a service provider and were designed to reflect the specific characteristics of the eight regions and their populations.

- Campaign rollout (2025–2027)

Launch: The campaign was launched in June 2025 and is scheduled to end in February 2027.

Message dissemination: The materials were distributed through the previously mentioned channels from June 2025 to October 2026.  
Closure: A campaign-wrap-up workshop will be incorporated into the project-wrap-up workshop.  
As the regional awareness campaign draws to a close, PIRAC wishes to evaluate it according to the criteria defined in the following sections.

## EVALUATION OBJECTIVES

General Objective  
The general objective of the evaluation is as follows:

● To evaluate the relevance, scope, and effectiveness of the regional awareness campaign in order to identify the main results achieved, the factors that contributed to or limited its performance, the lessons learned from its design and implementation, and to formulate recommendations.

Evaluation Questions  
● Relevance

- Do the messages and materials align with the actual needs and risks of the eight territories and the characteristics of the target audience (the general public, including people with disabilities, seniors, and caregivers)?
- Were the strategy and choice of channels appropriate for the Caribbean context, particularly in terms of accessibility?

● Effectiveness

- Did the audiences reach understand the messages?
- Did the campaign increase knowledge or the intention to adopt preventive behaviors?
- Was the strategy implemented as planned, and adjusted when necessary?

● Reach

- How many people were actually exposed to the campaign (digital exposure, since the materials were distributed primarily through digital channels), and does this exposure correspond to the intended target audience (breakdown by region and age group according to channel/medium)?
- Did the partners (Red Cross, OECS, and CDEMA) promote the campaign as planned?

## METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH TO THE ACTIVITY

The evaluator is expected to propose a detailed methodology that addresses the evaluation questions. The proposed approach should prioritize a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods and ensure, to the extent possible, the triangulation of different data sources.  
The methodology must include, but is not limited to:

- A literature review
- Analysis of outreach and engagement statistics
- Interviews with operational partners and beneficiaries

To the extent that available data permit, the evaluation must analyze results in a differentiated manner according to geographic areas, target audience categories, distribution channels, and types of media/content. Particular attention will be paid to accessibility and outreach to specific audiences, particularly people with disabilities, seniors, and caregivers. The evaluator must also outline the methodological limitations of the evaluation.

## PROJECT TIMELINE

The evaluation must take place between March and April 2027. The final report is due by mid April 2027.

DELIVERABLES

- 1 methodological note including an evaluation matrix
- 1 indicative timeline
- 1 budget proposal
- 1 interim report
- 1 final report including recommendations

PROPOSAL EVALUATION

Evaluator Profile

- Experience in evaluating public awareness campaigns
- Experience in the Caribbean and in disaster risk management
- Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative analysis
- Proficiency in KPI analysis

Criteria for Evaluating Proposals

- Contractor’s expertise
- Alignment between the technical proposal and the terms of reference
- Quality and relevance of the portfolio in relation to the terms of reference
- The service provider’s experience in the regions covered by the program and ability to travel quickly
- The contractor’s availability for the duration specified in the terms of reference
- Financial Proposal

Administrative provisions

- The contractor must provide proof at the time of submission that its business operations are in good standing (tax documents, business registration, registration as a self-employed individual—depending on the country of reference where it is established).
- The service provider must independently provide all necessary resources for the fulfillment of its assignment, whether material or human (airline tickets, computer, insurance).
- The service provider may delegate part of the assignment to members of its team or to a collaborator of its choice, but it remains the sole authority with regard to management and discipline concerning its employees.

title: Grants Management Specialist
body:
**About the job**

The Grants Management Specialist assumes responsibility over the efficient management and maintenance of grants related information, documentation, reporting, and processes across DRC Syria, under the supervision of the Grants Management Manager (GMM). The Grants Management Specialist is responsible for the coordination, compilation, and review of donor narrative reports. This includes meeting external reporting deadlines; triggering and coordinating inputs; and compiling, reviewing, and finalizing narrative reports through to donor submission. Grants management responsibilities also include advising on donor regulations and compliance, reviewing of contractual terms, managing deadlines within and across grants, managing instalments, inputting and controlling of grants data in DRC’s Global Grants Management System (Dynamics) and SharePoint, and preparedness for audits. The Grants Management Specialist facilitates DRC grants management processes in terms of information management and administration tasks, including maintaining and circulating various trackers and grants management tools. The Grants Management Specialist plays a leading role in coordinating and facilitating monthly grant opening, review, and close-out meetings, including follow up on action points. The role requires significant liaison with counterparts in DRC Area Offices, Country Office, and HQ. The Grants Management Specialist will contribute to DRC Syria’s localisation commitments by strengthening equitable and compliant grant management practices with national partners, supporting transparent fund flows, and promoting capacity strengthening in donor compliance, reporting, and financial accountability across DRC and consortium partners.

In addition to the main roles and responsibilities outlined above, the Grants Management Specialist will support proposal development processes and other grants-related tasks upon delegation by the GMM and Head of Programme.

**Responsibilities**

**1. Grants Management**

- Facilitate the administration of grants management processes (reminders of deadlines; coordination of reports; submission via online portals; coordination of comments/revisions).
- Promote quality information management by maintaining an up-to-date filing system on SharePoint, including careful version control of proposals, grant amendments, top-ups, donor reports, etc.
- Ensure that DRC Dynamics is continually updated (reporting, instalments, start date, end date, total budget, and uploading of documents).
- Ensure the maintenance of an internal grants tracker, reporting schedule, grants review schedule, and proposal pipeline.
- Track and follow-up on installment requests, in close coordination with HQ and Finance counterparts.
- Support the Finance team with audit processes when grants-related documents are requested.
- Support the GMM for compliance checks in Donor Grant Agreements (compliance with codes, donor visibility requirements, etc.).
- Coordinate inputs and preparations for grant opening, review, and close-out meetings, including preparation of the Project Management Tool (PMT).
- Prepare internal guidance and updates on donor compliance, to be presented in grant meetings.
- Facilitate the meetings as delegated by the GMM, taking note of the action points, for circulation and follow-up post-meeting.
- Provide guidance to DRC staff on donor compliance, requirements and guidelines.

**2. Reporting**

- Take responsibility for donor reporting deadlines (setting internal deadlines, preparing templates providing clear guidance to relevant colleagues, and following up on inputs).
- Lead the coordination, compilation, review and finalization of donor narrative reports, including submission via online portals, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and DRC requirements.
- Support partners in improving report quality through structured feedback and mentoring on narrative and compliance standards.

**3. Partnerships**

- Support the Partnership Manager in conducting due diligence for new partnerships.
- Participate in local partner capacity assessments and the development of capacity building plans, where relevant.
- Support local partners with capacity building related to grants management.

**4. Proposal Development**

- As assigned by the GMM, support the development of project proposals, including coordination and follow up to ensure timely submission.
- Support quality assurance and submission including via online portals.

Other tasks delegated by the GMM, as required.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- Excellent written English communication skills; experience writing and copy editing complex and lengthy reports
- At least 3 years professional work experience in business development, reporting, or grants management in an NGO/INGO or similar
- Experience with grant management, and donor reporting
- Experience with inter-departmental coordination
- Understanding of localisation principles and equitable partnership frameworks in humanitarian programming.
- Cultural sensitivity and adaptability
- Ability to manage a high workload and manage stress
- Proven ability to manage stakeholders with strong communication, coordination, influencing and interpersonal skills.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and DRC values.
- Strong understanding of global protection sector standards, protection analysis, and Results-Based Protection
- Experience in project development (including proposal writing) an advantage
- Experience in DRC Core Sectors (Protection, SWI, Economic Recovery, HDP) an advantage

**Education:**

Bachelor of Arts or other relevant degree

**Languages:**

- English – fluent
- Arabic – fluent

*n this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract Length**: 6 months (Renewable, based on performance and fund availability).
- **Salary Level**: Non Management – G level 2 (Based on DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Syria, Damascus.
- **Expected Start date**: 10 December 2026

**About Acted**

“We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

title: Research project management support consultant
body:
**About Truth Guardians:**

Truth Guardians is a non-profit organisation working in Syria and The Netherlands. The Organization is founded by White Helmets members aiming to provide aid to communities and persons recovering from conflicts and disasters; provide support to displaced people and hosting communities; support justice, accountability, rule of law, human rights efforts, and research activities.

Truth Guardians is an equal opportunities employer and applications are actively encouraged from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of sex, race, disability, age, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity.

**Introduction:**

Supporting the Syrian National Commission for Transitional Justice (NCTJ) through short-term, start-up project management support for the initial phase of the NCTJ Transitional Justice Research Support Project.

**1. Background**

The NCTJ is mandated to lead transitional justice processes in Syria, including through evidence-based research, legal analysis and advisory functions that underpin its work.

As part of the wider NCTJ-TG project, the NCTJ and Truth Guardians (TG) are developing the NCTJ Transitional Justice Research Support Project (the Research Support Project), which will begin with an initial phase of research activities to lay the foundations for a broader research and thought-leadership agenda in the future.

A consultant is therefore sought for a short, intensive assignment to provide start-up project management support for the Research Support Project. The consultant will be contracted by TG and report to the TG focal point, who will instruct the consultant based on guidance from the NCTJ, and will work closely with both the TG and NCTJ focal points.

**2. Purpose of the Assignment**

More specifically, the consultant will:

- Provide start-up project management and implementation support to the TG and NCTJ focal points, complementing the NCTJ focal points’ technical and academic expertise;
- Support the NCTJ to translate the research gaps and themes it has identified into an external call for small research studies;
- Support a transparent selection process, guided by the NCTJ's research priorities, and the contracting by TG and onboarding of the selected research studies;
- Help establish simple project management, monitoring and quality assurance tools for the research studies;
- Support the NCTJ focal point and relevant staff to lead management of the research activities by the end of the assignment.

Throughout the assignment, the consultant will apply conflict-sensitive and Do No Harm approaches, and ensure appropriate attention to confidentiality and institutional ownership by the Commission.

**3. Scope of Work**

**3.1** ***Call Design and Launch*** – the consultant will:

- Support the NCTJ to design and launch an external call for research, based on the research gaps and priorities identified by the Commission.

**3.2** ***Selection and Contracting*** – the consultant will

- Support a transparent selection process, guided by the NCTJ, for approximately six small research studies in the first call, and support the contracting by TG and onboarding of the selected research studies.

**3.3** ***Project Management, Early Implementation and Handover***

The consultant will:

- Help establish simple project management, monitoring and quality assurance tools for the research studies;
- Support the start of the selected research studies and early engagement between researchers and the NCTJ, and report on progress to the TG and NCTJ focal points;
- Support the TG and NCTJ focal points to take over day-to-day management of the research activities by the end of the assignment.

**3.4** ***Coordination and Facilitation***– the consultant will:

- Coordinate with relevant TG and NCTJ staff to ensure coherence with the wider NCTJ-TG project, and facilitate meetings or workshops.

The assignment is adaptive: this scope is an initial framework and may be refined during inception and implementation, in agreement with TG and the Commission.

**4. Deliverables - the consultant will produce:**

1. Inception note - workplan and timeline, coordination arrangements with the NCTJ focal point and TG, and quality assurance approach.
2. Call package - call for proposals, research questions, eligibility and selection criteria, application templates and timeline, validated by the NCTJ and approved by TG.
3. Selection and contracting procedures - review and selection process, panel arrangements, and templates for contracting and onboarding researchers.
4. Selection report - summary of the review process and the studies recommended for funding, submitted to TG for funding decisions based on NCTJ guidance.
5. Project management toolkit - project management plan, tracking and reporting tools, and quality assurance and peer review procedures for the research activities.
6. Periodic progress updates and coordination meeting notes - shared at agreed milestones with the NCTJ focal point and TG.
7. Handover note - status of the studies, outstanding actions, and recommendations for the TG and NCTJ focal points to manage the remaining implementation and future research rounds.

**5**. **Management and Reporting Arrangements**

TG is the contracting party for this assignment. The consultant reports to the TG focal point, who will instruct the consultant based on guidance from the NCTJ focal point; the TG and NCTJ focal points will work closely together. The NCTJ guides the research priorities and content of the Research Support Project.

**6. Quality Assurance**

All deliverables should demonstrate: :

- Evidence-based analysis and recommendations;
- Clear linkage to the research gaps and priorities identified by the Commission;
- Practical applicability and feasibility within the NCTJ's current institutional capacity and resources;
- Incorporation of perspectives from multiple NCTJ Directorates;
- Compliance with agreed confidentiality and conflict-sensitivity requirements;
- Clarity, accessibility and usability for decision-making by the Commission.

During the inception phase, the consultant shall propose a quality assurance framework, including deliverable review and validation processes, for approval by the Commission and Truth Guardians.

**7. Duration**

- Indicative initial duration: 3 months full-time (with possibility of extension)

**8. Required Expertise - the consultant should demonstrate experience in:**

We are looking for an experienced project manager with a background in research project start-up, able to work alongside the TG and NCTJ focal points during a short start-up phase. The consultant should demonstrate:

- Project management experience, ideally including research projects, grant programmes or calls for research proposals;
- Good knowledge of the Syrian context, including research, academic and civil society networks;
- Familiarity with transitional justice or human rights is an advantage.
- The consultant must be able to work in both Arabic and English.
    
    The consultant should be able to be present in Syria for extended periods for in-person work with stakeholders.

**8. Confidentiality and Sensitivity**

Given the sensitive nature of the project, the consultant is expected to:

- Exercise discretion in all external communications
- Avoid public attribution of the work without prior agreement
- Adhere to agreed protocols regarding institutional representation and visibility
- The consultant may be required to sign relevant confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding, and ethical conduct commitments as part of the contracting process.

title: Below The Line Marketing Agency- Kenya
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Contractor / Consultant

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY  
Access to adequate and affordable housing remains a pressing challenge across Africa, particularly in the face of rapid urbanization and climate change. Compressed Earth Blocks (CEBs) present a sustainable, cost-effective, and locally sourced alternative to conventional building materials. To promote the adoption of this technology, HFHI, in partnership with a private sector actor, has been supporting efforts to stimulate the local housing market through innovation, demonstration activities, and awareness creation on the benefits of CEBs.

To catalyse greater market adoption of CEBs, HFHI seeks to support its private-sector partner to invest in and strengthen its market-development function through the engagement of a skilled below-the-line (BTL) experiential marketing agency. The agency will design and execute integrated consumer engagement and behaviour change campaigns that address information gaps and perception barriers, increase consumer awareness and confidence, and generate demand for CEB products. The objective is to demonstrate viable market-led approaches to customer acquisition and demand generation that can be sustained and scaled by the partner beyond the period of support.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Background

Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is anchored on a fundamental vision of a world where everyone has a decent place to live. This vision has been the driving force in all of Habitat’s actions and activities and has seen HFHI helping more than 29 million people around the world build or improve the place they call home. To further fulfil this vision, HFHI established the Terwilliger Centre for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) to Build and Expand Inclusive Housing Markets by supporting local firms to innovate and expand client-responsive services and products. TCIS understands that the role of local markets is critical in closing adequate housing gaps among the low-income and incremental market segment. TCIS strives to make markets work more effectively for low-income people in need of decent, affordable housing.

Context

Access to adequate and affordable housing remains a pressing challenge across Africa, particularly in the face of rapid urbanization and climate change. Compressed Earth Blocks (CEBs) present a sustainable, cost-effective, and locally sourced alternative to conventional building materials. To promote the adoption of this technology, HFHI, in partnership with a private sector actor, has been supporting efforts to stimulate the local housing market through innovation, demonstration activities, and awareness creation on the benefits of CEBs.

To catalyse greater market adoption of CEBs, HFHI seeks to support its private-sector partner to invest in and strengthen its market-development function through the engagement of a skilled below-the-line (BTL) experiential marketing agency. The agency will design and execute integrated consumer engagement and behaviour change campaigns that address information gaps and perception barriers, increase consumer awareness and confidence, and generate demand for CEB products. The objective is to demonstrate viable market-led approaches to customer acquisition and demand generation that can be sustained and scaled by the partner beyond the period of support.

Key objectives

- Design and implement integrated behaviour change communication (BCC) and BTL experiential marketing campaigns that addresses prevailing myths, misconceptions, promotes awareness, knowledge, demand and use of CEBs among identified households.
- Enhance the visibility and market presence of the private sector partner's CEB products and housing solutions among prospective customers, builders, artisans, developers, and other key market actors.
- Facilitate direct links between potential customers and the private sector partner for leads, product inquiries, referrals, and sales conversions.
- Monitor, document, and report on campaign performance and results, including reach, engagement, leads generation, converted leads, CEB adoption, partner sales and revenue changes and lessons learned.
- Develop a comprehensive Marketing Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) detailing marketing approaches, processes, collateral templates, and performance monitoring mechanisms, to strengthen the private sector partner’s capacity to independently implement future marketing and demand generation campaigns.

**Tasks and responsibilities**

- Conduct a review of secondary literature and existing project materials and market insights to inform campaign design and implementation.
- Develop a comprehensive BCC and BTL marketing approaches aligned with the project objectives and target audiences.
- Collaborate closely with the private sector partner and HFHI to ensure alignment of activities with project goals and business objectives.
- Design communication materials and promotional assets with clear, compelling, messaging that is tailored to the identified target audiences.
- Support in lead generation and customer referral database capturing consumer inquiries, leads, and referrals made to the private sector partner.
- Engage relevant local stakeholders, community representatives, housing sector actors, and influencers to support campaign implementation and message amplification
- Develop and implement a campaign reporting and monitoring framework to track performance against agreed indicators.
- Provide regular progress updates to the private sector partner and HFHI
- Develop a comprehensive Marketing SOP detailing marketing approaches, processes, collateral templates, and performance monitoring mechanisms for marketing and demand creation activities.

**Deliverables**

- BCC and BTL marketing campaign approach, including consumer engagement activities, key messages, promotional materials and designs.
- Detailed inception report detailing the campaign strategy, target audiences, key messages, implementation approach, activity schedule, and monitoring framework.
- Work plan detailing the campaign activities, milestones and timelines.
- Campaign monitoring reports providing updates on activities implemented, audience reach, engagement levels, lead generation, and emerging insights.
- Final campaign report summarizing activities, campaign performance against agreed indicators, key achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and recommendations for future demand creation efforts.
- A detailed Marketing SOP.

**Experience and qualification**

The selected agency should have the following qualification:

- Must be a legally registered firm with at least 5 years of proven experience in designing and implementing BTL marketing, consumer engagement, BCC, and demand creation campaigns.
- Strong regional presence
- Experience working with private sector companies especially Small, and Medium Enterprises to support market development.
- Experience in developing marketing SOPs to support continued implementation beyond the assignment period.
- Experience producing high-quality written technical reports
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively with cross-functional teams.
- Understanding of Market Systems approaches and experience working with housing sector is an added advantage.

Duration

The consultancy will be conducted in a duration of 6 months. This represents calendar period and not consultancy days.

Safeguarding and Data Protection

HFHI requires that all consultants take seriously their intended beneficiaries, their communities and all those with whom we work. The consultant shall support and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of all community members, especially children, and promotes implementation of HFHI’s code of conduct.

**Data Protection**

The contractor will be required to abide by HFHI’s data protection and security policy during the assignment period.

**Geographical scope:** The activities will focus on the Laikipia, Eastern and Western region

Submission

Interested agencies should submit the following:

- Technical Proposal providing a clear understanding of the assignment and proposed approach to achieve the objectives.
- A detailed financial proposal
- CVs of the team
- Case studies of similar work done

Application and Decision Process

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Submissions should be sent to by 25th Nov 2026, with subject line: **Below The Line Marketing Agency- Kenya.** The selected consultant may be required to show proof of professional indemnity cover

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

title: Officer, Prospect Research & Management
Country Head of Programmes Tanzania
body:
**Position**:Country Head of Programmes Tanzania

**Reporting to**: Country Representative

**Collaborating with**: Head of Departments and Project Managers

**Location:** Dar es Salaam, with frequent field visits

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline:** 08/12/2026

**Family Duty Station**: YES

**R&R**: NO

**Contract Type**: Expatriate (International)

**Working Context**

Since 2010, WeWorld has maintained a strong operational presence in Tanzania, implementing multisectoral, school-centredprogrammes in Dar es Salaam and Ludewa District, reaching nearly 25,000 beneficiaries, primarily children, adolescents, parents, and school personnel. These interventions integrate education, health, nutrition, child protection, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalised children, including children with disabilities. Through an integrated, community-based approach, WeWorld seeks to improve children's access to quality education, enhance their wellbeing and protection, and strengthen the capacity of families, schools, and community care systems to respond to their needs.

WeWorld works in close collaboration with local civil society organisations, government authorities, and other development stakeholders to promote sustainable, locally owned solutions. As an active member of the Tanzania Education Network (TENMET), the organisation contributes to national efforts to advance inclusive and equitable quality education in line with the Education for All agenda. Between 2017 and 2022, WeWorld also supported the Bunju Multipurpose Centre in Dar es Salaam, providing integrated psychosocial, legal, medical, educational, and vocational support to vulnerable children and young people, alongside family reintegration services.

Building on its longstanding engagement in education and child protection, WeWorld has progressively expanded its programmatic portfolio to encompass civil society strengthening, human rights, peacebuilding, youth empowerment, and environmental sustainability. Between 2020 and 2022, the organisation implemented the European Union-funded SautiMpya project in Kigoma, Mbeya, and Mtwara regions, strengthening partnerships between civil society organisations and media actors to advance the rights and participation of women and young people.

WeWorld is currently implementing a diversified portfolio of programmes supported by the European Union and other institutional donors. These include Kijani Pemba, which promotes urban eco-resilience and environmental sustainability in Zanzibar; Kujenga Amani Pamoja, a regional initiative advancing peacebuilding and meaningful youth engagement across Kenya, Mozambique, and Tanzania; and Pamoja Tudumishe Elimu, a cross-border Kenya–Tanzania programme supporting the retention, participation, and access of vulnerable learners to quality primary education.

As WeWorld Tanzania continues to consolidate its operational presence and strengthen its programmatic portfolio, the organisation is prioritising enhanced programme quality, strategic coherence, operational effectiveness, and sustainable resource mobilisation. This requires stronger integration across projects and thematic areas, more effective programme oversight and accountability, and increased investment in national staff leadership, institutional partnerships, and country-level programme development.

**Purpose of the Role**

Under the direct supervision of the Country Representative, the Country Head of Programmes provides strategic, technical and operational leadership for WeWorld Tanzania’s programme portfolio, ensuring quality, accountability, donor compliance and effective programme implementation.

He/She leads programme development and resource mobilisation, contributing to the country strategy, identifying funding opportunities, strengthening donor and partner engagement, and overseeing the development of proposals.

The Country Head of Programmes leads and supports programme teams, strengthens national staff capacity, ensures effective coordination with support functions, and contributes to WeWorld’s institutional representation and strategic partnerships with government, donors, civil society and implementing partners.

**Main Functions and Duties**

**1. Programme and Quality Management**

- Provide leadership and oversight to ensure high-quality implementation of all programmes in line with WeWorld’s strategy and contextual needs
- Supervise and support Project Managers, Grants and Programme Advisors, and technical staff in planning, monitoring, and reporting of activities and results
- Ensure programme implementation complies with internal policies, donor regulations, national legislation, and international standards
- Coordinate with the Head of Support Services and Country Representative to oversee the financial management of the country programme portfolio
- Ensure timely and quality preparation of internal and external reports, donor submissions, briefing notes, and other reporting requirements
- Lead coordination and integration across programme sectors (e.g., education, protection, livelihoods, basic assistance, civil society)
- Lead the integration of cross-cutting themes such as gender, inclusion, climate resilience, and accountability
- Directly manage or support project implementation in the absence of a dedicated Project Manager, based on needs and guidance from the Country Representative
- Facilitate harmonization of tools, methodologies, procedures, and guidelines across projects
- Ensure quality criteria and indicators are monitored and used for evidence-based decision-making

**2. Strategic Planning and Fundraising**

- Collaborate with the Country Representative to define and implement the long-term country strategy
- Identify and assess programming and funding opportunities aligned with country priorities and WeWorld’s global strategy
- Lead and coordinate proposal development, engaging technical and support teams, and liaising with HQ technical coordinators and the regional unit
- Ensure proposals are competitive, technically sound, and responsive to donor requirements and contextual realities
- Promote synergies between humanitarian response and development programmes

**3. Representation and Institutional Relations**

- Represent WeWorld in strategic fora, donor meetings, technical working groups, cluster coordination mechanisms, and consortia
- Build and maintain relationships with institutional donors, UN agencies, INGOs, national and local authorities, and civil society actors
- Provide strategic input into communication and visibility activities, including documentation, lessons learned, and programme capitalization

**4. HR Management and Capacity Building**

- Line manageprogramme and technical staff, ensuring performance objectives are set and regularly reviewed
- Promote a supportive environment that encourages accountability, learning, and professional growth
- Identify capacity-building needs and coordinate appropriate training for programme teams
- Foster transparent, inclusive, and equitable recruitment and staff management in accordance with WeWorld policies and national labor laws
- Ensure strong internal communication and collaboration across departments (e.g., MEAL, Admin, Logistics, HR)
- Promote staff well-being and uphold WeWorld’s values and standards of conduct, emphasizing diversity and inclusion

**5. MEAL and Accountability**

- Oversee the design and implementation of MEAL systems across all projects
- Ensure monitoring tools are in place and data is used to inform programme planning and decision-making
- Coordinate with the MEAL Officer/Manager to support evaluations, learning, accountability mechanisms, and quality reporting

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in the field of Social or Political Science, Development Studies, Economics, International relations, Project Management, Agronomy, Business development.
- Knowledge of main donors’ policies and procedures (EU, UN Agencies, Italian Cooperation, ECHO)
- Fluent in written and spoken English
- Good computer skills, in particular MS Office package

**Professional experience**

- At least 5 years of relevant working experience in humanitarian or development settings
- At least 4 years of experience in Project Cycle Management
- Proven experience in project proposal writing

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong interpersonal relationships and good communication and leadership skills
- Ability to perform under stress conditions
- Capacity to work autonomously and in problem prevention/resolution
- Proven organizational skills and ability to effectively manage multiple tasks while fostering quality, team spirit and positive working relationships with colleagues
- Integrity in line with the Humanitarian Principles and ethical standards
- Cultural, gender, religionsensitivity and adaptability

**DESIRABLE REQUIREMENTS**

- Previous experience in Tanzania and East Africa
- Previous experience in Development and Emergency programmes
- Knowledge of the Swahili language

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) months contract subject to verification (achievement of specific objectives); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first period of collaboration and depending on available funding.

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy

Base Salary (3.190€ - 3.790€ monthly)+ Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Annual leave**: 2,5 days/month (working days).

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station).

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family Duty Station**: YES

**R&R**: NO

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

title: Social and Behavior Change educator (Syria - Homs )
body:
**Job Title: Social and Behavior Change educator**

**Job location: Syria - Homs - Al-Dabaa PHC**

**Reports to: Project Coordinator**

**JOB SUMMARY**

Conducting campaigns and health awareness through PHC and visits to community and public places.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

The **Social and Behavior Change educator** has the following responsibilities and duties:

1\. Conducting ongoing awareness campaigns, both at the center and in public facilities such as schools and community gathering places.

2\. Serve as a link between the beneficiary and the services available at the center.

3\. Performs sensitivity assessments and identifies cases in need according to predetermined criteria.

The focus will be on changing community behavior through a thorough assessment of cases and tailoring messages to suit each individual situation.

4\. Manages cases, including maintaining faithful to protocols on privacy and individual leave.

5\. Makes internal and external referrals of cases, updates feedback and referral forms,

6\. Updates case files with the help of the health Officer and ensures that the information is secured.

7\. To carry out preventive healthcare and guidance activities on reproductive health, newborn and child nutrition, early diagnosis of breast cancer, personal and home hygiene, tooth cleaning and vaccination.

8\. Advises and guides cases and community groups on issues related to diagnosis screening, such as cancer screening, pap smear, glaucoma tests, and diabetes screening.

9\. To provide informative training for pregnant women and children.

10\. To perform family planning services, health and hygiene incentives, screening of infectious diseases, carrying out health education activities, collecting statistics and health care referrals at the same time.

11\. To meet basic needs such as first aid.

12\. Visiting service providers to ensure that the intervention, information, and referral activities on community health are carried out effectively,

13\. To make weekly and monthly reports on the activities, interventions, orientation, and mapping activities performed.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

1\. Formal university or diploma degree.

2\. Knowledge and/or work experience in community health development preferable.

3\. Able to prioritize, communicate effectively, and meet deadlines

4\. Experience as a team member of working in community health or nutrition or other related health-related intervention.

5\. Knowledge of Microsoft office with a good command of Microsoft Excel.

6\. Strong leadership and coordination skills.

7\. Able to work both independently and in a team environment.

8\. Previous NGO experience in a similar context is a plus.

Principles and rules of conduct. Strict compliance with safety and ethical standards is required.

**الوصف الوظيفي**

المسمى الوظيفي: مثقف/ة صحي/ة

مكان العمل: سوريا - حمص - المركز الصحي الأولي في الضبعة

يقدم تقاريره إلى: منسق المشروع

**نطاق المسؤولية:**

تنفيذ حملات التوعية الصحية في المركز الصحي الأولي، ومن خلال زيارات المجتمع المحلي والأماكن العامة.

**المهام والمسؤوليات:**

يتولى المثقف الصحي المهام والمسؤوليات التالية:

1\. تنفيذ حملات توعية مستمرة في المركز وفي المرافق العامة، مثل المدارس وأماكن التجمعات المجتمعية.

2\. العمل كصلة وصل بين المستفيدين والخدمات المتوفرة في المركز.

3\. إجراء تقييمات الهشاشة وتحديد الحالات المحتاجة وفق معايير محددة مسبقاً.

ويتركز العمل على تغيير السلوك المجتمعي من خلال التقييم الدقيق للحالات، وتكييف الرسائل بما يناسب كل حالة.

4\. إدارة الحالات مع الالتزام ببروتوكولات الخصوصية والموافقة الفردية.

5\. إجراء الإحالات الداخلية والخارجية للحالات، وتحديث نماذج التغذية الراجعة والإحالة.

6\. تحديث ملفات الحالات بمساعدة الموظف الصحي، وضمان أمن المعلومات وسريتها.

7\. تنفيذ أنشطة الرعاية الصحية الوقائية والتوجيه حول الصحة الإنجابية، وتغذية حديثي الولادة والأطفال، والكشف المبكر عن سرطان الثدي، والنظافة الشخصية والمنزلية، ونظافة الأسنان، واللقاح.

8\. تقديم المشورة والتوجيه للحالات والمجموعات المجتمعية حول الفحوصات التشخيصية، مثل الكشف عن السرطان، ولطاخة عنق الرحم، وفحوصات الزرق (الغلوكوما)، والكشف عن السكري.

9\. تقديم جلسات تثقيفية للنساء الحوامل والأطفال.

10\. تقديم خدمات تنظيم الأسرة، وتعزيز الصحة والنظافة، والكشف عن الأمراض المعدية، وتنفيذ أنشطة التثقيف الصحي، وجمع الإحصائيات، وإحالة الحالات إلى خدمات الرعاية الصحية.

11\. تلبية الاحتياجات الأساسية مثل الإسعافات الأولية.

12\. زيارة مقدمي الخدمات لضمان تنفيذ أنشطة التدخل والتوعية والإحالة في مجال صحة المجتمع بفعالية.

13\. إعداد تقارير أسبوعية وشهرية عن الأنشطة والتدخلات وجلسات التوجيه وأنشطة رسم خرائط الخدمات المنفذة.

**المؤهلات والمهارات:**

يجب أن تتوفر لدى المتقدم المهارات والمؤهلات والخبرات التالية:

1\. شهادة جامعية أو شهادة معهد.

2\. يُفضّل وجود معرفة و/أو خبرة عملية في مجال تنمية صحة المجتمع.

3\. القدرة على تحديد الأولويات والتواصل الفعّال والالتزام بالمواعيد المحددة.

4\. خبرة في العمل ضمن فريق في مجال صحة المجتمع أو التغذية أو التدخلات الصحية ذات الصلة.

5\. معرفة ببرامج Microsoft Office مع إتقان جيد لبرنامج Excel.

6\. مهارات قيادة وتنسيق قوية.

7\. القدرة على العمل باستقلالية وضمن فريق.

8\. تُعد الخبرة السابقة مع المنظمات غير الحكومية في سياق مشابه ميزة إضافية.

title: Regional Communications Officer – Central America Region
body:
**The Regional Communications Officer** is an execution-focused regional role responsible for translating the global communications and brand framework into high-quality communications products, content, storytelling, digital outputs and country-level communications support across Central America (El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras). The position coordinates regional communications delivery, production planning and operational requirements, while implementing the regional communications strategy established by the Vice President, Integrated Brand & Communications. Indicative balance of time: 45% producing materials and content · 35% planning, coordination and managing demand across the three countries · 20% supporting country offices.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Graphic Design, or a related field.
- At least three years of professional experience in communications or content production, preferably in the humanitarian or international development sector.
- Demonstrated anticipation: evidence of having identified what an organization would need and prepared for it before being asked. Candidates will be asked to demonstrate this during the selection process.
- Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite; Illustrator, InDesign and Photoshop, with a working command of output specifications for print and digital. Premiere Pro or equivalent for basic video editing. Canva is not a substitute.
- Practical field photography and video capture: interview framing, lavalier and directional audio, stabilization, exposure control and use of filters.
- Experience planning production against supplier lead times and working with procurement processes.
- Experience operating organizational social media accounts and reporting on engagement.
- Working proficiency in Spanish and English, written and spoken.
- Competence with collaborative planning tools; experience with Monday.com or equivalent is an advantage.
- Right to work in Guatemala, and able to attend the country office on a hybrid basis in line with regional policy.
- Experience driving standard 4WD vehicles in rough terrain. Valid driver's license.
- Ability to project and maintain a calm work environment while operating in a time and
- deadline-defined environment required by internal and external clients.
- Excellent interpersonal, relational, and communication skills, with a history of inspiring collaboration across multiple functions.
- Possessing a deep connection with the local context of communities in social risk conditions.
- Ability to adopt and promote a positive attitude towards processes of change, renewal, and transformation.
- Committed to creating a positive impact on the world with inspiration, passion, compassion, and a sense of service vocation.
- Ability to travel regularly to program locations, both nationally and internationally.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Oversight and Governance Responsibilities:**

- Ensure that all communications outputs produced in or for the region adhere to organizational policies, brand standards, safeguarding requirements and ethical storytelling standards.
- Identify and escalate to the line manager any reputational, brand or safeguarding risk arising from regional communications activity, including materials produced by implementing partners.
- Maintain complete consent and release documentation for all content produced in the region, and verify it is in place before any material is used or published.
- Ensure that country offices and implementing partners use the organizational identity only through the defined authorization process and report any unauthorized use.
- Maintain accurate records of production, suppliers and communications expenditure, and report them to the line manager.
- Support training and awareness for country staff and implementing partner staff on brand standards, consent and safeguarding in communications.
- Recommend improvements to communications processes and controls to strengthen consistency, accountability and quality across the region.

**Production of Communications Materials**

- Produce communications and visibility materials for the three countries: brochures, reports, IEC tools, banners, signage, event materials, staff identification and program collateral.
- Adapt global campaign materials for regional use, working from approved templates and brand assets.
- Specify materials correctly for their intended use, including application, resolution, color space, bleed, and finishing.
- Prepare supplier briefs and specifications, coordinate with Procurement and Finance on execution, and obtain a printer’s proof before any full production run, without exception.
- Maintain supplier and printer records for the region, with current lead times and costs.

**Content and Storytelling**

- Deliver an agreed monthly volume of approved success stories from the three country offices to the global repository, with complete metadata, working with country program staff to source them.
- Write and edit success stories and donor-facing content to the organization’s global voice and quality standards.
- Capture photography and short-form video interviews in the field to a professional standard, including framing, audio, stabilization and exposure control.

**Planning and Coordination**

- Develop an annual communications work plan jointly with the country office teams, setting out their planned activities, dates and material requirements for the year, so that needs are mapped early enough to be produced properly. Update it through the quarterly Requirements Report.
- Maintain the regional production calendar: record every communications deliverable with its material type, lead time, the date final artwork is required, and the date it must reach procurement. Reviewed monthly with the line manager.
- Submit a Regional Communications Requirements Report before the start of each quarter, listing, for each country, the commemorative dates, program milestones, partner events, and activities that will require communications support, along with the lead time each requires.
- Flag in writing, as soon as it is known, any activity whose timeline is no longer viable, and propose an alternative material or scope.
- Maintain the regional workstream board and keep the status of each item up to date.

**Regional Digital Presence and Media**

- Operate and administer the regional social media accounts: schedule and publish posts, stories, reels and short-form content approved within the global framework, maintain a content calendar one month in advance, and report engagement quarterly.
- Maintain an organizational media contact database for the three countries, held on the regional system and kept current. Personal contact lists are not a substitute.
- Liaise with local and regional media outlets to enhance visibility and maintain the regional media kit: organizational fact sheet, spokesperson protocol, and approved boilerplate.

**Country Office Support and Capacity**

- Train and support country program staff and implementing partner staff in interviewing, photography specifications, consent documentation, and the use of approved templates and brand assets.
- Operate the shared mechanisms through which program teams submit content and requests.
- Work with country teams to incorporate their communication requirements into the annual plan and propose the approaches most likely to work for each country and audience.
- Provide guidance to country offices on brand application so that materials start from approved templates rather than being corrected at approval stage.

**Brand Application and Partner Materials**

- Apply the organizational identity consistently across all regional outputs, and ensure that country offices and implementing partners work from the currently approved assets.
- Route every partner request to use the organizational identity on physical materials through the defined authorization process. The postholder does not approve partner use of the organizational identity.
- Produce final artwork for approved co-branded materials from organizational templates rather than amending partner-originated files.

**Service Standard**

- Acknowledge every internal and partner request upon receipt, and respond with a specific date within two working days.
- Where a request arrives without the information needed to act, obtain it from the requester rather than waiting.
- Report status by stage — not started, in design, pending approval, final artwork ready, with procurement, in production, delivered — never as a general assessment.

**Scope and Interface with Headquarters**

- Held by this post: regional adaptation of global campaigns, field capture, templated and routine production, supplier briefing and coordination, regional channels, local media liaison, and country office support.
- Routed to headquarters Creative Services: campaign concept development, complex design, finished video editing and institutional publications. The postholder is responsible for recognizing which is which and routing in good time.
- The postholder implements the regional communications strategy designed by the Vice President, Integrated Brand & Communications, within the global Marketing & Communications frameork.
