title: Terre des Hommes - External Evaluation of Decentralized Organizational Model
body:
## 1.Presentation of Terre des hommes

As he leading Swiss organization for children’s rights, created in 1960, the Terre des hommes foundation is committed to protecting children’s lives and their rights, and improving their well-being. We aim to do so through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have both short- and long-term impacts.

For more than 60 years, we have been working in difficult situations, in countries at war, regions devastated by natural disasters, and places where poverty and malnutrition force millions of children and their families to migrate elsewhere. We provide direct and indirect support to millions of children, their families and communities in around thirty countries every year, in close cooperation with our local partners. [www.tdh.org](http://www.tdh.org)

## 2.Context

The Terre des hommes Decentralization Project (hereinafter ‘the Project’) is an organizational transformation project consistent with the evolution of the international development sector.

The objective is to identify, build and implement a decentralized organizational model that empowers regions and countries and converts its headquarters in Switzerland into a centre of expertise.

More specifically, the objectives of the Project are based on the following items:

- **Proximity** to the field, improved context-specific knowledge, meaningful regional projects and consortia, and an improved response to children's needs.
- **Influence & advocacy** in relation to regional policies of interest to Tdh, initiate and contribute to regional advocacy.
- **Positioning & visibility** towards the regional aid and coordination agencies, recognition as a key organization in the field of children's rights, and authority based on our expertise.
- Integration of **local expertise** into regional offices as much as possible.
- Increased institutional **fundraising**, influence of donor strategies, strong relationships with key donors.
- **Efficiency** through optimized functions, processes, with strong reliance on local expertise.

The Project began in 2022, with a planned completion by the end of 2025; the roll out of the third and last Regional setup was delayed because of the reexamination of its modalities and reporting lines especially, and the new organizational model will be fully operational at the end of 2026.

Terre des hommes is now undertaking an external evaluation to assess the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, and fitness for purpose of the decentralized model in relation to its mission, strategy, and operating context.

Consistent with [OECD/DAC Evaluation Criteria](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2019/12/better-criteria-for-better-evaluation_f7a307eb/15a9c26b-en.pdf), the evaluation is commissioned at a time of governance review, with the intention of informing decision‑making by senior management and the governing body. The evaluation will allow for significant developments in the global development sector in 2025 and 2026, that is, after its design and roll-out.

### Monitoring

Under the sponsorship of the Director General, the **Project Steering Committee** the Directors of Operations and his Deputy, People & Culture, Finance & Logistics, Resource Mobilization & Communication, Digital, Innovation and ICT, and the Chief of Staff.

An initial **assessment** was conducted in mid-2025, involving the then fully deployed Regional Office (MENA); in early 2026, an intermediate assessment was conducted involving all three Regions. Progress agis monitored on quarterly basis.

## 3.Objective of the evaluation

The purpose of the evaluation is to provide an independent, evidence‑based assessment of the decentralized organizational model and to generate clear conclusions and strategic recommendations to inform future organizational directions. As such, its main purpose is to inform the **learning process**; it does however pursue objectives of external and internal accountability (strategic, managerial, and financial). The evaluation will:

- Assess how well the decentralized organizational model supports the organization’s mission, strategy, and objectives
- Identify strengths, limitations, and risks inherent in the model
- Provide practical recommendations for improvement or adaptation

The specific objectives are to review and analyze:

- The relevance and strategic alignment of the decentralized organizational model, in particular the achievements against the six objectives of the decentralization project.
- Cross-region **system coherence** and **adaptation** to context, including the potential for cross-fertilization\*\*.\*\*
- The effectiveness and efficiency of **governance**, management, and operational arrangements, including the existing **process** framework (steering mechanisms, including decision‑making, accountability, and coordination), **resource use** and cost‑effectiveness.
- **Organizational culture**, ways of working, change management, and attitude to change.
- **Risks**, mitigation measures and future considerations.

## 4.Scope of the evaluation

Given the breadth of themes and organizational dimensions covered by this evaluation, the assessment is expected to focus on **strategic and systemic analysis** rather than an exhaustive review of all processes, functions and organizational units. The evaluation should examine the extent to which the decentralized organizational model is fit for purpose, identify key achievements, challenges, enabling factors and risks, and generate evidence-based insights to **inform future decision-making**. The Consultant is expected to balance depth and breadth appropriately, prioritizing areas of greatest relevance to organizational effectiveness, governance, sustainability and achievement of the decentralization objectives.

The evaluation will cover:

- Key processes
- Management and operational roles and responsibilities
- Relevant interdependencies
- Periodic implementation reviews
- Decision‑making and accountability arrangements
- Resourcing (financial, human, …) and efficiency
- Organizational culture, leadership, and power dynamics

Out of scope (unless otherwise specified):

- Individual programme/project impact or sectoral effectiveness.
- Detailed financial audits or compliance reviews.

## 5.Intended users of the evaluation, stakeholders & informants

The **intended users** of the evaluation findings include all Terre des hommes staff at country, regional and HQ levels and the Foundation Board, in addition to key external stakeholders, such as selected strategic and/or local partners and institutional donors.

**Key stakeholders** and informants include:

- **Country level**: country directors, selected coordinators, first-responder and junior staff, local partners
- **Regional level**: regional directors, regional coordinators and support staff
- **HQ level**: sector staff (experts, all departments)

Key informants include **former Tdh staff** who were involved in the design and/or roll-out of the decentralized organizational model.

The evaluation results will inform the Tdh decentralized organizational model standard operating procedures; these will replace the 2023 Decentralization Guidance accordingly.

## 6. Evaluation Criteria and questions

Criterion:

- Criteria : Relevance -> Question: To what extent has the Project adequately targeted the real needs of the organization, allowing for existing constraints, potential and strengths?
- Criteria : Coherence -> Question: How well does the Project fit with other similar approaches in the aid sector? What good practice can be integrated? To what extent is the cross-region system coherent, and how can it be improved?
- Criteria : Effectiveness -> Question: To what extent have the Project’s objectives been met?
- Criteria : Efficiency-> Question: Have available resources been utilized in the best way?
- Criteria : Impact-> Question: What difference does the Project make? What are its broader, long-term effects (both intended and unintended, positive or negative)?
- Criteria : Sustainability-> Question: Will the system last (foresight analysis)?

## 7. Methodology

The consultant is free to define their methodology in dialogue with the team that accompanies the evaluation; the proposed methodology will be presented in an **inception report**, which will be examined and approved by the Tdh Evaluation Steering Committee.

The proposed methodology will address the following items:

- Analytical framework (evaluation matrix)
    - Stakeholder mapping & engagement plan
    - Data collection (methods and tools)
    - Organizational model mapping
    - Analysis & synthesis
    - Judgment:

i) **options** (scenarios/future models) and

ii) resulting actionable **recommendations**

- Working plan, including a timeline

The evaluation will involve visits to Tdh Headquarters, the three Tdh Regional Offices (in Amman/Jordan, Dakar/Senegal and the Europe-Asia Region).

## 8.Deliverables

The consultant is expected to deliver clear, usable evaluation products, as follows.

- Inception (initial) report including a description of the proposed methodology, evaluation matrix, timeline and working plan, initial documentary analysis, and the proposed use of AI for analytical purposes (if any).
- Full report (methods, findings, **options** max 40 pages): v. 1.0
- Executive summary (max. 5 pages)
- Visuals (org maps, decision flows, dashboards)
- Workshop to convert options into **recommendations**.
- Final report (v. 2.0), including follow-up items and summary tables indicating the main conclusions and recommendations, separating:
    - Short-, medium- and long-term items
    - Lessons learned (including items for global standardization, those requiring regional adaptation, and those that should remain locally-defined) and roadmaps
    - **Annexes:** technical details of the evaluation (including clean and raw data, rendered anonymous), terms of reference, surveys protocols and questionnaires, protocols of interviews and observation, tables or graphics, photographs, secondary review references, persons and institutions contacted, a PowerPoint presentation of the findings and recommendations.

## 9.Timeline

- Phase I: desk review and inception report (May 2027)
- Phase II: Field work, presentation and debriefing to the Evaluation Steering Committee (July 2027)
- Phase III: analysis & report (August 2027).
- Phase IV: workshop (conversion of options into recommendations, September 2027)
- Phase V: final report and recommendations (December 2027).

## 10.Roles and responsibilities

The Decentralized Model Evaluation Steering Committee (SC) manages the evaluation at Tdh. It comprises the General Direction and Operations, and reports to the Direction Committee CODIR:

- Sponsor: Director General
- Lead: Chief of Staff
- Members:
    - HQ Operations & Child Rights (1)
    - People & Culture (1)
    - Regional Directors (3)
    - Quality & Accountability Sector (1)

The Steering Committee responsibilities include:

- Approval of the terms of reference for the evaluation;
- Selection of the successful consultant(s): the Steering Committee kindly requests the support of the P&C Department for this item (short listing);
- Pre-departure briefings and information throughout the evaluation;
- Examination and approval of the inception report and subsequent deliverables;
- Management of communications, organization and provision of the documentation required, logistic arrangements as necessary (responsibility and/or facilitation of transport, accommodation, organization of field work), translations;
- Access to material at Tdh Headquarters as necessary (working space, etc.).

The consultant will receive an onboarding briefing and commits to abiding by:

- Specific procedures (e.g. Code of Conduct, behaviour towards the media and security measures).
- Respect for the Child Protection Policy.
- The climate, travel and socio-cultural facts that could influence the collection of data.
- Ethics – confidentiality.

## 11.Profile of the Service Provider (team) qualifications and experience

The assignment requires an independent consultant with strong expertise in organizational development and efficiency, and research within humanitarian, development, and private sectors.

### Qualifications

Advanced university degree (Master's or PhD candidate) in fields such as Business and/or Organizational Development, Public Policy Development, Management Consulting, Public Administration / Nonprofit Management or equivalent.

### Experience and Expertise

The consultant should demonstrate:

- Strong academic and applied research experience
- Proven experience conducting technical assessments, mixed-method evaluations, or validation of governance systems and organizational reform, especially in decentralized and/or locally devolved models
- Experience working in a variety of cultural and business/organizational contexts
- Experience working within humanitarian, development, safeguarding, or child protection-related environments is desirable

### Skills

The consultant should possess:

- Strong analytical and technical research skills
- Excellent writing skills
- Experience in comparative analysis and evidence-based reporting
- Strong facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills
- Ability to synthesize technical findings into actionable recommendations
- Strong cultural sensitivity

### Language

Excellent written and spoken English, and excellent spoken French are required.

title: International Partnerships and Business Development Officer
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Partnerships,** **Integration and Resource Mobilisation Office (PIRMO)** leads SPC’s strategic partnerships, drives business development in support of SPC’s Strategic Plan 2022-2031, and contributes to SPC’s development effectiveness by championing an integrated approach to the way we work.

The **International Partnerships and Business Development Officer** will play a key role in supporting SPC’s strategic resource mobilisation and partnership development efforts. Working within PIRMO and in collaboration with SPC divisions and flagships. This role contributes to securing sustainable funding, enhancing and monitoring donor engagement on various finance instruments, and supporting the development of strategic partnerships. The officer will help embed UBPP within the pilot period and play a key role in the Blue Finance Mobilisation function. They will ensure consistent, high-quality engagement with key donors and partners, and support divisional efforts to align with SPC’s strategic goals and funding priorities.

**The key responsibilities of the role include the following:**

**Resource Mobilisation and Partnerships**

- Help identify and track funding opportunities aligned with SPC’s strategic goals and its flagships, more specifically the Climate change flagship and Climate finance for ocean climate nexus.
- Ensure alignment with divisional requirements, business plans and flagships supporting integrated and cross-sectoral programming.
- Assist in preparing documents and research to support funding proposals, in particular for blue economy initiatives
- Use tools and templates to support fundraising and programme development.
- Keep the funding pipeline updated and aligned with members’ needs.
- Support monitoring and coordination of new funding opportunities across SPC including a range of funding instruments and modalities.
- Help draft and format proposals and grant agreements.
- Maintain records of partnerships and engagement activities.
- Support development and implementation of the GEF-funded proposal and complementary financing pathways for Component 3, including engagement with bilateral, multilateral, philanthropic and private-sector partners

**Integration, Engagement and UBPP Support**

- Collaborate on and quality assure UBPP knowledge products for alignment with donors, SPC and members requirements.
- Help coordinate meeting and event planning and arrangements including UBPP informal working group, virtual donor roundtable and sub-regional missions.
- Collect and organise information to support integrated planning.
- Assist in linking partnership activities to UBPP process ensuring knowledge management of UBPP programme including the funding and engagement data is accurate and accessible.
- Maintain strong working relationships with stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, and civil society.

**Communication and stakeholder engagement**

- Align tasks with the Resource Mobilisation Strategy, SPC Strategic Plan and climate change flagship.
- Help coordinate member country engagement activities.
- Collect and organise information to support integrated planning.
- Assist in linking partnership activities to the UBPP process and SPC’s flagships.
- Ensure funding and engagement data is accurate and accessible.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in political or social sciences, business management, law, international relations, environmental management or a related field, is required or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- A minimum of 7 years of progressively responsible professional work experience in a project management, policy development or related role.
- Good knowledge and understanding of project design, technical cooperation, resource mobilisation and stakeholder engagement.
- Demonstrated experience in climate change, biodiversity or conservation policy development.
- Experience in managing project budgets, procurement and consultant contracts.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Good research and analytical skills.
- Able to apply sound judgement in the context of assignments given.
- Excellent computer skills (Microsoft Word and Excel).
- Ability to work self-sufficiently and self-motivate.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in English.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This vacant position is budgeted until 18 November 2029 and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **International Partnerships and Business Development Officer** is a band 9 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale.

*For a Noumea based position* – a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,350-4,092 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 483,424-590,374 (USD 4,489-5,483; EUR 4,051-4,947). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

*For a Suva based position* – a starting salary range of 2,399‒2,998 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 7,412–9,265 (USD 3,214–4,018; EUR 2,900–3,625). Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea or Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance (or subsidised housing in Noumea). Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

title: Kiwa Regional Technical Assistance Coordinator
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Climate Change and Sustainability (CCS)** division strengthens and streamlines SPC’s actions on climate change by bringing together work already undertaken by the organisation under a coherent strategic and technical leadership. In addition, it leads the actions of SPC on climate change and sustainability, works with SPC’s regional and international partners and promotes the integration of these issues into all development activities conducted by its divisions.

The **Kiwa Regional Technical Assistance Coordinator** will coordinate SPC’s delivery of the Kiwa Initiative Phase II Regional Technical Assistance, providing overall coordination of programme activities, technical oversight for ecosystem and forest restoration interventions, and ensuring effective administration and financial management of the financing agreement. The position will work closely with SPC’s Land Resources Division to support the technical quality and implementation of restoration activities and liaise with the dedicated GEDSI Adviser within the Human Rights and Social Development Division to promote inclusive, equitable and socially responsive approaches across all activities.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Coordination & Financial Management**

- Coordinating SPC’s delivery of the Kiwa Technical Assistance, ensuring coherence across restoration, GEDSI, and knowledge-sharing components.
- Acting as focal point with the Kiwa Secretariat, AFD, SPREP, and other partners.

- Coordinating with SPC’s Finance, Procurement, MEL, and Legal units to ensure compliance with SPC and donor standards.
- Ensuring timely responses to requests from AFD, the Kiwa Secretariat, and partners.

**Capacity Strengthening and Technical Oversight for Forest and Ecosystem Restoration**

- Providing technical oversight on ecosystem/forest restoration, in close partnership with LRD.
- Identifying specific needs from Kiwa’s grantees and partners.
- Guiding the design, delivery, and monitoring of the restoration-focused micro-qualification.
- Supporting targeted capacity building activities for Kiwa’s grantees and partners including national forestry/environment departments.
- Documenting lessons learned and best practices on restoration approaches.
- Ensuring restoration work integrates NbS principles and is scientifically sound and context-specific.

- Promoting Pacific-led restoration and inclusive NbS practices at regional and international events.
- Engaging with government agencies, NGOs, and training institutions to strengthen ownership and uptake.

title: Technician – Genebank
body:
## **Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Land Resources Division (LRD**) provides effective expert scientific advice, capacity building and services on conservation, development and utilization of plant genetic resources, forest and landscape management, resilient agricultural systems, diversification of livelihood strategies and access to markets to maintain ecosystem services and improve land productivity and the food, nutrition security and resilience of Pacific communities. LRD has expertise in genetic resource conservation, resilient agriculture, biosecurity, pest and disease management, agricultural extension, plant pathology, entomology and animal health. title: Myanmar - Deputy Country Director Operations & Partnership (M/F) - Yangon
body:
## About us

**Desired start date : 01/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission : 6 months**  
**Location : Yangon**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SI has been in Myanmar since 2008, first responding to the devastating Cyclone Nargis. In 2011 and 2012, SI expanded to new regions focusing on Livelihoods, Food Security, Shelter, and WASH sectors. SI is currently mainly operating in Rakhine and in Kachin States with outreach emergency capacities through its local partners in other locations. The operations are supported by a Coordination team based in Yangon.

While continuing to support the vulnerable communities suffering from a long-term protracted crisis, SI is also developing a stronger and more responsive Emergency component, either directly or through local partners, to tackle the growing needs spreading across the country.

Projects are currently funded by FCDO, ECHO, CIAA, CDCS and UN agencies with potential for development in terms of geographical coverage and activities’ scope to address the emerging needs.

As of October 2026, SI has 13 international staff and more than 200 national staff working in Myanmar to implement projects focusing on Wash, FSL and Emergency response. Projects range from immediate life-saving response (Water Scarcity in Rakhine, Emergency response to new displacements etc.) to the search for more sustainable solutions to protracted crisis (handover to communities and local organizations, capacity-building, community empowerment etc.)

## About the job

**General objective:**

Strategic Partnership Leadership: As SI shifts more programming toward partners, operationalise SI commitments, ensuring processes match partner capacities while establishing a merged partnership unit.

Operational Oversight: Supervise partner vetting, project cycles, and quality delivery across hard-to-reach access areas, integrating key cross-cutting themes.

Representation & Funding: Represent SI with stakeholders and donors while facilitating joint proposal design.

Governance & Team Management: Lead multidisciplinary teams, uphold ethical standards, ensure compliance, and manage operational risks.

**The main challenges:**

Limited access to field areas

High number of partners

New operational model for the mission

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

Establish Merged Partnership Structure: Merge existing program coordination and base partnership structures into a unified Partnership Unit under the Coordination Office to streamline team workflows and resource efficiency.

Adapt Procedures to Partner Capacity: Operationalise SI’s partnership commitments by adapting internal administrative, financial, and compliance processes to align with partners' practical capacities.

Capitalise on Partnership Experience: Review past partnership management frameworks to define clear ways of working, operational workflows, and joint technical support mechanisms.

Consolidate Team Management & Context Monitoring: Integrate and onboard the new partnership finance and program teams while establishing context monitoring for high-priority indirect management areas.

**Security constraints :**

"Limited in Yangon

All operational bases in Myanmar are now presenting medium to severe security constraints."

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCES :**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experiment in the humanitarian sector : more than 5 years

Experiment on similar positions : 3-4 years

**SKILLS :**

Technical skills :

1. Proven experience in partnership management or indirect implementation
2. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making

Transversal skills :

1. Cross-Cultural Communication & Adaptability: Proven ability to navigate diverse multicultural environments by actively observing local ways of working, adjusting interpersonal approaches, and fostering inclusive, collaborative relationships across diverse teams and institutional partners.
2. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
3. Demonstrated planning, prioritisation and organisational skills

**Language :**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Burmese (strong asset)

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 600.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

" Individual Housing pack in Yangon

Internet and telephone network are sometimes lower quality and reliability when in Myanmar (overall OK in Yangon with specific internet restrictions by the authorities)

Restaurant & social life: When in Yangon, the social life scene has shrunk a bit since 2021, but there is still a community and a diversity of options for social and outgoing life."

title: Director, People Development- CRRD
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

**The Director, People Development is responsible for planning and implementing a variety of people development initiatives for the IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department. Partnering closely with the Global Learning & Development Team and P&C Partners across CRRD, the Director, People Development, will plan and facilitate workshops, peer learning groups, facilitate talent review processes, and support other talent management and learning efforts across CRRD. CRRD people development activities must build capability and competency to achieve CRRD's strategic action plans, leadership diversity targets, and the overall development, retention, and improved internal promotion rates of top talent across CRRD.**

**Duties/Responsibilities:**

- Serve as a member of CRRD People & Culture leadership team and contribute to its strategy development and establishment of L&D priorities connected to IRCs Strategy 100 and Delivery Letter goals.
- Build and maintain trusted partnerships with senior CRRD leaders, regional directors, and country directors to ensure sustained engagement and measurable adoption of people development programs across CRRD.
- Serve as the primary voice of CRRD within the Global Learning & Development team by participating in strategy and planning sessions to ensure globally implemented programming reflects the needs, contexts, and constraints of field-based staff and leaders.
- Translate CRRD's strategic priorities — including Strategy 100, leadership diversity targets, and retention goals — into scalable learning and talent development plans, providing guidance on how programs should be adapted to varying operational contexts across a complex, globally distributed humanitarian operation.
- Partner with CRRD P&C Partners to design and deliver new leader integration and country director onboarding experiences that accelerate effectiveness and cultural alignment.
- Contextualize, communicate and drive org-wide learning and development initiatives across CRRD.
- Design and implement people development programs — including, but not limited to, talent review, succession planning, manager capability building, and P&C capacity strengthening — that equip, engage, and retain CRRD staff, managers and leaders.
- Build CRRD's talent movement and capability-building infrastructure — including workforce planning and succession readiness pipelines.
- Maintain and deliver a strategic roadmap of people development initiatives in CRRD while also remaining agile and able to deliver against last-minute and unexpected needs that may arise.
- Identify and champion the responsible use of AI tools and technologies to enhance talent development and learning and development work — improving the personalization, efficiency, and scalability of programs across CRRD's globally distributed teams — in alignment with IRC's approved AI tools and governance standards.
- Establish and track key metrics to evaluate program effectiveness and report progress to CRRD and P&C leadership.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to**: Dual reporting to Senior Director, CRRD People & Culture and Director, Global Learning and Development  
**Position directly supervises**: N/A

**Key Internal Relationships**:

- Collaborate with colleagues across the People & Culture function including all CRRD Regional P&C Directors, Gender Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (GEDI), HR Operations, Compensation & Benefits, Global Learning and Development and others to achieve meaningful impact.
- CRRD Leadership and Country People and Culture teams.

**Qualifications:**

- Minimum 8–10 years of progressive experience in learning & development, talent management, or organizational development.
- Demonstrated experience designing and implementing people development programs across a complex, matrixed organization.
- Proven ability to design and facilitate leadership and manager development programs, talent reviews, and succession planning processes.
- Experience conducting learning needs assessments and translating findings into targeted, scalable development solutions.
- Proficiency in tracking and reporting on L&D metrics and using data to evaluate and iterate program effectiveness.
- Familiarity with instructional design methodologies and adult learning principles.
- Exceptional relationship-building and influencing skills, with demonstrated ability to partner effectively with senior leaders and stakeholders across functions and geographies.
- Strong in-person and virtual facilitation skills, with experience leading workshops, peer learning groups, and leadership programs across diverse, multicultural audiences.
- Ability to navigate ambiguity and competing priorities, balancing a strategic roadmap with agile responsiveness to emerging needs.
- Deep understanding of the operational realities of field-based and humanitarian contexts, with the ability to design programs that are relevant and accessible across limited resource environments.
- Ability to work across multiple time zones and with globally distributed teams; willingness to travel internationally as needed.
- Some experience applying AI tools and technologies to talent development work — such as learning content design, program personalization, or talent/workforce analytics — preferred.
- English fluency. Proficiency in an additional core IRC language (French, Arabic, Spanish) strongly preferred.

**Compensation:** (GBP 65,785 - GBP 73,095). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Request for Proposal Independent Red Teaming and AI Safety Evaluation Open Competitive Tender
body:
**Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title Independent Red Teaming and AI Safety Evaluation

Procurement Method Open competitive tender

Assignment Type Independent organisation or specialist consultancy

Primary Market Kenya

Contract Period Approximately 10 weeks

Reporting To Head of Technology and Product

Clarification Deadline 10 November 2026

Proposal Deadline 18 November 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

Independence is a mandatory condition. The selected evaluator must not be involved in building, operating, or commercially benefiting from the systems evaluated under this assignment.

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that adolescent girls want, trust and need. We create digital-first brands and products that reach girls at scale across Africa and Asia, supporting them to make informed choices about their health, education and futures — with a particular focus on sexual and reproductive health (SRH).

Girl Effect has worked in responsible AI for several years and has published its own Ethical AI Guidelines and a Generative AI Whitepaper, co-authored sector guidance on the safe use of chatbots for social and behaviour change, and operates named accountability for AI safety — including a Failure Mode Register with safeguarding sign-off, and defined escalation protocols with service-level commitments for human follow-up. We believe that AI serving young people in the Global South must be held to the highest evidential standard, and that the organisations building such systems should not be the only ones marking their own homework. This engagement exists to put that principle into practice.

## **Background**

WAZZII is Girl Effect’s WhatsApp-based chatbot in Kenya. It provides adolescent girls and young women with confidential and non-judgemental information about their bodies, relationships and health. It also connects users to relevant products, referrals and health services, supported by a human help desk responsible for moderation and escalation.

WAZZII’s next phase will expand the use of generative AI in the girl-facing experience. This includes:

- Retrieval-grounded responses using clinically approved content;
- AI-assisted tools for human help-desk operators;
- Safeguarding and clinical escalation pathways;
- Internal evaluation of model outputs; and
- Defined policies covering content and actions that the system must never produce.

Girl Effect seeks an independent partner to test whether these safeguards perform as intended and identify risks that may not have been detected through internal evaluation.

The selected partner must be separate from the organisations developing or operating the systems being tested.

## **Objective**

The objective is to conduct a focused and independent red-team evaluation of WAZZII’s girl-facing generative AI capability.

The assignment will:

- Identify safety, safeguarding, clinical and technical vulnerabilities;
- Test whether the system recognises and safely escalates relevant risks;
- Assess whether existing evaluations and controls adequately reflect real-world use;
- Produce reproducible test cases that Girl Effect can rerun;
- Rank findings by severity, likelihood and potential impact; and
- Provide practical and prioritised recommendations for remediation and future evaluation.

The core assignment is a single time-bound evaluation. Remediation re-testing, review of agentic designs and periodic testing will be priced separately as optional extensions.

## **What You will do**

The core engagement runs over an indicative ten weeks. All work follows Girl Effect’s Ethical AI Guidelines, data policy and safeguarding policy: testing is conducted against staging environments using synthetic personas, no real user data is accessed or collected, data collection is minimised throughout, and no safeguarding case content is handled at any point. Girl Effect will provide staging access, including programmatic (API) access to the conversational endpoint, supporting automated test harnesses; testing may be conducted fully remotely, with no in-country presence required. Key activities include:

Phase 1 — Orientation and test design (indicatively weeks 1–3)

- Focused desk review of Girl Effect’s evaluation framework, red-line policies and escalation protocol — sufficient to design a well-targeted test plan, not a standalone audit
- Co-scoping of the scenario taxonomy and severity rubric with Girl Effect’s AI Ethics Officer and safeguarding leads, and agreement of the responsible-disclosure protocol for critical findings

Phase 2 — Red-teaming sprint (indicatively weeks 3–8)

- A structured, tool-supported testing exercise against the girl-facing GenAI experience in staging, combining adversarial and realistic non-adversarial scenarios and producing logged, machine-readable, re-runnable test cases, prioritising: clinically incorrect or harmful health advice; failure to recognise and escalate safeguarding disclosures; jailbreaks, prompt injection and policy circumvention; and age-inappropriate content
- Testing across the languages and code-switching patterns of real users (including Kiswahili and Sheng); local-language competence may be provided by the partner or in pairing with Girl Effect's own team
- Stress-testing of the human-escalation pathway, primarily with realistic non-adversarial scenarios (genuine distress, disclosure and clinical-concern personas where the system should hand over without being attacked): does it hand over to the help desk when it should

Phase 3 — Findings and briefing (indicatively weeks 8–10)

- A severity-ranked findings report with reproducible test cases, handed over so Girl Effect’s team can re-run them continuously after the engagement ends
- A findings briefing for Girl Effect leadership, with prioritised recommendations — including what a fuller evaluation should cover next and at what cadence

Optional priced extensions (quoted separately, commissioned at Girl Effect’s discretion)

- Re-test of remediated critical findings
- Architecture-level adversarial review of agentic system designs (threat-modelling autonomy, tool use and failure modes before deployment)
- Periodic re-testing and pre-launch adversarial gates for major releases

## **Deliverables**

Deliverable Description Indicative timing

Inception note & test plan Confirmed methodology, scenario taxonomy and

severity rubric, staging/access arrangements,

ethics and data-handling approach,

responsible-disclosure protocol Week 3

Red-team findings report Severity-ranked, reproducible findings

from the adversarial sprint, including

escalation-pathway results; test cases handed over

for continuous internal re-use Week 8

Leadership briefing & recommendations Findings briefing with prioritised recommendations

and proposed scope/cadence for future

independent evaluation Week 10

## **Duration and Working Arrangements**

The core engagement is expected to run for approximately 10 weeks.

Testing may be completed remotely. No in-country presence is required unless separately agreed.

Girl Effect will provide:

- Approved access to the staging environment;
- Programmatic access to the conversational endpoint where available;
- Relevant documentation and evaluation materials;
- Named technical, safeguarding and programme focal points; and
- Consolidated feedback on deliverables.

The partner will:

- Participate in a weekly progress meeting;
- Maintain a shared delivery tracker and risk register;
- Use secure communication and evidence-sharing channels;
- Escalate critical issues immediately;
- Protect access credentials and evaluation materials; and
- Manage its personnel and delivery approach independently.

## **Independence and Conflicts of Interest**

Independence is a mandatory condition of award.

The bidder must:

- Have no current contract to build or operate the system being evaluated;
- Have no commercial interest in the evaluation achieving a particular outcome;
- Disclose any current or previous relationship with Girl Effect’s AI, platform or technology suppliers;
- Disclose any relevant relationship held during the previous 24 months;
- Identify any tools or models being evaluated in which it has a financial interest; and
- Explain how any potential conflict will be managed.

Girl Effect will determine whether a disclosed relationship affects the bidder’s eligibility or independence.

## **Who You Are**

The successful bidder should demonstrate:

- Experience independently red-teaming deployed AI systems rather than only evaluating standalone models.
- Experience with conversational AI, retrieval-augmented generation and multi-turn systems.
- Experience in health, safeguarding-sensitive or other high-risk contexts.
- Experience working with adolescent or youth-facing digital services.
- Strong knowledge of AI safety, responsible AI and model evaluation.
- Ability to build automated, machine-readable and rerunnable testing harnesses.
- Understanding of human escalation and moderation workflows.
- Ability to test English, Kiswahili and Sheng directly or through a credible quality-controlled approach.
- Experience working in Kenya, Africa or comparable Global South contexts.
- Strong security, confidentiality and responsible-disclosure practices.
- Excellent analytical, technical-reporting and leadership-presentation capability.

The proposed team should include named individuals with appropriate AI evaluation, technical, safeguarding and language expertise.

## **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Bidders must submit separate technical and financial proposals (Max 10 pages).

### **Technical Proposal**

It should include:

- Understanding of the assignment;
- Proposed methodology and testing tools;
- Proposed scenario taxonomy and coverage;
- Approach to automated and manual testing;
- Approach to safeguarding and escalation testing;
- Language and cultural-context capability;
- Data-handling and information-security approach;
- Responsible-disclosure process;
- Workplan and team structure;
- Relevant experience and comparable assignments;
- Key assumptions, dependencies, limitations and exclusions;
- Independence and conflict-of-interest declaration;
- Three client references; and
- One redacted example of a relevant findings report.

### **Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal must be submitted in USD and include:

- A fixed price for the core 10-week engagement;
- A cost breakdown by phase and deliverable;
- Personnel roles, daily rates and level of effort;
- Applicable taxes shown separately;
- Tools, licences and third-party costs;
- Reimbursable expenses shown separately;
- Day rates for each optional extension; and
- Clear assumptions, exclusions and conditions.

## **Evaluation**

Proposals will be assessed in the following order:

1. Pre-screening;
2. Technical evaluation;
3. Pitch, demonstration or clarification stage, where required; and
4. Financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criterion**

- Relevant AI red-teaming and system-evaluation experience: 25%
- Quality, coverage and practicality of the proposed methodology: 25%
- Proposed team and safeguarding or AI-safety capability: 10%
- Language, local-context and affected-community perspective: 10%

Technical Total 70%

- Financial proposal and overall value for money 30%

Total 100%

Girl Effect may request written clarifications, invite shortlisted bidders to a pitch or technical demonstration, conduct reference checks and due diligence, or request a best-and-final offer.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: **4 November 2026**
- Questions/Clarification Deadline: **10th November 2026**
- Consolidated FAQ shared with all prospective bidders: **13th November 2026**
- Deadline for proposal submission: **18th November 2026**

### **Clarification Process**

Bidders may submit clarification questions to suppliers@girleffect.org by 10th November 2026

The email subject should state:

Clarification Question –**Independent AI Red-Team Evaluation**

To ensure a fair and transparent open-tender process:

- Girl Effect will not provide substantive answers to all bidders.
- All relevant questions and responses will be compiled into a consolidated FAQ.
- The FAQ will not identify the organisation that submitted each question.
- The consolidated FAQ will be shared with all prospective bidders through the same publication or communication channels used for the RFP.
- Bidders are responsible for reviewing the FAQ and any formal tender updates before submitting their proposals.
- Verbal information or guidance will not amend the RFP unless confirmed by Girl Effect in writing.

Girl Effect may decline to answer questions received after the clarification deadline.

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting:** The successful bidder will sign Girl Effect’s standard services agreement, statement of work and applicable data-processing and information-security documentation.
- **Payment:** Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and written acceptance of agreed deliverables. Girl Effect may withhold payment for incomplete, defective or unapproved work.
- **Pricing:** The agreed implementation pricing will remain fixed unless a change is approved through the formal written change-control process.
- **Expenses:** Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable. Reimbursable expenses must be supported by appropriate documentation.
- **Intellectual Property:** Girl Effect will own all foreground intellectual property, deliverables, source code, configurations, designs and documentation created specifically under the engagement, subject to agreed treatment of pre-existing tools and third-party materials.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The partner must protect Girl Effect’s confidential information and personal data and comply with applicable data-protection requirements.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference, safeguarding, information-security and compliance checks. The successful bidder must comply with Girl Effect’s code of conduct, safeguarding and anti-fraud requirements.
- **Subcontracting:** No material part of the assignment may be subcontracted without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The lead bidder remains responsible for all subcontracted work.
- **Warranties and Defects:** Bidders should propose a warranty period during which defects in accepted deliverables will be corrected at no additional cost.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Bidders must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.
- **Tender Costs:** Girl Effect will not reimburse costs incurred in preparing or submitting a proposal or participating in clarification, pitch or negotiation stages.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend, suspend or cancel the procurement; reject any or all proposals; award the full or partial scope; award in phases; or make no award.
- **No Commitment:** Publication of this RFP does not constitute a commitment to enter into a contract.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes submissions from qualified organisations that meet the stated regulatory, technical and service requirements.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

title: Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services
source: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
body:
**Nature of Consultancy:** Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services

**Place of Performance:** Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment (with mission travel to Port-au-Prince and designated departmental hubs). Any required mission travel, including its dates, arrangements, security requirements, and reimbursement of agreed expenses, shall be specified or separately agreed in writing.

**Level of Effort:** Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days/hours, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

**Type of Contract:** Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, deliverables, and estimated levels of effort agreed between COAR and the Consultant.

**Timeframe:** The anticipated term of this consultancy is from 01 December 2026 to 31 December 2027, subject to execution of the applicable agreement. The term establishes the period during which assignments may be agreed; it does not create an obligation to provide or accept assignments, guarantee a minimum workload, or require continuous availability. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written agreement.

**Primary Point of Contact:** COAR's designated Haiti Team Lead, acting as the contact for agreeing assignment requirements, coordinating necessary project inputs, clarifying deliverables, addressing technical queries and reviewing completed outputs against the agreed scope. This role is for assignment coordination and does not confer authority to direct the Consultant's day-to-day working methods or exercise line-management authority over the Consultant.

**Overview:** This Scope of Work (SoW) outlines the specific senior technical consultancy assignment with the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The Consultant may be commissioned to provide specialist analytical and advisory services for an in-depth study examining the systemic, historical, and multidimensional crisis in Haiti. Commissioned in the context of UNDP and UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) strategic planning, the study is intended to establish an evidence-based baseline to guide conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and sustainable recovery initiatives across Haiti. The assignment may include the preparation of a comprehensive, formally published biennial report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks, accompanied by a strategic intervention approach for the United Nations system. The Consultant's responsibility shall be limited to the agreed research, analytical, drafting, advisory, and facilitation outputs. Decisions concerning publication, institutional endorsement, strategic adoption, and implementation shall remain with COAR and the commissioning institutions.

**Nature of the consultancy:** This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

**About COAR:** COAR is an independent social enterprise that directly supports practitioners, policymakers, and donors by facilitating humanitarian and development interventions in complex, fragile, and high-risk environments. COAR delivers neutral and objective research and analysis, which identifies - but does not influence - local stakeholders, relationships, interests, and analyzes broader political, economic, social, and security dynamics and trends. COAR research leverages social media, personal networks, field research teams, and local experts in order to map and translate the local human context; COAR analysis synthesizes and studies this data in order to inform both programmatic and strategic decision-making, reduce security and conflict sensitivity risks, and increase the impact of humanitarian, development, stabilization, peace-building, and peacekeeping initiatives.

**Objectives**

For the specific study assignment, the Consultant may be commissioned to:

- Conduct an analysis of historical trends and trajectories of Haiti’s systemic, social, community, political, and economic crisis to develop a comprehensive understanding of underlying structural dynamics;
- Analyze the multidimensional drivers of fragility and crisis across national, departmental, and cross-border domains;
- Map crises and trace underlying drivers of distinct forms of violence (criminal, gang-driven, political, and gender-based) to elucidate crisis systems;
- Evaluate crisis dynamics through intersectional gender, generational, and social inequality perspectives, highlighting the contributions and protection of women and youth in conflict prevention and mediation;
- Review and assess past and ongoing conflict prevention and peacebuilding interventions supported by the UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) and key multilateral/bilateral partners;
- Propose a tailored intervention approach for the United Nations system anchored in conflict prevention and peacebuilding principles; and
- Where included in the agreed assignment, provide substantive input into the preparation of an inclusive multi-stakeholder validation workshop, including contributing to validation discussions and moderating specified panel sessions.

**Activities and Key Responsibilities**

The following activities describe potential services under the study assignment. The specific activities to be performed, their estimated effort, and the associated outputs shall be confirmed in writing before commencement.

1\. Analytical Framing & Methodological Design

- Develop an analytical framework and research matrix tailored to the Haitian operational context, integrating OECD DAC peacebuilding criteria and UN Integrated Strategic Framework (ISF) objectives.
- Formulate and calibrate qualitative and quantitative research instruments, including semi-structured Key Informant Interview (KII) guides, Focus Group Discussion (FGD) protocols, and secondary assessment templates.
- Incorporate strict Conflict Sensitivity, Do No Harm, and data protection protocols, reflecting localized security constraints and protection considerations in gang-controlled and fragile environments.

2\. Multidimensional Fragility, Violence & Hotspot Mapping

- Trace historical fault lines, institutional degradation, and economic patterns driving instability across Port-au-Prince and outlying departments (e.g., Artibonite, Nord, Grand'Anse).
- Document geographic conflict hotspots, illicit trade flows, arms proliferation corridors, and cross-border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Assess formal and informal mechanisms, social cohesion structures, customary dispute-resolution mechanisms, and local resilience dynamics fostering community stability.

3\. Intersectional Analysis & PBF Portfolio Assessment

- Analyze structural socio-economic inequalities, youth recruitment vulnerabilities, and gender-based violence (GBV) as systemic drivers of fragility.
- Conduct a focused desk review and stakeholder assessment of UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects and partner peacebuilding programming in Haiti, evaluating impact, lessons learned, and systemic gaps.
- Identify practical entry points and age- and gender-sensitive recommendations to strengthen the leadership of women and youth in peacebuilding architectures.

4\. Report Authoring & UN Strategic Intervention Approach

- Prepare and coordinate the analytical synthesis and drafting of the formal, publication-ready baseline report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks in Haiti.
- Draft a pragmatic, forward-looking UN intervention approach that connects empirical research findings with strategic programming across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus.
- Integrate technical review comments from COAR leadership, UNDP, PBF, and institutional counterparts into final publishable outputs to the extent that such comments are provided within the agreed review process and schedule. The Consultant shall identify and discuss any material changes to the agreed scope or analytical conclusions that arise during review.

5\. Stakeholder Workshop Coordination & Panel Moderation

- Where specified in the assignment, provide substantive recommendations on the agenda and content of the national multi-stakeholder validation workshop.
- Deliver technical presentations on analytical findings, methodological approaches, and strategic recommendations to UN leadership, civil society, and international partners, at agreed events or sessions.
- Moderate thematic panel discussions during inclusive consultations to cultivate national ownership and partnership consensus where the relevant sessions, preparation requirements, and expected level of effort have been agreed in writing.

**Expected Results and Deliverables**

The primary result of this assignment will be a publicly available, formally published large-scale report examining fragilities and risks related to peacebuilding and development in Haiti. The report serves three primary purposes:

1. Understanding Haiti’s Crisis: Deepening multilateral and national understanding of the systems, drivers, and trajectories underlying the crisis.
2. Strategic & Programmatic Decision-Making: Informing conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and HDP nexus resource allocation.
3. Advocacy & Dialogue: Supporting continuous, multilevel dialogue among national authorities, civil society, and international partners.

**Required Experience and Expertise**

- Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s or Ph.D.) in Peace and Conflict Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, or a related discipline required.
- UN System Experience: Required minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience advising or implementing peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and stabilization programming within or alongside the UN System (e.g., UNDP, BINUH, DPO/DPPA, IOM, or UN Country Teams).
- Country & Contextual Expertise: Desired analytical or operational track record in Haiti, with nuanced understanding of Haitian political history, gang territorial dynamics, departmental socio-economic disparities, and border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Analytical Capabilities: Proven track record conducting complex conflict analyses, fragility assessments, and intersectional studies focusing on gender, youth, and structural inequalities.
- Facilitation & Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue: Proven experience designing and moderating high-level validation workshops, roundtables, and policy panels involving government counterparts, UN leadership, and grassroots civil society organizations.
- Languages: Professional proficiency in both French and English (written and spoken) is required; fluency or working knowledge of Haitian Creole (Kreyòl) is a distinct asset.

**Safeguarding, Ethics, and Confidentiality**

In performing the Services, the Consultant shall comply with COAR’s Code of Conduct, any applicable Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA), and safeguarding requirements that COAR identifies in writing as applicable to external consultants and relevant to the accepted assignment. In light of the delicate security and protection environment in Haiti, the Consultant shall conduct agreed research and stakeholder interactions in accordance with Do No Harm principles, informant anonymity, data protection protocols, and UN standards on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client. The Consultant shall promptly notify COAR of any material ethical, safeguarding, data-protection, or security concern arising in the course of the assignment, while retaining responsibility for the independent professional judgment required to perform the Services safely and ethically.

All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client, subject to the terms of the applicable consultancy agreement, including any agreed provisions concerning pre-existing materials, third-party materials, research data, intellectual property, and permitted retention of records.

title: Business & Human Rights Data Analyst - MyVox Product Owner
body:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

 In Cambodia, GRC works with trade unions and civil society organisations to strengthen labour rights accountability in the garment and apparel sector. It supports garment workers and their representatives to document and monitor labour rights violations, and to use that evidence to secure remedy through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, and international accountability routes. Alongside monitoring, the project delivers awareness-raising, community building and tailored legal aid.

We are seeking a Business & Human Rights Data Analyst to join our team. The Data Analyst supports the analysis of data collected through MyVox (including the mobile/web app and the live dashboard). The role is responsible for managing, analysing, and interpreting data collected through the mobile and web application to provide actionable insights that will inform advocacy and awareness-raising efforts.

**The Role**

- Collect, organize, and clean data from the MyVox application, ensuring data integrity and accuracy by identifying and rectifying any data anomalies or errors.
- Perform statistical analysis and interpret the results to identify trends, patterns, and insights.
- Use data visualization tools to present data in a clear and actionable manner.
- Develop quarterly comprehensive reports and presentations based on data analysis.
- Collaborate with the development team to ensure data-related issues are addressed promptly.
- Provide ongoing support for data-related inquiries and troubleshooting.
- Support and contribute to the ongoing development of the team’s work by identifying potential areas for future activity and collaboration, consistent with strategic priorities.
- Develop documentation and guides for data management and analysis processes.

**Your Background**

- Bachelor's degree in data science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field. A master’s degree is preferred.
- 5+ years experience as a Data Analyst or in a similar role.
- Strong proficiency in data analysis tools and software (e.g., Python, R, SQL, Excel).
- Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex data clearly and concisely.
- Experience working with non-profit organizations is a plus.
- Work or academic experience focused on topics related to peacebuilding, conflict, human rights, and/or global affairs (or similar).
- Ability to work remotely with limited supervision.
- Excellent organization and time management skills.
- Good judgement and high attention to detail.
- Fluency in English - both written and verbal skills.

title: Mental Health Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**DESCRIPTION:**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 to respond to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of refugees from Darfur into eastern Chad. Assistance to Sudanese refugees expanded to include the management of eleven camps in the east and one camp in the west, providing support to refugees and local communities in the areas of health, nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation. In 2012, IRC expanded its geographic coverage to Guéra Province, where the organization currently works in five health districts and provides malnutrition prevention and treatment services to the local population, as well as family planning, response, and prevention activities related to gender-based violence (GBV). In May 2016, IRC established a presence in Lac Province to respond to the crisis caused by Boko Haram. In its 2022–2024 Strategic Action Plan, IRC Chad is committed to continuing to provide essential humanitarian services in health, nutrition, and protection/GBV, while improving the economic well-being and strengthening the resilience of beneficiaries, particularly women and girls. IRC Chad will continue to work closely with and support government actors and line ministries in key sectors to ensure that IRC’s actions are integrated into national policies, thereby fostering greater ownership of the initiatives undertaken.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Senior Health Coordinator, the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist based in Hadjer Hadid will be responsible for the overall management and implementation of a high-quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) program in all of IRC’s areas of operation, and more specifically in refugee camps. The Mental Health Specialist will work closely with the Ministry of Public Health’s mental health program, UNHCR, IRC, HIAS, and all members of the mental health working group in Chad to facilitate the coordination of mental health interventions in the country and strengthen their integration into the minimum package of services provided in health centers and hospitals. The mental health and psychosocial support specialist will supervise health workers in providing prevention, diagnosis, and treatment services for patients with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, using the guidelines of the WHO/UNHCR Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP), and will train new providers on the mhGAP model. She/he will develop standard operating procedures for providing psychological support and psychiatric care, as well as psychosocial support through group psychoeducation and community-based programs. She/he will represent IRC at all mental health working group meetings.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Program Coordination:
- Coordinate mental health needs assessments;
- Organize regular meetings on mental health with health program managers and the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) team, in collaboration with other technical coordinators;
- Ensure that mental health and psychosocial support are fully integrated into the various sectors of the health program (primary health care, sexual and reproductive health, nutrition, environmental health) and other IRC programs (WPE and ERD);
- Coordinate the implementation of all interventions in the field of mental health and psychosocial support
- Contribute to capacity building for the MHPSS team to enable them to effectively carry out their duties and ensure a smooth transition;
- Participate in capacity building for local partners (Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, United Nations agencies, etc.) in the field of mental health and psychosocial support;
- Contribute to the development of new funding proposals for mental health and psychosocial support;

**Evaluation and Monitoring of the Quality of Clinical and Community Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services**

- Conduct a situational analysis to identify and assess mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) needs in IRC’s areas of operation in Chad
- Provide formative supervision and/or refresher training for healthcare providers and community health workers.
- Provide specialized mental health consultations and psychosocial support to people with specific needs, including survivors of gender-based violence
- Support the organization of community-based services to improve care, follow-up, and referrals between the community and health facilities.
- Conduct formative supervision of health workers to improve the quality of mental health services provided in health facilities and the community using IRC supervision checklists.
- Ensure that essential medicines and psychotropic drugs approved by the Ministry of Public Health (MSP)/WHO are available in health facilities and that they are properly stored and prescribed by providers.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, Learning, and Reporting**

- In collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator, conduct a monthly analysis of mental health and psychosocial support data and share the database and report with the Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribute to improving the quality of periodic health program reports and donor reports.
- Support the monitoring and evaluation framework for the mental health program through regular data analysis and supervision of program activities in the field;
- Document lessons learned, innovative approaches, and the generation of information and evidence to contribute to IRC’s overall learning;
