- Provide subject matter expertise and technical advisory support to other departments and initiatives within HFHI.

**5. Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery Support (5%)**

Provide advisory support to integrate climate risk reduction and resilience into disaster preparedness, response and recovery efforts

**Key Responsibilities**

Work with the Housing Disaster Risk and Resilience (HDRR) team on climate risk reduction measures in response and recovery

Provide technical input on risk-informed approaches to recovery planning and implementation

Support alignment of recovery interventions with long-term resilience objectives

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Risk Reduction, Urban Planning, Engineering, Development Studies, or a related field
- Minimum 5–7 years of relevant experience in climate resilience, DRR, or risk-informed programming, preferably in the Asia-Pacific region
- Demonstrated experience supporting multi-country programs and working with decentralized teams
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, and resilience approaches in housing, settlements, or community development
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, resilience, and mitigation approaches in housing, settlements, infrastructure, or community development.
- Experience in humanitarian, recovery, or nexus programming is an asset
- Experience in donor engagement, proposal development, or climate finance is an advantage

**Key Skills & Competencies**

- Strong technical expertise in climate adaptation and the built environment
- Sound understanding of climate mitigation, with the ability to understand where synergies and tradeoffs exist between mitigation and adaptation (especially where these impact affordability)
- Ability to translate technical concepts into practical, field-oriented guidance
- Proven advisory, facilitation, and capacity-building skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English (regional languages an asset)
- Strong cross-cultural collaboration skills and ability to work in matrixed environments
- Willingness and ability to travel within the Asia-Pacific region

**Core Behavioral Competencies**

- Commitment to HFHI’s mission, values, equity, and safeguarding principles
- Collaboration and partnership mindset
- Learning oriented and solution focused
- Accountability and integrity

**Working Conditions**

- Regional role with frequent collaboration across multiple countries and time zones.
- Periodic travel to Country Offices and Country Offices, including fragile, climate-vulnerable, and disaster-affected contexts.
- Ability and willingness to travel within the Asia-Pacific region as required.

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

title: Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** will provide strategic and technical expertise in the design, development, governance, and deployment of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data systems, including databases, digital platforms, and AI-enabled solutions. Support evidence-based management and strengthen capacity across Pacific Island countries through innovative, standardised, and sustainable data systems.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Develop and maintain high-quality regional and national coastal fisheries and aquaculture databases and information systems and provide training in their use**

- Develops, maintains and updates the regional coastal fisheries (science, management and development) and aquaculture databases including training in the use of databases, data extraction and analysis
- Develops new web and mobile applications for the regional and national databases in line with country needs and the needs of the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff
- Develops and assists in maintaining national databases based on the regional databases and additional modules.
- Develops specific queries for data extraction and analysis as required by countries or the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff.
- Promotes and encourages the use of standard databases and information systems across the region for coastal fisheries and aquaculture data, and countries to providing the data they collect for back-up and storage at SPC.
- Identifies and develops linkages between the coastal fisheries and oceanic fisheries databases in collaboration with oceanic fisheries statistics and data collection section.
- Identifies ways to better use GIS and remote sensing products in relation to the analysis of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data.

**Practical assistance to members in the designing and targeting of appropriate awareness raising and educational information**

- Develops training materials on data entry, cleaning and extraction.
- Assists with developing and maintaining the website for the CFAP with the Information Unit to assist with the dissemination of information in general.
- Provides input to awareness raising and educational materials focused on coastal fisheries science and/or management or livelihoods and aquaculture

**Develop Artificial Intelligence based tools and models for data collection**

- Improves coastal fisheries and aquaculture data collection using photos and videos automatically processed by computer vision and artificial intelligence
- Develops and trains models to calibrate and reproject pictures for measurement from picture
- Develops and trains models to automate measurements of fishes and invertebrates for the various types of measurements
- Develops and trains models for species identification

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration in coastal fisheries and aquaculture**

- Develops links with other CROP agencies and NGOs in regard to database needs and design for coastal fisheries and aquaculture
- Advocates at global forums on behalf of the Pacific region sectoral interests
- Develops and promotes collaborations within the CFAP on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.
- Works closely with other sections of CFAP to ensure smooth implementation of projects.

**Administration and communication**

- Assists the CFAP Deputy Director and Section heads, to include information and database needs in the annual work plans and work plan reports for each Section, consistent with the strategic plan.
- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, and Divisional reports for CRGA.
- Produces reports for all activities undertaken in the appropriate format for the activity including technical reports and trip reports, and input to funding proposals, donor reports.
- Manage, develop and train direct report.
- Fills in for senior staff when they are on leave or duty travel, when required

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Master’s in computer science, database development or a related field/discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years’ of demonstrated experience in database management, project management and software development associated with the successful implementation of medium- to large-scale web and desktop application systems.
- At least 8 years’ of demonstrated experience in the use of Microsoft products, both as a user and developer, in particular, (i) experience in software engineering, (ii) programming in client-server environments in C# with MS Visual Studio, (iii) ASP.NET Core and single page web applications with MS Visual Studio (C#, JavaScript and angularjs), (iv) database technologies (preferably SQL Server) and other database formats, (v) development of mobile application in C# (.NET MAUI).
- Demonstrated experience with (i) producing system and user manual documentation, (ii) user training and (iii) ongoing technical support for deployed applications.
- Demonstrated problem solving skills, detail orientation, and ability to multi-task.

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and negotiate with people from different ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds.
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 5,012-6,169 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 723,251-890,185 (USD 6,717-8,267; EUR 6,061-7,460). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

title: Finance & HR Manager
body:
**MSF is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. We are a non-profit, self-governed worldwide movement of more than 63,000 people.**

**We provide emergency medical assistance during armed conflict, natural disasters, outbreaks of deadly diseases and assist those who are excluded from healthcare. MSF delivers care based on need and when we see injustice, we speak out. We are an organization that remains impartial, knowledgeable, and effective, and this is what makes the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect.**

**Finance & HR Manager - Country Programmes**

**French speaker**

**Based in country programmes of MSF-OCA**

The Fin/HR Manager is responsible for the implementation of Human Resources policies in the project and the Administrative Management of all staff working in the project (including those recruited locally and internationally), along with the proper implementation of financial administration, management and control in the project.

This job description provides a framework for the main responsibilities and primary activities of the position, it is not all-encompassing. Therefore, the responsibilities and activities of the position may differ from those described in this job description due to organizational and operational needs.

**Objectives and responsibilities of the position**

- In close coordination with the Project Coordinator and the HR Coordinator, calculate the HR operational needs and the associated budget to efficiently ensure the project's required sizing and capabilities and facilitate budget follow-up.
- Plan, supervise and ensure the implementation of the staffing processes (including recruitment, training, briefing, induction, evaluation, development and communication) of the project staff, in close coordination with the HRCo.
- Take ownership of recruitment processes by ensuring effective hiring practices, integrating safeguarding measures at every stage, and strengthening staff capabilities, engagement, contribution to mission objectives, and commitment to MSF values.
- Supervise, coach and develop the Finance and HR team, ensuring appropriate delegation, performance follow-up and capacity building.
- Advise on set-up and updating the project's organizational chart and job descriptions and assisting the Project Coordinator, and/or team leaders and supervisors to draw up annual holiday planning and staff shifts in order to forecast HR needs and to ensure HR availability for the project activities.
- Ensure hiring, carry out amendments and contract termination formalities for employees at project level, according to labour local laws, managing individual employee files, informing them on their rights and preparing all mandatory tax declarations, in order to ensure legal compliance of the project activities.
- Supervise/perform payroll procedures, ensuring correct entry of all data related to monthly salary calculation of employees of the project.
- In close collaboration with the Project Coordinator and HRCo, look for options to avoid/solve possible labour conflicts in the project.
- Is responsible for all movements and/or accommodation of staff in the project.
- Ensure that MSF staff who have financial responsibilities are aware of and comply with local finance procedures, including those related to security.
- Ensure that project finance activities are carried out in line with OCA and mission finance policies & procedures, for example cash & safe management, advances management, authorizations (expenses and payments), payments (cash, bank & cheque), cash flow management, etc.
- Is responsible for assessing and suggesting mitigation measures of the financial risks of the project.
- Ensure that reliable internal control systems are in place, and financial ethics are respected within the project.
- Ensure proper and timely day-to-day bookkeeping takes place in the accounting software per MSF OCA Chart of accounts
- Ensure proper bookkeeping support documentation (hardcopy invoices/receipts, PO/PL/contract as applicable) is available for each bookkeeping entry.
- Ensure that daily and monthly bookkeeping closure takes place in line with the standard procedure, with due quality and on time.
- Support Project Coordinator and the Finance Coordinator with budgeting and monthly budget control activities, in order to ensure that funds are used in line with last approved budgets.

**Requirements**

- A degree in finance, management (business, HR) or administration is desirable.
- Essential working experience of at least five years in relevant and similar jobs.
- MSF or other NGO experience is desirable.
- Working proficiency in English and French (minimum B2 or equivalent) are required.
- Computer literacy (word, excel, internet) is essential.
- Knowledge of HR and Financial (MSF) software or willingness to learn.
- Availability for project durations of 6-9-12 months depending on operational needs.
- Willingness and ability to work in high insecurity zones and emergency responses.

**Assets**

- A good command of Arabic and/or Spanish language.

**Information and Application**

If you recognise yourself in this profile and meet the requirements, we encourage you to apply directly via the Apply button on this page and upload the following documents:

- Your most recent CV (in English) not exceeding 3 pages
- A cover letter explaining your motivation to work with MSF

***Female candidates who meet the requirements are strongly encouraged to apply.***

If you are interested and would like to have additional information, please contact Recruitment, recruitment@amsterdam.msf.org.

title: Program Development and Awards Advisor, WACAR
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***The IRC is seeking two (2) Program Development & Award Advisors. These positions are open to candidates in the West and Central Africa Region (WACAR), or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply.***

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD**.** The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**West and Central Africa Regional Overview**

The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR) supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches.

WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The regional team responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the PDAAs oversee a diverse portfolio of awards across the humanitarian, recovery, and development sectors. PDAAs liaise with country programs, HQ departments and donor contacts to ensure high-quality guidance and support to country offices throughout the award lifecycle.

These roles will support country programs in the West and Central Africa region (WACAR) with donor compliance, award management, and producing high-quality donor deliverables. They will advise on IRC’s partnership system (PEERS), manage donor relationships including with HQ counterparts.

In addition, these roles will support WACAR country programs in securing funding for their programmes, through supporting and leading pursuit of new funding opportunities, in line with IRC’s Business Development Strategy. Support includes all phases of the business development process, from opportunity identification to contract signature, including pre-positioning, partnerships building, proposal development, and due diligence phases.

Successful candidates will have a strong track record of contributing to new humanitarian and development funding opportunities, deep knowledge of donor rules and regulations, and experience collaborating with local partner organizations.

**Scope and Authority**

These roles have no line management responsibilities.

**Key Working Relationships**

These positions will report jointly to the Senior Program and Awards Advisor (SPAA) and the Head of Business Development (HBD) for the WACAR region and work closely with RPAS team members, country program grants and partnership teams, and across all teams within the Awards Management Unit, Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, Technical Excellence, and other key departments within IRC. PDAAs also serve as donor and partner points of contact as applicable per region.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

***Awards Management and Compliance***

- Manage a portfolio of awards for the WACAR region as assigned.
- Provide timely support on narrative reporting and post-award deliverables, guiding country offices on amendments, modifications, and submissions while collaborating with technical and financial staff.
- Provide support on budget realignments, changes in scope, NCEs, and other amendments for project elements not captured at proposal stage or emerging needs.
- Serve as first point of contact for country program-based awards staff to problem solve, guide and advise them on compliance post-award issues within the mentioned portfolio and to act as a connecting point between country program and other AMU teams to facilitate the timely flow of key information between them.
- Manage donor relationships by maintaining communication on contractual issues, updates on program implementation and following up on compliance queries and securing changes and approvals as needed.
- With support from the Program & Awards Officer (PAO), guide and coach country offices on partner management policies and PEER system compliance, and review and process sub-grants/partnership agreements. Coordinate with the Sub-awards and Partnerships (S&P) team as needed.
- Provide support to and monitor projects to ensure compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, project implementation meetings and targeted calls following specific donor internal guidelines and IRC established processes.
- In collaboration with other regional team members, monitor award spending and help problem-solve for under-/over-spending. Partner with country programs and regional team as needed, to address implementations challenges.
- Provide technical advice to country offices on ad-hoc queries on donor compliance issues in coordination with AMU’s Compliance and Policy team on non-routine and high-level compliance matters and escalate to leadership for support as needed.
- Take part in meetings and calls with country teams where required to provide support and collaborate closely on specific issues related to donor compliance, submissions and/or monitoring/award management.
- Ensure lessons learned from finalized projects are fed back into new Business Development.
- Advise and support country programs appropriately to enable them to successfully follow internal IRC policies and procedures and maintain the integrity of awards-related data (e.g. OTIS, PEERS).
- Stay informed about programmatic issues and security and political developments affecting implementation.
- Coordinate with other members of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) Team and other AMU members for information sharing and establishing a coherent awards support.
- Ensure proper donor-related and contractual documentation to support compliance and audit readiness (including maintaining up-to-date, organized award files).
- Participate in the recruitment of and the onboarding of new CP Grants Coordinators/Heads of Grants teams.
- Contribute to the development of training materials, and deliver training to in-country staff, as required and in coordination with the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and Program and Award Support (PAS) team leaders. In coordination with the DAM and PAS leaders, develop and maintain work-processes and checklists for award implementation and report review, as well as record lessons learned.
- Onboard new country office Grants and Partnerships staff and new PAS team members to assigned donors, policies and/or IRC processes, as requested.
- Mentor and coach Grants and Partnerships staff on IRC systems and processes to ensure capacity is built at country level.
- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

***Business Development***

- undefined
- Help drive business development in the region by providing effective proposal support, ranging from direct proposal management to light quality assurance.
- Support country offices with donor engagement, intel sharing and positioning with prioritized donors in the PDAA portfolio; prepare for and participate in donor calls as needed.
- Represent IRC externally at country-specific meetings, with donors and stakeholder networks in donor capitals as needed.
- Coordinate proposal development, including sharing initial assessments of new opportunities, preparing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections.
- Collaborate with regional technical leads and technical advisors, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning proposals and designs for new project activities and/or amendments to current projects.
- Provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements, including the PEER system.
- Lead or support coordination, communication, and inputs from consortium partners in accordance with donor and IRC processes.
- Coordinate and support regional reviews and approvals of proposal packages depending on country and regional needs. This includes partners’ packages if applicable.
- Review agreements to ensure accurateness and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with compliance and country grants teams and support in award negotiation and hand-over as required.
- Work with RPAS to incorporate lessons learned from implementation at the proposal stage.
- Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers.
- Deploying offices to lead proposal development as available and needed.
- Facilitate internal post-submission debrief sessions with country teams, technical units, regional team and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Essential**

Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:

- Degree, preferably in a subject related to IRC’s work (International Relations, Refugee or Migration Studies, Development Studies, Public Policy) or equivalent experience
- \*\*Fluency in English and French, both spoken and written
- \*\*Good understanding of humanitarian aid and development programming
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a diverse team and handle a multifaceted workload
- Good financial management and budgeting skills
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information
- Proven organizational skills, detail-oriented, ability to prioritize tasks, and to learn quickly
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to work independently in a very fast paced environment
- A flexible and calm work attitude
- International work experience in the Global South is a plus
- Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)
- Ability to travel internationally, sometimes on short notice and to insecure areas (15%)

Experience:

- Experience with and a strong understanding of institutional donors’ compliance requirements, e.g. UN, World Bank, US government, and/or European government donors (experience with all is not required, but a good mix would be a strong asset)
- Working at a distance and supporting country-based staff
- Writing, reviewing and editing narrative and financial reports and excellent attention to detail
- Working on new funding opportunities in the humanitarian and international development sectors with a range of multilateral and bilateral donors (FCDO, EU and ECHO, GFFO, BMZ, Sida, SDC, World Bank, US Department of State, etc.), as well as experience collaborating with local partner organizations.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US, UK, EU, German, Scandinavian, etc.

**Compensation (UK):** (GBP 52,210 -GBP 58,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Emergency Response Team Protection Coordinator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**FLUENCY IN WRITTEN & SPOKEN FRENCH & ENGLISH REQUIRED.**

**Job Overview:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you are skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours. Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

The Violence Prevention and Response in Emergencies (VPRIE) team sits jointly within IRC's Emergency Unit (EmU) and IRC’s Protection Unit. With few predictable, effective protection providers in emergencies, major gaps remain in delivering life-saving and life-sustaining VPR interventions at scale. VPRIE programming in acute emergencies spans integrated protection, Child Protection (CP), Women's Protection and Empowerment (WPE)/Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and Protection Rule of Law (PROL), focusing on four core service offerings: Social Work in Emergencies, Focused MHPSS Interventions, Responsive Information Services in Emergencies, and Community Risk Mitigation and Access. These complementary, mutually reinforcing interventions address the most urgent protection threats facing emergency-affected communities in all their diversity.

**Scope of Work**

The Emergency Response Team (ERT) is a specialized group within the Emergency Unit (EmU), deployed to support existing country programs in emergency response or to launch new programs in crisis zones. The team's core responsibility is to rapidly and effectively design, develop, and manage the IRC's on-site humanitarian response to meet the immediate needs of the affected population, while also transferring responsibilities and knowledge to long-term staff to ensure continuity of IRC programming and operations.

All ERT staff must be prepared to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification and should expect to spend up to 65% of their time in the field, in either an emergency or roving capacity.

The ERT Protection Coordinator (Child Protection) will be responsible for starting up and leading integrated protection and/or child protection programming in acute emergency responses. This may include rapid assessment, program start-up, strategy development, proposal development, technical oversight, staff recruitment and management, budget management, grants compliance and local partner relations. When not deployed, the ERT Protection Coordinator will contribute to IRC's strategic objectives and technical workstreams for CP and violence prevention and response in emergencies. A successful candidate will demonstrate a track record of working independently in fast-paced environments and applying creative, flexible design to protection programming in acute emergency contexts.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Emergency Responses:***

**Context Evaluation**

- Following the onset of an emergency, identify areas with greatest impact, highest needs, and emerging safety protection risks for diverse populations (integrated protection, CP, WPE / GBV, PROL), including specific protection risks for young children, adolescents, and families, and care arrangements
- Conduct stakeholder analysis: continually review existing actor mapping with a view to identifying key actors and establishing partnerships with focused on the delivery of protection services
- Design and conduct multisector needs assessments

**Program design and management**

- Provide strategic direction, leadership and overall technical management of IRC’s protection response aligned to the response strategy and emergency safety outcomes, while ensuring high program quality and alignment with IRC’s standards and approaches
- Lead and directly contribute to the start-up, implementation and coordination of emergency protection programming, including (depending on the context): emergency case management; support to Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC), including Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) and alternative care; cash for protection; rapid group MHPSS interventions; emergency safety and wellbeing sessions; two-way, responsive information services; community-based protection and risk mitigation; group cash transfers for community-led protection actions; and safe, inclusive programming and protection mainstreaming.
- In collaboration with partners, develop a VPRIE strategy to respond to identified protection risks and needs, outlining a problem statement, response modalities, activity sequencing, and required resources
- In collaboration with response leadership and technical coordinators, input into the design of an overall emergency response strategy, including partnerships so that the IRC is working in ways that are complementary to and in support of partners and child protection actors
- Participate in cross-departmental collaboration and coordination with other sector colleagues to ensure that linkages between programs are made and programs gain from protection best practice
- Ensure – through program design and practice, team capacity and behavior – that clients, including young children, adolescents, and caregivers, participate in the design and implementation of IRC programs, and that their access to services and programs is meaningful and safe
- Develop and/or adapt technical tools and approaches, and deliver creative solutions to mitigate challenges in the operating context, to facilitate response start-up and day to day implementation
- Support emergency protection staff to implement and monitor work plans ensuring that activities reflect the commitments IRC made to the donor and the community
- Oversee IRC’s relationship with partners, ensuring co-design, regular exchange, and project performance monitoring to achieve program objectives
- Design and implement appropriate monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems ensuring consistent reporting and analysis of results to improve program effectiveness and quality
- Provide a comprehensive handover to successor, including ensuring transfer of all related documentation, program data and staff performance information

**Grant and financial management**

- Manage emergency grant/program implementation including recruitment and training, work plan development, procurement and inventory planning, budget management, and M&E plans
- Develop high quality technical proposals and reports with relevant program staff in line with IRC and donor requirements
- Collaborate with IRC grants and finance staff to finalize proposals and respond to any requests for additional information

**Staff management**

- Recruit, onboard, and supervise emergency protection staff, and provide ongoing training and targeted capacity building, including technical guidance, on the job coaching and supervision, and capacity development plans on technical and managerial skills
- Comply with and ensure that new protection staff understand the IRC Code of Conduct and policies related to Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Child Safeguarding. This includes ensuring that staff and communities have knowledge of and safe, confidential access to reporting mechanisms and support services
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions

**Coordination and representation**

- Actively develop and maintain effective working relationships with key actors, including donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs, and other relevant actors
- Regularly attend emergency protection coordination and task force meetings, at appropriate levels to feed in IRC priorities from the field
- Ensure protection concerns and challenges are brought to relevant fora to advocate for standards and procedures that systematize how protection programming is implemented and coordinated at the field level

***Technical support and guidance***

When not deployed, the ERT Protection Coordinator (CP) will:

- Contribute to IRC’s strategic priorities for violence prevention and response in emergencies, and lead on CP-specific ambitions, including: refining emergency CP program models, toolkits, and technical guidance; supporting emergency preparedness and readiness; contributing to integrated and multi-sectoral program design, etc.
- Provide technical support, coaching, and backstopping to CP-centered emergency responses in countries with existing IRC programming, as needed
- Participate in cross-departmental collaboration and coordination with WPE, PROL, Education / ECD, and other sector colleagues to ensure that linkages between programs are made and programs gain from protection best practice
- Represent acute emergency approaches and priorities within IRC’s global CP team, including liaising and coordinating with CP TAs and Global Practice Lead, contributing to IRC’s global CP ambitions and representation as needed
- Contribute to delivery of IRC’s Emergency and Humanitarian Action strategic action plan and commitments to partnerships, safeguarding, and Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion (DEI)

**Job Requirements:**

- Post-graduate degree in social work, psychology, international humanitarian law, other related field, or equivalent work experience
- At least five years’ experience working in the field of Protection, Child Protection, or WPE / GBV programming at the Coordinator level or above required, with proven track record managing multi-donor portfolios in acute emergency response, program and project start-up
- Experience working with IRC and an understanding of IRC’s systems and processes is strongly preferred
- Familiarity with key donor regulations such as UNHCR, FCDO, BPRM and ECHO
- Experience in working with and coordinating with the UN, donors, INGOs and other humanitarian actors
- Demonstrated experience in staff supervision, capacity building, project design and budget management
- Proven leadership of multi-disciplinary, cross-cultural teams, with strong mentoring, coaching, motivational, and team-building skills.
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response.
- Proven communication, writing and editing skills, including the ability to effectively write and edit grant proposals and reports.
- Flexible work attitude: Be flexible and yet focused & reliable in an environment of limited resources and changing demands. Ability to work well, promote teamwork, be comfortable in a multi-cultural environment.
- Good digital literacy: Facility with MS Word, Excel, and email/internet software.
- Fluency in English and French. Ability to additionally Spanish and/or Arabic strongly preferred. Excellent oral and written communication skills.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Caseworker
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other US Office for Refugee Resettlement (ORR) eligible populations. The Caseworker, is expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Determine client eligibility for case management programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client.
- Develop individualized plans for each client enrolled in the SCM, OIRS, and Youth Health Programming.
- Assist clients in navigating social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments.
- Record services and evaluate client progress during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed.
- Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs.
- Provide clients with extended orientation on a variety of topics such as developing social support networks, navigating transportation systems, and navigating physical healthcare systems with families.
- Respond to client crises, with guidance from supervisor as needed.
- Assist clients with requesting financial assistance when applicable and track the received financial assistance within case files.
- Maintain up-to-date documentation in client’s case file to ensure services are properly documented throughout the client’s service period; document all services provided in IRC’s database, Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Attend relevant trainings and meetings at the local and national level.
- May train and guide the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion, and cohesion in IRC Missoula.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work, public health, or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- A minimum of 1-2 years of case management experience with similar populations and/or client needs required.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English required, both spoken and written; proficiency in Pashto, Dari, Arabic, Swahili, Spanish is preferred.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- The IRC and IRC workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Equality, and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti Workplace Harassment, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Access to reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area is required.
- May require occasional evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23.91-$25.92/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, Research & Learning (MEARL) Officer, Nepal (Local Consultant)
body:
**Project HOPE** is an international NGO with more than 1,000 engaged employees and volunteers who work around the globe, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients, provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up, and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

**Code of Conduct**

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a ***culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.***

**Summary:**

Project HOPE is seeking a MEARL Officer (Consultant) to provide monitoring, evaluation, accountability, research, and learning support for its Nepal emergency response.

The consultant will support routine program monitoring, data collection and verification, partner reporting, field monitoring, and community feedback mechanisms to ensure accurate tracking of project results and compliance with donor reporting requirements.

The consultant will report to the Nepal Team Lead and work closely with Project HOPE's program team, implementing partners, and Regional MEARL Manager.

**Scope of Consultancy**

The deliverables that will be expected to be performed successfully are:

- Update the MEAL plan, indicator tracking table and data collection and reporting tools with the program team and Regional MEARL Manager
- Collect and consolidate routine results from Partners and Project HOPE activities
- Check partner reports against registers, distribution records and other supporting documentation; follow up on data gaps and inconsistencies
- Monitor medical consultations, treatments, referrals, psychosocial support, kit distributions, WASH activities and facility support against agreed indicators
- Conduct field monitoring visits and document findings, required corrections and follow-up actions.
- Maintain secure databases and supporting records, applying agreed indicator definitions, confidentiality and data protection procedures.
- Support post-distribution monitoring, beneficiary feedback, pre and post assessments and other surveys as required.
- Help establish and monitor accessible community feedback and complaints channels, including safe handling and referral of sensitive feedback.
- Prepare monthly MEAL updates and verified indicator figures for quarterly donor reports and the final report
- Provide practical guidance to partners on data collection, beneficiary counting, verification and reporting.
- Analyze monitoring findings and discuss improvements with the Nepal team; document lessons learned and agreed actions
- Coordinate work priorities and technical questions with the Nepal Team Lead and Regional MEARL Manager.
- Follow Project HOPE safeguarding, accountability, Do No Harm and conflict-sensitivity requirements
- Perform other related duties within the scope of the position.

**Expected Outputs:**

- **Updated MEAL plan and reliable monitoring tools** (First month; updated as needed): Updated MEAL plan, indicator tracking table, reporting templates, and agreed indicator definitions to track progress against donor agreements and maintain consistent indicator records.
- **Consolidated partner and Project HOPE results** (Monthly): Consolidated partner and Project HOPE results, including review of partner data and supporting documentation, documented data checks, and follow-up on discrepancies.
- **Field monitoring and accountability** (Quarterly, ongoing): Documentation of monitoring findings covering service delivery, distributions, and WASH activities, with findings and follow-up actions to inform program improvements.
- **Community feedback and complaints tracking** (Ongoing; monthly summary): Feedback and complaints tracking summaries, with confidential handling and appropriate referral of sensitive cases.
- **Post-distribution monitoring and assessments** (As scheduled): Assessment tools, cleaned datasets, and brief findings summaries to support monitoring and learning.
- **Donor reporting inputs** (Quarterly): Verified indicator figures and MEARL analysis and verified indicator figures for quarterly donor progress reports.
- **Progress and monitoring updates** (Monthly): Brief analysis of program progress, data gaps, challenges, community feedback, lessons learned, and follow-up actions for the Nepal team.
- **Final MEARL reporting** (At project closeout): Consolidated final indicator results, supporting records, and MEARL inputs for final reporting.

Detailed deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations will be agreed upon with the consultant and documented as part of the consultancy engagement.

Duration of Assignment: Approximately 3 months

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Public Health, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Economics, Information Management or a related field; master’s degree an advantage.
- At least three years of relevant experience in MEAL, preferably in humanitarian, development or public health programs.
- Practical experience in indicator tracking, data collection, data quality checks, analysis and reporting.
- Experience supporting needs/risk assessments, surveys, monitoring visits and work with implementing partners.
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including data cleaning, formulas, pivot tables and summary charts.
- Experience with DHIS2, Power BI, SPSS, R or similar systems
- Understanding of qualitative and quantitative methods and basic sampling.
- Ability to communicate findings clearly and work independently with program teams.
- Experience using KoboToolbox, ODK or comparable digital data collection tools is an advantage.
- Knowledge of consent, confidentiality, safeguarding and responsible data management.
- Good written and spoken Nepali and English.

**Notice to applicants:** Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only applicants who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

title: AI Technical Specialist: Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness
body:
## AI Technical Specialist: Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness

Full-Time in Baghdad, IQ - Remote (within locations)

Terms of Reference: Development Gateway AI Technical Specialist for the Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness Program

## About Development Gateway and the Program

Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 15 countries. Over the last 20 years, DG has researched data ecosystems, built digital tools to support them, and advised on data strategy, AI readiness, and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

The Iraq Higher Education AI Workforce Readiness Program is a 12-month program implemented by IREX and DG, in coordination with the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR) and the Kurdistan Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (KMoHESR). The program helps Iraqi universities prepare students and graduates for an AI-driven economy by assessing AI readiness across at least 40 universities, convening universities, ministries, and U.S. and Iraqi employers, and building practical capability through a generative AI micro-credential course and AI readiness roadmaps for high-potential universities.

## Position Summary

The AI Technical Specialist will be a full-time, in-person role based in **Baghdad, Iraq**, for a period of 10 months. Serving as DG’s hands-on AI lead on the program, the role will turn AI readiness findings and employer input into practical training, tools, and recommendations that Iraqi universities can adopt, and will own the program’s technical AI content, above all the generative AI micro-credential course.

The role works alongside DG’s Project Manager who leads program delivery, the readiness research, and senior stakeholder relationships. The AI Technical Specialist provides complementarity through technical depth, shaping the assessment’s AI, data, and infrastructure dimensions, co-designing and rolling out the micro-credential course, and writing the AI use case and policy content of the university roadmaps.

The ideal candidate combines practical experience with AI with experience designing training or digital learning. The post holder must be able to explain AI and its responsible use clearly to students, faculty, ministry officials, and business audiences, in both Arabic and English.

## Reporting and Working Relationships

The AI Technical Specialist will report to DG’s program leadership. The role will coordinate regularly with DG technical colleagues based in other countries, as well as work closely with IREX colleagues in Iraq and the United States to ensure DG’s work is well integrated with the wider program.

The role is also expected to work closely with university IT and teaching staff, ministry counterparts, and U.S. technology partners.

## Key Responsibilities

### AI Readiness Assessment

● Adapt the AI readiness assessment tools developed by IREX and DG for Iraq, covering AI governance and risk, data governance, digital infrastructure and interoperability, workforce capability, and priority use cases.

● Support the AI ecosystem mapping by assessing the technical capabilities and constraints of universities and ministry units, including connectivity, platforms, and data practices.

● Support data collection and analysis with the Project Manager, and translate technical findings into practical recommendations for universities and the ministries.

### Generative AI Micro-Credential Course

● Co-design the four-week generative AI micro-credential course, adapting IREX and DG materials from Jordan, in Arabic and English, with at least three versions tailored to priority sectors.

● Cover AI fundamentals in commercial settings, prompt design and workflow integration, and responsible use, including ethics, bias mitigation, and safeguarding, using employer input to build realistic use cases.

● Pilot and roll out the course on participating universities’ learning management systems, supporting university IT and teaching staff, and tracking enrollment, completion, and pre- and post-course results.

● Deliver orientation sessions and training for faculty, students, and administrators, and preview the course at the program’s AI workforce convening.

### Tools, Roadmaps, and Learning

● Identify openly available U.S. AI learning resources and toolkits, such as IBM SkillsBuild, and help universities adopt them, working with U.S. technology partners.

● Write the AI use case, skills, and responsible AI policy content of the AI readiness roadmaps for high-potential universities.

● Track course analytics and learning outcomes for program monitoring, and document tools and lessons that MoHESR and universities can reuse after the program ends.

## Qualifications

### Required Qualifications

● Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, information systems, engineering, or a related field.

● 5+ years of professional experience in AI, machine learning, data, or digital technology roles, including hands-on work with generative AI tools.

● Experience designing and delivering training, courses, or curricula on technology topics, preferably in higher education or workforce development.

● Working knowledge of responsible AI, including ethics, bias, data privacy, and AI governance.

● Experience with learning management systems or online learning platforms, such as Moodle or Blackboard.

● Professional fluency in English and Arabic, both written and spoken, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

● Existing work authorization in Iraq.

### Preferred Qualifications

● Master’s degree in a technology, data, or education-related field.

● Experience working with Iraqi universities, ministries, or technology firms.

● Experience developing micro-credentials, e-learning content, or instructional materials.

● Familiarity with AI readiness assessments or digital maturity frameworks.

● Experience with U.S. technology company skills programs, such as IBM, Microsoft, Google, or Cisco training resources.

● Experience on U.S. Government-funded or other donor-funded programs, including consortium-based programs.

● Experience facilitating workshops for government, academic, and private sector audiences.

## Compensation

The expected annual compensation range is **USD 42,000 - 45,000**, depending on relevant experience. The position is for the duration of the project, which is 10 months.

DG will review applications on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Interviews are expected to begin in mid-November.

title: Head of Business Development, MENAU
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Germany, Jordan and Lebanon.**

**Background**

Over the past 90+ years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild through long-term, sustainable development solutions. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD. The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**The Purpose of the Role**

Reporting to the Director, Awards Management, the Head of Business Development (HBD), MENAU, leads IRC’s business development efforts in support of the region’s country programs and is a key part of IRC’s global business development team, serving as the region's representative in developing and implementing IRC’s global business development strategy. The HBD plays a strategic role in the planning, identification, and successful pursuit of new business in line with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs). HBD support includes all phases of the business development process, including strategic planning, donor outreach and engagement, pre-positioning (capture), partnering, proposal development, due diligence, issues letter and agreement negotiation.

The HBD is responsible for maintaining regional level oversight of all business development for institutional donors in the IRC’s Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region, which comprises country programs in Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Ukraine, and Yemen. As a member of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the HBD also provides business development support to IRC’s Emergency Response in the Occupied Palestinian Territories (oPt).

**Scope and Authority**

The Head of Business Development exercises overall leadership for business development in the region and line management of regional Program Development Advisors (PDAs). The role oversees regional and supports country business development strategies and planning, including reviewing the pipeline and individual opportunities and ensuring appropriate resourcing for successful bid submissions. The HBD provides development oversight of regionally assigned opportunities and serves as a key regional focal point for global opportunities supported by AMU’s Proposal Leadership team.

**Key Working Relationships**

The HBD reports to the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and manages regional PDAs. The HBD works closely with the regional Senior Management Team, all RPAS team members, and the wider AMU Global Business Development team, including peers in the Donor Engagement, BD Services, and BD Strategy, Operations, & Resourcing teams. The HBD also collaborates with other teams within the Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, especially AMU, the Emergency Unit, and Technical Excellence, as well as with External Relations, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, and other key departments within IRC who contribute to regional business development efforts. The HBD serves as point of contact with external donor and partner stakeholders during the pre-award stage, as applicable per region.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES**

***Planning and Strategic Leadership (40%)***

- Provide strategic vision on regional BD efforts in support of country program Strategy Action Plans (SAP), in collaboration with regional and AMU leadership.
- Maintain visibility on the overall pipeline across all public and institutional donors, in collaboration with RPAS team members.
- Maintain up to date knowledge of donor funding priorities and geographical interests relevant to IRC’s areas of work.
- Provide advice, analysis and guidance to AMU, Regional and Country leadership on BD trends, target-setting, donor engagement, and support needs in the region, ensuring leaders have the right level of information to make decisions.
- Lead and support BD strategy development efforts and planning at regional and country level, to establish clear funding priorities and targets, to support decision making and enable effective positioning and resource planning.
- Coordinate support to country teams in the identification, tracking and pursuit of new business opportunities across a variety of technical sectors and donors, including ensuring that technical brainstorming, partner, and competitor landscape analysis and win theme sessions with technical and country staff are occurring.

***End to End Program Development (20%)***

- Support effective and timely Go/No Go decisions, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities and providing insight and inputs based on donor knowledge, likelihood of success and experience.
- Plan and manage effective division of bid leadership across the portfolio at capture and live stages of development to ensure appropriate support on all opportunities.
- At the early stage of opportunity identification, work with country teams, DAM and others in identifying and addressing escalated support needs.
- Act as the regional business development focal point for escalated bid opportunities, providing regional advice and coordinating escalated support in connection with bid leads assigned by the Proposal Leadership team or others.
- Collaborate with other BD staff, especially Proposal Leadership team members and technical staff on high demand opportunities and multi-country and TU-led bids.
- Ensure the following Bid Leadership responsibilities are performed consistently and effectively by the assigned BD Lead (HBD, PDA, Proposal Leadership team member, or other) on each public opportunity in the regional portfolio:
    - Collaborate with technical units, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning program and bid designs, including support to building effective partnerships and consortia.
    - Provide effective proposal support, ranging from proposal management to comprehensive support, confirming responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements. Ensure required reviews and approvals are secured prior to submission to donor.
    - Provide guidance on donor policies and ensure project design is responsive and compliant with donor expectations, rules, and regulations.
    - When providing proposal management support, coordinate concept note and/or proposal development, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities, reviewing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings, and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections. This includes support to country office teams in the management and maintenance of IRC’s award management system.
    - Review agreements, in coordination with relevant RPAS post-award focal point, to ensure accuracy and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with post-award, Compliance & Policy and country Grants teams.
