title: Finance Manager, South Korea
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in some 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient.

The IRC global network has its headquarters in New York and London. IRC Europe is part of this network with offices in the UK, Germany, Sweden, Belgium and Switzerland. In addition, the IRC has a partnership with Stichting Vluchteling in the Netherlands.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

Read more about the IRC here: [https://www.rescue.or.kr](https://www.rescue.or.kr/)

**EXTERNAL RELATIONS AND THE PRIVATE FUNDRAISING FUNCTION**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions, including Private fundraising, in which this role falls under. To enable IRC to deliver its organizational commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance its ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

Within Private Fundraising sits the Mass Markets unit. This unit is currently made up of seven teams – US, UK, Germany, Sweden, Korea, Digital & Remote Markets and our Supporter Journey and Acquisition teams. Mass Market’s primary goal is to increase the number of sustainers we have globally, via targeted and cost effective acquisition and by building meaningful connections with our donors to ensure we can retain them. By increasing our sustainer numbers and capitalizing on cash giving moments we aim to grow unrestricted revenue for IRC and the people we serve.

**STRUCTURE AND PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

In the role of Finance Manager, you will be the strategic finance leader for IRC Korea, responsible for driving financial results, transparency, and system modernization – most immediately through leading the rollout and localization of Integra, IRC’s global finance system, for the Korea office. You will manage and mentor the Finance team and serve as the primary liaison for other functional areas supporting the Korea office, contributing to strategic direction and operational problem-solving through your area of professional expertise.

**KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Working within a Finance matrix structure, you will be responsible for and oversee:

 **1. Controllership:**

- Ensure compliance of donor funds in Korea with local and relevant international regulations, including tax, accounting standards, and reporting requirements.
- Manage the financial records of IRC Korea and responsible for timely monthly/annual closing, financial reporting.
- Managing Audit and financial compliance, acting as a key point of contact with external parties including auditors and tax authorities.
- Lead the deployment of IRC’s global ERP system “Integra” for IRC Korea, ensuring both IRC and local statutory requirements are met.
- Act as primary focal point for the Integra Delivery team during the deployment period.
- Preparation of annual statutory financial statements and other local financial regulatory reporting as required, in coordination with HQ Global Finance and external parties where required.
- Provide monthly payroll information to the outsourcing firm and review calculations before finalizing.
- Maintain an appropriate financial control environment, ensuring financial records are maintained and that weekly and monthly financial routines are completed.
- Ensure accurate data between Integra and fundraising system (Donus), maintaining monthly financial reconciliations.
- Ensure regular communications with the IRC Global Finance Accounting & Consolidation team, particularly during month end/year end.
- Ensure internal IRC financial reporting is carried out to time and quality.
- Prepare reports for the Executive Director on an agreed basis

 **2. Treasury & Risk Management:**

- Identify and manage financial risks, including currency exchange. Provide insights into the financial health of IRC Korea.
- Working with the treasury team, identify and recommend appropriate banking service providers and lead setting up banking relationships, if needed.

 **3. Financial Planning & Analysis**:

- Lead the annual budget and planning process for IRC Korea in cooperation with the Executive Director, including reporting and follow-up.
- Work in conjunction with the Executive Director and Global FP&A team to finalize annual budgets.
- Ensure appropriate financial planning, budgeting and monitoring for IRC Korea and in line with IRC requirements.

 **4. Functional Leadership**:

- Manage, train and mentor the Finance team members in using Integra and as the finance function grows.
- Foster a high-performance culture of learning and best practice to ensure the finance function’s goals are met.

**OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- To comply with the culture and policies governing IRC Korea.
- To represent IRC in a manner that ensures appropriate communication with our supporters and stakeholders.
- To develop and maintain a positive working relationship with other departments and teams in IRC Korea and IRC globally.
- To attend meetings, conferences, and training courses as directed.
- Abide by organizational policies and practices, and the Code of Conduct.
- Support diversity and equality of opportunity in the workplace

**WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:**

- You will report to the Executive Director of South Korea, in partnership with the Director of Finance, Europe.
- Regular liaison with the Global Finance Accounting & Consolidation team and Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team in HQ.
- External Relations colleagues as needed.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

**Qualifications:**

**Essentials:**

- Multi-year background from qualified financial work (Min. 10 years of experience in Fiance with more than 3 years of managerial roles)
- Academic education (degree) business administration and accounting
- Strongly preferred experience with finance/ERP systems (e.g., Microsoft D365 Finance & Operations, or similar)
- Fluent Knowledge of English and Korean

**Preferrable:**

- Experience in Operations management

 **Skills/character:**

- Ability to be strategic and creative in developing and implementing new income-generating activities.
- Strong relationship-building, interpersonal and negotiation skills.
- Excellent people management skills, including the demonstrated capacity to lead, motivate, develop and engage a multi-disciplinary team with a collaborative and supportive management style.
- Ability to lead effectively through a period of significant systems and process transition.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: (Senior) Global Project Manager for HQ, based in Geneva, Switzerland
body:
## **BACKGROUNG ON IMPACT & REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

## **BACKGROUNG ON THE POSITION**

We are currently looking for a **(Senior) Global Project Manager** to join IMPACT’s Global Programmes section at IMPACT Headquarters in Geneva.

**Title:** (Senior) Global Project Manager

**Location:** Geneva, with occasional travels

**Line management:** Reports to the Head of Global Programmes

**Contract duration:** Open ended contract

**Start date:** ASAP

## **POSITION PROFILE**

The Global Project Manager will be responsible for overseeing the effective management and implementation of a portfolio of strategic global projects secured by IMPACT Initiatives, under the supervision of the Head of Global Programmes. The Global Project Manager will work closely with Global Programmes Managers, country teams, HQ departments, donors and external partners, and maintain a functional link with the Head of Projects and Partnerships Support (PPS).

The Global Project Manager will oversee and coordinate key aspects of the programme cycle across the portfolio, including implementation follow-up, donor reporting, support to grant management processes, partner engagement, funding allocations and the identification of programme-level risks and dependencies. In doing so, they will support organisational leadership in maintaining visibility over programme performance, facilitating effective decision-making, and ensuring alignment across the various stakeholders involved in programme delivery.

The position aims to complement, rather than duplicate, existing grant administration, compliance, financial monitoring and contractual management functions led by PPS and Finance. The role leverages tracking systems and processes maintained by these teams to support programme-level coordination, oversight and decision-making. Likewise, the role complements, rather than replaces, the leadership responsibilities of Global Programmes Managers and other designated activity leads, such as country representatives for the country-level portion of project implementation, who retain accountability for programme strategy, technical direction, methodological choices and implementation approaches.

The position requires a profile combining strong project management skills with a practical understanding of humanitarian programme implementation in the field of assessments, analysis and applied research. The Global Project Manager should be comfortable coordinating across multiple countries and teams, consolidating complex information for institutional donor reporting, facilitating engagement across a wide range of stakeholders, supporting funding allocation processes, and helping resolve implementation bottlenecks in complex operating environments. Previous experience managing humanitarian programmes, familiarity with IMPACT's work and understanding of the assessment and analysis sector are therefore strongly valued.

## **FUNCTION & RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Global Project Manager's responsibilities will be delivered under the supervision of the Head of Global Programmes and in close collaboration with all SLT members, HQ departments and country teams, particularly the Head of PPS. The role serves as a key programme management focal point across complex global programmes, supporting effective coordination, decision-making and follow-up across multiple stakeholders and functions. They will include:

1. **PROJECT COORDINATION AND DONOR REPORTING**

- Oversee the implementation of assigned global projects and ensure progress against approved activities, deliverables, indicators, budgets and contractual commitments, building from existing tracking tools implemented by PPS and Finance teams where relevant.
- Develop and maintain detailed project-level workplans that can be shared with all project stakeholders to increase visibility on project ambitions, timelines and status.
- Coordinate project kick off meetings and regular project progress and quality reviews with Global Programmes Managers, country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;
- Maintain oversight of contractually required deliverables and reporting deadlines across assigned grants and coordinate/consolidate high-quality narrative reporting to institutional donors, including inputs from country teams, partners and relevant HQ departments;
- In close coordination with the Project and Partnership Support (PPS) and Finance teams, coordinate donor queries and contractual modifications, including amendments, budget revisions and no-cost extensions, as required;

**2. RISK IDENTIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT**

- Identify implementation delays, bottlenecks and risks, and support relevant teams in defining and following up on corrective measures;
- In the case of major risks that can have organizational implications or require cross-department engagement, ensure, via the Head of Global Programmes, that the Executive Team and the Senior Leadership Team are informed and enabled to take action.
- When required, liaise with Finance and PPS teams to initiate possible contractual realignment;
- Ensure that implementation challenges, lessons learned and associated mitigation measures are appropriately documented and leveraged in subsequent phases of the project.

**3. POOLED FUND MANAGEMENT**

- In collaboration with the Head of Global Programmes and the Head of PPS, support the coordination internal pooled funding and allocation mechanisms, from the preparation of allocation processes through tracking of activity progress and deliverables;
- Coordinate the review and follow-up of allocations, ensuring processes are appropriately documented and aligned with project objectives and donor requirements;
- Monitor implementation, deliverables and reporting across recipient countries and maintain a consolidated overview of progress;
- Liaise with the Projects and Partnership support team Finance Department to ensure organizational visibility around implementation delays, under-spending and other risks and facilitate corrective action, reprogramming or reallocation where required.

**4. DONOR AND PARTNER ENGAGEMENT**

- Engage with project focal points on the donor side to provide updates on activity progress, and help orient them to the right focal points within the organization depending on their queries (for example, re-direct questions around contracting and payment modalities to the PPS or finance teams).
- For projects delivered in a consortium (as of October 2026, the ECHO Policy HIP project) :
    - Track partners’ activity progress against project level workplans, and consolidate reporting.
    - Facilitate and chair partner meetings to provide and collect progress updates on the delivery of the project, identify and troubleshoot delivery issues.
- Ensure partners understand and comply with relevant project, donor and IMPACT programmatic, financial and reporting requirements, and communicate any compliance risks promptly with PPS for action.
- Identify partnership-related challenges or compliance issues and facilitate their timely resolution with the support of PPS and Finance teams.

**5. FUNDRAISING**

- In close coordination with the Head of Global Programmes and the PPS team, initiate engagement with existing donors around project renewals or extensions
- Convene project activity leads and key partners around the identification of programmatic priorities for the next iteration of projects in the context of a renewal
- In support of the Executive Team, contribute to funding diversification by supporting the implementation of an organizational fundraising appeal, which may require engagement and relationship building with new institutional donors as well as philanthropies.
- With the support of the Communications and Advocacy and Global Programmes team, develop fundraising materials that can help convey IMPACT’s value added to a wide variety of potential funding partners across the humanitarian, development and private sectors.

## **KEY DELIVERABLES**

- Assigned global and multi-country projects are implemented in line with agreed workplans, budgets, deliverables and donor requirements.
- High-quality donor reports and other contractual deliverables are consolidated and submitted on time.
- Up-to-date consolidated project monitoring provides clear visibility on implementation progress, expenditure, risks and upcoming milestones.
- Pooled fund allocations are effectively managed and monitored from allocation through implementation and close-out.
- Implementing partnerships are effectively established and followed up, with timely identification and resolution of implementation and compliance issues.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- Excellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. project management, development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences).
- At least 10 years of experience in the development or humanitarian sector; experience in field-based roles and across multiple geographies an asset.
- Familiarity with needs assessments and analysis, applied research in humanitarian or development settings.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.
- Demonstrated experience directly managing and implementing humanitarian projects, preferably including experience at country/field level. Experience with complex, multi-country and/or multi-partner projects is a strong asset;
- Demonstrated experience managing institutional donor grants throughout the project cycle, including implementation follow-up, donor reporting and contractual compliance;
- Strong understanding of institutional donor requirements; prior experience with ECHO, Sida, SDC, GAC and/or comparable institutional donors is highly desirable;
- Demonstrated experience working with implementing partners, including partnership set-up, implementation follow-up and reporting; example leading complex consortia a strong asset.
- Excellent organisational, coordination and planning skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines and coordinate effectively across teams, countries and functions;
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills.
- Willingness and ability for short term deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Fluency in English and French required, given the regional remit of the position; Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese or Ukrainian an asset.
- Ability to operate InDesign is a plus.

## COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

For this position, gross salary between **5,892 CHF and 6,221** CHF monthly (before income tax). NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education and experience of staff. A contribution to medical insurance of 489 CHF per month is already included in the salary figure.

- Insurance covering professional and non-professional accidents throughout the period of employment with IMPACT
- Health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance in case of field visits/temporary deployments
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- Applicants must hold a valid work permit for Switzerland or be EU/EFTA citizens
- Up to 40% of remote work on a weekly basis

title: Technical Advisor , Law Enforcement and Wildlife Crime Prevention.
body:
**Reporting to:** Technical Director.  
**Working Relationships:** Senior Consultant in Protected Area Management, Marine Landscape Coordinator, WCS Gabon technical teams, WCS park managers, ANPN, MINEF, DGPA, Ministry of the Sea, and other relevant government agencies.  
**Work Location:** Libreville, with frequent field assignments in national parks, landscapes, and project sites where WCS operates in Gabon.

**Position Type:** Full time

**Overview of the Program in Gabon:**

WCS’s history in Gabon began in 1985 with the first national census of forest elephants, followed by a comprehensive assessment of conservation priorities. This work contributed to the creation of the network of 13 national parks in 2002 and subsequently to the development of the network of marine protected areas. In October 2025, WCS and the National Agency for National Parks (ANPN) signed a partnership agreement establishing a roadmap to prepare for long-term collaborative management partnerships for several parks. This roadmap includes Priority Support Projects (PSPs) designed to address urgent operational needs, strengthen management systems, and lay the technical, institutional, operational, and financial groundwork for future Collaborative Management Partnerships (CMPs). Law enforcement and wildlife crime prevention efforts are further supported by several projects and funding sources within the WCS Gabon portfolio, notably the INL project to combat wildlife trafficking and the NaturAfrica project to support protected area management. The objective is to mobilize this support within a common programmatic framework by strengthening systems, capacities, and tools that can be used sustainably by national authorities and park managers, including in the preparation of future CMPs.

**Job Summary**

WCS is seeking a LEM/CWT ((Law Enforcement Management/ Counter Wildlife Trafficking) Technical Advisor to strengthen protection, monitoring, and law enforcement in terrestrial and marine protected areas supported by its program, in support of the relevant government agencies and in accordance with their sovereign mandates.

As WCS’s technical lead in this field, he or she will support operational mechanisms and supervise specialized teams. Park managers retain operational control of the sites; the Senior Protected Area Management Consultant consolidates cross-cutting contributions under the supervision of the technical directorate.

He or she coordinates support from various projects to build shared and sustainable systems and capacities, and contributes to the development of new projects and funding.

At the national level, he or she monitors and supports developments in legal and institutional frameworks, particularly with regard to the CMPs and the Water and Forestry Paramilitary Corps. For targeted parks, he or she prepares LEM/CWT contributions to WCS’s internal commitment documents and to the transition to the CMPs.

**Job Objectives**

- Develop an LEM/CWT framework tailored to terrestrial and marine contexts, contributing to its legal and institutional evolution through technical provisions.
- Strengthen the capacities of partner government agencies, WCS teams, and park managers according to their roles and needs.
- Develop interoperable information and operational monitoring systems to support planning and decision-making.
- Improve the effectiveness of wildlife protection and anti-poaching measures at priority sites.
- Prepare the LEM/CWT component of WCS’s commitments and future CMPs, with clearly defined responsibilities, capacities, and financial needs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**A) LEM/CWT Technical Support for Priority Sites and the PSP/CMP Process**

- Assess, together with Director Conservators, WCS park managers, and relevant government agencies, LEM/CWT threats, capacities, and needs; define priorities and roadmaps for monitoring and anti-poaching programs.
- Enhance intelligence-led patrols, information collection and analysis, case management, and legal follow-up, with inter-institutional and, where relevant, cross-border coordination.
- Plan the equipment, infrastructure, logistics, and maintenance required for operations: mobility, communications, command posts and operations rooms, drones, and geospatial tools. Deploy interoperable systems, including SMART, EarthRanger, and—in marine environments—Skylight/Global Fishing Watch, in conjunction with relevant national systems.
- In northeastern Gabon, provide support in particular to the CWT coordination center in Makokou and the LEM/CWT units in Ivindo, Minkébé, and the associated landscape. Along the coast, support land, coastal, and maritime surveillance operations and, in Mayumba, the cooperation mechanisms of the Mayumba-Conkouati Transboundary Park.
- For parks participating in the PSP/CMP, prepare LEM/CWT contributions in collaboration with the senior consultant, park managers, regional WCS experts, and relevant authorities: risks, responsibilities, and chains of command; standards; investment needs and recurring costs; transition conditions; and points requiring resolution. These contributions inform the operational plans, business plans, and commitment proposals according to a shared timeline; the Technical Committee addresses review comments. Commitment decisions and institutional approvals are the responsibility of WCS and the relevant authorities, respectively.

**B) LEM/CWT Structural Support at the National Level, Coordination, and Knowledge Sharing**

- Organize technical reviews and exchanges between sites and with the ANPN operations center; document best practices, limitations, and cost models to identify solutions to be harmonized or scaled up nationwide.
- With the support of legal experts, competent authorities, and partners, monitor current and proposed legal and institutional frameworks; analyze their impact on the mandates, status of ecoguards and rangers, responsibilities, coordination, and governance of protected areas.
- Based on challenges documented in the field, propose improvements to the future LEM/CWT framework: rationale, options, feasibility, costs, and operational impacts. Review these with legal experts as needed and finalize them with the senior consultant for cross-cutting issues before submitting them to the authorized authorities.
- Support the updating and harmonization of LEM/CWT methods, tools, and standards used by WCS and its partners, by capitalizing on field experiences and integrating, where relevant, innovative approaches and new technologies: operational concepts, SOPs, emergency protocols, data collection and analysis systems, monitoring and decision-support tools, operations room architecture, training programs, and post-training follow-up mechanisms.
- Coordinate WCS Gabon’s LEM/CWT portfolio: supervise technical staff, consultants, and trainers; contribute to planning, budgeting, and procurement in collaboration with the Program and Finance teams, as well as to monitoring results, reporting, and funding proposals.
- Assess skills needs by function and implement the LEM/CWT component of the overall capacity-building plan consolidated by the senior consultant: training, coaching, practical exercises, and internal knowledge transfer. Integrate human rights, crime scene management, and legal procedures; evaluate learning outcomes and their application. Fleet managers organize the implementation of these practices within their teams.

**Expected Results and Outputs for This Support**

- **Internal engagement and preparation of CMPs:** LEM/CWT contribution by fleet covering the elements described in Section A, in accordance with the content and review schedule agreed upon with the Technical Directorate and the senior consultant. Internal analyses are reused and updated—where relevant—in discussions with the ANPN regarding PSPs and CMPs.
- **Capacity building:** initial assessment, training or coaching program and materials, review of skills acquired and applied, remaining needs, and follow-up actions, based on criteria agreed upon at the outset.
- **Legal and institutional frameworks:** record of current and proposed changes, analysis of implications, monitoring of system and procedure adjustments, and proposal notes for the future framework where relevant.
- **Operational support and harmonization:** site-specific roadmaps, updated guidelines and tools, and summaries of technical reviews and lessons learned.

**Qualifications Requirements:**

**a) LEM/CWT expertise and protection operations**

- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in conservation, natural resource management, security, criminology, law, public administration, or a related field; or demonstrated equivalent professional experience.
- Significant experience in technical management or technical assistance for law enforcement operations, protected area conservation, or combating wildlife/environmental crime; experience in Central Africa is a significant asset.
- A good understanding of chains of command, operational planning, intelligence-led patrols, case management procedures, judicial follow-up, and interagency coordination.
- Experience coordinating multi-agency operations is an advantage.

**b) Information Systems and Operational Technologies**

- Proficiency or solid experience with SMART and/or comparable tools; experience with EarthRanger, GIS, GPS, and communication systems is highly valued.
- Ability to transform operational data into analyses, priorities, deployment plans, and recommendations that can be used by field leaders and decision-makers.

**c) Institutional Advisory Services, Planning, and Funding**

- Ability to analyze organizational structures, responsibilities, staffing needs, and operational costs, and to translate these analyses into procedures, roadmaps, budgets, and realistic scenarios.
- Experience advising public administrations; ability to analyze the operational implications of legal and institutional changes in collaboration with legal experts and to propose field-based improvements.
- Experience in preparing operational and financial plans for protected areas, business plans, or comparable frameworks is desirable, along with the ability to contribute to the definition of governance mechanisms and institutional interfaces.

**d) Management, Communication, and Languages**

- Ability to provide technical leadership to multidisciplinary teams, coordinate multiple partners, and simultaneously manage national, field, and project priorities.
- Excellent writing, analytical, synthesis, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills.
- Fluency in French; a working knowledge of English is a plus.
- Ability to undertake frequent field assignments and to work in field conditions that may be isolated or demanding.

title: MEAL Manager (National Position) -Re Advertised
body:
Near East Foundation (NEF)

**Title:** Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Manager (National Position)

**Reports to:** Country Director

**Location:** Damascus, Syria

**Travel:** Up to 25% within Syria

**The Near East Foundation (NEF)** is seeking candidates for a **MEAL**[**\[1\]**](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_1) **Manager** to be based in Damascus, Syria. NEF is a non-profit international development organization that has supported livelihoods recovery and community-based economic development in the Middle East, Africa, and Caucasus since 1915. NEF draws on local teams, experience, and partnerships in these regions to create community-led solutions to reduce poverty, create economic opportunity, and empower conflict and crisis-affected groups to improve their outlook and wellbeing. Working through a network of country offices and local partners, NEF has operations in ten countries: Armenia, Lebanon, Iraq, Mali, Morocco, Palestine, Sudan, South Sudan, and Syria. HQ offices are based between Syracuse, NY, Washington, DC, London, UK, and Brussels, Belgium. Our programs are organized around three pillars: Inclusive Economic Development, Climate-resilient Development, and Stabilization and Peacebuilding.

**Position Description**

The MEAL Manager is a member of the NEF Syria team, reporting to the Syria Director. The purpose of the MEAL Manager is to ensure all MEAL responsibilities are performed to the highest standards and according to donor and NEF guidelines. The post-holder also assumes communication and visibility responsibilities for the Syria operation.

**Responsibilities**

- **Proposal Development and MEAL Planning:**
    - Participate in the development of project proposals, including designing logframes, selecting and defining indicators, and developing MEAL plans.
    - Design and update the project logframes and MEAL plans in collaboration with relevant team members.
- **MEAL System Implementation and Oversight:**
    - Ensure an appropriate MEAL system is in place, functioning effectively, and periodically reviewed to adapt to changing program and operating contexts.
    - Manage and report on the implementation of project MEAL plans, including regular progress tracking and reporting to the Director.
    - Coordinate closely with program team counterparts and ensure data is available in a timely and easily digestible format (e.g. dashboard creation) to facilitate data-informed and robust adaptive management processes
- **Data Management and Analysis:**
    - Operationalize NEF MEAL procedures and tools, including data collection, storage, analysis, and reporting (using KOBO, and other relevant tools).
    - Ensure the quality and accuracy of data collected and stored, overseeing data cleaning and validation, and conducting statistical analysis using tools such as SPSS and Excel.
    - Ensure appropriate data protection, confidentiality, access, and secure storage practices are applied across MEAL systems and datasets.
    - Analyze performance against indicators and targets, flag significant deviations, and work with program teams to identify appropriate corrective or adaptive actions.
    - Conduct qualitative and quantitative data analysis to provide comprehensive insights into project performance.
    - Facilitate various types of assessments, including impact, outcome, and process evaluations, in coordination with the HQ MEAL team.
- **Data Quality Assurance:**
- Lead and oversee internal Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), with support from the Data Analyst and relevant program teams, to ensure the validity, reliability, completeness, and consistency of program data. This includes:
    1. Conducting ongoing analysis of MEAL databases or trackers to identify data quality strengths, gaps, and inconsistencies.
    2. Supporting the development, implementation, and supervision of procedures to improve data quality and reporting.
    3. Ensuring identified data quality issues are documented, addressed, and followed up with relevant program and MEAL staff.
    4. Collecting and verifying, where applicable, supportive documentation to ensure consistency and accuracy in data management.
- **Training and Capacity Building:**
    - Train, support, and supervise MEAL staff, volunteers, and field agents on data collection, surveys, and project monitoring.
    - Where relevant, conduct capacity-building training for partner organizations and team members, including institutional needs assessments and socio-economic assessments.
- **Accountability and Feedback Mechanisms:**
    - Ensure accountability and feedback mechanisms are applied consistently across all projects, locations, and partners, including appropriate recording, referral, response, follow-up, and closure of feedback and complaints, in line with ethical, confidentiality, and transparency standards.
- **Learning and Documentation:**
    - Facilitate periodic learning sessions, reflection workshops or post-action reviews with project teams to identify lessons learned and best practices.
    - Contribute to project learning and adaptive management by documenting and sharing findings, lessons learned, learning papers, case studies, and beneficiary profiles.
    - Develop and disseminate communication and visibility materials (e.g., project overviews, fact sheets).
- **Evaluation and Reporting:**
    - Facilitate mid-term, final, and other ad hoc evaluations in coordination with the HQ MEAL team and regional office.
    - Contribute to and lead on projects' narrative reporting requirements, ensuring quality, data accuracy, and analysis.
    - Review and finalize MEAL reports (e.g., semiannual, endline) and provide feedback on project strategies to enhance performance and sustainability.
- **Collaboration and Coordination:**
    - Participate in monthly country coordination calls organized by HQ-based Program Officers.
    - Collaborate with the broader Syria team to ensure alignment on data collection, and MEAL system implementation.
    - Coordinate with the HQ MEAL Team backstop on technical guidance, MEAL standards and tools, organizational data requirements, learning priorities, and regional or global MEAL initiatives.
    - Participate and contribute to donor meetings as required.
- **Field Monitoring and Support:**
    - Conduct and oversee regular field monitoring follow-up activities, including focus group discussions with NEF beneficiaries.
    - Support partner capacity assessments and build capacity where necessary.
- **Additional Duties:**
    - Prepare field visits for NEF and external visitors, including photographers, journalists, or media if relevant.
    - Perform other duties as required and requested by the direct line manager or technical supervisor.

**Position Criteria**

- Strategic thinking, including identification of MEAL system weaknesses and initiative to address problem(s);
- Excellent organizational skills, accuracy and attention to detail;
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines;
- Ability to operate both independently and collaboratively as required.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in social sciences, humanities, quantitative/qualitative research methods, or a related field;
- At least Seven years of relevant professional experience in data collection, preferably with a national or international NGO, or other civil society organization;
- Fluent in written and spoken Arabic and English;
- Proficient in MS Office applications, particularly Word and Excel;
- Experience using digital data collection applications (e.g., KoboCollect, Akvo) is an asset;
- Plays an effective role within a team, able to communicate, develop, and maintain effective working relationships within a dynamic team environment.

title: Rwanda District Senior Supervisor (Fixed-Term)
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## About the Role

Seeking a strong field leader to drive Forest and Landscape Restoration and seedling production, lead field teams, achieve ambitious targets, and work closely with farmers and local governments to deliver impact.

## Responsibilities

Forestry & Seedling Production Operations

- Drive the execution of the Forest and Landscape Restoration (FLR) Program and oversee high-quality seedling production across assigned district sites.

Field Team Leadership & Capacity Building

- Direct and supervise Sector Supervisors, Site Supervisors, and Senior Field Officers, conducting regular training to build staff capacity and manage turnover.

Target Tracking & Operational Problem-Solving

- Monitor district performance metrics against key seasonal milestones, proactively identifying and resolving field operational or weather-related production challenges.

Stakeholder Management & Government Engagement

- Maintain strong collaborative relationships with local government officials, community leaders, and regional coordinators to support seamless program delivery.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's Degree in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, or a closely related field.
- 2 years of practical field experience in forestry, agroforestry, or agricultural project implementation.
- Demonstrated leadership experience in managing field teams, including Sector Supervisors and Field Officers.
- Experience in data analysis and tracking operational performance against field targets.
- Proven problem-solving ability to address seedling production challenges and seasonal field constraints.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills to engage local government authorities and smallholder farmers.
- Fluency in Kinyarwanda and English is required.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bugesera, Rwanda or Rwamagana, Rwanda or Rwanda, Karongi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

2 years

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

## Application Deadline

20 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

title: Officer, Events and Entertainment Relations Engagement
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**IRC UK**  
IRC UK is part of the IRC global network, which has its global headquarters in New York. Our team in the UK works to raise profile, deliver policy and practice change, and increase funding to help restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Since 2021, IRC UK has also provided integration services directly to refugees in England.  
In Europe, the IRC also has offices in Berlin, Bonn, Brussels, Geneva and Stockholm.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Experiential Marketing Team—working across the Marketing & Mobilization (M&M) Team and the UK Communications Team—this role is primarily responsible for elevating the IRC’s profile, brand, and influence, while supporting fundraising efforts. This will be achieved through event support, strategic engagement of celebrity ambassadors and digital tactics. In alignment with our Strategy100 commitments and the UK strategic plan, the position will deliver event production and talent-focused strategies that enhance the impact of IRC campaigns, initiatives, and appeals.

**Scope and Authority**

- Oversee the UK and European market events portfolio with flexibility to support other priority markets on a case-by-case basis as directed by leadership
- Lead and oversee various aspects of event project management (in-person and virtual), including team coordination, logistics, production, and execution from planning through post-event wrap-up. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

\- Drafting concept notes

\- Creating creative briefs

\- Conducting venue/vendor searches or setting up virtual platforms

\- Collaborating with various teams to align on event messaging and donor engagement strategies

\- Preparing and distributing event materials, communications, and other professional documents

\- Evaluating event effectiveness and analyzing audience data

- Assist on management of a global entertainment relations portfolio  
    \- Help identify and create opportunities to leverage existing talent in support of events and digital campaigns that advance the IRC’s fundraising, brand and advocacy goals (listed in order of priority)  
    \- Support Director with IRC’s celebrity supporters by managing ongoing communications to keep them informed, engaged, and aligned with IRC’s mission.
- Support in proactively identifying current events and cultural trends to leverage events and celebrity partners to meaningfully engage in support of IRC initiatives and events.
- Be available for occasional travel and work outside of standard hours, including evenings or weekends, to attend meetings or events.

**Key Working Relationships**

Ability to work effectively and creatively with a diverse array of external and internal collaborators in a way that represents the best of the IRC. These include IRC Fundraising, Policy & Advocacy, Digital and Media teams, as well as Celebrity representatives and contacts.

Strong social skills and project management skills, with emphasis on creating tangible outcomes. Ability to thrive in an fast-paced environment, to be flexible, to work across various internal teams and manage high-profile stakeholders.

Eager to learn about the entertainment industry and build meaningful relationships to help continue growing talent relations.

**Person Specification**

**Experience**

- Strong experience in event planning with the ability to organize events through all phases of development.
- Knowledge and experience of using social media channels as part of celebrity engagement and PR campaigns.
- Demonstrable experience of working strategically, identifying opportunities to support organisation-wide marketing strategies.

**Skills**

- Proven ability to project manage campaigns and events; working with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.
- Outstanding written and oral communication skills, and the ability to interact with a diverse range of people. In this post this would include senior leadership, celebrities, agents and journalists.
- Excellent relationship management skills.
- Exceptional judgement, analytical and prioritizing skills and experience of applying these in a fast-moving environment.
- Proven ability to take responsibility for tasks and act on own initiative particularly to solve problems and find solutions.
- Outstanding MS office and Event database management skills (Salesforce and Pardot, aka Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement, experience preferred).

Candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

**Compensation:** (GBP46,780 - GBP57922.78 GBP/Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

IRC UK strives to be an equal opportunities employer. IRC UK is committed to equality of opportunity and to non-discrimination for all job applicants and employees, and we seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce regardless of gender, race, religious beliefs, nationality, ethnic/national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.  
  
IRC UK welcomes applications from all candidates, including underrepresented groups and refugees who have the right to work in the UK.

  
IRC UK will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application and/or interview process, and for essential job functions if appointed to a role. Please contact us if you may need such adjustments.   
  
If you have any questions or need assistance with the online recruitment process, please contact the IRC UK HR team at applications@rescue-uk.org

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Senior Data Analyst
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Candidate Verification Step:** As part of our application process, candidates are asked to complete a brief verification exercise. This will involves In place of a cover letter, please complete a short data task. Download donors.csv and gifts.csv from [https://github.com/neilcuz/recruitment](https://github.com/neilcuz/recruitment) and use any tool you like (SQL, Python, R or similar) to answer the three multiple-choice questions there. It should take less time than writing a traditional cover letter. Upload a Word document (.docx) in the cover letter field containing only your answers, one per line, in this format:

- Q1: A
- Q2: B
- Q3: C

**Why we’re asking:** This step helps us confirm that every applicant is a real person and keeps the selection process fair for all candidates. It is not part of your skills assessment, and it will take only a few minutes.

**BACKGROUND**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The External Relations (ER) department was created in February 2020 and is comprised of 3 main but complementary functional areas: Private fundraising, Communications and Advocacy. The ER department is at the beginning stages of creating a radical and ambitious global strategy that will enhance IRC’s ability to ‘punch above its weight’ in private income, advocacy, and brand awareness. The main objective of the department is to enable this organization of more than 12,000 staff to have the resources needed to continue serving 18 million people worldwide in places affected by war and disaster, shape the humanitarian sector by influencing key policies and reforms, and build and grow IRC’s reputation.

We are looking for an experienced and highly analytical Senior Data Analyst to join our team, with a primary focus on supporting our Philanthropy and High Value fundraising teams. As a Senior Analyst within our Global Analytics team, you will play a pivotal role in supporting and driving data-driven insights for our fundraising efforts across the globe.

You will leverage your expertise in data analysis, statistical modeling, and reporting to guide the strategic decisions of our fundraising initiatives, ensuring that we continue to meet and exceed our goals. This position offers the opportunity to work closely with cross-functional teams, including fundraising, marketing, and finance, to deliver actionable insights that enhance donor engagement and maximize fundraising outcomes.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Data Analysis & Reporting:
    - Analyze and interpret large datasets to uncover trends, patterns, and insights that inform global fundraising strategies.
    - Create and maintain dashboards, visualizations, and reports to track fundraising performance and donor engagement metrics.
    - Develop and deliver regular performance reports to key stakeholders, highlighting actionable insights and areas of opportunity for growth.
    - Develop comprehensive data models and reports for external benchmarking to assess performance against peers and identify opportunities for new investments.
- Strategic Insights & Recommendations:
    - Collaborate with senior leadership to translate analytical findings into strategic recommendations for improving fundraising effectiveness.
    - Provide insights that influence global fundraising campaigns, donor retention strategies, and personalized donor experiences.
- Stakeholder Collaboration:
    - Act as the main analytics partner to the Philanthropy and High Value teams, building trusted relationships, understanding their priorities and building strong business knowledge of how these teams operate.
    - Work closely with cross-functional teams (e.g., fundraising, marketing, and finance) to ensure data-driven decisions are integrated into the global strategy.
    - Present findings to senior management, explaining complex data insights in a clear and actionable manner.
- Process Improvement & Innovation:
    - Identify opportunities to enhance the data collection and reporting processes, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and alignment with global goals.
    - Keep abreast of industry trends and emerging analytics tools, and bring innovative ideas for improving the team’s capabilities.
    - Acting as a technical leader, collaborate with fellow Analytics colleagues to ensure best practices in coding, statistics, and general analysis.
- Work with integrity and accountability to the “IRC Way” – IRC Global Standards for Professional Conduct.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

**Experience**

- 3+ years working in the field of data analytics.
- Proven experience with advanced data analytics tools (e.g., SQL, Python, R, Tableau, Power BI) and data visualization platforms.
- Demonstrable experience planning and executing complex analytics projects across multiple stakeholders.

**Skills & Competencies**

- More than two years of professional experience with SQL and relational databases.
- Knowledge of dimensional modeling and experience with workflow orchestration tools.
- Familiarity with PowerBI, Tableau, Looker, or other business intelligence tools.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data and provide actionable insights.

**Soft Skills**

- Curiosity and willingness to explore complex and ambiguous problems and deliver actionable insights through both quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
- Desire to work in a multi-cultural environment and collaborate with people from different backgrounds and experiences, with a partner-first approach to interacting with stakeholders.
- Strong data visualization and communication skills: ability to “tell a story” with numbers in a variety of formats: PowerPoints, dashboards, memos, and presentations.
- Strong attention to detail & commitment to a high standard of work product.

**Nice-to-Haves / Areas You Will Grow:**

- Knowledge of philanthropy, major gifts, or nonprofit fundraising analytics.
- Experience with Databricks and dbt.
- Experience with web analytics and behavioral data, and relevant tooling like Heap or Amplitude.
- Knowledge of Salesforce or similar CRM technology.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard office working environment.
- Some international travel.
- This role may require working remotely full or part time and part time remote employees may be required to share workspace.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America and United Kingdom.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $85,000 - $100,000/yr; UK Pay Rate £65,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. **US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Mission France - Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec les responsables de la protection, des activités médicales et de la santé mentale de l’unité migration, vous piloterez la stratégie de promotion et de médiation en santé et d’engagement communautaire.

Vous encadrerez les médiateur·rices en santé et les médiateur·rices interculturel·les, superviserez les interventions de terrain et contribuerez à adapter les activités du projet aux besoins et aux retours des personnes accompagnées.

Votre fonction associera pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe, mobilisation communautaire et présence opérationnelle sur le terrain.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de promotion et de médiation en santé**

- Concevoir, déployer et actualiser la stratégie de promotion de la santé, de médiation et d’engagement communautaire, en lien avec le·la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration.
- Définir les priorités, les activités, les outils et les modalités de suivi en fonction des besoins identifiés et de l’évolution du contexte.
- Garantir une approche participative, en associant les personnes accompagnées et les communautés à l’identification de leurs besoins et à l’élaboration des réponses.
- Superviser la création de supports de prévention et d’éducation à la santé, adaptés aux différents publics, en veillant à leur pertinence, à leur validation et à leur accessibilité linguistique et culturelle.
- Contribuer aux réflexions stratégiques et opérationnelles du projet, en collaboration avec les responsables des autres pôles.

**Piloter les activités communautaires et les interventions de terrain**

- Organiser et superviser les activités d’« aller-vers », les actions de sensibilisation, les ateliers collectifs et les activités de médiation individuelle.
- Veiller à la qualité des interventions menées sur les lieux de vie, lors des activités collectives et dans le lieu de répit.
- Développer des approches favorisant l’écoute, la confiance et la participation des personnes aux décisions qui concernent leur santé.
- Superviser la surveillance à base communautaire, notamment l’identification des besoins et des situations préoccupantes, la recherche active de cas et l’orientation vers les services de santé adaptés.
- Accompagner les médiateur·rices dans l’organisation des entretiens individuels et des rencontres communautaires.
- Coordonner, avec les autres responsables de pôles, les évaluations rapides des besoins et les interventions nécessitant une approche pluridisciplinaire.

**Manager, accompagner et développer les compétences de l’équipe**

- Encadrer les médiateur·rices en santé et les médiateur·rices interculturel·les, et organiser leurs plannings en fonction des activités du projet.
- Participer aux recrutements, à l’intégration et à l’évaluation des membres de l’équipe, en collaboration avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences associant formation, accompagnement individuel, coaching et partage de pratiques.
- Superviser la qualité des activités, notamment les méthodes participatives, les techniques pédagogiques, l’écoute active et l’utilisation des outils de médiation.
- Favoriser la coopération, la circulation des informations et la complémentarité entre les équipes, tout en assurant la continuité des activités en cas d’absence.

**Analyser les besoins et renforcer les liens avec les communautés et les partenaires**

- Mettre en place des dispositifs de recueil et d’analyse des retours des personnes et des communautés, notamment des perceptions, préoccupations et rumeurs liées à la santé.
- Contribuer aux évaluations rapides, aux enquêtes et à l’analyse qualitative des besoins individuels et des dynamiques communautaires.
- Développer et actualiser une cartographie participative des communautés, des associations et des acteurs du territoire, en intégrant les observations des équipes de maraude.
- Entretenir les relations avec les partenaires et partager les informations utiles à l’adaptation des interventions.
- Superviser la collecte des données, analyser les tendances, produire les rapports d’activité et documenter les enseignements tirés des interventions.
- Utiliser ces analyses pour proposer des ajustements opérationnels et améliorer la pertinence des actions de promotion et de médiation en santé.

**Garantir la sécurité, la qualité et les moyens nécessaires aux activités**

- Assurer la fonction de point focal sécurité pour les équipes lors des interventions  
    d’« aller-vers ».
- Veiller à l’application des mesures de safeguarding dans l’ensemble des activités et à leur bonne compréhension par les membres de l’équipe.
- Garantir le respect des principes, protocoles et standards de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Planifier et suivre les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires au fonctionnement du pôle, en collaboration avec les départements concernés.
- Contribuer à l’amélioration continue des pratiques et à la capitalisation des expériences du projet.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Licence en sciences sociales, sciences du comportement, santé publique, médiation en santé ou santé communautaire, ou diplôme d’infirmier·ère en santé communautaire.
- Une expérience significative dans l’accompagnement de publics vulnérables et le management d’équipe peut également correspondre au profil recherché.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes ou de projets de médiation en santé ou de santé communautaire, en France, à l’étranger ou au sein de MSF.
- Expérience indispensable dans l’utilisation de méthodes qualitatives.
- Expérience requise dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi de stratégies.
- Expérience en management d’équipe.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Solides capacités d’analyse, de réflexion stratégique et d’adaptation des interventions aux réalités du terrain.
- Aptitude à encadrer, accompagner et faire progresser une équipe.
- Sens de l’écoute, qualités relationnelles et capacité à instaurer un dialogue avec des publics divers.
- Capacité à travailler en équipe pluridisciplinaire et à coopérer avec différents partenaires.
- Sens de l’organisation, orientation vers les résultats et exigence de qualité.
- Engagement envers les principes de promotion de la santé et de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Flexibilité et capacité à évoluer dans des environnements difficiles et changeants, y compris lors d’activités de nuit.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne maîtrise de l’anglais souhaitée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.
- La connaissance de logiciels de traitement de données qualitatives (NVivo), de création graphique (Photoshop), de collecte de données ou de cartographie (KoboCollect, OsmAnd, QGIS) constitue un atout.
