Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood, and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge. For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries. We won’t stop until we are all equal

Plan International has been working in the Asia Pacific (APAC) Region since 1960. Currently there are 12 Country Offices (COs) that includes Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Thailand, Timor Leste, and Vietnam and 3 Fundraising Country/National Offices (FCNOs): (Indonesia, India, and Philippines); and 4 National Offices (NOs): HongKong, Australia, Japan, and Korea in the Asia Pacific Region.

In Asia Pacific region, through Humanitarian and Resilience programing, we build communities’ resilience and support children’s right to dignity and protection before, during and after disasters and conflicts. Aligned with the Global Strategy 2022 – 2027, Plan International will Scale up humanitarian impact as one of the program priorities where we aim to become a leading agency protection children’s right and promoting equality for girls in crisis. We will enhance humanitarian preparedness throughout the organisation, strengthen integration of humanitarian-development and peace work and finally improve ways of working to respond quickly and effective to emergencies. Plan International want to reach more children especially girls, in less time, save lives and leave lasting impact.

 Under the supervision of the Regional Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience,   
 the Regional Humanitarian Preparedness and Response Coordinator will provide support to   
 strengthen the disaster preparedness, readiness and response to disaster caused by natural   
 hazard nor climate related hazards as well as conflict and protracted crisis in Asia Pacific   
 region.

 The expected role is to support oversee the achievement of Country’s Ready to Respond (R2R), conduct regular analysis of disaster risk and conflict trends in the region, manage the emergency response data base and its documentation, promote the importance of Accountability to Affected People and support coordinate the APAC’ Children in Crisis Fund (CiCF) and representing Plan International in specific emergency technical working groups in particular the Accountability to Affected People (AAP) Working Group, CVA Working Group and the Regional Gender in Humanitarian Action (GiHA) network. Lastly this post holder is expected to be deployed in the initial phase of response and or during recovery phase to support COs in his/her capacity as technical advisor and or Deputy Emergency Response Manager as well as potential seconded to Country Offices to provide technical support in any humanitarian preparedness and readiness work in normal situation and support with delivering humanitarian related training i.e. Emergency Response Team (ERT) Training.

**DIMENSIONS OF THE ROLE**

The post holder serves as the principal regional coordinator on humanitarian preparedness and response related deliverables in Asia Pacific region and work in close coordination and collaboration with the Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience and the Regional Anticipatory Action and Climate Specialist.

This post covers 15 countries in the region with supervision of Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience and is expected to be part of Plan International Global Roster and deployed to support other COs in other region especially during Red alert emergencies.

The role works with Country Offices and regional teams to support ensuring a quality of humanitarian preparedness, readiness and response in an accountable and timely manner and contribute to strengthening Plan International’s visibility as Humanitarian actor in the region.

The Specific Dimension of the roles comprises of:

**Support programmatic and data management of humanitarian action in APAC:**

- A primary support function to the 15 Country Offices on issues relating to Emergency Preparedness, Readiness and Response, i.e. quarterly hotspot analysis, manage humanitarian preparedness and database and collecting CO contribution for monthly humanitarian round up.
- Provide support to ensure the timely update of CO’s Ready to Respond (R2R) Minimum Preparedness Action (MPA) implementation and it progress.
- Support manages the humanitarian dashboard of APAC
- Coordinating the APAC Children in Crisis Fund (CiCF) together with the assigned CiCF task-team; including responsible for drafting reports to respective donor.
- This post holder is expected to be deployed in the initial phase of response or during recovery phase to support COs in his/her capacity as technical advisor and or Deputy Emergency Response Manager as well as potential seconded to Country Offices to provide technical support in any humanitarian preparedness and readiness work in normal situation.

**Support strengthening COs capacity to be ready to respond**

- Provide support in facilitating CO’s humanitarian related training i.e. Emergency Response Team (ERT) training and CVA training; and other training linking with thematic sector lead in the organization.
- Provide support in roll out the R2R approach to the remaining CO in FY 27/28 together with the Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience.

**Support regional coordination and networking**

- The post holder will have to maintain excellent working relationships with colleagues in COs, Nos, the Global Humanitarian Team (APAC) and Regional Hub colleagues.
- This post will also act as thematic leads for different humanitarian networks in APAC in particular the regional Accountability to Affected People (AAP) Working Group, Regional Cash Voucher Assistance (CVA) Working Group, Regional GiHA Working Group and should have a strong Gender in Emergencies understanding and knowledge.

**Accountabilities**

**In non-emergencies: strengthen disaster preparedness, readiness and response capacity**

- Facilitate and support the roll out of various training and capacity building initiatives related to the implementation of the humanitarian scale up priorities.
- Prepare, and periodically update, a disaster/hazard calendar ( the ‘Hotspots analysis’) for the Asia Pacific and undertake an analysis and recommend use of existing early warning systems for Plan’s programming.
- Facilitate and support all countries in the region to go through an intensive Ready to Respond (R2R) Approach and ensure all agreed Minimum Preparedness Action (MPAs) are implemented according to its timeframe.
- Continue promoting the utilization of the Emergency Response manual for Operation and Programme in country offices in the region.
- Manage the emergency response’s database for Asia Pacific and present it in infographic in semester basis including contributing the GHT humanitarian footprint data.
- Facilitate learning and sharing of humanitarian relate resources/tools/experiences between countries in the region.
- Identify and produce a high-quality documentation of evidence in APAC region to justify the contribution for humanitarian scale up priorities in collaboration with MERL Specialists in APAC.
- Support the supervisor and Humanitarian and Resilience Team to review a new Country Strategy document and ensure the inclusion of risks/hazards related to disasters, conflict and environment in their child rights analysis and designed programs accordingly
- Support strengthens external engagement and coordination with other humanitarian actors (UN, NGOs, donors, etc) in the different technical sector through regular attendance in relevant networks and coordination forums, clusters especially on AAP, CPiE, EiE and CVA Network.
- Provide technical support at COs level to increase representation in the humanitarian network i.e. Humanitarian Country Team and other relevant national clusters. Conduct mentoring to COs representative in the leading/coordinating role in the in-county network as required.
- Working in collaboration with APAC technical specialists in development to promote the utilization if the Emergency Response Manual for Programme and promote nexus approach.
- Potential to be seconded to Country Office to provide technical support for humanitarian preparedness and readiness work in normal situation
- Coordinating the APAC Children in Crisis Fund (CiCF) in collaboration with its task force including drafting the donor reports in semester basis.

**In emergencies context**

- In all significant disasters, ready to deploy to assist the assigned ERM/Deputy ERM/Managers/Focal points at country level to design rapid assessment, compile reports, and drafting response plan, in consultations with Country Director and the Emergency Response Management Team (ERMT). The duration of deployment could be vary from 4 – 12 weeks at the initial phase of response.
- In all responses in APAC (regardless the scale), support COs in identifying the surge capacity needs internal COs, within the Region or require support from the Global Roster in close coordination with the supervisor.
- During deployment and or remote support for all emergencies, support strengthen the accountability of the response and the incorporation of Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI), Safeguarding, PSHEA and promoting CVA and MPCA as modality whenever appropriate.
- In the later stage of the response (early recovery and recovery phase) ready to be deployed to support CO in her/his capacity to provide technical support advice both at programmatic and operation as agreed with the Country Management Team and the supervisor. The duration of deployment in this stage could be varied from 4 – 8 weeks-time.
- Support COs in preparing the Real Time Review (RTR) for all orange 2 emergencies and facilitate coordination with the Supervisor.
- Support countries in documentation of lessons from all significant disasters and ensure it circulation to the internal and external organization as needed.

**Key relationships**

**Internal:**

- APAC Humanitarian and Resilience team
- APAC’s Program and Influencing Team
- APAC’s communication Team
- APAC Grants, Admin, Supply Chain and P&C team
- Country Humanitarian Manager/Advisors/ERMs and H&R teams at CO level
- Global Humanitarian Team
- CPiE Network
- EiE Network
- Cash Network
- SRHRiE Network
- GiE Network
- Accountability to Affected People (AAP) Network
- National Organisation’s Humanitarian team especially who in charge for humanitarian work

**External:**

- IASC Network
- Relevant Humanitarian actors to coordinate Plan’s work with other international/regional/national institutions, clusters and donors in line with Plan’s global strategy
- Academics, research institute and thought leaders in humanitarian work in Asia Pacific region

**Technical expertise, skills and knowledge**

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Documented experience from disaster risk management work, including disaster preparedness, readiness and managing response programmes.
- Documented experience from at least 2 major disaster events, working in “disaster /high risk” environments.
- Documented experience as a trainer/facilitator on humanitarian issues especially on international Humanitarian standard and one of the technical sectors CPiE, EiE, CVA, SRHRiE or WASHiE and Gender in Emergencies.
- Ability to priorities and manage complex and varied workload, often to tight deadlines
- Experience of strategy, i.e. analysing relevant factors from both the internal and external environments, identifying crucial issues that have to be addressed, setting objectives and developing plans of actions.
- Excellent communication skills, written and verbal in order to present arguments clearly and powerfully to a variety of audiences.
- Direct experience of working with children and young people and in understanding and responding to their needs and rights.
- Experience of working with institutional donors/fundraisers.
- Experience in utilisation of humanitarian standards i.e. Sphere, CHS, INEE MS on EiE, CPMS and other standards included in the Humanitarian Standard Partnership (HSP).
- Experience of promoting coordination and cooperation with other agencies through networking and alliance building.

**Skills**

- Energetic and motivated individual, with a proven track record of undertaking similar assignments successfully
- Expert in one of the technical sectors such as CPiE or EiE or SRHRiE, WASHiE and familiar with cash voucher assistance (CVA) as modality in emergency situations**.**
- Familiar with the concept of gender in emergencies
- Good interpersonal skills and able to work in a dynamic environment with multiple stakeholders at different level.
- Ability to think strategically, but also result oriented and get things done.
- Commitment to continuous learning and willingness to keep abreast of new developments in the field of humanitarian and resilience and it adherence to the humanitarian principles and standards.
- Able to work independently, but to function within a virtual team.
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to establish and sustain good working relations with colleagues
- Strong negotiation, facilitating, representation and influencing skills including familiar with Artificial Intelligence (AI) for humanitarian work
- Culturally and socially sensitive, and able to work successfully with partners and sector professionals

**Leadership Behaviours**

- Leads the theoretical discussion and strategy development.
- Coaches and builds capacity of both program and support staff in APAC and COs
- Promotes innovation and learning
- Communicates clearly and effectively
- Strong team building and motivational skills
- Critical and creative thinking
- Ability to influence
- Result oriented
- Flexible
- Good interpersonal skills

**Physical Environment and Demands:**

This position entails 50-60 % travel both within and outside region, often in hardship locations.

**Level of Contact with Children:**

Mid contact: Occasional interaction with children

**Plan International’s Values in Practice**

**We are open and accountable**

- Promotes a culture of openness and transparency, including with sponsors and donors.
- Holds self and others accountable to achieve the highest standards of integrity.
- Consistent and fair in the treatment of people.
- Open about mistakes and keen to learn from them.
- Accountable for ensuring we are a safe organisation for all children, girls & young people

**We strive for lasting impact**

- Articulates a clear purpose for staff and sets high expectations.
- Creates a climate of continuous improvement, open to challenge and new ideas.
- Focuses resources to drive change and maximise long-term impact, responsive to changed priorities or crises.
- Evidence-based and evaluates effectiveness.

**We work well together**

- Seeks constructive outcomes, listens to others, willing to compromise when appropriate.
- Builds constructive relationships across Plan International to support our shared goals.
- Develops trusting and ‘win-win’ relationships with funders, partners and communities.
- Engages and works well with others outside the organization to build a better world for girls and all children.

**We are inclusive and empowering**

- We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential
- We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge equality in our programs and our workplace
- We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives

**Physical Environment**

Position is based at Plan International Thailand’s Country Office in Thailand with occasional work in local partner offices as needed for delivering project activities and outcomes.

title: ICT Strategy & Digital Transformation Consultancy
body:
**Purpose & Scope of work**  
Afghanaid seeks to engage an independent ICT consultant or consulting firm to undertake a focused review  
of its ICT environment and develop a practical ICT Strategy and Digital Transformation Roadmap. The  
assignment will focus on strengthening operational resilience, cybersecurity, inter-office connectivity,  
systems integration, business continuity, and digital service delivery. The consultancy is expected to provide:  
a) Clear findings on the current ICT environment;  
b) Prioritised and practical recommendations;  
c) A high-level target ICT architecture and operating model; and  
d) A phased and costed implementation roadmap aligned with organisational priorities, capacity, and  
budget.  
The objective is to provide Afghanaid with an implementable roadmap that supports operational continuity,  
informed decision-making, and future ICT investment planning.  
The assignment will support Afghanaid in making informed and cost-effective ICT investment decisions by  
identifying priority areas for improvement, reducing operational and cybersecurity risks, strengthening interoffice connectivity, business continuity and organisational resilience, and ensuring that future ICT  
investments are planned, prioritised, and aligned with organisational needs and available resources. The  
resulting roadmap will provide a structured basis for budgeting, resource allocation, and medium-term  
planning.

**The Consultant shall:**  
a) Review Afghanaid's current ICT environment, governance, infrastructure, systems, service delivery,  
processes, and operational challenges;  
b) Identify risks, gaps, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities;  
Page 2 of 5  
c) Assess ICT asset lifecycle management, including device assignment, inventory management,  
maintenance, replacement planning, procurement governance, and end-user support processes.  
d) Develop a future-state ICT operating model and high-level enterprise architecture;  
e) Recommend priority for modernization, system integration, automation, AI adoption,  
cybersecurity, and data governance.  
f) Establish practical governance, service management, asset management frameworks to improve  
accountability, service quality and organization resilience;  
g) Prepare a phased and costed roadmap to support budgeting and decision-making.  
1\. Existing Strategic Decisions  
The following organisational initiatives are already approved and are not subject to strategic review:  
a) ERP modernisation (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central);  
b) CRM development and enhancement; and  
c) Website platform development.  
d) Odoo, CRM and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central integration.  
The Consultant shall focus on dependencies, risks, and alignment of these initiatives within the overall ICT  
roadmap rather than recommending alternative platforms. The assignment does not require detailed low  
level system design or implementation-level specifications.

**2. Current Landscape**  
Afghanaid operates across Afghanistan through a head office, provincial offices, district locations, and  
partner organisations. The organisation relies heavily on ICT systems to support programme delivery,  
financial management, fundraising, human resources, communication, monitoring and evaluation, and  
operational coordination.  
a) Over recent years, Afghanaid has invested in network infrastructure, collaboration tools, enterprise  
systems, connectivity, and digital capabilities. Core systems currently include:  
b) Microsoft Dynamics NAV 2013 (upgradation to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central in  
progress);  
c) Salesforce CRM;  
d) Odoo HRMIS;  
e) Google Workspace; and  
f) Microsoft Teams.  
While these systems support key business functions, they have developed over time with limited integration,  
creating challenges in data management, reporting, governance, operational efficiency, and service delivery.  
Key areas requiring improvement include business continuity, disaster recovery, cybersecurity, data  
protection, systems integration, service management, and operational resilience in low-connectivity and  
high-risk environments.

**3. Strategic Priorities and Transformation Drivers**  
Afghanaid operates in a complex and volatile environment characterised by security risks, political  
uncertainty, constrained connectivity, and periodic internet disruptions that may impact field operations.  
These conditions require ICT systems that are resilient, secure, and capable of sustaining operations under  
remote, low-connectivity, and high-risk scenarios.  
To support operational continuity, Afghanaid must strengthen its enterprise network architecture, inter office  
connectivity, collaboration tools to ensure uninterrupted communication between headquarters, provincial  
offices, and district-level structures, regardless of external disruptions. In parallel, the organisation must  
enhance its capability for secure remote working through the implementation of digitised workflow systems  
and standardised collaboration tools.  
There is also a critical need to strengthen cybersecurity controls, data protection mechanisms, and identity  
and access management, including improved governance of licensed software, online accounts, and  
password security. These measures are essential to mitigate evolving cyber threats and reduce organisational  
exposure to security risks. Continued investment in staff digital capacity is required to ensure effective system  
adoption and operational efficiency across all user groups.  
Afghanaid should also progressively expand and optimise the use of ERP capabilities across the organisation,  
where operationally and financially viable. In addition, the organisation must accelerate the digitisation of  
monitoring, evaluation, and needs assessment processes to improve data quality, timeliness, and decisionmaking.  
As Afghanaid’s digital presence continues to grow, its web and social media platforms must remain current,  
secure, and strategically aligned with organisational communications objectives. In parallel, there is a need  
to enhance donor management workflows to improve efficiency and accuracy.

**Key Priorities: The following strategic priorities have been identified:**  
▪ Network architecture, resilience, inter-office connectivity, and collaboration tools: This includes assessment  
and optimisation of enterprise network architecture, connectivity between HQ, provincial and district offices,  
and collaboration platforms to ensure secure, reliable, and uninterrupted communication under lowconnectivity, high-risk, and disruption-prone operating conditions.  
▪ Platform consolidation and standardisation: The parallel use of Google Workspace and Microsoft Teams  
increases exposure to phishing, account compromise, and unauthorised access. There is a need to standardise  
collaboration and communication platforms to strengthen governance, security, and operational control.  
▪ Digital transformation and automation: Develop a practical roadmap for digital transformation, workflow  
automation, AI readiness, and the controlled transition towards a paperless operating environment,  
supported by governance, change management, and user adoption.  
▪ Cybersecurity and resilience: Strengthening cybersecurity governance, technical controls, identity and access  
management, security monitoring, vulnerability management and organisational data protection, and  
business continuity frameworks is essential, particularly in the context of low-connectivity environments and  
operational risk exposure.  
▪ Data protection and ethical governance: Robust data protection, privacy, and ethical data governance  
frameworks must be established and enforced in line with international standards.  
▪ Business continuity and disaster recovery: Formalisation and strengthening of business continuity and  
disaster recovery capabilities is required to ensure operational stability under disruption scenarios.  
▪ Capacity development: Structured staff training and continuous digital capability development programmes  
are required to ensure sustainable adoption of systems and processes.  
▪ Information security and risk management: Strengthening enterprise-wide information security governance  
and risk management frameworks is required to support organisational resilience.  
▪ IT service management: Improvement of ICT service delivery, service desk operations, incident management,  
request fulfilment, problem management, and change management, support project managers and M&E  
staff, and operational governance is required to enhance efficiency, accountability, and user experience.  
▪ Digital alignment: ICT systems must be continuously aligned and integrated in line with evolving technological  
trends and the organisation’s operational and strategic priorities.  
Afghanaid therefore requires independent technical expertise to assess its current ICT environment and  
develop strategic, technically robust, and implementation-ready recommendations for a secure, integrated,  
and scalable digital ecosystem aligned with organisational needs.

**4. Duration of the Assignment**  
The consultancy shall be executed in accordance with an agreed project implementation plan, detailing clearly  
defined milestones, deliverables, and timelines. The overall assignment is expected to be completed within 4  
months from the date of contract signing, unless an extension is formally agreed in writing by both parties.  
The Consultant shall ensure timely delivery of all outputs in accordance with the approved work plan and  
shall report progress regularly to Afghanaid’s designated project manager or senior management.

**5. Consultant Qualifications**  
The consulting firm or individual consultant must demonstrate the following qualifications, expertise, and  
experience:  
• Experience in developing and implementing enterprise-wide ICT strategies and digital transformation  
plans.  
• Evidence of previous assignments of a similar nature with NGOs or grant funded organisations, the  
firm shall provide a list of relevant clients and references, including contact details “where available”.  
• Proven expertise in enterprise architecture frameworks and designing integrated ICT ecosystems.  
• Experience in aligning ICT architecture with operational, governance, and data management  
requirements.  
• Knowledge and practical experience with cybersecurity frameworks, risk assessments, vulnerability  
management, and mitigation strategies.  
• Familiarity with ISO 27001 or equivalent security standards.  
• Knowledge of GDPR and internationally recognised data protection and privacy standards.  
• Experience establishing data governance, privacy, and ethical information management frameworks.  
• Strong understanding of digital workflows, automation, AI applications, cloud solutions, and  
emerging ICT technologies.  
• Experience in implementing practical digital innovations that enhance operational efficiency and  
decision-making.  
• Ability to propose training programmes to ensure sustainable adoption of recommended systems and  
processes.

**6. Confidentiality and Data Protection**  
The Consultant shall treat all information, data, and documentation obtained or accessed during the course  
of this assignment as strictly confidential. This includes, but is not limited to, organisational records, financial  
data, donor information, programme details, and staff information.  
The Consultant shall:  
• Comply fully with Afghanaid’s data protection policies and all applicable data protection laws,  
including GDPR.  
• Ensure that all sensitive information is stored, transmitted, and processed securely, preventing  
unauthorised access, disclosure, or loss.  
• Use the information solely for the purposes of delivering the consultancy assignment.  
• Return or securely destroy all organisational data and materials upon completion of the assignment,  
unless otherwise agreed in writing.  
• Immediately notify Afghanaid of any actual or suspected breach of confidentiality or data security.  
The Consultant acknowledges that any breach of confidentiality or improper handling of data may result in  
legal liability and termination of the consultancy contract.

**7. Evaluation and Selection Process**  
Afghanaid will apply a structured, transparent, and competitive evaluation process to assess all eligible  
proposals. Submissions will be evaluated in two stages: (i) technical evaluation and (ii) financial evaluation.  
Only proposals that meet the minimum technical threshold will proceed to financial assessment.  
The technical evaluation will assess the bidder’s understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology,  
and compliance with the functional and technical requirements. Financial proposals will be evaluated based  
on overall cost-effectiveness and value for money. Proposals will also be assessed for clarity, completeness,  
and alignment with the scope of work. Technical and financial proposals will be weighted, unless otherwise  
specified, at 70% for technical and 30% for financial evaluation. The combined score will be used to determine  
the most economically and technically advantageous proposal.  
Afghanaid may request clarifications, conduct interviews, and require shortlisted bidders to present or  
demonstrate their proposed solution either virtually or in person as part of the evaluation process. Afghanaid  
reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal, in whole or in part, and may cancel the procurement  
process at any stage without incurring any liability.

title: Strategy and Planning Senior Officer, Global Policy & Advocacy
body:
**Background**: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. We deliver lasting impact by providing health care, helping children learn, and empowering individuals and communities to become self-reliant, always with a focus on the unique needs of women and girls. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, we now work in over 40 crisis-affected countries as well as communities throughout the U.S., Europe and Latin America.

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The Strategy and Planning Senior Officer will lead on key strategic planning and prioritization efforts for the Policy & Advocacy team. The Senior Officer will coordinate portions of organization-wide strategy and investment planning, collaborate with the Vice President of Policy & Advocacy on team prioritization processes, and manage a collaborative but streamlined process for strategy development. This person will maintain crucial processes and relationships and collaborate at all levels within and across the teams, and across the IRC.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Facilitate priority-setting processes:** Translate organization-wide strategy and policy products into department strategies, market-specific advocacy priorities, and thematic policy areas of focus.
- **Lead strategy development processes:** Work closely with Policy and Advocacy team members to support the development of specific, actionable policy and advocacy strategies, helping individual units develop strategies relevant to their priority issues and their geographic/political markets that include stakeholder mapping, activity planning, product development plans, and desired external change metrics as relevant. Lead Policy and Advocacy engagement in organization-wide annual planning processes, linking Policy and Advocacy planning to multi-year organizational strategies and Department-wide objectives.
- **Develop and facilitate activities and processes across Policy and Advocacy teams:** Facilitate and maintain efficient ways of working within, across, and with the Policy and Advocacy teams as appropriate. Identify and elevate collaboration challenges and develop ways of working systems to address those issues. Ensure ways of working are routinely updated to address feedback from team members and represent team in org-wide, multi-departmental process conversations.
- **Manage long-term projects**: Own project management, strategic content development, and logistics for key team efforts such as the Annual Planning and Quarterly Pause processes, retreat planning, and others.
- **Facilitate cross-team collaboration and communication:** Create tools and processes for effectively sharing information and collaborating internally, communicating with IRC stakeholders routinely, and managing workflows in a streamlined and smooth manner. Facilitate regular, effective, and efficient communication between team members and from organizational leadership to the rest of the teams, cascading information from ER leadership, finance, and HR as necessary. Manage the internal website and routine reporting to senior leaders. Develop deep understanding of Policy and Advocacy priorities and strategies in order to communicate effectively about team objectives and outcomes with internal stakeholders through reporting processes, internal websites, email and other means as appropriate.
- **Lead KPI development and progress tracking:** Working with the VP and members of the Policy and Advocacy team develop a set of high-level objectives for teams alongside a more detailed set of KPIs to enable reporting out to the organization on progress. Plan and facilitate quarterly internal progress reviews of individual strategies (and associated metrics) across Policy and Advocacy. Ensure KPIs and reporting metrics are logical, consistent, and regularly reported on by team members on a weekly basis.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Organize team retreats, staff meetings, team building activities and trainings.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Vice President of Policy & Advocacy with a Management in Partnership to the Director of Strategy & Planning  
**Position directly supervises:** N/A  
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:*** Global Policy and Advocacy team; Strategy & Planning Team; Business Operations; Marketing and Mobilization; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department; President’s Office; Finance; Information Technology; Human Resources

***External:*** NGOs, think tanks, U.S. government agencies, Congress, multilateral institutions and other organizations as needed

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:*** Bachelor’s degree in International Relations, Political Science or other related field

***Work Experience:***

- 5-6 years work experience, experience in policy and advocacy preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent organizational and time management skills, including juggling competing priorities and tight deadlines and prioritizing tasks appropriately
- Experience designing and implementing strategic planning processes and progress metrics
- Positive, resourceful and flexible attitude with ability to problem solve, work productively both in a team environment or independently as needed, and take initiative in a fast-faced environment
- Familiarity with or experience in policy analysis or advocacy to high-level policymakers and thought leaders
- Strong project management skills, ideally within a cross-organizational team to deliver on projects/strategies
- Solid English language writing and editing skills with a focus on details
- Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to develop and manage complex relationships, including with high-level individuals
- Familiarity with or proven interest in humanitarian aid sector, foreign policy, and/or refugee issues
- Fluency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and ability to learn online web-based applications
- Ambition to learn and grow skills by taking on challenging tasks, and mastering complex content and concepts
- Commitment to advancing equity, diversity, and inclusion at the IRC and in the humanitarian field
- Lived experience with conflict or crisis-driven displacement, resettlement, asylum, immigration or migration is an asset in this role

\*\*Working Environment:\*\*Hybrid office work environment. Up to 5% travel may be required.

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $92,000 - $99,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Project Director, Virtual Services
body:
**Job Overview:**

The Project Director of Virtual Services at the International Rescue Committee (IRC) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of a national portfolio of virtual resettlement programs that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, particularly those living outside traditional service areas. The portfolio includes legacy resettlement programs, state-run programs as well as [ALMA](https://welcome.rescue.org/us/en/services/alma), an AI-powered virtual assistant that helps newcomers navigate essential resources and services. The Project Director also contributes to the Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department’s virtual and information services strategy.

The role oversees virtual program strategy, implementation, performance, and budget management. It also ensures compliance with award requirements through programmatic monitoring and rigorous direct assistance operations, and it oversees the case management and data systems that support reporting and evidence of impact. The Director leads a geographically dispersed team and cultivates partnerships with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders. A central focus of the position is developing and scaling innovative, technology-enabled service delivery models that strengthen operational efficiency and promote client self-sufficiency. This position reports to the Senior Director of Resettlement.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Program Implementation**: Lead the design, implementation, and scaling of a national portfolio of virtual programs (some examples include Program of Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, Preferred Communities) that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, leveraging innovative, client-centered service delivery models to reach underserved populations.
- **Interagency Collaboration:** Provide strategic leadership and oversight of interagency virtual services working groups, fostering collaboration and alignment across resettlement agencies to inform program strategy, coordinate implementation, and strengthen virtual service delivery.
- **People & Culture:** Build and cultivate an inclusive, impactful team. Support managers in their leadership of teams in line with IRC's People Manager Standards to ensure successful program delivery and a safe, supportive environment for clients and staff.
- **Monitoring & Compliance:** Design and enable effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on program services. Ensure a data-driven approach that informs program adaptation and provides further evidence of virtual services impact.
- **Budget & Financial Management:** Coordinate with HQ Finance staff to ensure compliance with donor and organizational requirements including financial planning, expenditure monitoring, caseload forecasting, and effective resource allocation.
- **AI Product Strategy and Management:** Lead the product strategy, development, and deployment of ALMA, IRC's AI-powered virtual assistant, in collaboration with the Airbel Impact Lab and IRC's technical development teams. Oversee product roadmaps, iterative development, testing, and the rollout of new features and international adaptations, including expansion to Poland.
- **Client Engagement and Co-Design:** Lead IRC's Service Excellence Advisory Committee, creating structured opportunities for refugees and other newcomers to inform program design, implementation, and continuous improvement. Integrate client feedback and lived experiences into service delivery, technology development, and strategic decision-making.
- **Technical Expertise and Resource Mobilization:** Provide technical expertise and strategic input into the development of grant proposals, funding opportunities, and program designs that expand and strengthen virtual service delivery across IRC's resettlement network. Identify and apply for opportunities to advance virtual services.
- **Strategic Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement:** Cultivate and maintain partnerships with government agencies, national resettlement organizations, and other key stakeholders to advance virtual service delivery, strengthen interagency coordination, and identify opportunities for program expansion.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

***Work Experience:***

- Minimum 5-7 years of progressively responsible work experience with refugee resettlement; experience and deep familiarity with initial resettlement programming.
- 3-4 years of program management experience; experience scaling program response preferred.
- Significant staff management, program development, monitoring, and evaluation experience.

***Education:***

- Master's degree in non-profit management, social work, sociology, migration studies, law, or international development or equivalent preferred.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.

- Financial management, including effective management of contract-based budgets.

- Proven people management skills; demonstrated ability to deliver results and translate words into action.

- Superior organizational skills: ability to set priorities and effectively manage time in a fast-paced team environment.

- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Strong digital literacy, including MS Office suite, database systems.

- Familiarity with generative AI in client settings.

***Language Skills:***

- Fluency in written and spoken English.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Fully remote.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $85,000 - $105,00/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Associate, Malaria and NTDs
body:
## **Overview**

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: [http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org](http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org/).

*CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.*

**Position Overview**

Your responsibilities will involve supporting the malaria program in scaling up interventions to effectively reduce the disease burden in Angola. The selected candidate will be responsible for a wide range of tasks, from conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses, to designing data-driven strategic plans, to providing operational support to ensure the execution of effective, high-impact programs. The Associate will develop and maintain strong relationships with CHAI teams supporting the malaria program, as well as with relevant government, technical, and implementing partners. They will also identify areas for intervention related to improvements in vector control, surveillance, and program implementation, and be able to initiate work plans to address these issues quickly and with limited guidance.

The candidate must have excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, communication, and project management skills, as well as strong cultural sensitivity and emotional intelligence. The selected candidate must embody CHAI's values, including resourcefulness, patience, tenacity, humility, independence, frugality, and a strong work ethic.

The position will be based in Luanda, with frequent travel to Angola's provinces and occasional international travel.

## **Responsibilities**

- Provide technical assistance to the national malaria program to refine malaria control interventions.
- Support the development and monitoring of government strategies, roadmaps, and costed work plans.
- Work with CHAI colleagues and government counterparts to assess strategies, identify and prioritize resource gaps, and develop new funding proposals for the country.
- Contribute to the drafting, review, and feedback of technical products, which may include strategic plans, guidelines, grant proposals, donor reports, or implementation updates.
- Contribute to the design and execution of monitoring and evaluation to measure progress toward malaria control objectives (analysis of key indicators, design, and execution of monitoring and evaluation of surveillance platforms, etc.).
- Monitor program activities against project objectives and donor commitments, identify bottlenecks or operational shortcomings, and work collaboratively with national and global CHAI teams to achieve exceptional results within tight timelines.
- Identify new opportunities within and beyond the project's initial scope, anticipate risks, and be proactive in responding to them.
- Support the drafting of programmatic reports for government and donors, as well as concept notes or other external communication products.
- Perform any other duties requested by management.

## **Qualifications**

- Professional fluency in Portuguese and English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills in both languages.
- Bachelor's degree and two to three years of relevant professional experience.
- High level of proficiency in the MS Office suite, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to work independently and autonomously, balancing multiple tasks simultaneously.
- Exceptional analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to deliver persuasive presentations and reports.
- Ability to think strategically while maintaining strong organizational skills and a detail-oriented approach.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and set priorities.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and a proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships in a multicultural environment.
- Willingness to travel frequently (30-50 percent of the time), including occasional travel to rural areas.

**Preferred qualifications**

- A master's degree or postgraduate qualification.
- Prior knowledge of malaria control and infectious diseases.
- Experience working in resource-limited settings, particularly in Angola.
- Fluency in at least one relevant local language.
- Prior experience working in fast-paced, results-oriented environments, such as consulting, management, investment banking, or industry.
- Experience working and communicating with government officials, multilateral organizations, or development donors.
- Experience working remotely with a decentralized/remote team.
- Experience working in developing-country contexts.

title: Logistics Manager - Manila (Filipino Nationals Only)
body:
Duration : **6 months (with a possibility of an extension)**  
Start date : **01-Nov-2026**

## **You'll contribute to ending world hunger by ...**

- Ensuring coordination between Logistics and the other departments in the Mission, in order to provide the adequate level of support to Action Against Hunger operations in the Philippines.
- Managing the Logistics department, monitoring its performance in all the processes related to Logistics and Security to ensure they are in line with the Headquarters and the Mission´s Logistics Strategy, policies and guidelines.
- Contributing to the development and implementation of the mission logistics strategy in coordination with the members of Coordination Team
- Engaging and representing Action Against Hunger Philippines in consortium -led logistics strategies and participate in relevant logistics coordination platform

## **Key activities in your role will include**

**Objective 1: Coordinate logistics at the national level**

Internal coordination of the Logistics team in the mission:

- Analyze and define logistics team members' role and responsibilities on regular basis based on the mission and project/program requirement resources between bases
- Manage, monitor and follow-up of logistics, IT and security staff and functional management of base Logistics Officers
- Lead the consolidation and monitoring of the Mission Procurement Plan
- Manage and follow up to the logistics staff when deployed in the field to support emergency response
- Ensure compliance and support to the standardization of logistics procedures and templates, particularly at Manila and field level
- Lead and ensure the implementation of Action Against Hunger´s logistics procedures (KitLog) and strategy across the operations, including application and promotion of the LINK system across the mission
- Ensure procurement forecasting is conducted regularly with programme and support departments
- Monitor compliance and escalate significant risks and deviations to senior management
- Support the mission with partners and service providers as delegated by the senior management

Drafting of Proposals and Reports to donors:

- Lead and contribute technical, logistics and security related inputs to proposals and budgets in coordination with the Head of Departments
- Ensure timely coordination between the Program, finance, HR and communication departments
- Provide logistics information and supporting documentation required for donor reporting

Supervision of the supply chain:

- Lead and ensure implementation and monitoring of Action Against Hunger´s Supply Chain Management Tools
- Monitor and ensure compliance with Action Against Hunger and donors' logistics procedures
- Monitor procurement lead times and identify bottlenecks affecting programme implementation
- Implementation of the anti-fraud policy and its tools within the logistics department
- Facilitate the preparation of tender plans and procurement schedules for major purchases
- Ensure procurement activities are aligned with project implementation timelines

Budgeting:

- Contribute logistics budget forecasts and resource planning for projects and annual budgeting
- Contribute to any budget/proposal to be submitted to donors
- Review and validate the monthly logistics expenditure forecast across the mission in coordination with field offices and Head of Departments

Reporting, analysis and information management:

- Control and analyze the Mission´s Logistics costs on a monthly basis
- Consolidate, monitor and analyze Logistics Department's information submitted by the field offices and departments
- Analyze and optimize equipment use, including forecasting, disposal and replacement of equipment in line with Action Against Hunger and donor policy and guidelines
- Ensure the implementation of Action Against Hunger´s Archiving Policy
- Support audit processes and provide logistics documentation as required
- Ensure that monthly reporting requirements to Headquarters is met by the Mission

Communication Management:

- Implement adequate and relevant communication systems
- Analyze new requirements and the cost/efficiency of existing systems
- Lead and implement Action Against Hunger´s IT policy in the Mission, including troubleshooting and addressing IT related concerns in the mission in coordination and consultation with HQ

Equipment/asset management:

- Create and implement an equipment policy for the Mission
- Manage equipment according to Action Against Hunger and donors’ guidelines
- Ensure the correct and documented transfer of equipment on the completion of projects
- Ensure adequacy and efficient management of equipment in the Mission
- Lead ensuring accommodation/office/guest house contracts are drafted, reviewed, signed and renewed based on the needs in coordination with the line manager and finance department

Fleet Management:

- Ensure an efficient fleet planning and management in the Mission
- Create and disseminate a vehicle use policy and monitor safety compliance
- Monitor the maintenance and control of vehicles in accordance with Action Against Hunger´s procedures, including renewal of Framework Agreement

**Objective 2: Contribute to the definition of the mission strategy**

- Contribute operational logistics analysis and recommendations to support the development of the Mission's strategy
- Lead and support the implementation and dissemination of the Mission's Logistics Strategy
- Lead, promote and contribute to the implementation of the carbon footprint reduction plan over the mission and ensure collection of data to measure our contribution to Co2 emissions and implementation of environmental policies
- Lead the review, identify operational improvement opportunities on regular basis and propose corrective actions to the management

**Objective 3: Line-management of the Logistics team in Manila, and technical management of the Base Logisticians in the Bases**

- Ensure the cohesion and good communication within the department
- Lead, develop and regularly monitor individual logistics staff objectives and action plans
- Contribute to the implementation of Mission Training Plan, and monitor its implementation within the logistics department
- Provide technical support to field logistics team through weekly meeting and regular field visits
- Evaluate the performance of every team member, and contribute to the development their relevant skills

**Objective 4: Support humanitarian activities of Action Against Hunger**

- Lead and ensure systems and process are in place for emergency response in the Philippines
- Build logistics staff capacity and maintain emergency response deployment ready at any time
- Be available to be deployed in the field for new emergencies as requested by the line manager
- Lead the development, monitoring and periodic renewal of Framework Agreements for frequently purchased goods and services
- Ensure Framework Agreements are strategically established to reduce procurement lead times and support emergency response capacity
- Monitor Framework Agreement utilization and supplier performance
- Monitor supplier performance against agreed service levels and contractual obligations
- Conduct periodic market assessments to identify qualified suppliers and procurement risks
- Support the development of sourcing strategies for key categories of expenditure
- Assess supplier capacity, financial stability and operational risks
- Ensure adequate supplier diversification to mitigate operational and emergency response risks

**Objective 5: Operational support to the Mission´s security management**

- Lead and analyze the safety and security context in operational areas in coordination with the assigned Security Officer, Heads of Base and Country Director
- Advise the Country Director on matters related to safety and security management
- Contribute to monitor the compliance of all staff with the Mission´s security regulations
- Lead and ensure local standard operation procedures are developed and updated according to the timeline established at the mission and HQ level in coordination with the assigned Security Officer, Head of Base and Country Director
- Ensure physical status and availability of contingency measures and equipment (e.g. hibernation boxes, back-up vehicles), as needed
- Coordinate and ensure regular updating of Business Continuity Plans of the mission, including bases in coordination with line manager and head of departments
- Support Risk Assessment and Management in the mission

## **Do you meet the profile required criteria?**

- University Degree
- Experience of logistics management with an INGO in the Philippines
- Knowledge of donor guidelines and procedures
- Ability to work strategically
- Understanding of safety and security context in the Philippines
- Good analytical skills
- At least 3 years previous hand on logistic management experience in emergency response and development programs with a NGO in the Philippines
- At least 3 years of experience in safety and security management
- Experience working with and supporting people remotely
- Experience overseeing IT services, communications systems and IT support functions is desirable
- English is a must
- MS Office very strong command
- Advanced level of Excel
- Valuable prior experience in issues related to the promotion of gender equality or personal commitment to gender equality

## **Our remuneration package:**

- Compensation: based on Action Against Hunger grid
- Benefits: health insurance, accident and life insurance, leave entitlement, government-mandated benefits
- Fixed-term Employment

**Action against Hunger is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work such as but not limited to sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and/or financial misconduct; We expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through endorsing our code of conduct and other related policies and only those who share our values and code of conduct will be recruited to work for us.**

title: Chargé-e des Opérations - SENEGAL (JPO)
body:
**Entrée en fonction :** 1.12.26

**Durée :** 6 mois

**Lieu :** Dakar, Sénégal

**Statut :** non accompagné

Terre des hommes ne fixe pas de date de clôture pour ce poste ; le recrutement se poursuit jusqu'à ce que le poste soit pourvu.

**Tdh :**

La Fondation Terre des hommes (Tdh), dont le siège est à Lausanne et le bureau à Zurich, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant avec plus de 2000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices dans le monde. Nous nous engageons aux côtés des enfants pour garantir leurs droits, protéger leur vie et améliorer leur bien-être. Nous y parvenons grâce à nos programmes innovants dans les domaines de la santé, de la migration et de l'accès à la justice, conçus pour avoir un impact positif et durable.

**Contexte :**

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), fondée en 1960, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant. Tdh se consacre à apporter des changements significatifs et durables dans la vie des enfants et des jeunes, en particulier ceux et celles qui sont le plus en danger. Tdh est active dans une trentaine de pays, dans des contextes humanitaires et de développement.

En Afrique subsaharienne, Tdh intervient directement dans 8 pays (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinée-Conakry, Kenya Mali, Mauritanie, Nigeria et Sénégal,) et via des partenariats dans 6 autres pays (Benin, Cameroun, Madagascar, Niger, Togo et Ouganda).

Dans le cadre de la décentralisation de son modèle d'organisation, Tdh à ouvert un bureau régional à Dakar au Sénégal pour lequel un poste de Chargé.e des Opérations est ouvert.

**Responsabilités :**

Sous la supervision de la Conseillère Régionale en recherche de fonds, le.la Chargé.e des Opérations appuie le bureau régional et les équipes pays dans la mise en œuvre des activités liées aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds dans la région Afrique.

Ce poste contribue aux processus relatifs aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds — du suivi des opportunités à l'élaboration des propositions et au reporting auprès des bailleurs — tout en soutenant les efforts en matière d'engagement des bailleurs et de partenariats à l'échelle de la région.

Grant Acquisition Process

- Contribue à l'identification et au suivi des opportunités de financement pertinentes pour les programmes de Tdh dans la région Afrique.
- Appuie le développement et la soumission de propositions de projet régionales, multipays et pays : appui ou coordination du processus d’écriture, respect des procédures bailleurs, développement de plans d’action, écriture, traduction, enregistrement sur les plateformes de soumission.
- Contribue au contrôle qualité et à la finalisation des rapports pour des financements institutionnels tout en s’assurant de la soumission en temps voulu (suivi du calendrier et des échéances, relances lorsque nécessaire auprès des contributeurs, consolidation des données, etc.), conformément aux exigences contractuelles et aux normes de Tdh.
- Assure le suivi des besoins en cofinancement avec la CR Finance, appui l'élaboration de propositions et rapports de projets à destination de fondations en coordination avec le secteur philanthropie.
- Veille à ce que les informations relatives aux subventions et aux financements dans Engage360 et les GFU pays et région (système interne de Tdh) soient exactes et régulièrement mises à jour, et assure le suivi auprès des équipes concernées pour garantir l'exhaustivité des données. En cas d’absence de Chargé.e de Grant dans une délégation, assure directement la mise à jour des données pour le pays concerné.
- Appuie le développement des contrats de partenariats opérationnels (contenu, signature, archivage, etc.).
- Contribue à l’analyse des réponses aux demandes de financements institutionnels et philanthropiques.
- S’assure de la collecte et de l’archivage des documents institutionnels nécessaires à la signature des contrats en collaboration avec le siège, la région, les délégations et les partenaires.

Communication

- Appuie la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds et les partenaires, y compris la préparation de supports de recherche de fonds (ex. : témoignages, récits de réussite).
- Appuie le rapportage annuel à travers la vérification et la consolidation des données et informations projets, en coordination avec les équipes PREX, Q&A et Grants, ainsi qu’avec les autres parties prenantes concernées aux niveaux des délégations et de la région.
- Contribue à la communication interne liée aux projets (newsletter mensuelle, supports spécifiques, etc.) et consolide les éléments proposés par les délégations et la région, en veillant à la cohérence, à l’exactitude et à la qualité des informations rapportées.

*La description complète du poste sera communiquée aux candidats sélectionnés pour lancer le processus de recrutement.*

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

Etude supérieure (Master ou autre diplôme équivalant en relations internationales, développement ou autre domaine pertinent)

**Langues :**

Excellentes compétences linguistiques en Français et Anglais.

**Compétences :**

- Bonne compréhension de la gestion du cycle de projet dans les environnements de développement, d'urgence et de crises prolongées, notamment en Afrique
- Bonne compréhension du processus d’aquisition de financements.

**IT :** Maitrise des outils et applications usuels (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

**Conditions :**

Contrat suisse

Salaire mensuel brut CHF 2450- x13,36 mois

Assurances : maladie, accident, rapatriement

Congés annuels : 25 jours/an

Vols aller-retour vers le lieu d'affectation

**Code Global de Conduite et Politiques Ethiques de Tdh :**

S'engage à promouvoir et à respecter le Code de Conduite Global, à rapporter systématiquement toute violation du Code à travers les mécanismes formels de rapport de Tdh et à traiter toute violation des procédures et des processus de manière appropriée.

Sensibilise la Fondation aux risques de non-respect des politiques, de violence et d'abus, et aux droits qui en découlent, à l'égard des enfants, des membres de la communauté et de nos propres employé.e.s.

S'engage à respecter les principales politiques et directives éthiques, notamment la politique de sauvegarde, la politique de lutte contre la fraude et la corruption, la politique relative aux conflits d'intérêts et d'autres politiques liées à la prévention du financement du terrorisme et des activités criminelles, ainsi qu’au comportement sur le lieu de travail.

S'engage à mettre en pratique les valeurs et les principes en adoptant un comportement exemplaire, en parfaite adéquation avec le code de conduite, et en respectant toujours les procédures et les processus établis.

S'engage à développer une culture de management conforme et éclairée au sein de l'organisation et dans notre travail avec les enfants et les communautés dans lesquelles nous opérons.

title: MHPSS and Protection Coordinator - LEBANON - based in Beyrouth
body:
**PUI all around the world**

**Deadline for application: 30/11/2026**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** Millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents
- Thanks to the work and commitment of :
- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

**Focus on our activities in Lebanon**

Our mission in Lebanon has been open since 2012. PUI develops its integrated approach with health, protection, food security & livelihoods, and shelter interventions. Furthermore, PUI works on strengthening existing public systems and infrastructure, while also providing direct, emergency support to affected population depending on the local context. Today, the mission is implementing 12 projects.

**What about the MHPSS and Protection Coordinator ?**

**As Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and Protection Coordinator, you are responsible for the development and implementation of the mission's operational MHPSS and Protection strategies respectively as well as for the quality of current and future MHPSS and Protection programmes throughout the design, implementation monitoring and evaluation phases. You build the capacity of the mission’s MHPSS department and Protection department (technical teams and projets’ teams) and provide technical support to the project teams. You represent PUI to the authorities, humanitarian actors and donors for the MHPSS and Protection sector.**

For this purpose, you will be responsible for :

- Context analysis / Strategy / Development : You participate in the development of the operational strategy in MHPSS and Protection and contribute to the design of new relevant MHPSS and Protection interventions on the mission based on the identified MHPSS and Protection needs in the country, and in line with PUI MHPSS and Protection intervention frameworks. In coordination with the MHPSS and Protection teams in the bases, you monitor MHPSS and Protection activities in the country and analyse their strengths and weaknesses, offer programmatic adjustments in line with the needs, regulations and contextual developments.
- Programmes quality: You provide technical support in your field of expertise to the technical and programme teams (Specialists, PMs, Deputies PMs, Supervisors and implementing staff) and ensure the quality and effectiveness of the mission's MHPSS and Protection programmes through field visits, data analysis and regular check ins with the base teams within their specific areas of expertise.
- Representation / Coordination: You ensure PUI's external representation for the MHPSS and Protection sector to partners, donors, national authorities and local actors. You represent PUI in relevant Clusters/Sub-Clusters (Protection, GBV) or MHPSS sector working group meetings. You contribute to the good information sharing within the MHPSS and Protection sector and inform PUI of the discussions and update from these discussions.
- Human Resources / Training: You provide technical support to the project teams and in particular to the MHPSS and Protection teams. You provide support to the project managers for the recruitment of technical staff in MHPSS and Protection. Working alongside the Deputy HoM for Programs and the HQ MHPSS and Protection and Gender Advisors, you identify key strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and gaps within MHPSS and Protection departments. You work on a capacity building plan/training plan for the teams and supervise the content of these trainings where relevant. You also provide clinical supervision to the psychologists in the bases.
- Logistics and Administration: You ensure the teams under your responsibility follow logistic and administrative procedures and keep the logistic and administrative departments informed of any relevant developments.
- Security: You contribute to the compliance with security rules on the mission and share all information related to security to your line manager and/or to the mission's security manager.

**The challenges that await you :**

Support to enhance visibility and fundraising for Protection activities and Protection mainstreaming Lead the full integration of MHPSS services in the national system, including but not limited to supporting the integration of MHPSS in the national health information system, piloting the support for psychiatric hospitalization and supporting the primary healthcare network to directly provide quality MHPSS services Lead the integration between MHPSS, Protection and Health departments Respond to the rapidly changing and compounding needs of displaced and conflict-affected populations

**What you will need to succeed**

- **Training** You hold a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in psychology, psychiatry, mental health, or similar relevant field.
- **Experience** With at least 3 years of experience implementing MHPSS programs, at minimum 2 years of clinical practice in mental health or psychosocial care and 3 years of Protection Programmes management (including including design, implementation, and monitoring of interventions) or a similar position. You have a strong understanding of global Protection and/or GBV principles and standards and relevant bodies of international law. You have previous experience with NGO and in humanitarian or development settings, ideally with populations affected by crisis, displacement, or conflict. You have worked in environments with protection/GBV threats.
- **Skills** You have solid understanding of the IASC Guidelines on MHPSS in Emergency Settings and MHPSS intervention pyramid and of the IASC Guidelines GBV in Emergency, on Protection and on Gender in Humanitarian Action. You have competence in designing and monitoring psychosocial and psychological interventions, including referral systems and stepped-care approaches and in designing and monitoring community based and general protection and/or GBV case management interventions, including person/survivor centered approach and referral systems.
- **Qualities** You demonstrate good written communication skills, good knowledge of program management and quality monitoring, excellent writing and speaking skills, and good knowledge of donors. You demonstrate strong and proven capacity in diplomatically working among an integrated multi-cultural project team.
- **Languages** English and French have no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak another language, it would be a definite asset.

**A word from the manager**

*« In the challenging and interesting context of Lebanon, PUI is among the largest NGOs providing health/MH services and a highly responsive actor nationwide, including in the south and Baalbeck-Hermel. The MHPSS/Protection Coordinator leads a dynamic team of specialists in Beirut and oversees programming across our 3 field-offices. With the rapidly changing context and high needs, this is a demanding but interesting role contributing to safety and wellbeing at a large scale. »*

**PUI will offer you**

- **Status :** Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income :** 2 650,00 - 2 970,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
