title: Logistics coordinator (F/M) - Syria
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Syria**

Since December 2024, about 1.8 million refugees and 2 million internally displaced people have returned to their areas of origin (UNHCR, 1 October 2026, indicative), and many others remain displaced. Many return to areas where roads, public services, and health facilities are damaged or only partially functional. Humanitarian needs remain high, while access, administrative procedures and security conditions can change quickly from one area to another.

Médecins du Monde (MdM) works in Syria to protect vulnerable people's access to essential health care, including returnees and displaced communities. Our programs are run from the coordination office in Damascus, with teams and partners in several governorates.

MdM is currently operating in Aleppo and Idlib governorates, supporting three health facilities. Since 2026, program activities have been extended to Rural Damascus and Daraa governorates, where MdM will support two health centers.

**About the role**

You will provide strategic and technical leadership to the logistics team, support program planning and proposal development, manage logistics risks and ensures compliance with MdM France procedures, donor requirements, and applicable Syrian regulations.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator, you define, plan and implement all supply and logistics activities, while ensuring budget compliance and respect of MdM’s protocols and procedures. You lead and manage the logistics team.

More specifically, your main responsibilities are:

- Define, plan and budget logistical needs for the mission and monitor logistical activities
- Define, implement and adapt procurement plan and procedures
- Manage contracts related to logistics and supply activities
- Recruit and manage the logistics team, set objectives, define training needs, ensure skills management
- Ensure monitoring and reporting on logistical activities, adapt indicators when needed
- Supervise and manage the transportation of goods and people
- Supervise the installation and maintenance of office and accommodation areas
- Define and monitor IT and communication resources
- Ensure that the archiving system for logistics documents is respected
- Participate in the definition, implementation and monitoring of the safety and security standards
- Provide logistics guidance, training, advising and technical support to all field teams

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the logistics advisor at HQ, the program coordinators and the health managers, the support coordinators, the MEAL team and the security focal point, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following : logistics, supply chain management, procurement, business administration or a related field.
- Have at least 5 years of relevant professional experience, including experience in a coordination or management role in a humanitarian or international NGO setting.
- Have experience managing local and international supply chains, preferably including medicines and health commodities.
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently, Arabic is highly appreciated

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in premises management, infrastructure, energy systems and rehabilitation or renovation works.
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in complex, restrictive and volatile operational environments.
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of October.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Damascus, Syria
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: DCO Extender
body:
Overview of position

- Deploying district communication officers to support demand generation for polio vaccine and reduce missed children in immunization campaigns through coordination and engagement of communities and district authorities, and capacity building of frontline workers.
- Afghanistan and Pakistan remain the world’s only polio-endemic countries. In 2024, Afghanistan reported 25 cases of wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) and 106 environmental isolates, primarily from the eastern and southern regions. As of May 2025, two WPV1 cases and 25 environmental isolations have been reported. The eastern and southern regions continue to be classified as high-risk and remain priority areas for the polio eradication program.
- Given the ongoing risk of virus circulation and the shift in campaign modality from house-to-house to site-to-site, there is an increased need for community engagement between campaign rounds. This also necessitates adapting campaign-based social mobilization strategies to align with the site-to-site modality to ensure optimal coverage.
- To address these needs, the PULL strategy has been developed, focusing specifically on high-risk areas. As part of the strategy’s implementation, the realignment of frontline workers (FLWs) has been undertaken to concentrate efforts in high-risk zones while maintaining a minimal footprint in low-risk areas.
- Given the ongoing risk of virus circulation and the shift in campaign modality from house-to-house to site-to-site, there is an increased need for community engagement between campaign rounds. This also necessitates adapting campaign-based social mobilization strategies to align with the site-to-site modality to ensure optimal coverage.
- To address these needs, the PULL strategy has been developed, focusing specifically on high-risk areas. As part of the strategy’s implementation, the realignment of frontline workers (FLWs) has been undertaken to concentrate efforts in high-risk zones while maintaining a minimal footprint in low-risk areas.
- To further support the implementation of the PULL strategy, our client is planning to recruit District Communication Officers (DCOs). They will work under the direct supervision of PCO/SBC Extender and overall oversight of regional SBC Specialist/Officer. DCOs will supervise FMVs/Cluster Communication Supervisor (CCS)/ Campaign-based Social Mobilizers (CB-SM) and collaborate closely with other FLWs, partners, district authorities, stakeholders, community-based structures, and caregivers.
- The polio eradication programme is operating in polio high risk areas. Access to communities at risk is essential for the program to contain the polio virus transmission through increasing the community collective immunity. Polio outreach workers recruited from the local communities are deployed to address vaccine uptake issues and mobilise their communities. Due to the need to cover all the polio high-risk areas, including the most remote ones, our client staff members are unable to carry out such tasks. Under this contract, supervision and facilitation of community engagement activities, field/district level coordination and capacity building of FLWs is conducted through district communication officers.

Role objectives

Specific Tasks/Activities – District Communication Officer:

Planning and Coordination:

- Develop and regularly update integrated SBC and operational microplans at district and cluster levels.
- Design and implement quarterly evidence-based communication plans with a focus on missed children and refusals.
- Coordinate pre-, intra-, and post-campaign communication activities at district level.
- Lead planning and coordination of immunization campaign inaugurations at district, cluster and site levels.
- Ensure alignment of all key messages with national guidelines and community-specific needs.

Community Engagement and Influencer Mobilization:

- Map and engage local influencers (religious leaders, elders, women leaders, etc.) to support social mobilization and refusal reduction.
- Implement community-led initiatives and interface dialogues with various refusal groups.
- Conduct and monitor regular engagement activities to PULL children toward vaccination sites, reduce missed children and maintain zero refusal status.

Support to FMVs and Social Mobilizers:

- Oversee recruitment, onboarding, and deployment of campaign-based SMs in collaboration with PCO and district selection committees.
- Supervise FMVs and SMs, conduct on-the-job training, and ensure quality implementation of health education sessions.
- Plan and implement training sessions for social mobilizers, FMVs, and community influencers based on identified needs.

Monitoring, Supervision, and Data Collection:

- Conduct field visits to monitor RI, community engagement, and social mobilization activities.
- Collect and analyze social and immunization data of districts (e.g., BCG, OPV1/3, HepB) to inform targeted interventions.
- Retrieve and review lists of missed children after each campaign and facilitate revisits.
- Participate in and report from evening meetings during campaigns; follow up on corrective actions.

Vaccine and Cold Chain Management:

- Work with supply committees to ensure timely delivery and inventory of vaccines and supplies.
- Monitor cold chain capacity and vaccine management in pre, intra, and post campaigns at the cluster level.
- Fill and submit all required forms (Daily Summary Sheets, Vaccine Vials Tracking Forms, Forms on ODK and paper-based systems).

Campaign-Specific Responsibilities:

Pre-Campaign:

- Train CCS and CB-SM on social mobilization, child registration book, tally sheets, use of area map and reporting.
- Conduct cold chain inventory and readiness checks.
- Supervise pre-campaign awareness and engagement activities by SMs and FMVs.
- Plan and coordinate SBC interventions in low performance clusters

Intra Campaign:

- Monitor high-refusal clusters, ensure swift action, and report to PCO and regional coordination teams.
- Conduct intra-campaign monitoring using the ICM checklist and ensure daily updates on vaccine use.
- Monitor vaccine availability and address stock-outs promptly.

Post Campaign:

- Analyze PCA and administrative data for quality improvement.
- Ensure timely return of usable vials and proper destruction of unusable ones.
- Complete all reporting forms and submit within designated timelines.

Operations and Financial Management:

- Facilitate payments to performing SMs and FMVs.
- Prepare and verify district-level financial documents.
- Maintain documentation on campaign activities, payment records, and training expenses.

Reporting and Documentation:

- Prepare and submit weekly and monthly reports covering key SBC/communication activities, challenges, and solutions.
- Share collected social and communication data with the PCO in a timely manner.
- Document lessons learned, success stories, and best practices for district-level activities

DELIVERABLE(s)

- Integrated SBC and operational microplans developed and regularly updated for all clusters of the district.
- Monthly evidence-based communication plans implemented with focus on refusal reduction and missed children.
- Community engagement and influencer-led activities conducted and documented.
- FMVs and campaign-based social mobilizers recruited, trained, deployed, and supervised across all high-risk and convergence districts.
- Monthly training sessions completed for social mobilizers, FMVs, and community groups based on assessed needs.
- Join RI session monitoring visits conducted monthly, with feedback reports submitted to REMT/PEMT/DoPH.
- Cold chain inventories completed and shared.
- Pre-campaign; vaccine stock monitored and managed during campaign.
- Pre-, intra-, and post-campaign reports completed, including Daily Summary Sheets, Vaccine Vial Tracking Forms, online Form (ODK and paper-based).
- All social and immunization data (e.g., OPV dropout, missed children, refusal clusters) collected, analyzed, and reported.
- District, cluster and team level inauguration conducted.
- Payments to eligible frontline workers processed and verified; financial utilization reports submitted monthly.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Minimum qualifications and experience required:

- University degree in social science, political science, Sharia and law, medical science, public health, .
- Experience in the polio programme is given a priority.
- At least three years’ experience in relevant fields.
- Experience in health promotion is a plus.
- Ability to travel to the health facilities in the districts and villages for monitoring and support as required.
- Fluent in local languages of the area.
- Fluency in English language is desirable.
- Good computer skills including MS. Office.

Team management

 This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

title: Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.

- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.

- **Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. title: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor
body:
## About the Role

All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Advisor to build and lead the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems for its humanitarian response in Gaza. Operating in a fast-changing environment with constrained access, AHAH needs reliable, timely evidence on what is reaching communities, what is working, and where programs must adapt. The successful candidate will focus primarily on nutrition Monitoring and Evaluation, ensure quality data collection and reporting to leadership and donors, and put in place mechanisms that let affected communities give feedback and hold the organization accountable.

## Key Responsibilities

- **M&E Systems and Frameworks:** Design and roll out AHAH's M&E framework for Gaza nutrition program, including results frameworks, data collection and analysis, indicator reference sheets and performance monitoring plans aligned with donor requirements and cluster standards.
- **Distribution and Commodity Monitoring:** Establish post-distribution monitoring, commodity tracking and verification processes to confirm that AHAH assistance reaches intended civilian beneficiaries, and flag diversion or access risks to leadership.
- **Data Collection and Management:** Develop data collection tools and lead the use of mobile data platforms; ensure data quality, security, beneficiary data protection and safe storage.
- **Assessments and Evaluations:** Lead or support needs assessments, baseline and endline surveys, and periodic program reviews; manage external evaluations where required.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Produce timely, accurate reports and dashboards for AHAH leadership and donors; document lessons learned and use findings to guide program adaptation.
- **Coordination:** Represent AHAH in inter-agency information management and assessment working groups; contribute data to cluster reporting, as appropriate.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor field staff, on M&E methods, data collection and ethical data practices.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute M&E plans, indicators and budgets to proposals for institutional and private donors.

## Qualifications & Experience

- Master's degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Public Health, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of M&E experience, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in designing M&E systems, quantitative and qualitative methods, and donor reporting.
- Proficiency with mobile data collection platforms and data analysis tools
- Excellent analytical, communication and report-writing skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is an 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

title: Senior Nutrition Advisor
body:
All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Senior Nutrition Advisor to lead the design, delivery and quality of its emergency nutrition programming in Gaza. Acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women has risen sharply amid prolonged conflict, displacement and severe restrictions on food access. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership on nutrition across All Hands and Hearts' humanitarian response, ensure programs meet international standards, and represent the organization with the Nutrition Cluster, UN agencies, donors and partner NGOs. The Advisor will also help integrate nutrition into AHAH's wider food distribution, community health, shelter and education programs, and build the capacity of local staff and community health workers.

## Key Responsibilities

- **Technical Leadership:** Serve as AHAH's lead technical expert on nutrition in emergencies, setting program strategy and ensuring all nutrition activities align with Sphere standards, Nutrition Cluster guidance and Ministry of Health protocols.
- **Program Design and Delivery:** Design, launch and oversee nutrition interventions, which may include community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), MUAC screening and referral, supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E).
- **Integration with Food Assistance:** Advise AHAH leadership and logistics teams on the nutritional adequacy of food baskets and distributions, targeting of vulnerable groups, and safe handling of specialized nutrition commodities (RUTF, RUSF, LNS).
- **Assessment and Surveillance:** Lead or support nutrition assessments, screening campaigns and surveillance (including SMART-style surveys where feasible) to identify needs, track trends and guide program decisions.
- **Coordination and Representation:** Represent AHAH in the Nutrition Cluster and relevant working groups; build partnerships with UNICEF, WFP, WHO, health facilities and local NGOs to strengthen referral pathways and avoid duplication.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor AHAH staff, partner organizations and community health workers on nutrition screening, counseling, IYCF-E and the Code on breastmilk substitutes.
- **Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability:** Develop indicators and monitoring tools, ensure quality data collection, and report program results to AHAH leadership and donors. Ensure feedback and accountability mechanisms are in place for affected communities.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute technical content to proposals, budgets and donor reports for institutional and private donors (e.g., USAID/BHA successor mechanisms, ECHO, UN pooled funds, foundations and Gulf donors).

## Qualifications & Experience

- MD or Master's degree in Public Health, Nursing, Nutrition, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of experience in health or nutrition programming, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in nutrition programming.
- Proven experience managing teams, training staff and working through local partners.
- Excellent analytical, communication and representation skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is a 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

body:

Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Housing & Integration Specialist supports the long-term housing stability, integration, and self-sufficiency of IRC clients by educating clients on their rights and responsibilities as tenants and assisting clients with applications, recertifications, and renewals for public and subsidized housing programs. This role focuses on empowering established clients to independently navigate and maintain their own housing over time.

**Major responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Provide housing stability case management to IRC clients working toward long-term housing security and self-sufficiency, addressing needs that arise well beyond initial resettlement or arrival.
- Educate clients on tenant rights and responsibilities, lease renewals, move-in/move-out procedures, maintenance request processes, and change of address procedures, empowering clients with the practical knowledge to independently maintain stable housing and advocate for themselves as tenants.
- Providing financial education and coaching on budgeting for rent and utilities, housing costs and identifying housing that is sustainable based on household income.
- Assist clients with applications, recertifications, and renewals for public and subsidized housing programs (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8, public housing authority programs, and other government rental assistance), including gathering documentation, completing forms, and following up with housing authorities and landlords to ensure continuity of housing.
- Identify clients at risk of eviction or housing loss and provide early intervention, connecting clients to emergency rental assistance and other resources, and advocating on clients' behalf with landlords and public housing authorities to prevent displacement.
- Maintain working relationships with public housing authorities, subsidized housing providers, and landlords to support clients' long-term housing stability. Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations to support clients' integration.
- Track program outputs and outcomes (e.g., households served through housing education, applications and renewals completed) and maintain accurate documentation and data entry in IRC's client database to satisfy funder and contract reporting requirements.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- Use personal, insured vehicle with valid driver’s license to travel to client homes, housing authorities, and community partners as needed throughout the service delivery area
- Minimum of 1 year of relevant professional experience.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations preferred.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Superb organization, planning, and logistical skills.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Knowledge of, or ability to quickly learn, public and subsidized housing systems and processes (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8) preferred.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time at partner sites—including apartment complexes and public/government service centers—within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: NVPPA Supervisor (Service Staff Supervisor)
body:
**IRC background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job overview**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year:”*

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which IRC will serve newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal.

The NVPPA Supervisor manages the day-to-day work of the program's direct service team across a fully virtual, national caseload. This role is responsible for caseload management, case file review, escalation and resolution of participant issues, and consistent quality across Professional Advancement Plans (PAPs) and uses of direct financial assistance.

**Major responsibilities**

**Supervision and caseload management**

- Manage day-to-day caseloads for direct service staff, including assigning and balancing participants across Career Navigators and routing participants on credentialing and recertification pathways to specialized navigators.
- Conduct regular case file review to confirm that participant records, including eligibility documentation, PAPs, and case notes, are complete, accurate, and timely.
- Resolve escalated participant issues in partnership with the Customer Service Representative, and determine when an issue requires the Deputy Director's involvement.
- Support onboarding and ongoing training of direct service staff.
- Translate program requirements into standard operating procedures and desk guides for the direct service team.

**Program quality and compliance**

- Review PAPs for soundness and confirm that career goals and proposed uses of funds meet ORR eligibility requirements before assistance is requested.
- Ensure required safeguards are applied to higher-risk uses of financial assistance, such as vehicle purchases.
- Work with the data team to ensure required data is recorded in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) and electronic case files are complete for ORR reporting.
- Monitor progress against program targets, identify barriers in the service model such as digital access, language access, or credential evaluation delays, and work with the Deputy Director on practical adjustments.

**Coordination**

- Coordinate handoffs among navigation, training, financial assistance, and job placement so that participants move smoothly through the program.
- Work with administrative and finance staff to ensure financial assistance requests are complete, documented, and aligned with each participant's PAP.
- Coordinate with other resettlement and employment programs, IRC offices, sister agencies, and local partners serving the same participants to support appropriate co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Job requirements**

- Undergraduate degree required, ideally in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 2 years of management or supervision experience required, including onboarding, coaching, and managing staff performance; experience with remote or distributed teams strongly preferred.
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in human services, preferably in resettlement, workforce development, or employment services.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume caseloads in a compliance-heavy environment, including case file review and quality assurance.
- Demonstrated skills tracking and reporting information in a database; experience with ETO preferred.
- Familiarity with federally funded program compliance and eligibility documentation; experience with ORR-funded programming preferred.
- Experience developing standard operating procedures or workflow documentation, and familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways, preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to client confidentiality and data protection, including oversight of how a remote team handles sensitive personal and immigration documents, required.
- Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and time management skills, and demonstrated success working in a multicultural environment.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients regardless of national origin, language, location, or resettlement agency, required.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and remote collaboration tools required.
- Fluency in spoken and written English required; fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations desired.

**Working environment**

- Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet and a private work space suitable for confidential client conversations.
- Scheduling flexibility is required to serve participants across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($58,000 - $70,000 / Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Deputy Director, NVPPA
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE:**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year.”*

The Deputy Director, NVPPA provides leadership to the National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) funded program implemented in FY27. The Deputy Director leads the NVPPA team and ensures sound program implementation, compliance with ORR regulations, client success, and strong staff supervision and support.

NVPPA is a cooperative agreement carried out over a single 12-month period of performance, September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027. The Deputy Director is accountable for delivering the program on time, within budget, and in compliance with the terms of the award.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Program Implementation and Deliverables***

- Lead program start-up so that intake, staffing, data tools, and referral protocols are in place as clients arrive, with interpretation and device support where access is a barrier.
- Set and enforce service standards across a high-volume, light-touch model, including a completed Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and documented career navigation for every enrolled participant.
- Oversee delivery of training, job development, and placement support, and ensure related records are maintained.

***Grant Compliance and Award Management***

- Ensure the program is implemented in accordance with ORR policy, the terms of the cooperative agreement, applicable federal award regulations and cost principles, and IRC policies on data protection, client confidentiality, and safeguarding.
- In partnership with the Senior Director, serve as the program's primary point of contact with the ORR program officer and coordinate with ORR staff, partners, and technical assistance providers.
- Protect the integrity of program eligibility, ensuring eligibility rules are applied consistently and documentation is collected and retained for every enrolled participant.
- Own the internal control environment for direct financial assistance, including documentation before disbursement, alignment with the participant's approved PAP, vendor and training provider verification, and application of IRC Global Supply Chain protocols.
- Maintain audit-ready documentation and ensure required program and financial reports are accurate and submitted on schedule.
- Identify, escalate, and resolve compliance risks, including suspected fraud, working with IRC finance, compliance, and award management colleagues on corrective action.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- With the Finance Manager, manage the program budget, monitor spending, and ensure full and timely spend-down and closeout of the award.
- Where a shortfall is projected, provide revised projections and propose reallocation to additional eligible services or a budget revision, at ORR's direction.

***Data, Performance, and Quality Assurance***

- Ensure Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) is configured to program requirements and serves as the system of record, working with the data team on data quality, reporting, and staff training.
- Monitor performance against outcome targets and use data to identify barriers and adjust the service model.
- Establish and oversee a routine quality assurance cycle covering case files, PAPs, and assistance documentation, with findings tracked to resolution.

***Supervision and Staffing***

- Lead recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of a newly formed, fully remote team, and ensure all staff are trained on eligibility rules, eligible uses of funds, documentation standards, and the database.
- Directly supervise the NVPPA Supervisor and the Customer Service Representative, and manage performance, workload distribution, and professional development, and structure staffing so that direct service capacity can be adjusted as enrollment volume becomes known.

***Coordination and Representation***

- In close collaboration with the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), oversee guidance on appropriate co-enrollment with PIR and other ORR programs, such as Matching Grant, so that participants can meet initial self-sufficiency requirements while pursuing career goals.
- Establish referral and coordination protocols with sister resettlement agencies, IRC offices, and other service providers so that eligible clients can access the program regardless of which agency resettled them, and represent the program to IRC office leadership and external partners.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Senior Director, Economic Empowerment

**Directly supervises:** NVPPA Supervisor; Customer Service Representative

**Indirect supervision:** Direct service team, through the NVPPA Supervisor

**Key relationships:** Internally, the NVPPA team, Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, IRC office leadership, and headquarters finance, compliance, and award management colleagues. Externally, ORR, PIR providers, sister resettlement agencies, training providers, and employers.

**Requirements:**

- University degree in Business, Public Administration, Social Work, Economics, Community Development, or a related field required; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience with progressive responsibility in the design, development, and implementation of workforce, employment, or broader economic empowerment programming, including program monitoring and evaluation.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience managing staff, including remote or geographically distributed teams, with demonstrated ability to coach staff and manage performance directly and through supervisors.
- Demonstrated experience managing federally funded awards and their compliance and reporting requirements; ORR or other HHS award experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing client-level direct financial assistance or comparable payment processes, with a strong grasp of internal controls, required; experience with audits or funder monitoring preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to launch a program quickly and manage a budget of comparable scale through spend-down.
- Demonstrated understanding of refugee resettlement and employment services in the U.S. context; familiarity with credential evaluation and professional licensing pathways preferred.
- Excellent communication and organizational skills, including a track record of reporting difficult information to funders accurately and on time.

**Working Environment**

Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet, a private work space suitable for confidential discussions, and scheduling flexibility across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

title: Senior AI Technical Specialist
body:
## About Development Gateway and the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA)

[Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG)](https://developmentgateway.org/) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 10 countries worldwide. By leveraging the combination of programmatic and IT developer capacity and skills within DG, over the last 20 years we have *researched* data ecosystems, *built* digital tools to support those data ecosystems, and *advised* on data strategy and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

DG is one of several consortium partners, led by [IREX](https://www.irex.org/), implementing the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA, also known as ‘ASAS’) program in Jordan between 2023-2028, funded by the U.S. Department of State. As a large-scale development program, ASAS is a complex, high-paced and outcome-oriented initiative. The consortium itself comprises well over 50 individuals working on the program at any given time (based both in Jordan and abroad). From DG’s side alone, there are likely to be approximately 8-10 personnel supporting implementation at any given time, with at least 4 staff based in Amman, including the Senior AI Technical Specialist.

The overarching objective of ASAS is to improve the quality of early grades (K-G3) education outcomes for children in Jordan. The program aims to achieve this objective by supporting the education of student teachers while they are still at university (pre-service teachers), and also by supporting early grades students and teachers (in-service teachers).

DG’s role within the consortium includes supporting the safe, effective, and responsible integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Jordan’s education sector, in alignment with the national AI policy. In partnership with the Ministry of Education and Human Resources DevelopmentDG is embarking on an ambitious set of activities that will test AI capabilities in real-world settings.

## Job description

This is an exciting opportunity for an AI specialist who can situate cutting-edge developments in AI within Jordan’s policy context and understand how new technologies can strengthen education systems. Based in Amman, you will turn fast-moving AI advances into practical opportunities for the Ministry of Education, schools, and universities, and explain their value clearly and simply to non-technical audiences.

Rather than executing backend software development or heavy algorithmic coding, your focus is on driving active stakeholder participation, co-designing AI sandbox environments in schools and universities, and explaining complex technical concepts in accessible Arabic and English. You will directly complement IREX’s overarching coordination work by grounding high-level planning into practical, school- and university-level deliverables–ensuring MoEHRD counterparts, school staff, faculty, and administrators remain energized, engaged, and aligned with core project requirements.

Embedded within the ASAS project office in Amman, you will report directly to DG’s Director of Software Development (US) for technical strategy, with a dotted reporting line to DG’s local Project Lead/Advisor for daily operational alignment. Working alongside 30+ Jordan-based consortium colleagues, you will join a creative, globally distributed team that values hard work, practical problem-solving, and collaboration. If you excel at turning institutional friction into clear technical momentum, this role offers the platform to drive meaningful digital adoption across Jordan's education ecosystem.

At DG, we are a creative and dynamic group of people based around the globe. We value and reward hard work, innovative thinking, a commitment to teamwork, and a good sense of humor. With this role, we are looking for a new colleague to join our team and be our Senior AI Technical Specialist on the ASAS program in Amman.

The work you get to do

*In-Service AI: School-Level AI Centers & Sandbox Pilots*

- Provide technical support to establish six AI Centers in MoEHRD-selected schools, including assessing facility readiness, defining equipment and technical specifications, and verifying that installed centers are ready for use.
- Work with the MoEHRD and relevant stakeholders to co-design the scope, governance, school selection, institutional roles and implementation approach for AI sandbox pilots in three schools across the country including facilitating technical consultations and participatory workshops. Support the preparation of a technical brief outlining the objectives, scope, expected outcomes, and implementation approach for the school AI sandbox pilots, aligned with the Year 3 AI Readiness Assessment and policy brief.
- Lead the technical set-up of school sandboxes, support the design and delivery of sensitization workshops and hands-on training, , and help pilot schools shortlist 2–3 priority AI use cases.
- Support monitoring and evaluation of AI sandbox pilots, including assessment of technical performance, usability, pedagogical relevance, user adoption, and documentation of results, challenges, and lessons learned.
- Support the organization and technical facilitation of workshops to present and validate pilot results with MoEHRD, participating schools, and relevant stakeholders.
- Provide ongoing virtual sandboxing support, including a helpdesk that responds to technical questions and pedagogical questions on applying AI to agreed use cases.
- Translate pilot results into evidence and recommendations for MoEHRD leadership, the National AI for Education Forum, and a national approach to scaling successful use cases.
- Support MoEHRD and Field Directorates in assessing technical, institutional, and operational requirements for sustaining school AI Centers and scaling successful AI applications.

*Pre-Service AI: University Engagement & Institutional Integration*

- Serve as the lead technical interlocutor for partner universities, directly tackling engagement friction and driving active academic participation in project activities.
- Uncover operational bottlenecks and university requirements, translating qualitative institutional feedback into structured digital use cases.
- Lead the co-design, testing, and university-level rollout of sandbox AI environments, establishing clear feedback loops with faculty and administrators.

*Requirements Scoping & Technical Translation*

- Scope functional requirements for applied AI initiatives (e.g., automated reporting, documentation synthesis, data collection tools) without needing to write heavy software code.
- Translate complex technical concepts into accessible, bilingual (Arabic/English) specs and guidance notes for non-technical stakeholders, MoEHRD and university leadership, and vendors.
- Establish User Acceptance Testing (UAT) protocols, rollout sequencing, and data stewardship standards for school, university and ministry systems.

*Alignment with IREX Coordination & Programmatic Support*

- Complement IREX's programmatic coordination and oversight by serving as the Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX, MoEHRD, schools, and partner universities, translating agreed plans into actionable technical activities and supporting the timely resolution of implementation challenges.
- Serve as the primary Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX technical teams, MoEHRDHRD counterparts, schools, and partner universities, ensuring timely validation of requirements, coordination of technical implementation, resolution of operational challenges, and alignment with agreed work plans and institutional priorities
- Co-develop SOPs, workflows, and training materials that enable school and university staff to practically adopt AI tools in their daily routines.
- Provide regular, proactive updates on school and university technical readiness, operational risks, and adoption milestones to project leadership.

*Data Governance & Responsible AI*

- Establish practical ethical standards, governance rules, and privacy protections across all school and university AI sandbox pilots.
- Define data de-identification practices, accuracy checks, and hosting protocols to protect sensitive institutional and student data.

## Qualifications and experience requirements

- **Experience:** 5+ years of experience in data systems, digital transformation, or technology adoption, with proven success driving stakeholder engagement within Jordanian universities or national institutions. Experience with AI applications, data science tools, or emerging technologies in education.
- **Technical Alignment:** Demonstrated capacity to map user requirements to applied AI/data tools and structure low-risk use cases (no direct programming required).
- **Language Skills:** Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English, with demonstrated ability to draft technical specifications in both languages.
- **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in STEM, Information Management, Education, or a related field.

## Preferred (desirable) qualifications

- Degree and/or certification in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computer science is a plus.
- Familiarity with donor-funded programming (e.g., U.S. State Department) and their reporting standards.

Position Details

This is a **full-time staff position**, embedded in the ASAS office in Amman. The role is expected to run for approx. 2 years, pending annual performance reviews. The expected annual salary range is USD 50,000-65,000, depending on relevant experience.

title: Grants and Reporting Officer
body:
**Job Title:** Grants and Reporting Officer

**Function:** Programme Support

**Job Group:** Programmes

**Duty Station:** Odesa, Ukraine (with potential travel to field locations)

**Line Manager:** Programme Development Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/a

**ABOUT US:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict. Programming is founded on unarmed civilian protection and is thematically focused on protection in displacement, child protection, gender-based violence protection and inter-communal violence reduction, social cohesion, and civic engagement.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014-15 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022 and is operational in Kharkiv, Donetska, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson, Mykolaiv and Odesa oblasts. NP occupies an established space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB PURPOSE:**

The Grants and Reporting Officer (GRO) will collaboratively work with the Programmes, Finance and Operational Teams in NP’s Ukraine Country Office to ensure compliance with donor regulations and monitor grant implementation in-line with agreed workplans and objectives. This includes project activity oversight, donor reporting and supporting proposal development (where applicable).

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Grants Management and Reporting**

- Lead in drafting narrative donor reports and relevant annexes (i.e. logical frameworks, impact assessments, case studies), ensuring excellent quality, accuracy and adherence to donor guidelines.
- Support programmes, finance and field teams to understand donor contractual requirements, ensuring grant compliance from the outset of grant roll-out (i.e. through inception workshops).
- Maintain information management and involve all internal stakeholders in communications on fundraising issues for grants.
- Lead on updating relevant online platforms (e.g. UN’s Grants Management System (GMS)) with project data and reports, as well as responding to notifications and/or additional information requests from key donors.
- Compile and analyse data to write field activity reports submitted by staff and partners, aligning with grant deliverables.
- Act as team focal point for Salesforce (NP’s global online project management system), including creating new opportunities / projects, updating project activities, monitoring project outputs, tracking progress and extracting relevant information for reporting.
- Coordinate with the finance department to ensure that financial reports are submitted on time, comply with financial reporting requirements and align with narrative reported activity progress.
- Review donor reports, project proposals and communication materials as required.

**Partnership Support**

- Maintain regular communication and coordination with NP’s Partnership department to collect and synthesise data for activity and donor reports.
- Support NP’s Partnership department to draft sub-grant contracts in-line with donor compliance and agreed logframes, objectives and activities.
- Follow up with partners’ implemented activities and report progress through Salesforce.
- Support ad-hoc capacity development requests from partners and provide trainings, guidance and mentoring as needed.

**Other**

- Support with rolling out NPUA’s country strategy across all project sites.
- Travel to project sites to enhance understanding of the context and programming to develop proposals and report to/liaise with donors.
- Undertake other relevant tasks as requested.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Excellent and precise command of English, with exemplary oral and written communication skills, and an ability to develop high quality and engaging communications. There is a significant amount of writing required in this position.
- Significant experience developing narrative donor reports (for multilateral and institutional donors including the UN, FCDO, GAC, ECHO, SDC) under minimal supervision.
- Previous grants management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) or reporting experience within a non-governmental organisation (NGO).
- Experience in institutional donor compliance and familiarity with basic rules and regulations. An understanding of basic statutory requirements would also be an asset.
- Experience in implementing, analysing and utilising M&E tools.
- Experience implementing programmes, ideally in humanitarian emergencies and/or in Ukraine.
- Knowledge or demonstrable interest in civilian protection, human security, violence reduction, protection and/or peacebuilding.
- Relevant university degree in social sciences, international development or related area of studies is preferred but not required. Corresponding work experience will also be considered.

**Skills**

- Diplomacy, professionalism and adept at relationship building.
- Ability to manage sensitive information with discretion.
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies.
- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and work and live in a multicultural environment.
- Solutions-focused, creative problem solver.
- Genuine commitment to, and interest in, living and working at the community level.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

title: Grants Manager
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Grants Team at IRC in Sacramento works to leverage public and private funding opportunities through prospecting, proposal development, grants, and subaward contract management. The Grants Manager is primarily responsible for overseeing the full range of pre- and post-award activities required to prepare concept notes, proposals, and budgets, comply with internal approval processes, and align with compliance requirements of public agencies and private foundations. Work is performed under the supervision of a Development Director and in collaboration with IRC Sacramento’s leadership, finance, programs, as well as headquarters’ technical team, and awards and business development units.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Development and Grants Management***

Prospecting

- Represent Sacramento office in all regional opportunities, particularly for restricted funding, in close coordination with Site Directors, Development Director, Technical Advisors, relevant program leads, and grant coordinators.
- Collaborate with the Development Director in prospecting efforts, utilizing an internal standard operating procedure to support both restricted and unrestricted fundraising needs.
- In collaboration with IRC Sacramento Development Director, work with the Site Director to develop a funding strategy and timeline and perform prospective research on potential public and private funders.

Proposal Development (Pre-Award)

- Develop and manage the Sacramento region’s proposal calendar.
- Lead concepts note, proposal, and budget development, including ensuring log frames, program design, and narrative meet high quality standards in coordination with Programs/Site director, Finance Director, and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM), and ensure all supporting documentation in the applications are up to date.
- Provide pre-award support and coverage when needed to the local offices.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Coordinate grant opening and closing meetings for every funded opportunity across the Sacramento office portfolio.

Grants Management (Post-Award)

- Modify final budgets as requested by donor and Site Director/program lead and communicate with Finance and RAM to ensure incoming restricted funds will be tracked.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Provide support with reports, including copy-editing, coordinating report timelines with headquarters, and submission.
- Serve as a main point of contact for donors across Sacramento office to ensure communication adheres to IRC policy and best practices.
- Develop and ensure the effective maintenance of contract and grant files for each funded program with consistent documentation standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s Business Development Standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s internal grants systems (PEERS and OTIS).

Partnerships

- Be a local subject expert in IRC’s internal partnership process, PEERS, to provide technical support to the Partnership Grants Coordinator to ensure subawardees’ contracts are drafted with detailed information on scope of work, deliverables, fund disbursement, and monitoring plans in coordination with the partners and program staff, and in compliance with Finance and RAM.

***Supervision & training:***

- Provide leadership and management of the Grant Coordinator in Turlock, to ensure all tasks are covered and team workload is managed in a way that respects and promotes work life balance and professional growth.
- Provide training and support to new hires ensuring staff meet the expectations of their role and meet responsibilities in a timely manner.
- Be a local subject expert in OTIS and IRC’ RAM’s Business Development processes, and the local Sacramento/Turlock Business Development workflow.

***Systems & Accountability:***

- Maintain proposal calendar, pipelines, grants tracking, and regularly update senior management with up-to-date data
- Ensure the go/no-go review process of opportunities are consistently applied and strengthened by working with senior management to ensure proposals are of high quality and grants staff are at capacity
- Ensure continuous improvement on the utilization of Asana to track opportunity pipelines, award management, and reporting in coordination with senior management, Finance, and program staff
- Establish and continuously update a Standard of Practice (SOP) for Grants staff in coordination with the Finance team and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM
- Leverage regular communications with Finance, RAM, and the Sacramento office to improve SOP and workflow

**Secondary duties:**

- Work closely with site leads and program staff to prepare interim and final reports to grantors.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Development Director
- **Position Supervises:** Grants Coordinator (in Turlock office)
- **Indirect Reporting:** Site Director  
    **Other Internal and/or External Contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Director of Finance, Sacramento/Turlock Executive Director, Sacramento Program Managers & Coordinators, Technical Advisors, HQ Resource Acquisition and Management department
- ***External***: Foundations and public funders at city, county, state, and federal levels

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Bachelor’s Degree required in nonprofit management, community development, social sciences, social work, or related fields, or demonstrated work experience of similar knowledge. Master’s degree a plus.
- Certification or continuing education in project management, proposal development and/or fundraising a strong plus.

***Work Experience:***

- Five+ years of nonprofit or public sector experience in development and grants.
- Five+ years of experience in a supervisory role.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent writing, research, and organizational skills.
- Familiarity with grants process of government funding agency(ies) (federal, state, or county/city level)
- Familiarity with the Sacramento non-profit/philanthropy environment a plus
- Familiarity and comfort working with budgets and finance departments
- Ability to work autonomously in their scheduling and prioritizing within tight deadlines and focused on the work product.
- Self-directed but with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work well within a team
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications: Word, Excel, Outlook, and project management tools, e.g. Asana
- Experience in IRC systems of PEERS and OTIS a plus (for IRC internal candidates)
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

***Language Skills:***

- Excellence in written and spoken English

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard hybrid office environment (this is not a fully remote position)
- Occasional travel to Turlock office site as needed

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Compensation:** ($84,872-$91,137 - Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. **Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.
