title: Tupande Export Logistics Senior Specialist
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

The Export Logistics Specialist oversees and manages end-to-end export operations to ensure that goods leave the organization’s facilities and reach international vendors on time, within budget and in full compliance of all agreed regulations; including safety standards.

The role is focused on planning, coordination, documentation & stakeholder management for all exports handled by Soko.

## **Responsibilities**

Export Operations & Coordination

- Plan, organize, and oversee the entire export process from order placement to delivery at the destination.
- Coordinate with production, warehousing, and procurement teams to ensure accurate and timely order fulfillment.
- Liaise with freight forwarders, carriers, and third-party logistics providers to schedule shipments.
- Track shipments, resolve delays, and ensure smooth cargo movement.

Documentation & Compliance

- Prepare and review all required export documentation (invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, export licenses, etc.).
- Ensure compliance with international trade laws, customs regulations, and organizational policies.
- Maintain accurate records of shipments for audit and reporting purposes.
- Stay updated on changes in export/import regulations, customs procedures, and trade agreements.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

- Act as the primary point of contact for clients regarding export logistics inquiries.
- Provide timely updates to customers on order and shipment status.
- Resolve customer complaints, shipment issues, or documentation errors promptly.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with shipping agents, port authorities, and regulatory agencies.

Performance Management

- Negotiate shipping rates and terms with carriers and freight forwarders to optimize costs.
- Analyze export logistics performance and recommend process improvements for efficiency and cost savings.

Reconditioning

- Support and coordinate container reconditioning logistics when overseas regulators identify non-compliance issues.
- Ensure all reconditioning processes follow approved SOPs and documentation standards before goods are released to buyers.
- Maintain close communication with third-party service providers managing sterilization or product rework.

Supply Chain Traceability

- Ensure all exported goods have a clear, verifiable origin and traceable supply chain documentation.
- Work with sourcing and quality teams to build systems that enable end-to-end traceability of export products.
- Maintain audit-ready export documentation, certifications, and inspection records in compliance with global regulatory standards.

Cost efficiency

- Monitor freight costs, customs duties, and tariffs to control budgets.
- Identify opportunities for cost reduction across shipping, warehousing, and handling processes.
- Implement strategies that improve container utilization, reduce demurrage/detention, and optimize route planning.
- Regularly review freight spend and propose cost-saving initiatives without compromising quality or timelines.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 5+ years of experience in Supply chain, with at least 3 years focusing on Exports.
- Proficiency in export management systems and tracking tools.
- Proficiency in building complex formulas and functions in Google Sheets to support data analysis and reporting.
- Language requirement: English is required. Working knowledge of Swahili is also useful
- Strong planning and organizational skills.
- Excellent communication and coordination abilities.
- Proficient in export management systems and tracking tools.
- Analytical mindset for cost projections and performance tracking.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work under pressure.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

title: Clinical Services Supervisor
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, inclusive and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Clinical Services Supervisor oversees and provides culturally, and linguistically appropriate mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) designed to improve the holistic well-being of human trafficking survivors. The position has four main functions: 1) Clinical services - conducting mental health intakes and assessments, developing individual service plans, and delivering evidence-based and evidence-informed interventions, 2) Clinical supervision - supervising non-licensed psychosocial support staff to ensure services are of quality, trauma informed, and culturally relevant, and 3) Care coordination - with internal and external providers to ensure holistic client support, and 4) Outreach and engagement - to build provider and community capacity to identify, respond to, and serve survivors of human trafficking. The Clinical Services Supervisor must be an independently licensed counselor/therapist in WA State. Strong candidates must have experience helping help high barriers clients navigate and access systems, and delivering culturally responsive, linguistically accessible services. This position reports to the MHPSS Program Manager with clinical supervision provided by IRC’s MHPSS Technical Advisor.

**Clinical Responsibilities:**

- Supervision
- Ensure clinical quality of programming
- Conduct intake and assessment and develop individual service plans
- Provide interventions and activities in-office, remotely, and in community settings
- Maintain a clinical case load (approx. 15-20 clients)
- Manage crisis (i.e., suicide assessments, safety planning, mandatory reporting, etc.)
- Care coordination including warm hand-offs as needed
- Support development and delivery of psychoeducation training to IRC staff and community partners to strengthen response and services for survivors of human trafficking.
- Supervise master’s level Practicum Interns

**Project Management Responsibilities:**

- Arrange for interpreters as needed to appropriately engage clients in services
- Ensure timely and accurate documentation, data entry, and reporting
- Monitor program activity and quality through oversight and support related to case and project documentation
- Evaluate effectiveness of program related to client progress and individual service plan objectives
- Communicate and coordinate regularly with all levels of program staff to ensure that services are being delivered effectively and in a timely manner
- Strengthen and maintain partnerships with community mental health agencies to expand client resources
- Deliver capacity-building initiatives to strengthen community response and services for human trafficking victims
- Other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** MHPSS Program Manager

**Position Supervises:** WARN Mental Health MSW interns

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal*****:** *WARN Team, Family Wellness Team, Resettlement Team, Employment Team, Immigration Team, Youth Program Team, New Roots Team, Health Empowerment Team, Volunteer Coordinator, Finance Team, Operations Team, Development Team.*

***External*****:** *API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.*

**Job Requirements:**

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Holds a valid Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW) in the state of Washington
- In accordance with state Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card
- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy

**Work Experience:**

- Proficiency in English, and Spanish language(s) required
- At least three years’ experience with therapeutic intake, assessment, service planning, treatment reviews and case closures
- At least two years’ experience providing evidence-based, evidence-informed, or best-practice interventions
- At least one year of supervisor experience
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Strong intercultural communication skills: demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds
- Strong computer, keyboard, email, and general office skills

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard, professional office environment (hybrid remote and in-office)
- Access to reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area
- Position may involve evening and weekend work and travel

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $81,000 - $89,100/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: PIR Case Management Specialist
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Case Management Specialist provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. This position splits time between two programs: approximately 70% in ORR's Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and approximately 30% in the Home ARP program. The Case Management Specialist works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide case management services across two funding streams, dedicating approximately 70% of time to PIR clients and 30% to Home ARP clients, ensuring program requirements and documentation standards are met for each.
- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Help clients find and apply for permanent housing and support them through the move-in process.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days, up to 90 days of service.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information into IRC’s case documentation database, ETO, and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Case Management Coordinator

**Indirect Reporting:** Economic Wellbeing Manager and Senior Health and Wellness Program Manager

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal*****:** Immigration team, Housing Services team, Intensive Case Management team, Economic Wellbeing team, Development team, Finance, Operations and other IRC teams as needed.

***External*****:** All community service providers, landlords, partners and organizations.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- 1-3 years of experience working in an administrative role.
- Ability to work independently and as a team member in a fast-paced, cross-cultural environment.

title: Caseworker (Dari speaking)
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. Domestically, our offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.

**Job Overview:** The UHP Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The UHP Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

title: Malawi Extension Lead
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## **About the Role**

The Agronomy & Extension Lead will own the implementation of Malawi’s extension strategy, using HCD and SBC approaches to translate agronomic recommendations into simple, practical and adoptable support for farmers. The role will strengthen extension delivery, training and communication content, and use farmer feedback and impact data to continuously improve our approaches. They will work closely with Field Operations and Innovations to turn validated research into scalable farmer-facing solutions.

## **Responsibilities**

The role combines technical agronomy leadership with the design and management of a practical, farmer-centered extension system.

Own Malawi's agronomy and extension strategy

- Co-design and maintain a multi-year strategy aligned with Malawi’s impact priorities and farmers’ needs.
- Turn the strategy into annual OKRs, budgets, seasonal plans and clear ownership across teams.

Embed extension in Field Operations execution

- Build agronomy and extension priorities into the Field Operations seasonal calendar, training cascade, field tools and performance routines.
- Strengthen the technical capability of Field Managers, Field Officers and other delivery partners through training-of-trainers, coaching and practical support.
- Create clear feedback and support channels so field teams receive timely technical answers and can share implementation challenges and farmer responses.

Own the process of qualitative technical agronomic recommendations

- Use Human-Centred Design, farmer feedback and impact data to develop, test and refine agronomic recommendations.
- Work with Innovations, MEL and global technical teams to assess recommendations against local evidence, farmers’ realities and government guidance before they are scaled.
- Conduct formative research to understand farmers’ needs, behaviours and barriers to adoption.

Design farmer-centered extension and behavior-change interventions

- Translate technical recommendations into simple, memorable and actionable guidance for field teams and farmers.
- Develop extension approaches that use the right mix of group training, demonstrations, coaching and digital channels.
- Use the findings to design, test and improve extension approaches and communication content.
- Apply adult-learning, behavior-change and human-centered design approaches to understand barriers to adoption and ensure content works for different farmer profiles.

Monitor adoption, learning and impact

- Analyze results across farmer groups, locations and delivery channels to identify where recommendations or delivery approaches need to change.
- Lead seasonal learning reviews and maintain clear records of lessons and decisions to continue, adapt or stop interventions or crop offerings.

Build and manage a high-performing team

- Set clear goals, roles and decision-making responsibilities, and hold the team accountable for timely, high-quality delivery.
- Coach direct reports, strengthen the team’s technical expertise and support staff to take on greater ownership.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Expertise

- A bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Agricultural Systems, Agricultural Extension, Sociology, Anthropology, Design or a related field;
- Experience working in the agricultural sector, ideally with smallholder farmers, is strongly preferred.
- At least 5+ years of relevant professional experience in Agricultural Extension, Human-Centred Design, Social Behaviour Change Campaigns, or Rural Marketing, with experience applying these approaches in the agricultural sector
- Demonstrated experience developing, testing or scaling agronomic recommendations or rural extension interventions.
- Experience using adult-learning, instructional-design, SBCC or human-centered design approaches is strongly preferred

Core skills

- Technical judgment: Able to assess agronomic evidence, identify limitations and translate it into responsible recommendations.
- Farmer-centered design: Able to understand farmer constraints and create practical interventions that improve understanding and adoption.
- Data and learning: Comfortable using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions; strong Excel skills required, with R or Stata as an advantage.
- Strategy and project management: Able to prioritize, build critical paths and keep multiple seasonal workstreams on track.
- Communication: Able to make complex technical information simple and persuasive for field teams, farmers, leaders and external partners.
- Collaboration and influence: Able to work across Field Operations, Innovations, MEL and government-facing teams without relying solely on formal authority.
- People leadership: Able to set high standards, coach others and build a healthy, accountable team culture.

Cultural Fit & Communication

- Value Alignment: Deeply aligned with One Acre Fund values: *Farmers First*, *Work Hard*, *Grow Through Feedback*, and *Own Your Results*.
- Communication: Clear, compelling written and verbal style with a strong eye for data presentation and visual design (English required).
- Commitment: Willingness to relocate and commit to living in Africa (Malawi) for at least two years for a long-term career track.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Zomba, Malawi

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

## **Application Deadline**

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Immigrant Youth Program Coordinator
body:
**Job Overview:** The Immigrant Youth Program Coordinator or Success Coach will coordinate the services provided to immigrant children and their families to ensure they have access to basic needs, education, community resources, and other services crucial to their well-being and stability. The Program Coordinator will function as the primary case manager for the family and coordinate services with other IRC partners and subgrantees, as well as help expand the network of service providers to strengthen services and improve the family’s success. Additionally, the Program Coordinator is responsible for attending local events and cultivating community partnerships and other community resources. The Program Coordinator will provide technical assistance and leadership to a team of interns and volunteers and will help with the selection of candidates during each cohort recruitment period. This position will report to the Immigrant Youth Program Supervisor. Travel within Miami-Dade County.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive wrap-around case management services to immigrant children and their families, ensuring individualized support and advocacy.
- Conduct thorough needs assessments and ongoing evaluations to develop and implement tailored service plans that promote client safety, stability, and well-being.
- Empower clients by connecting them with appropriate resources and services and ensuring they have the tools to achieve their personal goals.
- Coordinate referrals and service planning with relevant stakeholders, ensuring a client-centered approach across all service areas.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for each family's case, maintaining strong working relationships with legal service providers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
- Deliver orientation services and ensure families understand available resources and program expectations.
- Provide crisis intervention, including mandated reporting to Child Protective Services when necessary.
- Participate actively in case management and staffing meetings to ensure consistent and informed client care.
- Meet regularly with Case Aide/Natural Helper to collaborate on relevant urgent cases and projects related to program implementation.
- Maintain accurate, confidential, and up-to-date case documentation in accordance with agency policies and regulatory requirements.
- Ensure high-quality data collection across all cases and contribute to data reporting and program development efforts.
- Promote program enrollment through client referrals and partnerships with other community providers.
- Collect client satisfaction surveys at case closure to track program success.
- Submit required reports and documentation in a timely and organized manner.
- Lead and supervise a team of interns and volunteers, including:

    - Ongoing feedback, communication, and coaching
    - Support for professional development and training
- Represent the IRC at community meetings and public forums, strengthening partnerships with local service providers and promoting program visibility.

body:
**Job Overview:**

The P&C Design and Change Management Specialist ensures that P&C transformation initiatives — Workday enhancements, process redesigns, and digital rollouts — are genuinely adopted across IRC's global workforce, not just technically delivered. This role owns the people-readiness side of transformation: understanding who's affected, how ready they are, what could go wrong, and how to address it before it does.

Working closely with the Training & Learning Delivery Specialist, Business Analysts, and P&C Partners, this role designs the change management approach for every initiative and embeds it from day one — from stakeholder impact assessments through go-live readiness and post-launch adoption tracking. The findings from this role directly feed the training design work led by the Training & Learning Delivery Specialist, ensuring training is built on a real understanding of who needs what.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Change Management**

- Design and execute structured change management plans and approaches for assigned P&C transformation initiatives, applying recognized methodologies such as ADKAR or Prosci, using templates and planning tools needed to do this consistently across projects
- Design and conduct stakeholder impact assessments at the start of every initiative, using a repeatable approach that captures affected populations, scale of change, adoption risks, and readiness gaps
- Develop stakeholder engagement plans for each initiative, determining the right messages, channels, and timing for each audience
- Build and execute communication plans for transformation initiatives, drafting audience-appropriate content in coordination with the Transformation & Digital Delivery Manager and relevant P&C teams
- Identify and proactively manage change resistance, developing approaches to address blockers and escalating significant risks with clear recommendations
- Establish change readiness checkpoints ahead of go-live, using tools and criteria to assess whether affected teams are prepared before launch
- Define and track adoption readiness metrics, identifying where adoption is lagging and recommending targeted interventions
- Identify and document change risks as part of regular project governance, with clear recommendations

**Partnership & Knowledge Management**

- Partner closely with the Training & Learning Delivery Specialist to ensure stakeholder impact assessments and readiness findings directly inform training design and sequencing
- Document change approaches, decisions, and lessons learned, contributing to the team's shared knowledge base
- Conduct post-implementation reviews on change effectiveness for every major initiative
- Stay current on change management best practices and organizational readiness approaches

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience**

- 3–5 years of experience in change management or P&C/HR transformation roles
- Demonstrated experience executing structured change management on P&C technology or business transformation projects
- Experience using or adapting change management tools, templates, or frameworks
- Solid working knowledge of Workday from an end-user or project delivery perspective is a strong advantage
- Change management certification (Prosci, CCMP, or equivalent) is an advantage
- Experience in a complex, matrixed organization preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Solid working knowledge of change management methodologies (ADKAR, Prosci, or equivalent), applied practically
- Clear and adaptable communicator across audiences, from frontline users to senior stakeholders
- Data-aware: able to define readiness and adoption metrics, interpret findings, and recommend action
- Skilled at identifying and addressing resistance and readiness gaps
- Comfortable executing established methodology with precision and consistency, while identifying gaps or improvements to flag upward

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Columbia.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Communications and Advocacy Officer
Logistics Officer
body:
Overview of position

To contribute to daily planning and coordination of WFP logistics operations including monitoring of services provided by contracted external organizations to ensure cost-effective operations and that set objectives are achieved in full.

Role objectives

- Contribute towards the development of logistics plans and processes ensuring compliance with wider logistics policies and WFP standards.
- Support or manage logistics projects or operational activities following standard processes and contributing, directly or indirectly, to the effective delivery of food assistance to beneficiaries.
- Collect and analyse data through research and networking with colleagues to recommend actions to senior staff to improve performance of local logistics operations.
- Conduct regular financial analysis and budget reviews, drawing out insights and recommending actions to senior staff to optimise use of available funds.
- Contribute to consolidation and preparation of operational pipeline planning, and to the management of operational aspects of the supply chain (procurement, shipping, port operation), including checking document and customs clearance readiness, loading and discharging operations and contracting of applicable transport, warehouse and any relevant logistics services.
- Contribute to supply chain by providing technical support and guidance to other CO unit/ services, divisions, particularly for emergency response.
- Guide and supervise more junior staff, acting as a point of referral and supporting them with more complex analysis and queries.
- Collate data and contribute to preparation of accurate and timely reporting, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), supporting a WFP-wide view of logistics activities that enables informed decision-making and consistency of information presented to stakeholders.
- Support the capacity building of WFP staff and partners for efficient and effective delivery of food assistance to beneficiaries (e.g. through the design and review of training materials).
- Identify and build productive relationships with logistics colleagues and staff within the area of assignment to support an integrated approach to food assistance.
- Follow emergency logistics preparedness practices, participate in preparation of CO Logistics Capacity Assessment (LCA), to ensure WFP are able to quickly respond and deploy food and needed resources to affected areas at the onset of the crisis.
- Participate in the on-going review of internal processes and procedures and identify ways to increase the day-to-day efficiencies.
- Act in an assigned emergency response capacity as required to meet emergency food assistance needs.
- Other as required.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Education:

- Advanced University degree in Transport Economics, Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Business Management, Mathematics or other related field, or First University degree with additional years of related work experience. Professional certification in SCM (Supply Chain Management) is an advantage.

Desired experiences for entry into the role:

- 3 years of post-graduate relevant professional / managerial experience with Master’s degree or 5 years of post-graduate relevant professional / managerial experience with Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain-related industry, Logistics, Shipping, Procurement.
- Experience in commercial or humanitarian transportation sectors.
- Experience monitoring and reporting on transport and freight market conditions and trends.
- Experience in dealing with shipments and clearing imports/exports with customs officials.
- Experience coordinating procurement and transportation processes with other units/ teams.
- Experience in warehouse and commodity management.
- Experience working with corporate systems (databases, software)

Language:

- Fluency (level C) in English language and the duty station’s language, if different.

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

- This Vacancy Announcement is for Pakistan Nationals Only.
- This vacancy announcement will be used to build a roster of prequalified applicants for future opportunities within same job profile at the current or lower level in Pakistan.

title: Logistics Associate / Logistics Assistant
body:
Overview of position

To provide specialized support functions and/or supervise staff performing standard logistics/supply chain processes and activities to enable effective delivery of goods and services for all delivery modalities.

Role objectives

- Provide specialized support to logistics operations and activities, following standard processes and contributing, directly or indirectly, to the effective delivery of food assistance to beneficiaries.
- Coordinate requisitioning and ensure timely delivery of commodities and supplies to authorized partners and destinations.
- Manage logistics vendors’ contracting activities including performance monitoring and measurement.
- Support gathering market intelligence, vendor assessments (e.g. transporters, retailers) to support vendor selection process.
- Identify, resolve and/or provide recommendations on specialized queries/requests for support, using initiative and following standard processes, to ensure timely and accurate resolution of enquiries with excellent client service mind-set.
- Prepare, monitor and revise budget for all delivery modalities, ensuring adherence to relevant procedures and in compliance with corporate standards.
- Monitor inventory management processes to track trends and account for the inventory status from source to beneficiary.
- Support oversight for commodity accounting data quality and integrity.
- Analyze operational pipeline and contribute to assessments and operational planning for all delivery modalities, to ensure that supply chain requirements are taken into consideration.
- Manage documentation processing for execution of logistics operations (e.g. customs clearance, invoice verification), take appropriate actions to resolve operational issues escalating complex issues to the supervisor.
- Perform research, collect data and conduct analysis, produce reports (e.g. CCTI, SPRs, financial closure, physical inventory, transport performance) and ensure information accuracy in corporate systems to enable informed decision-making.
- Liaise with internal and external stakeholders to support logistics operations management and contribute to effective service delivery.
- Supervise the work of support staff, providing practical advice and guidance, to ensure individual and team objectives are delivered to agreed standards and deadlines for all assistance modalities.
- Support logistics emergency preparedness and response activities including Logistics Capacity Assessment and Contingency Plan update, to support WFP’s response in emergencies.
- Perform other related duties or assignments in line with the position level and expertise as assigned by activity manager.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Education:

- Completion of secondary school education. A Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain, Business Administration, Economics, Engineering, Information technology, Mathematics, Data Science, Operational Research, and Business Analytics or any other related functional area is desirable.

Experience:

- A minimum of 6 years of experience in Supply Chain-related industry, Logistics, Shipping, Procurement, Material distribution is required.

Knowledge and Skills:

- Experience maintaining corporate systems and running queries on ongoing shipments, pipeline information, insurance claims, and food stock.
- Experience in administering third party service providers’ contracts.
- Experience in compiling contract documentation.
- Experience in contract execution.
- Experience in budget monitoring and reporting.

Language:

- Fluency in both oral and written communication in English and Urdu.

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

- This Vacancy Announcement is for Pakistan Nationals Only.
- This vacancy announcement will be used to build a roster of prequalified applicants for future opportunities within same job profile at the current or lower level in Pakistan.

body:

To manage a range of warehouse activities including safeguarding of commodities and supplies, and ensuring well-organized warehousing and storage service in compliance with WFP warehouse guidelines.

Role objectives

- Contribute to review of WFP corporate warehouse standards and procedures, to support efficiency and changing business needs.

title: Malawi Extension Lead
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## **About the Role**

The Agronomy & Extension Lead will own the implementation of Malawi’s extension strategy, using HCD and SBC approaches to translate agronomic recommendations into simple, practical and adoptable support for farmers. The role will strengthen extension delivery, training and communication content, and use farmer feedback and impact data to continuously improve our approaches. They will work closely with Field Operations and Innovations to turn validated research into scalable farmer-facing solutions.

## **Responsibilities**

The role combines technical agronomy leadership with the design and management of a practical, farmer-centered extension system.

Own Malawi's agronomy and extension strategy

- Co-design and maintain a multi-year strategy aligned with Malawi’s impact priorities and farmers’ needs.
- Turn the strategy into annual OKRs, budgets, seasonal plans and clear ownership across teams.

Embed extension in Field Operations execution

- Build agronomy and extension priorities into the Field Operations seasonal calendar, training cascade, field tools and performance routines.
- Strengthen the technical capability of Field Managers, Field Officers and other delivery partners through training-of-trainers, coaching and practical support.
- Create clear feedback and support channels so field teams receive timely technical answers and can share implementation challenges and farmer responses.

Own the process of qualitative technical agronomic recommendations

- Use Human-Centred Design, farmer feedback and impact data to develop, test and refine agronomic recommendations.
- Work with Innovations, MEL and global technical teams to assess recommendations against local evidence, farmers’ realities and government guidance before they are scaled.
- Conduct formative research to understand farmers’ needs, behaviours and barriers to adoption.

Design farmer-centered extension and behavior-change interventions

- Translate technical recommendations into simple, memorable and actionable guidance for field teams and farmers.
- Develop extension approaches that use the right mix of group training, demonstrations, coaching and digital channels.
- Use the findings to design, test and improve extension approaches and communication content.
- Apply adult-learning, behavior-change and human-centered design approaches to understand barriers to adoption and ensure content works for different farmer profiles.

Monitor adoption, learning and impact

- Analyze results across farmer groups, locations and delivery channels to identify where recommendations or delivery approaches need to change.
- Lead seasonal learning reviews and maintain clear records of lessons and decisions to continue, adapt or stop interventions or crop offerings.

Build and manage a high-performing team

- Set clear goals, roles and decision-making responsibilities, and hold the team accountable for timely, high-quality delivery.
- Coach direct reports, strengthen the team’s technical expertise and support staff to take on greater ownership.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Expertise

- A bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Agricultural Systems, Agricultural Extension, Sociology, Anthropology, Design or a related field;
- A bachelor’s degree in Agricultural Extension, Behavioural Science, Communications, Anthropology, Sociology, Design or a related field.
- Experience working in the agricultural sector, ideally with smallholder farmers, is strongly preferred.
- At least 5+ years of relevant professional experience in Agricultural Extension, Human-Centred Design, Social Behaviour Change Campaigns, or Rural Marketing, with experience applying these approaches in the agricultural sector
- Demonstrated experience developing, testing or scaling agronomic recommendations or rural extension interventions.
- Experience using adult-learning, instructional-design, SBCC or human-centered design approaches is strongly preferred

Core skills

- Technical judgment: Able to assess agronomic evidence, identify limitations and translate it into responsible recommendations.
- Farmer-centered design: Able to understand farmer constraints and create practical interventions that improve understanding and adoption.
- Data and learning: Comfortable using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions; strong Excel skills required, with R or Stata as an advantage.
- Strategy and project management: Able to prioritize, build critical paths and keep multiple seasonal workstreams on track.
- Communication: Able to make complex technical information simple and persuasive for field teams, farmers, leaders and external partners.
- Collaboration and influence: Able to work across Field Operations, Innovations, MEL and government-facing teams without relying solely on formal authority.
- People leadership: Able to set high standards, coach others and build a healthy, accountable team culture.

Cultural Fit & Communication

- Value Alignment: Deeply aligned with One Acre Fund values: *Farmers First*, *Work Hard*, *Grow Through Feedback*, and *Own Your Results*.
- Communication: Clear, compelling written and verbal style with a strong eye for data presentation and visual design (English required).
- Commitment: Willingness to relocate and commit to living in Africa (Malawi) for at least two years for a long-term career track.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Zomba, Malawi

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

## **Application Deadline**

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: AV Driver (HH)
body:
Overview of position

Required to transport cargo in the form of both food & NFI in accordance to the procedures & normative guidelines, as established by our client.

Role objectives

Under the direct supervision of the Traffic Officer the incumbent shall perform the following duties:

Drivers will have to perform trips to Sumy, Kharkov, Poltava, Zaporizha, Mykolaiv, Odessa, Kherson, Mariupol, Luhansk & Donetsk to deliver humanitarian aid.

Drivers will necessarily be part of humanitarian convoys organised & secured by the client to Mariupol, Luhansk, Kherson & Donetsk.

Security, clearances, advanced notification systems, deconfliction & negotiations with all relevant parties will be taken care of by the client.

Red Zones:

Average of 1 trip a week.

Part of UN organised & secured humanitarian convoys.

Security, clearances, advanced notification, deconfliction, negotiations with all relevant parties & risk assessments will be taken care of by the UNDSS (security arm of the UN).

Drive always in a safe & responsible manner with due respect & attention for other vehicles, property.

Any accident that may occur must be immediately reported to supervisor & / or other parties concerned.

Driver will only travel to authorized destination & only load authorized cargo, under no circumstance shall deviate from this unless authorized by immediate supervisor.

Will perform any other duties as requested by immediate supervisor.

Driver might be driving either 10 tonne truck or AV minivan (up to operations needs)

Project reporting

This role works under the direct supervision of the Traffic Officer.

Key competencies

Certificate in a relevant discipline.

Minimum of 2 years of demonstrable relevant transport experience is desirable.

Minimum of 2 years of experience in Europe is essential.

Working knowledge of English & fluent in Ukrainian & Russian.

Must hold a valid class C driver’s licence.

Must have had at least 2 years minimum experience preferably 5 years gained in the relevant driver license category.

Ensure that established route turn around times (expressed in days / hours) & distances (expressed in kilometers) are within parameters set as well as respecting the established standard night out allowances, notwithstanding abnormal circumstances, such as security.

Fuel consumption figures maintained within parameters set.

Vehicle maintained in good mechanical condition, limited tyre wear free from any breakages in accordance to standards set by the organization.

Cargo loaded, securely & safely, transported from origin to destination in a secure dry environment & duly received in a good sound condition at the receiving location.

Complete all vehicle administrative documents (vehicle log books, way bills) accurately & correctly & in turn, hand them over to Traffic Officer on a timely basis.

Required to report on time for duty as per establish established working hours & sign the time sheet prepared for this purpose.

Ensure that both loading / unloading times are kept to a minimum acceptable level & to report any abnormal waiting times.

AV minivans are likely to be Citroen/ Rolls-Royce (only cockpit will be armoured)

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Start date may be immediate - subject to be changed.

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

Candidates selected for this role will have to update their data at the military centre & / fill the exempt from conscription form at the same location, failure to do so will result in disqualification

title: WARN Mental Health Advocate
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Mental Health Advocate supports the mental health and resilience of survivors of trafficking through the WARN program, providing one-on-one peer support, referrals, and group-based services. This client-facing role includes one on one support, offering psychoeducation and skill-building workshops, and facilitating MHPSS groups. The Mental Health Advocate also coordinates program logistics, recruit participants, documents services, and supports evaluation through data collection. Additionally, they connect clients to appropriate mental health resources, assist with care coordination, and collaborate with supervisors to provide crisis support as needed.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Client Engagement & Support**

- Provide Psychosocial support including manualized interventions to clients. (Training in interventions will be provided.)
- Develop individualized action plans with clearly defined goals and activities based on assessment findings.
- With support from supervisor, provide health navigation services through referrals for clients requiring higher levels of mental health care to culturally and linguistically appropriate providers.
- Support crisis assessment and intervention for program participants in collaboration with supervisor.
- Represent the WARN Mental Health program at external and internal outreach events.

**Program Facilitation**

- Facilitate psychosocial group programs, ensuring alignment with contract guidelines.
- Facilitate psychoeducation and skill-building group sessions using evidence-based approaches under supervision.
- Recruit and enroll participants for WARN programs.
- Plan and organize logistics for WARN programs, including scheduling, transportation, materials, and space coordination.

**Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Prepare and administer Participant Service Reports with guidance from supervisor.
- Document client interactions and program activities through detailed case notes and data entry.
- Assist in evaluating current services and identifying opportunities for new program offerings.
- Use IRC software to document client information and other program materials.

**Administrative & Team Support**

- Attend and actively participate in team meetings, staff meetings, and relevant IRC trainings and conference calls.
- Collaborate with supervisor and team members to ensure program quality and compliance.
- Perform other duties as assigned to support the success of WARN programming.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** MHPSS Program Manager

**Indirect Reporting:** Clinical Services Supervisor

**Position Supervises:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal***\*\*:\*\* *WARN Team, Family Wellness Team, Resettlement Team, Employment Team, Immigration Team, Youth Program Team, New Roots Team, Health Empowerment Team, Volunteer Coordinator, Finance Team, Operations Team, Development Team.*

***External***\*\*:\*\* *API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant social services field (i.e., social work, human development, psychology) or equivalent professional and/or lived experience with social work, social service provision, psychosocial support, mental health, and community engagement.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant is preferred. However, in lieu of lived experience, experience working with refugees and/or immigrants; cross-cultural or overseas experience accepted.
- Understanding of the systems that intersect with migration and resettlement.
- Understanding of social service system.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Fluency in English and Spanish or other relevant language(s)
- Strong intercultural communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds.
- Strong computer, keyboard, email, and general office skills.
- Current driver’s license and valid insurance.

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\*

- Standard, professional office environment (flexible remote and in-office)
- Access to a reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area
- Position may involve evening and weekend work and travel

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $28-$31/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs.
